name: Inwangsan Shelter in the Woods
summary: Inwangsan Shelter in the Woods, a place where you can enjoy the tranquility of reading a book in the forest of Inwangsan Mountain
description_html: The Inwangsan Shelter in the Woods was originally one of the military guard posts built during the January 21 Incident in 1968. The Inwang 3rd Guard Post, which was the soldiers' living quarters (now the Inwangsan Shelter in the Woods), has been transformed into a public rest area by removing the reinforced concrete piloti structure and paneling and reconstructing it with a wooden architectural structure. The shelter offers both coziness and openness with its nature-friendly wooden interior and large panoramic windows that showcase the forest views of Inwangsan Mountain. It has become a popular spot for those seeking rest in nature, attracting not only hikers taking a break but also people looking for a quiet place to read and enjoy a peaceful moment in the forest.

name: Chundangji Pond
summary: On the rear garden grounds of Changgyeonggung Palace sits Chundangji Pond
description_html: On the rear garden grounds of Changgyeonggung Palace sits Chundangji Pond. It is known for its beautiful nature and fall foliage. Chundangji consists of two parts. The smaller upper half is the original location of the pond, while the lower half was initially used as a naenongpo , a place for the royal court to experiment with planting crops such as rice. However, during the Japanese occupation in 1909, the naenongpo was converted into a pond. In 1986, it was renovated into a traditional Korean style. Visitors can also see the seven-story pagoda, made in 1470, sitting on the shore of the pond.

name: Salgoji-gil
summary: A scenic path perfect for taking some beautiful autumn ginkgo trees and silver grass fields.
description_html: Beginning at Gwangnaru-gil (284-108, Seongsu-dong 2-ga, Seongdong-gu) while sometimes referred to as the "Ginkgo Tree Trail," Salgoji-gil is a beautiful path for taking that autumn stroll. The trail runs until Ttukseom-gil (72-129, Seongsu-dong 1-ga, Seongdong-gu) and earned its name from the Salgoji Bridge, which was built during the Joseon Dynasty and designated as National Treasure no. 1738 several decades later. The trail attracts crowds of eager walkers looking to enjoy a nice stroll as the trail itself connects where the Cheonggyecheon Stream meets the Hangang River. Along the trail, you can see Hanyang University, Hanyang Women's University, Seoul Metropolitan Facilities Management Corporation, and other sights of the city.

name: Hangang Art Park
summary: A beautiful interactive park and resting area for visitors to enjoy up to 37 different public art works that put an artistic spin on the Hangang River from a cultural arts perspective. Stop on by for some personal healing amid the cold, bustling life of the city in this beautifully imaginative park dedicated to the arts filled with inspiration, wonder, and enjoyment.
description_html: Breaking away from the common idea that the Hangang River serves as simply a place of leisure and picnicking, the Hangang Art Park aims to present the river in a much different light. Guided by the philosophy, "Hangang, art in the flow," the park seeks to create a Hangang River that gently flows along its course at the hands of artistry. In other words, the goal is to advocate the rebirth of the Hangang River park area as a place of thoughtful communication and exchange, in line with the concept of a more stimulating and impactful form of leisure that naturally melds with the "stop" and "flow" of the river body itself. The artwork found at the park was selected through a series of art competitions that featured both professional artists and artists among the public. An artwork selection committee, comprised of specialists from a variety of fields, then worked faithfully to develop and promote the chosen artwork, which the committee had selected on the basis of not only the representation of geographical characteristics, but also substance and diversity. It was through this process of selection that the artwork currently on display was chosen, all of which belong to one of the four specified themes of the park: "Lively," "Relaxed," "Inspiring," and "Secretive."

1. Dogs must be accompanied by their owners in the park.

2. Leash and waste bag are mandatory upon entrance to park.

3. Owners must supervise their dogs to prevent outbreaks of fighting.

4. Aggressive, sick dogs or dogs in heat are prohibited from entrance.

5. Smoking and food is prohibited inside park.

6. Please refrain from rude behavior and actions which threaten other dogs and pet owners.

name: Sayuksin Park
summary: Sayuksin Park is located atop a hill between the Hangang River and Noryangjin Station.
description_html: Sayuksin Park is located atop a hill between the Hangang River and Noryangjin Station. The park encompasses the historic Sayuksinmyo Tombs and the surrounding hilly area. The tombs hold the designation of Seoul Cultural Asset No. 8 and they are the burial site of seven Korean loyalists to the King Danjong, 6th king of the Joseon Dynasty. King Danjong was forced to abdicate by his uncle, who then assumed to the throne to become King Sejo. Seong Sam-Mun, Park Paeng-Nyeon, Ha Wi-Ji, Yi Gae, Yu Seong-Won, Yu Eung-Bu, and Kim Mun-Gi who opposed King Sejo and were buried here by the Hangang River.

name: Naksan Park at Night
summary: See the Seoul City Wall and beautiful views of downtown Seoul at Naksan Park.
description_html:
Naksan Park, located in Jongo-gu, is a great place to see the Seoul City Wall and take in views of downtown Seoul. The park is famous for the beauty of its nighttime views and the city wall. Seoul during the Joseon Dynasty was smaller than it is today. At the time, there were four mountains that were contained within the city limits, Naksan Mountain being one of them. Of the four mountains, Naksan was the smallest at just over 100m tall. The city wall that is along Naksan Mountain is divided by Hyehwamun Gate, Dongdaemun Gate, and Daehak-ro. For visitors that like to hike, they should take the Seoul City Wall trail from Hyehwamun to Dongdaemun or vice versa. If they prefer an easier route, they can begin the walk at Daehak-ro. Additionally, the park has been used as a filming location for many Hallyu dramas due to its beautiful scenary. Walk the old city wall and take in the beatiful twinkling lights of Seoul at Naksan Park. 



Frequently Asked Questions about Naksan Park

How much is parking at Naksan Park?

The parking fee at Naksan Park is 300 KRW per 10 minutes, and the parking can accommodate 29 cars. Since the parking lot is limited, it is recommended to inquire in advance (02-743-7985). (As of 2024)

How much is the entrance fee to Naksan Park?

Naksan Park is open to all and free of charge.

Can I enter Naksan Park 24 hours a day?

Yes. Naksan Park is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

name: Olympic Park
summary: Olympic Park was originally built for the 1988 Seoul Olympic Games and nowadays offers Seoulites a wide range of cultural, sporting and leisure opportunities.
description_html:
Olympic Park was originally built for the 1988 Seoul Olympic Games and nowadays offers Seoulites a wide range of cultural, sporting and leisure opportunities.Olympic Park is divided into four zones: arts and culture, recreation and sport, environment and history. In the northwest of the park are the environment and history zones featuring a walking trail along the ancient fortress and places to learn about the natural world. In the southern part of the park, the arts and culture zone is home to the SOMA Museum of Art and an outdoor sculpture park. In fact, Olympic Park is one of the world’s top 5 sculpture parks featuring over 200 sculptures by national and international artists including both famous names and emerging talents.


Frequently Asked Questions about Olympic Park
How much is parking at the Olympic Park?
The Olympic Park parking fees are as follows. The fee is a one-time fee. Please note that you will be charged again if you exit and then re-enter. (As of 2025)

  • • Regular car: 600 KRW per 10 minutes
  • • Compact cars, people with disabilities, people of national merit, low-emission vehicles, cars with children as passengers (more than three children): 50% discount
  • • Cars with children as passengers (two children): 25% discount
  • • Large vehicles (24 seats or more, 2.5 tons or more): 1,200 KRW per 10 minutes
What are the amenities in the Olympic Park performance hall?
The Olympic Park performance hall facilities include a convenience store, parking lot, ticket office, cafeteria, and luggage storage.
Is the Olympic Park always open?
To protect the facility and its visitors, please refrain from entering the park after 22:00. Entry is prohibited, and access hours are as follows. (As of 2025)

  • • Walking/bicycle access: 05:00-22:00 (24:00 in the square area)
  • • Vehicle access: 06:00~22:00

description_html: Hongik Culture Park (359 Seogyo-dong), which was created in 1984, had become worn and outdated over time. name: Seodaemun Independence Park
summary: Seodaemun Independence Park is a historic cultural site comprising a range of historic monuments and buildings.
description_html:
Seodaemun Independence Park is a park and important historic cultural site. During the Japanese colonial period, the park housed Seodaemun Prison. Japanese imperial authorities arrested and held political prisoners and independence activists here in brutal conditions before the liberation of Korea in 1945. Today, the park is home to a history museum and monuments to independence fighters.
At the Seodaemun Prison History Hall, visitors can learn about the history, struggles, and sacrifices made by Koreans during the colonial era. Visitors to the park can see the historic Dongnimmun Gate (Independence Gate), Independence Hall, and the March 1st Declaration of Independence Monument. There are several memorials and statues of patriots, such as a statue of Seo Jaepil (a Korean independence activist) and the Patriot Martyrs Monument.

name: Maeheon Citizens’ Forest
summary: Yangjae Citizens’ Forest is a lush public park located in Yangjae-dong.
description_html: Located in Yangjae-dong, Seocho-gu, Seoul, Maeheon Citizen's Forest is the first park in South Korea to introduce the concept of a forest, featuring a dense woodland rarely seen in urban areas. Established in 1986 to improve the environment around the Yangjae Tollgate, then a gateway to Seoul, in preparation for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Olympics, this park offers various facilities such as a lawn plaza, floor fountain, pergolas, volleyball court, basketball court, and tennis courts, ensuring residents' health and relaxation through free activities in nature. Additionally, the park houses the Maehun Yun Bonggil Memorial Hall and, to the south, significant historical monuments such as the Memorial Tower of Baengmagoji Battlefield, Korean Air Flight 858 Memorial, and the Sampoong Department Store Memorial, encapsulating key moments of modern Korean history.

name: Tapgol Park
summary: Tapgol Park was the first modern park built in Seoul and the birthplace of the March 1st Movement against the Japanese occupation in 1919.
description_html:
Tapgol Park was the first modern park built in Seoul and the birthplace of the March 1st Movement against the Japanese occupation in 1919. The park is home to several national treasures including Wongaksaji Sipcheungseoktap (a 10-story stone pagoda) as well as statues and monuments dedicated to various patriots and resistance members who fought for Korean independence during the Japanese occupation. It is also the place where the Declaration of Independence from Japan was read at Palgakjeong (an octagonal pavilion).


The park was once home to Heungboksa, a Buddhist temple, during the Goryo Dynasty period (918-1392). The temple underwent several subsequent changes and was later rebuilt under the name Wongaksa only to be destroyed during the Joseon Dynasty when Buddhism was officially repressed. In 1897, during the reign of King Gojong, the King’s financial advisor, John McLeavy Brown, proposed turning the site into a park. This was done and Tagpol Park opened to the public in 1920.

name: Naksan Park
summary: Naksan Park was founded in 2002 to preserve the remaining green spaces after much of the mountain was demolished during the Japanese Occupation.
description_html: Naksan Park was founded in 2002 to preserve the remaining green spaces after much of the mountain was demolished during the Japanese Occupation. There are a range of facilities for visitors including an exhibition hall, a hexagonal pavilion, a senior citizens' center, and sports facilities including badminton and basketball courts and several squares. Despite its modest scale, with a height of just over 100 meters, Naksan was one of the four guardian mountains, along with Bugaksan, Namsan, and Inwangsan, of the capital of the Joseon Dynasty. It took its name from the Korean words, nakta (camel) and san (mountain). In the past, the mountain was popular with yangban, the ruling class of the Joseon Dynasty, who came to see its famous sunset view. In Naksan Park, visitors can follow the walking trail along the Seoul Seonggwak (fortress wall) stretching about 2 km from Hyehwamun to Heunginjimun, the East Gate of Seoul.

name: Haneul Park
summary: Haneul Park is the most popular of the five parks situated in World Cup Park which was built to commemorate the 17th FIFA World Cup.
description_html:
Haneul Park is one of the five World Cup parks. It was established in 2002 to commemorate the 17th FIFA World Cup by transforming the former Nanjido landfill site. The park is arranged in a square shape and is divided into various themed sections, including areas planted with silver grass, native grasses, rock gardens, wildflower meadows, and sunflower fields. Notably, the observatory offers stunning views across the Hangang River, making it a popular spot for photography. Haneul Park is beloved for its annual Silver Grass Festival, held each October. Visitors can enjoy cultural events and programs set against the beautiful backdrop of silver grass fields. Ideal for visits with family and friends, Haneul Park is the perfect place to relax and enjoy nature.


Frequently Asked Questions about Haneul Park
Can I bring my dog to Haneul Park?
There is a dog play area at Haneul Park, and the information is as follows. (As of 2025)

  • • Operating hours: Open 24 hours a day, year-round.
  • • Location: Pyeonghwa Park Parking Lot Block G (near the World Cup Stadium Intersection)
  • • Fee: Free
  • • Terms of use
    • ① For dogs that have completed animal registration, they must be accompanied by a dog owner 13 years or older
    ② Bring a toilet bag and leash
    ③ Bringing in food is prohibited
Is it forbidden to enter Haneul Park outside of operating hours?
Yes. The World Cup Park, where Haneul Park is located, has been rehabilitated from a garbage island to an ecological park, and access is controlled at night to protect species. (As of 2025)
When is the Haneul Park Silver Grass Festival held?
The Seoul Silver Grass Festival is held every October, and you can see the silver grass in the fall. During the Seoul Silver Grass Festival, the park is open until 22:00. (As of 2025)

name: Jamsildaegyo Bridge
summary: Located between Jayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu, and 27 Jamsil-dong in Songpa-gu, Seoul, it is the 6th bridge in Seoul built on the Han River. It was named Jamsildaegyo Bridge because of its connection to Jamsil-dong.
description_html: The bridge between Jayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu, and 27 Jamsil-dong, Songpa-gu, was named Jamsildaegyo Bridge because of its connection to Jamsil-dong. Construction began in October 1970, and the sixth bridge in Seoul was built on the Hangang River in July 1972. It was a six-lane bridge at first, with a width of 25m, and in 2003, it expanded and re-opened as an eight-lane bridge. An underwater weir was installed on the Jamsildaegyo Bridge to maintain the water of the Hangang River at a constant level. It solved problems such as changes in the ecosystem caused by the reflux of seawater and aesthetic issues caused by exposure to river structures.

summary: Enjoy the sweeping view of Namsan Mountain while riding the cable car to the summit!
description_html: The Namsan Cable Car is the most convenient and fun way to reach the summit of Namsan Mountain! name: Haebangchon Alleyway
summary: Literally meaning "liberated village", Haebangchon is a popular attraction that was once made up of empty market spaces and alleyways before it underwent urban regeneration.
description_html: Literally meaning "liberated village", Haebangchon is a popular attraction that was once made up of empty market spaces and alleyways before it underwent urban regeneration. Connected to Namsan Mountain, the upper areas of this sloped village are hard to reach but worth the climb for its beautiful panoramic views. It is frequently visited not only by tourists and travelers, but also old residents and people from all walks of life. As Itaewon became popular in the mid-2000s, Haebangchon also started gaining attention from people passing by. Because of the gentrification of Gangnam, Hongdae, and Itaewon, Haebangchon began to transform into a gathering place for aspiring young artists and creators. The area is full of unique little workshops, cafes, and bookstores. Meanwhile, cafes and restaurant with a more sophisticated atmosphere have been appearing near the street of Sinheung-ro, continuing to bring in many more visitors to the area.

name: Yonsei University Campus
summary: Due to its beautiful campus grounds, Yonsei University is a popular shooting spot for TV shows and movies.
description_html: The Yonsei University campus is known for its beautiful architecture and often appears in movies and dramas. It's a vast campus, requiring at least a 2km walk to explore fully, making it the second-largest university campus in Seoul. Near the main gate, you’ll find mostly modern buildings. The campus also features numerous memorials, such as the Yun Dong-ju Monument and Han Yeol Hill, honoring individuals who have contributed to Yonsei's legacy.

Forming a gentle slope, the building has is a unique form of structure that surrounds a long centralized passageway. It even went to win the Seoul Architecture Awards back in 2008. Once holding the campus track field, the ECC site now holds a eco-friendly campus complex which stays cool during the summer and warm during the winter. Even more beautiful at night, ECC also houses study halls, lecture halls, exhibition halls, a bookstore, and many other school facilities within its walls.

name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
summary: Dongdaemun Design Plaza opened its door on 21st March 2014. DDP is running 24 hours a day and functioning as an open space for public.
description_html:
The Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), planned by Seoul City Hall in 2006, opened its doors on March 21, 2014. The purpose of DDP is to utilize design thinking for innovation and development. It also showcases global design trends and design innovation as a birthplace of creative knowledge in the 21st century. As a multi-purpose cultural space, Dongdaemun Design Plaza has been hosting various cultural events since its opening, including exhibitions, fashion shows, new product launches, forums, and conferences. Additionally, the seasonal Seoul Light event transforms DDP's exterior walls into a curved silver canvas, offering diverse scenery.

name: Bosingak Pavilion (Bell Ringing Ceremony)
summary: Bosingak Pavilion is the site of the giant bell and Seoul landmark, Bosingak.
description_html: Bosingak Pavilion, a bell tower located in Jongno 2-ga, Jongno-gu, was the original site of the Old Bronze Bell (Treasure No.2). Due to cracks that rendered the bell unringable, it is now housed at the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan. The current bell hanging in Bosingak Pavilion is a newly cast replica, funded through public donations. It was installed on August 14, 1985, and first rung the following day, August 15. Bosingak Pavilion is renowned for hosting Korea’s iconic New Year’s Eve bell-ringing ceremony, where the bell is struck 33 times at midnight on December 31. Additionally, the bell is rung 12 times daily at noon, except on Mondays.

name: Banpodaegyo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain
summary: The world’s longest bridge fountain (recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records) with 380 water jets and a dazzling array of multi-colored lights.
description_html:
Banpodaegyo Bridge is a two-tiered bridge over the Han River that features the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, (the world’s longest bridge fountain recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records) with 380 water jets and a dazzling array of multi-colored lights. The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain’s water jets are dynamic and can move in time to music creating spectacular ever-changing displays. Add to that the hundreds of rainbow-colored lighting combinations when night falls, and it is easy to see why Banpodaegyo Bridge is a magnet for tourists year round.

The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain operates from April to October every year, however the schedule of the fountain shows varies from month to month. Each fountain show lasts 20 minutes. In addition, Banpo Hangang Park hosts the "Moonlight Square Cultural Weekend" event every Saturday from 7:00 - 8:30 p.m. from May to October, featuring a variety of musical styles including classical music with commentary, acappella, popera, jazz, brass bands and orchestras.

name: Bukchon Hanok Village
summary: Bukchon Hanok Village reflects 600 years of Seoul’s history. The village is situated between Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace, and its streets are lined with traditional hanok
description_html:
Bukchon Hanok Village reflects 600 years of Seoul’s history. The village is situated between Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace, and its streets are lined with traditional hanok. Unlike other hanok villages (such as Namsangol Hanok Village), Bukchon was not created for tourists and it is a residential village inhabited by Seoulites. The best place within Bukchon to experience the old hanok atmosphere may be Gaehoe-dong. Here, hundreds of hanok sit shoulder to shoulder. Bukchon Hanok Village has been loved by many as a travel destination in Seoul as the charm of the traditional hanok is being rediscovered. There are also art galleries, traditional workshops, and restaurants that have been built out from from hanok, making these spaces both traditional and unique. In the Bukchon Hanok Village, which holds history and culture from time past in every alley, the Bukchon Cultural Center delivers information and cultural context for these traditional and historic spaces.

name: 63 Square
summary: The 63 Square skyscraper is a Yeouido landmark that features an aquarium, viewing observatory, gallery, IMAX cinema and performance hall.
description_html:
The 63 Square skyscraper is a Yeouido landmark commanding spectacular views of the city. Standing 249 meters (817 ft) high and comprising of 60 floors and three basement levels, 63 Square is one of Korea’s tallest and most recognized buildings. The glass elevators which serve the viewing observatory ascend at a speed of 460 meters per minute, taking just 25 seconds to reach the top, giving passengers the sensation of a rocket-powered take-off as they enjoy breathtaking views. Aqua Planet 63, a major tourist attraction within 63 Square, ceased operations on June 30, 2024. Additionally, the observatory “63 Art,” where visitors could enjoy views of Seoul and art pieces, also ceased operations on the same day. In 2025, the Centre Pompidou Hanwha Seoul is scheduled to open in 63 Square.


63 Square’s distinctive gold color is the real thing; each of the 14,000 panes of glass was coated with a thin film of 24-carat gold which catches the sunshine, reflecting gold, red and silver as the sun sets, giving the tower its stunning multi-colored sheen.

name: Namsan Seoul Tower
summary: Namsan Seoul Tower was built in 1969 as Korea's first integrated transmission tower beaming television and radio broadcasts across the capital.
description_html:
Namsan Seoul Tower, which has established itself as a romantic island in the heart of the city, is a 236.7-meter-tall tower located at the summit of Namsan Mountain (262m), a place long regarded as a site of good fortune for lifelong love. Offering a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view of Seoul from an elevation of 480 meters above sea level, it boasts the best vantage point in the city. As a symbol of Seoul and the top tourist destination chosen by international visitors, it has become a romantic sanctuary for couples worldwide who dream of eternal love. Popular attractions for couples include the "Locks of Love" and "Heart Chair," which are widely appreciated.


Namsan Seoul Tower comprises two main sections: the Lower Seoul Tower Plaza and the Upper N Seoul Tower. The Seoul Tower Plaza spans from the 1st to the 4th floor and includes attractions such as Gallery K, the Bodyfriend Lounge, and the Game Plaza. Visitors can also enjoy media art installations on a large 55-inch OLED panel. From the 5th floor up to the T7 floor, the N Seoul Tower features observation decks, the N Gift Shop, and various restaurants and cafes, all open 365 days a year.


Frequently Asked Questions about Namsan Seoul Tower

Can I visit Namsan Seoul Tower on national holidays or regular holidays?

Yes. The Namsan Seoul Tower is open 365 days a year. (As of 2025)

Can I visit Namsan Seoul Tower with my pet?

Pets are not allowed at the Namsan Seoul Tower. (As of 2025)

What are the operating hours of the Namsan Seoul Tower Cable Car and how much is it?

Namsan Seoul Tower Cable Car operates from 10 am to 11 pm. The ticket prices are as follows. (As of 2025)

• Round-trip fare: Adults 15,000 KRW / Children 11,500 KRW
• One-way fare: Adults 12,000 KRW / Children 9,000 KRW

name: Cheongwadae
summary: Cheongwadae, also known as the Blue House, is the Korean presidential residence.
description_html: Cheong Wa Dae, meaning "Blue House," was the official residence of the President of South Korea until it was opened to the public in June 2022, becoming a popular tourist destination. The main building features the president's office, reception rooms, and conference rooms, while auxiliary buildings include Chunchugwan, the State Guest House, and the rear garden. Cheong Wa Dae is closed every Tuesday, and tour reservations can be made on its official website. A tour of the Cheong Wa Dae grounds, which encompasses Nokjiwon, Sangchunjae, the residence, the State Guest House, and the main building, typically takes around 1 hour and 30 minutes to 2 hours. On rainy days, interior tours of key buildings like the main building and Chunchugwan may be restricted to prevent damage. In the event of natural disasters such as typhoons, tours of all or parts of Cheong Wa Dae may be suspended to ensure visitor safety.

name: Bugak Skyway Octagonal Pavilion
summary: Bugak Skyway, which runs along the northeast ridge of Bugaksan (Mt.), has become known as the most beautiful driving route in Korea ever since it opened in September of 1968.
description_html:
Bugak Skyway, which runs along the northeast ridge of Bugaksan (Mt.), has become known as the most beautiful driving route in Korea ever since it opened in September of 1968. The road is forested by thick greenery and leads to an octagonal pavilion (Palgakjeong) located at the top of the mountain, allowing visitors to appreciate a panoramic view of the whole city of Seoul. Ever since Palgakjeong and the surrounding areas underwent renovation and re-opened in April 2010, Bugak Skyway has grown to become a must for local residents and tourists alike. Palgakjeong is located at an elevation of 342 m, allowing visitors to appreciate not only the beauty of mother nature but also a panoramic view of the entire city. Visitors can enjoy a traditional plaza, a pagoda resting area, a wildflower garden and walking trails.

name: Myeongdong Cathedral
summary: Myeongdong Cathedral is the very first Roman Catholic parish church in Korea.
description_html: Myeongdong Cathedral is the very first Roman Catholic parish church in Korea. It is also the first Gothic building ever built in Korea and was designated as Historic site No. 285 in Korea. On the basement floor, there is a small sanctuary where the remains of the martyrs are enshrined, and where visitors to the cathedral can pay their respects. Every May, Myeongdong Cathedral holds a cultural festival. The construction of the cathedral started in 1892 and was completed in 1898. Unlike most Gothic buildings, Myeongdong Cathedral was built with bricks instead of stones. It gives the cathedral a characteristic atmosphere. The splendid high ceilings inside the church and the arches in between the magnificent inner pillars show the beautiful Gothic style well. The basement contains the remains of nine saints and martyrs, who devoted their lives to the propagation of Catholicism in Korea. Behind the cathedral, Seongmo Dongsan (St. Mary's garden) is situated. During lunch hour, pipe organs are playing here. The garden offers a peaceful resting space after visiting the cathedral.

name: Cheongwadae Sarangchae
summary: Korea’s presidential residence, Cheogwadae, has a newly-renovated “Sarangchae,” or a front-most section.
description_html:
Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a historical memorial museum where visitors can learn about the past, present, and future visions of Seoul and Korea. Originally the home of the public information hall of Cheongwadae (the Blue House, the Korean presidential residence) called “Hyojadong Sarangbang”, it re-opened with its present name in January 2010 after extensive renovation. Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a two-story building, with exhibition halls, souvenir shops, a resting area on the first floor, and experience zones on the second floor.


Cheongwadae Sarangchae features the Korea Hall, the Hi Seoul Hall, a traditional handicrafts demonstration room, a souvenir shop, and a café on the first floor. Various cultural events, such as demonstrations of traditional handicrafts and traditional Korean tea tasting, are held regularly in the lobby. The souvenir shop stocks Cheongwadae-themed goods and traditional Korean items. After viewing the exhibitions, it is pleasant to take a break at the café and enjoy a cup of traditional Korean tea.


The Presidential Hall on the second floor displays material about the former presidents of Korea. Here visitors can explore the political and economic events of Korea from the past up to the present day via pictures and visuals. Visitors can also see at a glance a chronology of the past 60 years of Korean history, as well as the major events in the democratization and industrialization of Korea.

description_html: The Seoul Science Museum, located in Hageo-dong, Nowon-gu, opened its doors for the first time in Seoul in 2017. It was established to enhance science and cultural facilities in the Gangbuk area, aiming to bridge the gap in science and culture among different regions and promote balanced development across Seoul's districts. As a science experiential facility aimed at youth, it operates six permanent exhibition halls with 221 exhibits and a special rotating exhibition hall featuring exhibits related to the history of objects. It offers various educational programs and events, including family-friendly science-making experiences, group science classes for elementary, middle, and high school students, expert lectures, science experiments, and nature ecology programs that families can enjoy together.

name: Joseon Yangban Hospitality Culture Experience Performance 'Onggi Concert'
summary: A two-hour curated journey to experience the one-table-per-person hospitality culture of Joseon Yangban families while appreciating Pansori, traditional performing arts, and dance.
description_html:
[Performance Introduction]

The Onggi Concert goes beyond simple appreciation of traditional Korean music (Gugak); it is a 'participatory prestige Gugak performance' where the audience becomes the protagonist of the Sarangbang (reception room) elegance of the Joseon Dynasty.


[Program Composition]


▶ Greeting (Approx. 10 minutes)

A docent personally welcomes each audience member in the lobby. Upon entry, an individual table (dok-sang) — tea and refreshments on a traditional small dining table — is set, allowing you to experience the essence of the Yangban guest reception culture of the Joseon Dynasty.


▶ Explanation and Performance (Approx. 75 minutes)

name: Seo-Seoul Museum of Art Inaugural Special Exhibition 《Our Time Begins Here》
summary: An exhibition that illuminates the construction process of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art and the narrative of time engraved in the southwestern region (and its people) as a 'record of memories'.
description_html:
《Our Time Begins Here》 is an exhibition that illuminates the construction process of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art and the narrative of time engraved in the southwestern region (and its people) as a 'record of memories'. Through the resonance of works that reflect the scenes of West Seoul remaining amidst the processes of creation and extinction, and the time differences that occur in between using the language of art, it constructs the memories of the construction of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art, its surrounding time, places, and community into a multi-layered structure. By weaving together the diverse layers of relationships surrounding the museum—from the people who passed through the birth of the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art together, to the region and future generations—under the name of 'us', it seeks to explore the meaning of 'time' that new media art possesses within the accumulated narratives.


You can encounter the artworks in niche spaces at address 0, which deviate from existing exhibition categories, such as the museum learning space, lobby, loading dock shutters, and grass plaza. Now, as the Seo-Seoul Museum of Art takes its first breath, we ask for your great interest in our time that will unfold 'here'.

name: Seoul Museum of Art Nanji Residency 20th Anniversary Exhibition 《AMOR EX MACHINA》
summary: An exhibition that recalls the old word 'love' once again through contemporary senses.
description_html: The 20th-anniversary exhibition of the Seoul Museum of Art's Nanji Residency, 《The Origin of Love (AMOR EX MACHINA)》, is structured as a journey to look back on the meaning of love by borrowing the archetypes of old stories in an era where technology rewrites relationships. Technology is no longer a tool placed outside of life, but has become an environment that conditions our senses and relationships. We wake up to smartphone alarms, move along paths indicated by satellites, and spend our days encountering news selected by algorithms. Within this, the ways we remember and form relationships are also changing. The exhibition proposes that our destination amidst the changing landscape of technology lies in love, the sense that makes us human.

name: Rembrandt to Goya, Master of European Painting from the Toledo Museum of Art
summary: An exhibition presenting over 50 original paintings by master artists who have led the history of Western art, selected from the representative collections of the Toledo Museum of Art in the United St
description_html:
Where you can directly encounter original paintings by European masters such as Rembrandt, Goya, Jacques-Louis David, and Turner, will be held at the ALT.1 Museum in The Hyundai Seoul from March 21 to July 4, 2026.

This exhibition is a large-scale classic painting exhibition that carefully selects and presents over 50 paintings by masters who led the flow of Western art history from the mid-16th century to the mid-19th century, among the representative collections of the Toledo Museum of Art located in Ohio, USA. You can observe in one place the works that formed major turning points in the history of European painting, from the post-Renaissance period to Baroque, Rococo, Neoclassicism, and Romanticism.

The exhibition is composed of a total of 6 sections, structured so that visitors can also examine the social and cultural roles that painting has played within the history of European art. Visitors can broadly experience not only the pictorial perfection of the works but also the historical background, philosophical context, patronage structures, and the flow of the art market contained within them.

This exhibition, which introduces the European painting collection of the Toledo Museum of Art with a history of over 100 years to Korea, is expected to be a special opportunity to directly verify the flow of Western art history and the artistic achievements of the masters as a blockbuster exhibition centered on original paintings.

name: Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh
summary: An exhibition exploring the new meanings and possibilities of what we define as "noise"—elements that seamless order has long excluded within the overwhelming torrent of information.
description_html: 《Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh》 is a two-person exhibition featuring Camille Norment and Min Oh that sheds new light on what is commonly referred to as "noise," including irregular sounds, unpredictable variables, and elements pushed outside the boundaries of established systems. Noise is recontextualized not as an obstruction to be eliminated, but as a fertile ground where new relationships and meanings emerge. Camille Norment and Min Oh respond to this inquiry through their respective creative methodologies. Min Oh presents her time-based installation series, Simultaneous, displayed together in one place for the first time—a body of work researched and produced over several years as part of the Arko Multi-disciplinary Arts Support Project. Concurrently, Camille Norment marks her inaugural solo presentation at a domestic museum with Plexus (Rhizome) Seoul, a sound installation commissioned specifically by the Arko Art Center.

name: A Wardrobe of Imagination - E-Land Collection Special Exhibition
summary: The magnificent beginnings of global designers, from Alexander McQueen to Yves Saint Laurent.
description_html:
We recall the moment of opening a wardrobe door. The time brushing past fabrics, the memories lingering on our fingertips, countless garments and stories, and small attempts accumulate to become a single legacy. This exhibition focuses on the unseen, initial moments before fashion is completed. It is a journey tracing how the smallest fragments of thought—an unfamiliar object, a passing landscape, a sudden imagination—are realized into a single garment.


A single flower, a folded piece of paper, and a moment of light and shadow are reborn as wearable art through a designer's perspective. Through a carefully selected collection from the 500,000 authentic archives amassed by the E-Land Museum over 30 years, you can encounter the magnificent beginnings of global designers, from Alexander McQueen to Yves Saint Laurent, in one place.

name: Welcome to Hanseongbu: Governing the Capital of Joseon
summary: Visit Hanseongbu, the Seoul City Hall of the Joseon Dynasty, to handle your affairs! Seoul Museum of History Special Exhibition.
description_html:
Hanseongbu was the institution that managed the affairs of the capital, much like today's Seoul City Hall, and its head, the Panyun, oversaw the entire capital city and led its urban administration. Furthermore, it also possessed the characteristics of a central administrative agency, directly participating in state administration. Therefore, Hanseongbu was in charge of urban administration—such as household registry compilation, housing management, and the processing of various civil complaints—while concurrently undertaking nationwide duties, including maintaining order in the royal capital, storing household registries, and handling legal disputes. This exhibition comprehensively illuminates the various functions and aspects of Hanseongbu, aiming to reflect on the appearance and significance of modern-day Seoul through this historical lens.


The realities of administration captured in historical records and the stories of the people who lived within those systems continue to offer valid questions and profound insights for us living today. We hope that the familiar yet unfamiliar story of Hanseongbu unfolding in this exhibition will serve as an opportunity to look anew at Seoul, the city where we work and live today.

name: Yoo Youngkuk : A Mountain Within Me
summary: The largest retrospective to date commemorating the 110th anniversary of Yoo Youngkuk's birth and the inaugural project of the 'Korean Modern Masters Exhibition' series at the Seoul Museum of Art.
description_html: 《Yoo Youngkuk: A Mountain Within Me》 is the largest retrospective to date commemorating the 110th anniversary of the birth of Yoo Youngkuk (1916–2002), a pioneer of Korean abstract art, and the inaugural project of the newly presented 'Korean Modern Masters Exhibition' series by the Seoul Museum of Art. This exhibition comprehensively illuminates his 60-year artistic career, from his early abstract experiments in Tokyo in 1935 to his later introspective abstraction, through over 170 works, including previously unreleased paintings, reliefs, photographs, drawings, and archival materials. Penetrating the turbulence of the Japanese colonial period, the Korean War, and the era of rapid economic growth, his paintings, which practiced abstraction, the avant-garde of his time, in both life and art, speak to us once again with profound resonance from today's perspective, questioning the very essence of creation.

name: Where Writing Breathes
summary: An exhibition that uses our familiar language as a map to read and sense writing in a different way.
description_html: 《Where Writing Breathes》 is an exhibition that explores 'Creation', the institutional agenda of the Seoul Museum of Art for 2026. The word 'author' is widely used not only in the art world but also in various fields such as literature and music, strongly connotes the meaning of creation or expressing an artwork originally. This exhibition is inspired by the general perception of an 'author' as a person who writes, namely a litterateur, and seeks to understand artistic creation through 'writing,' paying attention to the texts produced by artists. The exhibition's title, 'Geuljit' (Writing), refers to the gestures of writing that have taken on various forms of movement, metaphorically representing the vitality of writing that passes through the artist's body and unfolds in the exhibition space.

name: Mandy El-Sayegh : For Theresa
summary: A solo exhibition of Mandy El-Sayegh (b.1985), who is based in London.
description_html: Space K Seoul, Kolon’s cultural art sharing space, hosts the solo exhibition "For Theresa" by Mandy El-Sayegh (b.1985), who is based in London. Born in Malaysia with Palestinian and Chinese heritage, the artist has developed unique archival installation works using data collection and editing methods based on the 'outsider's perspective' she experienced while growing up in Western society. Mandy El-Sayegh questions what the institutionalized systems of knowledge and classification systems that have defined our world have excluded and what they have naturalized. In particular, for this exhibition, she extensively incorporates printed materials such as old maps, calligraphy, and banknotes that she directly collected while visiting museums, old bookstores, and flea markets in Korea. Through the archival techniques of collection and classification, she traces the political implications of how such material traces have contributed to the accumulation and maintenance of power.

summary: A moment when a familiar space feels unfamiliar, encounter the Strange K-Beauty from a new perspective with Cocoheali.

summary: A solo exhibition by Somokjang Semi, reinterpreting traditional somokjang (woodworking) techniques in a modern way.
description_html: How does our body operate in an art museum? While gazing at the artworks and walking through the exhibition hall, the viewer's body moves amidst concentration and tension. Nevertheless, when talking about viewing, the body rarely appears. The exhibition pays attention to the 'body', which is easily overlooked within the art museum experience in this way. An interlude is originally music played between acts in an opera or play, changing the atmosphere and preparing for the transition to the next scene. Like an interlude, the exhibition is situated amidst the journey of viewing, providing a buffer time to relax the body and tune the senses.

name: Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul
summary: A cultural journey to experience Louis Vuitton's travel, craftsmanship, and heritage
description_html:
'Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul' is a cultural journey to experience Louis Vuitton's travel, craftsmanship, and heritage, serving as an immersive exhibition illuminating the brand's legacy.

It is a space that unravels the philosophy of travel and the creative heritage that the Maison has continued for over 170 years into a single narrative. The story, starting from trunk production in 1854, introduces the journey of Louis Vuitton's development into a global cultural house through thematic spaces. Following the exhibition route leading from the 5th floor down to the 4th floor, the narrative of Louis Vuitton's creation and travel unfolds naturally.

The exhibition consists of a total of 12 spaces, unfolding the brand's history starting with trunks, the origin of the monogram, the artisan's workshop, the evolution of iconic bags, and Louis Vuitton's cultural narrative expanded through art and design collaborations, music, and fashion, just like a single journey.

name: Art Cube 2R2
summary: An exhibition platform that expands and connects digitally generated art into offline exhibition experiences.
description_html: Art Cube 2R2 is a complex exhibition space operated by Art Token Inc., an art content solution company. It serves as an exhibition platform that expands and connects digitally generated art into offline exhibition experiences. Based on the convergence of art and technology, it is designed to allow visitors to multi-dimensionally experience works of various genres, such as painting, drawing, installation, media art, and digital content, within a single space. Furthermore, as a space of connection bridging the inside and outside of boundaries, it oversees the flow of contemporary art where the past and present, reality and imagination, and the local and global intersect. By connecting domestic and international artists, content, technologies, and platforms, it expands the possibilities of exchange. Going beyond a simple exhibition hall, it experiments with the physical realization of digital art and new distribution methods for art content. Through these endeavors, it continuously explores new possibilities for art appreciation and exhibition formats, presenting a new gallery model reflecting contemporary art and media environments.

name: Dilkusha
summary: Dilkusha, a red-brick house signifying "a joyful heart" in Persian. A historic residence reflecting the lives of the Taylor family who built it a century ago, alongside the elegant narrative embedded
description_html: Dilkusha, meaning "a joyful heart" in Persian, is the historical name given to the residence of Albert W. Taylor and Mary L. Taylor. The Taylor family commenced construction in 1923 and completed Dilkusha in 1924. Following a devastating fire in 1926, the structure was rebuilt in 1930. After the Japanese colonial authorities deported the Taylor couple in 1942, the property was briefly managed by Albert's younger brother, William W. Taylor. In 1959, the house was purchased by lawmaker Cho Kyeong-kyu of the Liberal Party. However, following the forfeiture of his assets to the state in 1963, ownership of Dilkusha transferred to the government. Left neglected for decades, the property severely deteriorated and lost its original form. In 2005, Professor Kim Ik-sang of Seoile University located the estate at the request of Albert’s son, Bruce T. Taylor. In 2006, Bruce finally returned to his childhood home after 66 years, bringing Dilkusha back to public prominence.

name: Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall
summary: A space honoring the independence activist Woodang Lee Hoe-young, his five brothers, and their comrades.
description_html: Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall is a space honoring the independence activist Woodang Lee Hoe-young, his five brothers, and their comrades. This house is one of the early 20th-century Western-style buildings constructed by Westerners who entered Seoul, along the hills of Hongpa-dong, Sajik-dong, and Haengchon-dong in the Seodaemun area. Reborn as the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, this house possesses rich historical backgrounds and values even from an architectural history perspective. To remember its significance together, the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall gave this old Western-style building the nickname 'The Old House on Sajik-dong Hill' while reshaping the site. Mr. Lee Hoe-young devoted himself to the anti-Japanese independence movement, contributing his entire family wealth to establish the Shinheung Military Academy. At the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, encounter the history of the independence movement expressed with modern aesthetics, alongside the stories of the finest family of the Joseon Dynasty, the greatest revolutionaries of Joseon, the people who turned darkness into light, and the people who turned orchid leaves into blades.

name: Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall
summary: Exhibiting Gungisi relics and excavated artifacts from the Joseon Dynasty discovered during the construction process of the new Seoul City Hall.
description_html: During the site preparation construction process for the new Seoul City Hall in 2008, a large number of structural remains and artifacts presumed to be from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, leading to an excavation investigation. Here, various artifacts such as ceramics, coins, and roof tiles were excavated alongside structural remains like building sites and stone revetments constructed during the modern era and the Joseon Dynasty. In particular, many weapons from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, including Chongtong (gun barrels), Cheolhwan (iron cannonballs), and the Bullanggi Japo (breech-loading swivel gun) designated as a Treasure. As a result of investigating old maps and related materials, it was determined that Gungisi, a government office in charge of manufacturing weapons during the Joseon Dynasty, was located near Seoul City Hall. The Seoul City Hall site is presumed to have been part of the past Gungisi, and the Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall was created to preserve related structural remains and exhibit excavated artifacts.

The Reconstructed Former Mayor’s Office captures Seoul's history and records, replicating the Mayor’s Office, Reception Room, and Planning Situation Room of the former Seoul City Hall. This office space was used by successive mayors of Seoul for over 60 years, from the post-liberation period until May 2008.

Former mayors handled critical city affairs in the office, and the reception room welcomed important visitors to Seoul. The Planning Situation Room served as the heart of city administration, where the mayor, city officials, experts, and citizens received reports, deliberated, and made decisions on various agendas.

Originally located at the eastern end of the 3rd floor of the old city hall, it has now been reconstructed in the Secretary’s Office. Visitors can experience an immersive exhibition featuring administrative artifacts, including the original desk and chair used by the mayors and various gifts received from notable guests.

name: Mugyewon
summary: Located in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu, Mugyewon is a cultural space where visitors can go to enjoy the traditional and cultural beauty of Korea in a hanok experience.
description_html:
Mugyewon is a traditional cultural space located in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu. It is a restored hanok, reconstructed using materials from Ojinam, the first registered restaurant in Seoul. Nestled at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain, visitors can experience the serene beauty of Korean architecture and appreciate the tranquil scenery. 

The site of Mugyewon, known as Mugaejeongsa, was the villa of Grand Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong. Inspired by its resemblance to the utopian paradise he saw in a dream, Grand Prince Anpyeong built a pavilion where he composed poetry and practiced archery. This historically significant location is also where An Gyeon, the foremost painter of the time, created the famous "Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land" in just three days. 

Since its opening in 2014, Mugyewon has offered a variety of cultural programs, including performances, exhibitions, lectures, education, and hands-on experiences. If you wish to experience Korean tradition and culture amidst scenery as beautiful as the mythical Peach Blossom Land, we recommend visiting this place.

name: Seoul City Wall Museum
summary: A museum that introduces the history and value of the Seoul City Wall, which was constructed to display the authority of Hanyang, the capital during the Joseon Dynasty, and to defend against external
description_html:
The Seoul City Wall is a city-scale fortress heritage constructed to mark the boundaries of Hanseongbu, the capital of the Joseon Dynasty, to display the capital's authority, and to defend against external invasions. With an average height of about 5 to 8 meters and a total length of approximately 18.6 kilometers, the Seoul City Wall is a landmark of the historical and cultural city of Seoul, built upon Korea's unique fortification techniques and collective craftsmanship.

Located in Heunginjimun Park in Jongno-gu, Seoul, the Seoul City Wall Museum is a cultural space equipped with permanent exhibition halls, special exhibition halls, a Seoul City Wall resource room, and a learning room, encompassing the history and culture of the Seoul City Wall from the Joseon Dynasty to the present.

Please discover the history and value of the Seoul City Wall, spanning over 600 years, at the Seoul City Wall Museum.

name: Dongdaemun History Museum
summary: A museum that retraces the history of the former Dongdaemun Stadium site.
description_html: The Dongdaemun History Museum was established as a space to retrace the history of the former Dongdaemun Stadium site by preserving and exhibiting buried artifacts excavated during the construction of the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) and Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. In the past, this area was the eastern region of the Seoul City Wall, where fortress defense facilities and various military installations were deployed to overcome the geographical disadvantages vulnerable to defense. As a result of excavation investigations conducted in 2008-2009, the walls and bastions (Chiseong) of the Seoul City Wall, the Igansumun watergate, and building sites from the Joseon Dynasty ,which were presumed to have been destroyed during the park creation and stadium construction during the Japanese colonial period, were confirmed, and related artifacts were excavated in large quantities. Please confirm the history layered upon the former Dongdaemun Stadium site at the Dongdaemun History Museum.

summary: A museum where you can reminisce about the history of Dongdaemun Stadium, which opened as Gyeongseong Stadium during the Japanese colonial period and was demolished in 2007.
description_html: In October 1925, Gyeongseong Stadium first opened to the east of the Seoul City Wall. Over the course of 82 years, during which its name changed to Seoul Stadium and Dongdaemun Stadium, this modern stadium remained in the same location, going beyond its original role as a stadium and sharing history with the rapidly changing Republic of Korea. The Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial covers the history of the stadium from Gyeongseong Stadium, to Seoul Stadium which became a space for post-liberation sporting matches and various events, and until its demolition in 2007 after being renamed Dongdaemun Stadium. Please reminisce about the history of Dongdaemun Stadium within the flow of modern and contemporary Korean history at the Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial, where you can vividly feel the historical significance and the sense of place of Dongdaemun Stadium and its surrounding areas.

name: National Aviation Museum of Korea

description_html: The National Aviation Museum of Korea, located at Gimpo Airport, is the first national museum in the aviation field established by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to organize Korea's aviation history and promote collective understanding of the aviation industry. The National Aviation Museum of Korea consists of the Aviation History Hall, where visitors can learn about the history of Korean aviation, the Aviation Industry Hall, where visitors can get a glimpse of the current state of the aviation industry, and the Aviation Future Hall, where visitors can see various aviation technologies, airplanes and models for the future. Additionally, there is a unique experience space for those who have always dreamed of flying. Here, visitors can experience aviation through five different spaces including the Black Eagle boarding experience, an in-flight training experience, a pilot control experience, the air sports experience, and the children's airport experience.

name: Sungshin Women's University Costume Museum and Natural History Museum
summary: Located in the Woonjung Green Campus, the second campus of the Sungshin Women's University, invites visitors to learn about traditional Korean attires, as well as the history of nature.
description_html:
Opened on November 23, 2011, the Park Kwang Hoon Costume Museum is a special museum, displaying over 600 garments, which are currently designated as Seoul's Intangible Cultural Property No. 11, donated by the Master Artisan of Needlework, Park Kwang Hoon, as well as more than 2,000 pieces of fabrics and accessories. A variety of Korean attires and accessories are on display, from swaddling clothes and ordinary clothes as well as wedding clothes and royal ritual clothes to shrouds for the deceased.


Located in the basement (B1) of the same building, the Natural History Museum exhibits as many as 135,000 samples collected for over 40 years since the 1970s under four themes of rocks, embryogenesis, plants and insects to help visitors learn and feel the nature around them.


ㆍ Park Kwang Hoon Costume Museum offers various arts and culture programs, including the traditional pattern gilt stamping class, traditional pattern drawing class, and jokduri making class, in addition to its main exhibitions.
※ Extra charges apply for experience programs.

name: Donuimun Museum
summary: A new cultural space constructed from old buildings, located in Saemunan.
description_html:
Donuimun Museum is a new cultural space constructed from old restaurant buildings located in the old neighborhood of Saemunan. Originally built as residential homes back in 1960, these buildings were used as restaurants from 1990 to 2000, some of which included Italian restaurant AGIO and Korean restaurant Hanjeong. While preserving the architecture of the old structure, the buildings were reinforced for safety during their renovation into exhibition spaces.

  Located in a central location within Saemunan surrounded by Seoul City Wall and the walls of Gyeonghuigung Palace, the spaces inhabited by AGIO and Hanjeong hold great historical and cultural value. When portions of Gyeonghuigung Palace Wall were discovered underground, the site has been transformed to preserve and display the remains. At Donuimun Museum, visitors can learn about the culture and history surrounding the area around it.

name: A Look at Yonsei University's 3 Historic Halls

Underwood and the Underwood family. Appenzeller Hall was built in 1924 and holds the designation of Historic Site No. 277. The hall was built to commemorate Henry Appenzeller who established the famed Korean boys' school, Paichai Hakdang.

The National Palace Museum of Korea showcases 500 years of history with roughly 45,000 artifacts from the Joseon Dynasty. Artifacts on display include texts and poems that were handwritten by kings of the past, robes worn by royalty, jewelry, and other items from the royal courts of Korea. Highlights from the museum collection are many, one highlight is the royal vehicle of Emperor Sunjong, the last king of the Joseon Dynasty. Another highlight of the colelction is the rain gauge pedestal. The rain gauge pedestal was an invention that dated back to the Joseon era.


The museum also offers a learning program called "Experiencing Royal Culture;" the program is suitable for people of all ages. Spend time at the National Palace Museum of Korea to experience and learn about the grandeur and history of Korea's royalty.


※ Joseon Dynasty: The royal dynasty lasted from 1392 until 1910. The 518-year reign of the royal Lee family spanned 27 generations.
※ Rain Gauge Pedestal: The device was used to measure rainfall.
※ Royal Vehicle of Emperor Sunjong: The vehicle is a 1918 model of the General Motors Cadillac Limo usine.

name: Kyung Hee University Natural History Museum
summary: Founded in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum is run by the university.
description_html:
Upon opening its doors in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum served as a little respite of nature in the city that boasted of a collection of nearly 90,000 specimen on display. The museum was initially founded upon the purpose of realizing the Kyungee University founding ideology of "Creating a world of culture" grounded in the results that had been obtained through several years of studying nature. The effort continues to approach the distancing relationship between nature and humankind amid rapid societal changes and urbanization with a "respite of nature in the city" that provides a sense of living in harmony with nature. 


All six floors of the museum display easy-to-understand exhibits capturing a comparison between the current state of evolution and the process of transformation up to the present-day with specimen of different plants and animals, as well as various rocks from sedimentary to igneous and metamorphic rocks that were used for research purposes by specialized teams of professors in various fields. There are courses and tour programs offered to help understand and practice nature preservation and the importance of life within the framework of these exhibited specimen. 


The Kyunghee University Natural History Museum has collected numerous specimen since the 1940s, while possessing a collection of more recent domestic specimen that have already become extinct or show signs of endangerment. The museum offers the opportunity for children and adults alike to more systematically learn about the classification and ecosystems of animals and plants and prioritizes itself with the fervor of exploring nature, as well as the awareness of nature protection.
description_text: Upon opening its doors in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum served as a little respite of nature in the city that boasted of a collection of nearly 90,000 specimen on display. The effort continues to approach the distancing relationship between nature and humankind amid rapid societal changes and urbanization with a "respite of nature in the city" that provides a sense of living in harmony with nature. All six floors of the museum display easy-to-understand exhibits capturing a comparison between the current state of evolution and the process of transformation up to the present-day with specimen of different plants and animals, as well as various rocks from sedimentary to igneous and metamorphic rocks that were used for research purposes by specialized teams of professors in various fields. name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
summary: The National Museum of Korean Contemporary History houses exhibitions that spans modern Korean history, from the 19th century to today.
description_html: The National Museum of Korean Contemporary History houses exhibitions that span modern Korean history, from the first opening of Korea to outsiders in the late 19th century to today. The museum is the country's first national museum of contemporary history. The eight-story museum has many facilities: there are four permanent exhibition halls and two special exhibition halls, seminar rooms, lecture halls, a rooftop garden, a museum shop (that sells souvenirs), a cafe, and storage lockers. The four permanent exhibitions cover different periods of Korean history and there are over 1,500 artifacts and items here. Some of the displays are patriot Ahn Jung-Geun's last writings, the March 1st Declaration of Independence, belongings of fallen soldiers from the Korean War, and materials relating to democratic activism. The museum's first floor contains two special exhibition halls. Here, you will find a variety of limited-time exhibitions relating to Korean history, politics, society, and culture. Additionally, visitors can listen to, watch, and experience the modernization of Korea through state-of-the-art technology. There is also the Children's Museum, where children can learn and experience history for themselves with the museum’s “Our History’s Treasure Chest” area.

name: The Hangsangsoo Embroidery
summary: A Korean traditional embroidery museum where visitors can discover works of intangible cultural hertiage
description_html: This unique space preserves all the traces of traditional Korean embroidery techniques that have been restored by collecting and analyzing artifacts from the 1960s to revive Korean embroidery, which was lost through the Korean Empire and Japanese occupation. The Korean Handicraft Institute, which opened in 1963, is the origin of the Hansangsu Embroidery Museum. It has been established as a complex cultural space to preserve and present Korean embroidery to the public. The eldest daughter of Han Sang-soo, a National Intangible Cultural Property embroiderer, has been running the museum as the second director and is preparing for the third succession.

name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
summary: The Seoul Anglican Cathedral was built during the Japanese colonial era and it is located beside Deoksugung Palace.
description_html: The Seoul Anglican Cathedral was built during the Japanese colonial era and it is located beside Deoksugung Palace. The cathedral was constructed under the direction of the Rt. Reverend Mark Trollope, the third bishop of the Anglican Church of Korea and British architect Arthur Dixon. Although construction was completed in 1926, the Anglican Church of Korea considers 1890 as the date of the cathedral's foundation, since this was the year when the first service of Holy Communion was held. The cathedral is the seat of the Seoul Anglican Diocese and Tangible Cultural Property of Seoul No. 35.

name: Gyeongdong Market
summary: A representative market of Seoul in Cheongnyangni where tradition and modernity harmonize
description_html:
Gyeongdong Market is one of Seoul’s iconic traditional markets, located in Cheongnyangni, where tradition and modernity coexist. It is a vibrant cultural hub offering a wide range of goods including agricultural products, medicinal herbs, and seafood, and is a favorite destination among foreign tourists.

Established in June 1960 as a market specializing in agricultural goods, it has grown into a central traditional market in Seoul, offering a variety of mountain-harvested specialties and produce at reasonable prices. In 1985, with the completion of the Gyeongdong Building, the market expanded to become home to Korea’s largest ginseng and herbal medicine specialty zone, surpassing even Daegu Yakryeongsi in expertise and scale.
description_text: Gyeongdong Market is one of Seoul’s iconic traditional markets, located in Cheongnyangni, where tradition and modernity coexist. It is a vibrant cultural hub offering a wide range of goods including agricultural products, medicinal herbs, and seafood, and is a favorite destination among foreign tourists. Established in June 1960 as a market specializing in agricultural goods, it has grown into a central traditional market in Seoul, offering a variety of mountain-harvested specialties and produce at reasonable prices. In 1985, with the completion of the Gyeongdong Building, the market expanded to become home to Korea’s largest ginseng and herbal medicine specialty zone, surpassing even Daegu Yakryeongsi in expertise and scale.

name: buruttrak
summary: A record shop opened in Myeong-dong in 1979.
description_html: Buruttrak, established in 1978, is a long-standing record shop still in operation today. Known as a landmark in Myeong-dong, it has appeared in films and dramas several times. The first floor features K-pop albums and merchandise, the second floor sells jazz and pop CDs, and the third and fourth floors are dedicated to classical vinyl records. Within the vast collection of over 100,000 records, there is a particularly large selection of classical LPs. With some luck, you might also find rare albums by American Black musicians from the 1980s and 1990s. In the 1990s, as the hobbies of the Korean public shifted, record purchases began to decline. However, Japanese LP enthusiasts started buying records at high prices. During this period, the main customer base gradually shifted to foreigners. By the late 1990s, Korean record shops became essential tourist spots for Japanese visitors who could buy K-albums cheaper than in their country. Back then, the area around Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center and Myeong-dong had 11 record shops, with 'Buruttrak' being a well-established figure. Nowadays, with K-pop's global popularity, the shop attracts customers from Southeast Asia and Europe, and it stocks a wide variety of records to meet diverse tastes.

name: Park Seon-yeong Traditional Hanbok Research
summary: Traditional Hanbok made with the needlework of a Chimseonjang, a master artisan recognized as an intangible cultural heritage
description_html: Park Seon-yeong Traditional Hanbok Research is dedicated to preserving the essence of traditional hanbok. It was founded by Master Artisan Park Sun-young (Seoul's Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 11: Chimseonjang) who aimed to uphold the beauty of hanbok and the spirit of ancestors embedded within it. Currently, the studio is operated by her son, Kim Ki-sang, who has inherited her skills. Customers can choose from a variety of luxurious fabrics in different colors and decide on measurements and designs to create a custom-made hanbok. The production period is approximately 7-10 days, and international shipping is not available. The studio also offers educational programs on traditional hanbok.

summary: NR CERAMICS, a lifestyle brand that naturally blends in
description_html: NR CERAMICS is a lifestyle brand launched in 2018, offering a wide range of home goods and craft products, including vases, dishes, cutlery, and interior accessories. The brand is well-regarded for its simple designs that effortlessly blend into any setting and for its reasonable pricing, which has garnered a loyal following over time.

name: Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market
summary: Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors gathered near Hwarangdae
description_html: The Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors who gathered near Hwarangdae Station when the Gyeongchun Railway opened on July 25, 1939. Named for its fleeting nature, like a goblin's visit, the vendors would quickly disappear at the sign of a crackdown and reassemble snugly along the tracks to rebuild the market once things were clear. This traditional goblin market is the precursor to today's Gongneung-dong Goblin Market. Since then, the market has operated as a quintessential neighborhood market in Nowon-gu, as if a goblin's magic wand has made every possible item available. It offers a variety of products including livestock, groceries, restaurants, miscellaneous goods, and agricultural products. The market draws a steady stream of visitors due to its high-quality goods sold at affordable prices. Since 2019, it has been growing into an eastern landmark cultural tourism market, concurrent with the development of the Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest.

name: Times Square

name: COEX Mall
summary: COEX Mall is the largest underground shopping mall in Asia and is connected to several exhibition halls, a convention center, a hotel, a department store, and an office building.
description_html:
As the largest underground shopping mall in Asia, COEX Mall has got everything you need, all in one place. Shopaholics and fashionistas will appreciate the hundreds of clothing and accessories stores carrying both domestic brands and international brands, as well as designer and luxury brands. The dining options are endless with the many restaurants and cafes that are available here. The Megabox Cineplex, one of Korea's largest movie theater chains, is also located here, with a total of 17 screens. Other popular attractions at the mall include the Kimchi Museum, the COEX Aquarium, the ASEM Plaza and the Event Court, where various performances and exciting events, such as classical concerts, mini concerts, and magic shows are offered every week.


COEX Mall is generally considered to be one of the best places to go for shopping. The stores in the multi-fashion square feature trendy fashions targeted at younger customers, but there are plenty of shops geared towards people of all ages. The square is also connected to Hyundai Department Store, offering even more items to choose from. There are various ways to enjoy COEX Mall. You can enjoy shopping at COEX whether you've got money to blow or are just passing by for some window-shopping. If you are out with children, a great place to go would be the Aquarium, which also features a play area and Kids Aquarium in addition to the main aquarium. The Kimchi Museum is great for an educational experience and tourists who want to learn more about the history of Korea's most famous dish. Have fun for free at one of the many free exhibitions held throughout the year, or get rid of your change at the video arcade.


Frequently Asked Questions about Starfield COEX Mall

Which subway exit is connected to the Starfield COEX Mall?

The subway stations directly connected to Starfield COEX Mall are as follows.

  • • Samseong Station Exit 5 or 6 (Subway Line 2)

  • • Bongeunsa Station Exit 7 (Subway Line 9)

Are pets allowed in COEX Mall?

Starfield COEX Mall allows pets to enter when using a dedicated carrier.

Where are the lockers located at Starfield COEX Mall?

There are three lockers in the Starfield COEX Mall in the following locations. (As of 2025)

  • • Opposite Zara (F109)

  • • Next to Top Ten (F115)

  • • Next to Gowa Flower (N101)

name: I Park Mall
summary: A mega shopping and entertainment complex located in downtown Seoul. It is divided into three major areas: the I Park Department Store, the Digital Shopping Center, and the Event Park.
description_html:
I Park Mall is a mega shopping and entertainment complex located in downtown Seoul. It is divided into three major areas: the I Park Department Store (which is further divided into the Living Hall, the Culture Hall and the Fashion Hall), the Digital Shopping Center, and the Event Park. Other major highlights include the Culture Center, CGV (a major cinema chain), the e-Sports Stadium, putt-putt miniature golf, and E-mart. Due to the variety that this spacious shopping center offers, a large number of people come throughout the year. In addition to shopping, visitors can enjoy various events such as fashion shows and festivals at the Event Park, a central feature of I Park Mall. I Park Mall also features a wide range of dining options that will satisfy anyone's taste buds with over 100 restaurants, a diverse food court, and a number of cafés and bars. Other highlights include a large bookstore, a video-game arcade, and an outdoor garden.

name: Central City
summary: Central City is a multi-purpose complex, which is very accessible as three different subway lines pass through it. Central City is often referred to as Express Bus Terminal, because of its bus terminal that connects with 70 local cities.
description_html: Central City is a multi-purpose complex, which is very accessible as three different subway lines pass through it, namely Line 3 and 7 as well as Line 9, which connects to Incheon International Airport and Gimpo International Airport. Central City is often referred to as Express Bus Terminal, because of its bus terminal that connects with 70 local cities. With a daily floating population of over half a million, Central City features a wide variety of facilities including shopping, leisure, cultural, accommodation and public facilities. Central City features various cultural venues as well as a shopping mall. summary: A temple located on the eastern foothills of Samgaksan (Bukhansan) in Jeongneung-dong, Seongbuk-gu
description_html: Gyeongguksa Temple, nestled on the eastern slopes of Samgaksan (now known as Bukhansan), is a historic temple founded in the late Goryeo period. Renowned for its scenic mountain surroundings and fresh spring water, it attracts many visitors. The temple complex has 17 buildings, including Geungnakbojeon (Hall of Supreme Bliss), Yeongsanjeon, Myeongbujeon, Gwaneumjeon, and Sibangseonwon. Geungnakbojeon houses the Amitabha Buddha triad, along with wooden Buddhist paintings (designated as Treasure No. 748), Shinjungtaenghwa, and Palsangtaenghwa. Sibangseonwon offers a weekly Sunday meditation session, and the temple also hosts temple stay programs at Hwanheodang and Manwoldang. As one of Seoul's significant temples, Gyeongguksa was frequently visited by former President Syngman Rhee. During his tenure as Vice President, Richard Nixon of the United States visited the temple and later described it as one of his most memorable experiences in his memoirs, even including a photograph of his visit.

name: Seokguram
summary: Seokguram Grotto is nestled halfway up Inwangsan Mountain, just below Chimabawi Rock, and can be reached via the Inwangsan Mountain Trail.
description_html: Seokguram Grotto is nestled halfway up Inwangsan Mountain, just below Chimabawi Rock, and can be reached via the Inwangsan Mountain Trail. Inside, you'll find the Three Buddha Statues, while the surrounding forest path features a Buddha statue and a Maitreya Buddha carved into the rocks. Above the main hall at Sanshingak Shrine, a large rock bears a painting of the Mountain Spirit and a tiger that guards Inwangsan. About 30 meters to the right of Seokguram, you can also visit the Cheonhyangam Hermitage. From Seokguram, you'll enjoy stunning panoramic views of Seoul, with Namsan Tower visible on the opposite mountain and, on clear days, even Lotte Tower. Below, Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Blue House come into view.
