name: Hwagyesa Temple
summary: Hwagyesa Temple was founded by Seonsa (Seon master) Sinwol in 1522 (17th year of King Jungjong's reign).
description_html:
Hwagyesa Temple was founded by Seonsa (Seon master) Sinwol in 1522 (17th year of King Jungjong's reign). Originally, Daesa (a high Buddhist priest) Beopin, or Tanmun, built a hermitage called Bodeokam near the site of Hwagyesa Temple, preserving long-standingBuddhist tradition. Later on, Seonsa Sinwol would move the hermitage to the current location and rename it Hwagyesa. During the Joseon Period, the royal family frequented the temple and Regent Heungseon Daewongun supported the temple during the latteryears of Joseon.

A cradle of the enlightenment movement, Hwagyesa Temple produced a number of figures who embroiders the modern history of Korea, including Mubul and Cha Hong-sik, and is also known to have served as a place for monks who participated in the Gapsin Revolutionto prepare for the enlightenment movement.

Hwagyesa Temple is a historic venue where the Korean Language Society organized a stay of nine Korean language scholars, including Lee Hui-seung and Choe Hyeon-bae, wherein they completed the Unified Korean Orthography in 1933. Recently, the temple becameinternationally known as being a center for worldwide propagation. In 1991, the Daejeokgwangjeon Hall was established and an international seonwoen (Seon monastery) was opened on the 4th floor to accommodate buddhists from other countries.

name: Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery
summary: Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery is the final resting place for Korea's western residents, including Dr. Horace Allen, the first director of Gwanghyewon, which was the first western-style hospital in Korea, founded in 1885.
description_html:
Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery is the final resting place for Korea's western residents, including Dr. Horace Allen, the first director of Gwanghyewon, the first western-style hospital in Korea, founded in 1885. The cemetery is known as Foreign Missionary Cemetery because of the number of foreign missionaries buried here. Tombs and headstones were built in a western style creating an exotic atmosphere. The cemetery is located near the Hangang (River), an ideal spot for taking a pleasant stroll.


Yanghwajin Foreigners' Cemetery is situated on the other side of Yanghwajin, opposite the martyrs’ shrine. It is regarded as a Protestant shrine because many Protestant missionaries are buried there.  The “100th Anniversary Memorial Church” was established in Yanhwajin by the “Council for the 100th Anniversary of the Korean Church” to commemorate a century of missionary work in Korea. 


Many of the foreigners who have contributed to the story of modern Korean history are buried in the Yanghwajin cemetery, such as Thomas Bethell, the founder of Daehan Maeil Sinbo (Newspaper); Mary Scranton, the founder of Ewha Hakdang (a mission school for girls, now Ewha Womans University); and Henry Appenzeller, the founder of Chungdong First Methodist Church.


A guided tour in English or Japanese is available in Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery when booked in advance. These are conducted four times a day (10:00, 11:30, 14:00, 15:30) except during the New Year's holiday, Chuseok holiday and on Christmas day. 


Yanghwajin Foreign Missionary Cemetery is located in Hapjeong-dong, Mapo-gu. It is a haven for foreign missionaries and their families who loved, and wished to lie in, Korea. The cemetery is managed by 100th Anniversary Memorial Church and contains Mission Memorial Hall.

name: Bongeunsa Temple
summary: Bongeunsa is a Buddhist temple founded in 794 during the Silla (one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea) period.
description_html:
Bongeunsa is a Buddhist temple founded in 794 during the Silla (one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea) period. The temple has more than 1,000 years of history and has many interesting historic and cultural features, including woodblock carvings of the Avatamsaka Sutra (Flower Garland Sutra). The temple is also a very popular tourist destination, offering various programs relating to traditional Korean Buddhist culture, in a variety of languages.


Bongeunsa is more than a just temple. It provides a place to relax for busy city people and also gives people a chance to reflect upon themselves. The templestay program gives an opportunity to experience everyday life in the temple, which includes traditional Korean Buddhist culture and practices. Visitors can experience some simple Buddhist practices such as the daily dawn service, Korean Zen meditation, Dado (a tea drinking ceremony), and Balwoogongyang (a Buddhist meal with traditional bowls).  Every May on Buddha's birthday, Bongeunsa holds the Lotus Lantern Festival on nearby Samseong-don g.

name: Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum
summary: Learn about the history of education in Korea at the Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum.
description_html: Learn about the history of education in Korea at the Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum. The museum is housed in what was once the Pai Chai Hakdang, which was Korea's first Western-style school. Currently, the school's classrooms have been repurposed and are used as a permanent exhibition hall, a special exhibition hall, an experience zone, and a seminar room. In the permanent exhibition hall, visitors can see what the Pai Chai Hakdang looked like in the 1930s at the hall's recreated historical classroom. Admission to the museum is free.

name: Korea Central Mosque
summary: The Seoul Central Mosque was established to be a place to worship for Muslims in Korea as well as to educate the larger public about Islam and Islamic cultures.
description_html:
Located in Hannam-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, the Seoul Central Mosque is the first Islamic Mosque in Korea. It was established on May 21, 1976, after construction began in October 1974. The Korean government provided the site in May 1969 with approximately 4,958 square meters of land, and the construction costs were supported by Islamic countries worldwide, including Saudi Arabia. Situated between the Hangang River and Namsan Mountain, the mosque features prayer halls on the first and second floors, with ablution rooms for men and women in the basement of the annex building. The first floor of the annex houses classrooms, while the second floor has office spaces. The adjacent Islamic Center includes facilities such as an Islamic mission center for children, a Muslim congregation, a women's association, and a library. The exterior of the Seoul Central Mosque features a variety of amenities, including halal restaurants, a halal butcher shop, an Islamic bookstore, a halal supermarket, and a travel agency, making it convenient for Muslims and non-Muslims to visit.

name: Jogyesa Temple
summary: Jogyesa Temple is one of Korea's major Buddhist temples in central Seoul.
description_html: Jogyesa Temple was established in 1910 under the name Gakhwangsa by monks who aspired for the independence of Korean Buddhism and the restoration of the national capital. At the time, Gakhwangsa was the first temple to be situated within the four main gates of Seoul. In 1937, efforts began to relocate Gakhwangsa to its present site, now known as Jogyesa. Positioned in the heart of Jongno, Seoul, it is the only traditional temple in the city center, offering a place for visitors to rest. The temple grounds are open 24/7, welcoming locals and foreigners anytime. The temple hosts a temple stay program and the annual Lotus Lantern Festival.

name: Gilsangsa Temple
summary: Gilsangsa Temple was once one of the most famous restaurants in Korea called "Daewongak."
description_html: Gilsangsa Temple was once one of the foremost yojeong, a place where powerful men used to convene behind the scenes.The temple is named after the woman who donated the buildings, a gisaeng (a female entertainer and/or courtesan) named Kim Yeong-han who had a change of heart after reading "Non-Possession" by Venerable Beopjeong Sunim. The monk initially denied her request, but in 1995 decided to turn the buildings into a temple.  As a result, the temple has a very unusual atmosphere because it kept many of its original features. The temple is highly regarded for its involvement in cultural exchanges with other religions, and its programs to help visitors experience Buddhism.

Gangneung is the royal tomb of the Queen Munjeong's son and the 13th Joseon king, Myeongjong and his wife, Queen Insun. In June 2009, all 40 of the royal tombs of the Joseon Dynasty were designated UNESCO World Heritage sites.

name: Heonilleung
summary: Heonilleung is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the final resting place of two pairs of the Joseon Dynasty's kings and queens.
description_html: Heonilleung is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the final resting place of two pairs of the Joseon Dynasty's kings and queens. The name of the site is a combination of the names of the two separate tombs, Heonleung and Inleung. The tombs of Joseon's third king, Taejong (1367-1422), and his wife, Queen Wongyeong (1365-1420) are at Heonleung. Inleung is the resting place of Joseon's 23rd king, Sunjo (1790-1834), and his wife Queen Sunwon (1789-1857). Heonilleung is unique in that it houses two kings born 400 years apart. Visitors to the royal tombs can see examples of early and late Joseon Dynasty royal tombs and there is a weekly talk about the tombs every Saturday. On Lunar New Year's Day, traditional performances are held at Heonilleung for the public to enjoy.

name: Seonjeongneung (Tomb)
summary: Seonjeongneung is home to the royal tombs of King Seongjong (the 9th king of the Joseon Dynasty) and his family, including his second wife, Queen Consort Jeonghyeon, and his son, later to be king, King Jungjong.
description_html:
Seonjeongneung is the name of Seolleung and Jeongneung combined, and it refers to the royal tombs of King Seongjong (the 9th king of the Joseon Dynasty), Queen Jeonghyeon (the second wife of King Seongjong) and King Jungjong (a son of the two). Seonjeongneung was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2009, enhancing its status as historic remains. It is easily accessible as it is situated close to Seolleung Station, Subway Line 2. It makes an ideal place for the public to enjoy a stroll.

Seolleung, the tomb of King Seongjong (reigned 1469-1494) was built in 1495; subsequently, the tomb of Queen Jeonghyeon (1462-1530) was built on the east side of Seolleung in 1530. Jeongneung, which is the tomb of King Jungjong (the 11th king of the Joseon Dynasty, reigned 1506-1544), was built in 1544, and was moved from its original site in Wondang, Goyang-gun, Gyeonggi-do, to this current location in 1562 by Queen Munjeong (the second wife of King Jungjong, 1501-1565). Seonjeongneung is designated as Historic Site No. 199 as well as being a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon Royal Tombs
summary: Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon are the burial site of members of the Korean royal family and the site was designated Historic Site No. 361 in 1991.
description_html:
Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon are the burial site of members of the Korean royal family and the site was designated Historic Site No. 361 in 1991. Yeonghwiwon is the royal tomb of Princess Consort Sunheon, wife of the 26th king of the Joseon Dynasty, Gojong. Sunginwon is the burial place of Crown Prince Yi Jin, grandson of King Gojong and Princess Consort Sunheon. 

In Korea, tombs for kings and queens are traditionally called “neung” and tombs of princes and royal consorts are called “won”. Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon were once known as Hongneung as Queen Myeongseong, the first wife of King Gojong was entombed here. The grave was moved to Geumgok-dong in the city of Namyangju in 1919 following the death of King Gojong. Since then, the site has been known as Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon. Apart from its historic significance, the greenery and beautiful surroundings here have always attracted sightseers.

name: Jeongneung (A Royal Tomb)
summary: Jeongneung is the royal tomb of Queen Sindeok. She was the second wife of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html: Jeongneung is the royal tomb of Queen Sindeok. She was the second wife of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty. It is said that the tomb was originally located behind Deoksugong (Palace) but moved to the current location when a son of King Taejo's first wife, King Taejong ( the third king of the Joseon Dynasty) ascended the throne. The original scale of the tomb was reduced as well. Although it is a simple tomb without many of the stone figures traditionally placed before a royal tomb, it has historical interest as it has faithfully kept the style of an early Joseon period tomb. The tomb is in picturesque surrounds with Bukhansan National Park located nearby.

name: Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs
summary: The Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs are ancient tombs in located the Bangi-dong area that date back to the Hanseong Baekje era.
description_html: The Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs are ancient tombs in located the Bangi-dong area that date back to the Hanseong Baekje era. The ancient Hanseong Baekje Kingdom was founded along the Hangang River in 18 BCE and lasted for nearly 5 centuries. The tombs were discovered in the 1970s during the Jamsil District Zoning Project and there are 8 tombs altogether. Unfortunately, most of the artifacts were stolen at some point in time, but the tombs themselves were preserved well. Visitors can observe the original structures of the tombs and learn more about Hanseong Baekje. These ancient tombs are an important historical site and the area around the tombs was made into a park. There are paths between the tombs and visitors can take a quiet walk around the park and observe the tombs while enjoying the park's fresh air and grass. The site holds the designation of Historic Site No. 270.

name: Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway
summary: The stonewall path surrounding Gyeongbokgung Palace
description_html: The Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway is a walkway that surrounds Gyeongbokgung Palace. Centered around Gwanghwamun, to the left is the west gate of Gyeongbokgung, Yeongchumun; to the north is the north gate, Sinmumun; and to the right is the east gate, Geonchunmun. The left side of the Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway connects to Seochon, while the north connects to the Blue House. The right side leads to Bukchon and Samcheong-dong, where visitors can also explore the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art and the National Folk Museum of Korea. The path is well-maintained, perfect for a stroll while experiencing the changing seasons. Walking along the Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway offers a unique view that changes with the weather, whether it's raining or snowing.

Cheong Wa Dae, the official residence of the South Korean president is located not far from the gate and city wall. name: Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun)
summary: Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun) is one of Seoul's historic Four Great Gates and it was designated National Treasure no. 1 by the Korean government in 1962.
description_html:
Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun) is one of Seoul's historic Four Great Gates and it was designated National Treasure no. 1 by the Korean government in 1962. Though its official name is Sungnyemun, it is also popularly known as Namdaemun Gate due to its location at what was once the southern end of Seoul. As the centuries passed, Seoul grew in size but Sungnyemun Gate has endured through the ages.  


Construction on the gate was started in 1395 and completed in 1398. In 1447, Sungnyemun saw reconstruction work carried out. The gate is the largest city gate with an arched entrance in the city, and atop the gate's wooden base stands a 2-story wooden structure. The gate is Seoul's oldest wooden structure but on Feb. 10th, 2008, much of the gate's wooden structure was destroyed by fire. Following several years of restorative work, Sungnyemun Gate can now be enjoyed in all its glory. ​

Admission to Mongchontoseong Fortress is free.

name: Eungbongsan Mountain
summary: A low mountain located in Eungbong-dong, Seongdong-gu
description_html: Eungbong-dong, located in Eungbong-dong, Seongdong-gu, stands at about 95 meters and has long been renowned for its beautiful scenery. During the Joseon Dynasty, kings would release hawks here for hunting, which earned it the nickname Maebongsan Mountain (Hawk Mountain). The area was also home to Dongho Dokseodang, an educational site for scholars and pavilions like Hwanghwajeong and Yuhajeong. To the south of Eungbong was a storage facility for ice called Dongbinggo. Today, Eungbongsan is designated as a neighborhood park, attracting many visitors who enjoy Seoul’s sunsets and night views. The park also offers recreational facilities such as a children's park, rock climbing area, and badminton courts, making it an excellent spot for various activities.

name: Jungnangcheon Stream Embankment
summary: Jungnangcheon Stream, a green shelter in the city where humans and nature coexist
description_html: In spring, the embankment of Jungnangcheon Stream is covered with canola flowers. The 5.15-kilometer section from Jangpyeonggyo Bridge to Wolleunggyo Bridge is a land of bright yellow flowers. In the summer, you can see a colorful tunnel of 40,000 roses, and in autumn, silver grass, reeds, cosmos, and sunflower flower paths create a unique autumn scenery. If Jungnangcheon is famous for its spring, summer, and autumn flowers, winter is definitely the time for migratory birds. The 3.3-kilometer section where Jungnangcheon Stream joins the Hangang River from the confluence of Cheonggyecheon Stream and Jungnangcheon Stream is a protected area for migratory birds and is perfect for sightseeing. More than 4,000 birds of more than 40 species, including herons, herring gulls, and cormorants, fly in, and 21 species of migratory birds, such as mallards and kestrels, visit especially in winter. When migratory birds visit in winter, a birdwatching program and a migratory bird observation class also take place, making the place an ecological learning center for children.

name: Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
summary: A Place Where the Past, Present, and Future of Seoul Coexist, Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
description_html: This park, filled with thedreams and hopes of childhood, is actually a place that holds a painfulhistory. This place was originally where the tomb of Empress Sunmyeong, thewife of Sunjung, the last king of the Joseon Dynasty, was enshrined. However, the tomb was moved to another location during the Japanese occupation, while a golf course was built for the Japanese and remained even after liberation. Kkummaru (Dream Peak) in Children's Grand Park was Korea's first "clubhouse" for tourist visiting Korea. After the opening ofChildren’s Grand Park, Kkummaru wasused for different purposes such as an academic hall, exhibition space, andsuperintendent’s office. Later, Kkummaru was able torecover its original structure that was iconic of Korea’s modern andcontemporary architecture through the hands of famous renovation architects,Cho Sung-ryong and Choon Choi. They erased the superimposed layers and filledthe building with programs for a book cafe and picnic area to reintroduce it asa space to help children dream again, hence the kkum (dream) part of the name.

name: Yongsan Park Partially Open Site
summary: The site was a previous residence for US military officers. It was named 'Sobinggo' during the Joseon Dynasty because ice was stored nearby.
description_html: The site was a previous residence for US military officers. It was named Sobinggo during the Joseon Dynasty because ice was stored nearby. It is now called Yongsan Garrison, including the site of the U.S. Army officers' quarters. Still, the American soldiers stationed in Yongsan right after the defeat of Japan did not call it Yongsan Garrison but Camp Sobinggo. From the Liberation to the Korean War, it was called Camp Sobinggo, but after the ceasefire agreement was reached, it was named Yongsan Garrison when the 8th US Army moved in.

name: Ansan Mountain
summary: Ansan Mountain is 295.5 meters high and it is located in the Seodaemun-gu district of Seoul.
description_html: Located in the Seodaemun-gu district of Seoul, Ansan Mountain is 295.5 meters high and is popular for its easy hiking trails and beautiful scenery. While there are multiple paths to choose from, the trail on the eastern side of the mountain is the most well-known as it passes by Independence Park, the location of the historic Seodaemun Prison. Many of the paths up the mountain are made up of a boardwalk, so anyone of any age can make this trek without worrying about slipping or tripping. At the top of Ansan is an observation deck with a jaw-dropping view of Seoul and the surrounding area. Additionally, Bongwonsa Temple, which is the head temple of the Taego Order of Korean Buddhism, is located at the bottom of the southeastern hillside of the mountain.

name: Autumn Trail, Namsan Southern Walking Path
summary: A path spanning 1.3 km that starts from the Namsan National Theater intersection and ends near the Namsan 3-ho Tunnel!
description_html: The lengthy trail taking a wide sweep around Namsan Mountain while being known for its particularly scenic landscape during the autumn season, earned the name, "Autumn Trail" some years ago. There are a total of four distinct courses, including Namsan Southern Walking Path, Namsan Northern Walking Path, Sowol-ro, and Namsan Outdoor Botanical Garden. Also known as "Itaewon-ro," the Namsan Southern Walking Path is filled to the brim with striking Oriental Plane trees makng for an amazing vista of autumn foliage! It spans a total of 1.3 km from Namsan National Theater Intersection to the Namsan 3-ho Tunnel and is at the peak of fall viewing from late October to early November.

name: Banpo Hangang Park
summary: Recently renovated under the city's "Hangang Renaissance Project."
description_html: A piece of land stretching 6.4 km located at the southern banks of Hangang River between Banpodaegyo Bridge and Dongjakdaegyo Bridge, Banpo Hangang Park was recently renovated under the city's "Hangang Renaissance Project". The park is also home to famous attractions like Banpodaegyo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain and Moonlight Square. The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain is recorded as the longest bridge fountain (recognized by Guinness Book of World Records) with dynamic water jets and lights that move in time to the music. Moonlight Square continues to attract many visitors by holding various events and performances throughout the year. Additionally, an inline skating facility and eco-friendly park were built inside the park as well. Between Banpodaegyo Bridge and Dongjakdaegyo Bridge is Seoraeseom Island (Some Sevit), another popular attraction site.

name: Jamwon Hangang Park
summary: Acts as both a popular date spot, as well as home to numerous sports facilities, including 8.2 km inline skating rink.
description_html: A famous relaxing spot for locals and beloved dating spot for couples, Jamwon Hangang Park is well-known for its numerous sports facilities and 8.2 km inline skating rink. Featuring wide grassy fields perfect for picnics, a bike path stretching all the way to Banpo District, and also a tennis court for the disabled, Jamwon Hangang Park continues to attract many visitors. From the Joseon Dynasty to the Japanese Occupation, the area of Jamwon-dong was a large-scale mulberry field. To educate future generations about the history of this area, Seoul Metropolitan Government opened up a "Jamwon Nature Learning Center." The learning center consists of a lobby, silkworm exhibition hall, wildflower garden, and classrooms, offering various experience programs for children.

summary: A valley with cool, clear water, Uidong Valley is located between Dobongsan Mountain and Bukhansan Mountain.
description_html: The Ui-dong Valley, a notable valley in Gangbuk, is situated between Dobongsan and Bukhansan mountains. It features scattered waterfalls and ponds, with a long stream flowing from the entrance to Baegundae, the gentlest course in Bukhansan Mountain. While swimming is prohibited due to its location within Bukhansan National Park, simply sitting on a rock and breathing in the refreshing air is enough to beat the heat. The valley is well-equipped with amenities such as stairs and walking paths, enhancing convenience. Moreover, spending time at the nearby restaurants and cafes is delightful. Its proximity to downtown Seoul and easy access via public transportation make it a favored destination for Seoul residents.

name: Bongsan Mountain
summary: Located between Seoul's Eunpyeong-gu and Gyeonggi-do's Goyang, Bongsan Mountain outlines the edge of Western Seoul.
description_html: Bongsan Mountain, located between Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul and Goyang, Gyeonggi-do, is the mountain that marks the boundary of western of Seoul. Although it is not very tall, at only 209 meters, it is not necessarily an easy hiking course as there are quite a few steep hills. Pavilions that are named Bongsudae and Bongsujeong are located at the top of Bongsan Mountain. From the top of the mountain, visitors can enjoy the beautiful sunset over the Hangang River, which reflects the vibrant colors on the water. The most popular course is the Bongsan Sunrise Trail. Sunrise Park is located at the top of Bongsan Mountain where visitors can enjoy a beautiful view of Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul. Additionally, on the Bongsan Sunrise Trail course, there is Hyguksa Temple, a Korean temple made of pure gold. Even in the daytime, it shines beautifully, but at sunset, the golden sky and the temple come together to create a dazzling landscape.

name: Yangjaecheon Stream & Tancheon Stream
summary: Yangjaecheon Stream and Tancheon Stream are two tributaries of the Hangang River. The streams offer picturesque walking trails for visitors to enjoy.
description_html: Yangjaecheon Stream and Tancheon Stream are two tributaries of the Hangang River. The streams offer picturesque walking trails for visitors to enjoy. Yangjaecheon Stream, sometimes referred to as Hanyeoul Stream, is a tributary of the Hangang River. The stream is 18.5 km long and flows from Gwacheong in Gyeonggi-do Province to the southern part of Seoul. The stream's name is derived from the area in Seoul it flows through, Yangjae-dong. Tancheon Stream is another one of the Hangang's tributaries. The stream is 35.6 km long and starts in the city of Yongin in Gyeonggi-do Province and ends at the Hangang River in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. With its gently sloping walking paths and well-maintained cycling routes stretching along the stream, this urban waterway is a popular spot for walking, running, and riding. It is especially famous as a tourist destination for cherry blossoms in spring and colorful foliage in autumn.

name: Buramsan Mountain
summary: Buramsan Mountain is one of Seoul's many beautiful mountains. Buramsan sits between the Nowon-gu neighborhood in Seoul and the city of Namyangju.
description_html: Buramsan Mountain, located across Nowon-gu and Namyangju City, derives its name from a large summit rock resembling a Buddha wearing a peaked hat. It is also known as Cheonbosan Mountain and Pilam Mountain. The mountain features long ridges offering refreshing views. From the summit, you can see Byeollae in Namyangju to the east, Bukhansan and Dobongsan Mountains, Nowon-gu and Dobong-gu to the west, and Namsan Tower and Lotte World Tower to the south. Many visitors come to watch the sunrise. Although the mountain's terrain is relatively simple, it boasts beautiful scenery with its massive rock walls, cliffs, and lush trees. Notable landmarks include Seokjangbong Peak and Turtle Rock. The wooden stairs to the summit make it a relatively easy climb.

name: Bukhansan National Park
summary: Bukhansan National Park is the only national park in the Seoul metropolitan area and has many granite peaks and gorges punctuated by crystal clear streams.
description_html: Bukhansan National Park is the only national park in the Seoul metropolitan area and is also known as Samgaksan (Triangle Mountain) because of its three peaks: Baegunbong, Insubong and Mangyeongbong. The park’s many granite peaks and gorges are punctuated by crystal clear streams, creating a perfect harmony between the mountains and water. Rich in biodiversity, Bukhansan is home to more than 1,300 species of plants and animals and boasts a wealth of historical and cultural heritage sites as well as over 100 Buddhist temples and hermitages. With its many ridges and valleys, Bukhansan National Park is very popular with hikers, offering trails suited to every level of experience, from gentle slopes to steep rugged tracks while the ever-changing scenery each season makes every visit unique.

name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
summary: Cheonggyecheon Stream is a 11-km long stream that runs through downtown Seoul, created during an urban renewal project.
description_html:
Cheonggyecheon Stream is an 11 km-long stream that runs through downtown Seoul. Created as part of an urban renewal project, Cheonggyecheon Stream is a restoration of the stream that was once there during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). The stream was covered with an elevated highway after the Korean War (1950-1953), as part of the country's post-war economic development. Then in 2003, the elevated highway was removed to restore the stream to its present form today. The stream starts from Cheonggye Plaza, a popular cultural arts venue, and passes under a total of 22 bridges before flowing into the Hangang River, with many attractions along the way.

Cheonggyecheon’s turbulent history is on display at the Cheonggyecheon Museum, which opened in September 2005. The museum offers visitors the chance to learn about the many changes the stream has seen, including being buried underground and being restored. The story is told with the help of a scale-model and period photographs.

Frequently Asked Questions about Cheonggyecheon Stream
Is the Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade always open?
Yes. The Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. However, in the case of rain, access may be restricted for safety reasons.
What festivals are held at the Cheonggyecheon Stream?
The "Seoul Lantern Festival" is held annually at the end of the year around the Cheonggyecheon Stream area. (As of 2026)
What is the nearest subway station to Cheonggyecheon Stream?
There are a total of 11 subway stations connected to Cheonggyecheon Stream: City Hall Station (Subway Line 1, 2), Jonggak Station, Jongno 3-ga Station, Jongno 5-ga Station, Dongdaemun Station, Dongmyo Station, Sinseol-dong Station (Subway Line 1), Eulji-ro 1-ga Station, Eulji-ro 3-ga Station, Eulji-ro 4-ga Station, Dongdaemun History and Culture Park Station, Yongdu Station (Subway Line 2).

description_html: The Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park is the first ecological park ever established in Korea expressly for the purpose of preserving the area's ecosystem. There are informational signs placed on the park's footpaths to help visitors learn about and spot the native Korean flora in the park. Ecological and nature-related programs operate throughout the year. Admission to the Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park is free.

name: Hangang River Cycling Trail
summary: The Hangang River Cycling Trail stretches almost the riverside and spans a total of 240km. It is the longest cycling route in Korea.

name: Inwangsan Mountain
summary: Inwangsan Mountain is a rocky mountain that stands in central Seoul and offers great views of Gyeongbokgung Palace and the city's other mountains.
description_html: Inwangsan Mountain is a rocky mountain that stands in central Seoul and offers great views of Gyeongbokgung Palace and the city's other mountains. Inwangsan has many striking natural features and is also the home to Korea’s most important shamanistic shrine. Apart from its magnificent views, the mountain is a relatively easy hike, taking just two hours to hike along the ridges of the mountain. Part of Hanyangdoseong, the Seoul City Wall, runs along the mountain. The most popular trail goes from Sajik Tunnel to Buam-dong, along Hanyangdoseong, the Seoul City Wall, and on to Inwangsan Mountain.

name: Gwanaksan Mountain
summary: Gwanaksan Mountain is located in southern Seoul and is renowned for its magnificent scenery.
description_html: Gwanaksan Mountain was designated as an Urban Nature Park in 1968. Gwanaksan Mountain is famous for its large rocks and tall green trees that combine together to form a beautiful mountain. Gwanaksan Mountain is difficult to climb, but it is close to the city center and because of its smaller size, many hikers enjoy visiting it. Anyang Amusement Park is located to the south of Gwanaksan Mountain, and the Gwacheon Government Complex is located to the east. From the mountain, visitors can see many unique rock formations such as Yeolnyeoam Rock, Pig Rock, Frog Rock, and Haetae Rock.

name: Dobongsan Mountain
summary: Dobongsan Mountain is considered by many to be Seoul’s most dramatic mountain
description_html: Dobongsan Mountain is considered by many to be Seoul’s most dramatic and imposing granite mountain. The mountain's Seoninbong peak is especially popular with rock climbers. Located within Bukhansan National Park, Dobongsan is considered one of Seoul's finest mountains by hiking enthusiasts. The mountain is also surrounded by around 60 temples set in scenic valleys and the temples are great places to see some of Korea's history and culture while enjoying the outdoors.

name: Choansan Neighborhood Park Barefoot Loess Trail
summary: A healing space to enhance the well-being of city residents weary from daily life
description_html:
The Barefoot Loess Trail at Choansan Neighborhood Park opened in September 2024. It features a round-trip course of 134 meters, offering visitors a chance to relax in nature. This is the first trail in Seoul to incorporate a ground-spray cooling fog system, which helps maintain the texture and quality of the loess, allowing for a more pleasant walking experience.


In addition to the barefoot trail, the park also includes a loess foot bath and a loess ball zone for a variety of wellness experiences. To ensure user convenience, the site provides a foot-washing station, sitting wall blocks for resting or putting on and taking off shoes, and shoe storage facilities.

name: Bamseom Island
summary: An island located downstream of the Mapodaegyo Bridge on the Hangang River, where the Seogangdaegyo Bridge passes through
description_html: Bamseom is an island located downstream from Mapodaegyo Bridge on the Hangang River, intersected by Seogangdaegyo Bridge. Known as a habitat for migratory birds, Bamseom gets its name from its chestnut-like shape. In the past, the island was inhabited. Still, during the development of Yeouido, the island was split into Upper Bamseom and Lower Bamseom after an explosion forced residents to relocate to Mapo-gu. The upper part of Bamseom, with its bay-shaped shoreline, became an important bird nesting area. Over the next 20 years, sediment from the Hangang River allowed trees and grasses to flourish, attracting birds and establishing the island as a well-known urban bird sanctuary. Bamseom Island is now approximately six times larger than it was originally. In 1999, it was designated as a Natural Ecosystem Conservation Area; in 2012, it was recognized as a Ramsar Wetland. While direct access to the island is prohibited, Bamseom Island can be viewed from Bamseom Park.
description_text: Bamseom is an island located downstream from Mapodaegyo Bridge on the Hangang River, intersected by Seogangdaegyo Bridge. Known as a habitat for migratory birds, Bamseom gets its name from its chestnut-like shape. In the past, the island was inhabited. Still, during the development of Yeouido, the island was split into Upper Bamseom and Lower Bamseom after an explosion forced residents to relocate to Mapo-gu. The upper part of Bamseom, with its bay-shaped shoreline, became an important bird nesting area. Over the next 20 years, sediment from the Hangang River allowed trees and grasses to flourish, attracting birds and establishing the island as a well-known urban bird sanctuary. Bamseom Island is now approximately six times larger than it was originally. In 1999, it was designated as a Natural Ecosystem Conservation Area; in 2012, it was recognized as a Ramsar Wetland. While direct access to the island is prohibited, Bamseom Island can be viewed from Bamseom Park.

name: Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest
summary: The Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, Seoul, once traversed by trains bound for Chuncheon
description_html: The Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, Seoul, once traversed by trains bound for Chuncheon, captures a unique mix of historical and modern elements. In this area, the Gongneung-dong section has evolved into a lively area reminiscent of New York's Central Park. It is connected to the adjacent Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market and dotted with a growing array of cafes and pubs. Consequently, this area has earned the nickname "Gongtral Park," inspired by Gongneung-dong. It's also known as "Gyeongnidan-gil" (akin to Gyeongnidan-gil in Gongneung-dong). Traditionally, old railway lines converted into parks have their tracks removed, but what sets this place apart is the preservation of its original railway tracks.

name: Namsan Yejang Park
summary: A Way Walking with History, NamsanYejangPark
description_html: 'Namsan Yejang Park' is a place where was a training ground for the military in Joseon Dynasty, Residency-General was entered in Japanese colonial era and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) was placed where the torture investigation was carried out. A place where was historically isolated for a long time became the park of embracing the sad history of Korea's modern and contemporary history. 'Namsan Yejang Park' is comprised of the park with bushy trees and underground space which shows off it s architectural beauty. Yejang Madang and Lee Hoe-yeong Memorial Hall are located underground and historical places are located on the ground such as 'Memorial 6', the reenacted torture chamber of the Central Intelligence Agency and the trace site which preserved as it was the site of an official residence of Japanese government-general of Korea.

name: Seoul Botanic Park
summary: Located in Magok, Gangseo-gu, Seoul Botanic Park is the first facility in Seoul to combine both a botanical garden and a park in one space.
description_html:
Located in Magok, Gangseo-gu, Seoul Botanic Park is the first facility in Seoul to combine botanical garden and park in one space. A space where a forest, garden, lake, and marsh coexist together, Seoul Botanic Park's theme zone houses plants representing 12 major cities around the world. Within close distance from Gimpo Airport (10 minute) and Incheon Airport (40 minute), Seoul Botanic Park is also directly connected with the subway station, allowing visitors to easily access its facilities. Seoul Botanic Park was created to advance the urban ecology of Seoul and will display plants from 12 cities around the world. As part of an effort to expand green spaces around the city, this facility offers educational programs on top of hosting cultural events, serving as a space where city residents can get back in touch with nature. 



Frequently Asked Questions about Seoul Botanic Park

Can I bring my pets to the Seoul Botanic Park?

Only pets with leashes, name tags, and toilet bags are allowed to enter. However, pets are not permitted inside the theme gardens and plant culture center. However, guide dogs are an exception. (As of 2024)

When is Seoul Botanical Garden closed?

The Seoul Botanic Park’s Forest Field, Lake Garden, and Wetland are open year-round, and the Theme gardens and greenhouse are closed every Monday. (As of 2024)

What kind of plants are in the Seoul Botanic Park?

The Seoul Botanic Park has about 4,600 species of plants. Detailed plant information can be found on the website below.

name: Hongneung Arboretum
summary: Hongneung Arboretum is Korea's oldest arboretum and was established to support the study of Korean flora.
description_html: Located at the southwest side of the Cheonjangsan Mountain (Elev. 141 m) in the eastern part of Seoul, as well as serving as the grounds of Empress Myeongseong’s royal tomb, the Hongneung Arboretum is revered for its high historical, cultural, and academic value that functions as Korea's first and oldest arboretum,established to support the study of Korean flora in 1922. As such, several forestry-related studies and research projects are continually conducted, while the arboretum systematically manages as many as 2,035 species (trees: 1,224 / herbs & plants: 811) of plant genetic resources, both native and foreign to Korea. During the weekdays, the arboretum works as an ecological learning facility forchildren and students ranging from kindergarten up through university, while also remaining open every weekend for local residents as a place of learning for those interested in studying nature and learning about the environment since 1993.

name: Yongsan Park
summary: Yongsan Park is a vast green open space dotted with refreshing ponds and adorned with beautiful sculptures by world famous sculptors.
description_html:
Yongsan Park is a vast green open space dotted with refreshing ponds and adorned with beautiful sculptures by world famous sculptors. The location of Yongsan Park has historical significance: it was once used as an American command post after the Korean War, but has now been transformed into this peaceful leisure amenity open to the public. Yongsan Park is popular with Seoul families and always filled with people. Children playing and families enjoying picnics together are common sights, especially at weekends. The sculpture park, which is attached to the main park, is famous for displaying works of art by internationally – acclaimed sculptors from Germany, Switzerland, Canada, and other countries as well as Korea. Visitors can also enjoy the pleasure of free acupressure therapy in the Barefoot Park. 


The site of Yongsan Park is historically significant. It was used as a base by the Japanese army during the Imjin War (1592-1598), and later by the Chinese army during the Imo Incident in 1882 (the Joseon Dynasty’s political conflict between Japan and China). After the Korean War it was occupied by the American army, who used it as a golf course. Finally, it came back into Korean hands in 1992 in the form of a public park. The original park was scaled back to accommodate the establishment of the new National Museum of Korea in 1997. Since then, Yongsan Park has become a peaceful spot where people come to relax amid the endless green.

name: Dream Forest
summary: Dream Forest, located in northern Seoul, is the 4th largest park in the city after Seoul Forest, Olympic Park, and World Cup Park.
description_html:
Dream Forest, located in northern Seoul, is the 4th largest park in the city after Seoul Forest, Olympic Park, and World Cup Park. Neighboring six surrounding districts, including Gangbuk-gu, Seongbuk-gu, and Dobong-gu, the park was built on the site where Dreamland amusement park formerly existed.


Surrounded by densely forested mountains of Byeogosan Mountain and Opaesan Mountain, Dream Forest provides a variety of attractions to visitors, together with an abundant amount of natural vegetation. The Cherry Blossom Path in the spring or the Maple Tree Forest in the fall are especially beautiful. Visitors will also find attractions designed after traditional Korean architecture such as the Wolyeongji (Moon Reflecting Pond) and the Wolgwang Falls (Moonlight Falls). At the top of the observatory, visitors are treated to a panoramic view of the whole park and a view of Bukhansan Mountain, Dobongsan Mountain and Suraksan Mountain. Dream Forest also accommodates various cultural venues. The Dream Forest Arts Center, with its Performance Hall and Concert Hall, the Sangsang Toktok Art Museum and several grassy lawns and plazas offer concerts and performances throughout the year. Several restaurants and cafes are also conveniently located within the park, making Dream Forest one of the most comprehensive parks in Seoul.

name: Seoul Forest
summary: Seoul Forest was established to satisfy people’s desire to have more green space and recreational places in the center of the city.
description_html:
Opened in 2005, Seoul Forest is a vast urban park spanning approximately 495,868.5 square meters. It is a tranquil retreat where people of all ages can experience nature within the city. When cherry blossoms and tulips bloom in the spring, the forest is filled with families, couples, and friends enjoying outings together. 

In the fall, it becomes a popular spot for people to enjoy music festivals amidst the cool breeze. Even in summer and winter, Seoul Forest remains a bustling green haven whenever the weather is good.Seoul Forest has five theme parks: the Cultural and Arts Park, the Eco Forest, the Experiential Learning Park, the Wetland Eco Center, and the Hangang Riverside Park Project. The first theme park, the Cultural and Arts Park, offers a variety of leisure activities. It includes a gateball court, a forest playground, a family yard with a large lawn, a statue of a military horse, a ground fountain, and an atelier. 

The second theme park, the Eco Forest, is designed to recreate a natural forest where wild animals and plants can coexist. The third theme park, the Wetland Eco Center, consists of eco-friendly wellness spaces such as an environmental playground, an outdoor nature classroom, and a water purification garden. The fourth theme, the Experiential Learning Park, includes features like the Keeper's Forest, Butterfly Garden, and Insect Garden. The fifth theme, the Hangang Riverside Park Project, has the Seoul Forest Quay and bike paths. Additionally, various unique gardens like the Garden of Excitement, the Bee Garden, and the Bench Garden have been added through donations from individuals and corporations, transforming Seoul Forest into an even more attractive space each year.


 

Frequently Asked Questions about Seoul Forest Park

Can I bring my pet to Seoul Forest Park?

Seoul Forest allows entry with pets, but it is important to ensure that they do not inconvenience other visitors. Please properly handle pet waste and make sure to keep them on a leash (within 2 meters)

How much is parking at the Seoul Forest?

Yes, the Seoul Forest parking lot operates 24 hours a day and has 211 spaces, including six designated accessible parking. The fees are as follows (as of 2024)

• Large car: 400 won per 5 minutes

name: Namsan Park
summary: Namsan Park is the largest park in Seoul and is home to many species of trees, plants, and animals.
description_html:
Namsan Park is located at the base of Namsan Mountain in the heart of Seoul. It is the largest civic park in Seoul. The park is divided into four main districts: Jangchung, Yejang, Hoehyeon, and Hannam. As a space where people can enjoy nature within the city, it attracts many visitors, including tourists and locals. Various seasonal programs are organized throughout the year, offering numerous experiences to the public. In addition to these programs, the park features many attractions and activities, such as the Ahn Jung-geun Memorial Hall, a cable car, the Namsan Tower Observatory, and a children's forest experience center. The Namsan Seoul Tower Observatory is a famous landmark where visitors can enjoy a panoramic view of Seoul, making it a popular destination.

description_html: Myeongsindang Pilbang was founded in 1932 in Boryeong, Chungcheongnam-do, as an ink factory and moved to Insadong in 1987, where it has remained ever since. It is one of the few remaining paintbrush shops and is also famous for inscription which was carved by Queen Elizabeth and the King and Queen of Spain during their visit to Korea. Myeongsin-dang Pilbang's trade name, "Myeongsin," means "always moving forward, day by day and month by month. Top Korean calligraphers such as Idang Kim Eun-ho, Cheongjeon Lee Sang-beom, Sojung Byeon-kwan-sik, and Goam Lee Eung-no all purchased materials from Guhasanbang. Myeongshindang Pilbang is not only concerned with preserving tradition, but is also constantly researching new materials.

name: Kum Bak Yeon
summary: Where the Joseon dynasty's family business of etching gold leaf on royal silk
description_html:
Geumbakyeon is a place that has passed down the history of the royal family for five generations, from the royal goldsmith during the reign of King Cheoljong in 1856 to Kim Ki-ho, the national intangible cultural property No. 119. Since ancient times, gold has symbolized eternal beauty due to its unchanging light, and the royal family used gold foil to engrave patterns on their clothes. Geumbaekyeon maintains a unique traditional technique of coating gold leaf using woodblocks designed and produced by craftsmen, and promotes Korean gold leaf art by applying traditional gold leaf techniques to various materials. •


This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr/main/mainForm.do )

name: Breath, Rest: The journey to innocence
summary: The hope is that facing all these artworks of nature and taking a breath, the most fundamental element of our lives, will help us look at ourselves calmly.
description_html:
To live means that everyone has their own 'breath.’ This fact is so obvious that sometimes we live without recognizing its preciousness. However, in this era of loss, we live without being able to breathe properly. This exhibition is a process of finding ‘rest’ through ‘breath’ and was planned to awaken the importance of us as a whole. I want to be with you at the beginning of the journey to find myself little by little, but with a small but pure shining self, not a processed me who is constantly decorated and corrected in the eyes of others. Soil, wood, and thread, all materials like natural gifts to humanity, are expressed through crafts by borrowing the hands of the artist. Using that innocence as a motif, I tried to make things look unpretentious without processing them more than necessary. The hope is that facing all these artworks of nature and taking a breath, the most fundamental element of our lives, will help us look at ourselves calmly.

-Participating artist Hong Seongil

name: 《Kang Seok-ho: Three Minutes Delight》
summary: Kang Seok-ho (1971-2021) first retrospective exhibition 《Kang Seok-ho: Three Minutes Delight》 complexly portrays the images of Kang Seok-ho, who has expanded his aesthetic taste through the collection and production of design furniture while insisting on his unique way of painting.
description_html:
The Seoul Museum of Art is holding Kang Seok-ho's solo exhibition ‘Kang Seok-ho: 3 Minutes Delight’ as the last exhibition of 2022.

Kang Seok-ho’s (1971-2021) first retrospective exhibition 《Kang Seok-ho: 3 Minutes of Happiness》 complexly portrays the images of Kang Seok-ho, who has expanded his aesthetic taste through the collection and production of design furniture while insisting on his unique way of painting. name: The Abstract Field of Color: Color Beyond the Radiance
summary: Vivian Choi Gallery will host a three-person exhibition, "The Abstract Field of Color; Color Beyond the Radiance" featuring Won Kun Jun, Soo Jung Park, and Andy Harwood, who focus on the most essential elements, color, and captures visual space and light in a painting through a screen with accumulated repetitive performance.
description_html: Won Kun Jun is an artist based in Germany; Soo Jung Park is an artist based in California, USA; and Andy Harwood is an Australian artist based in Brisbane. The three artists focus on the essential properties of painting: dots, lines, shapes, and colors, which are basic elements. Their paintings are composed of geometric or floating color fields, which are restrained expressions and simple in form, but the repetitive patterns of color fields evoke emotion. Although they approach painting with minimal expression, the colors they create mean more than just colors. To the three artists, color is a tool and window that conveys the artist's feelings, visualizes light, and communicates with the audience. By combining color with other colors or spaces formed by notching with a knife, they expand color into a spectrum of light and explore the synesthetic experience of how color and light react with the viewer's consciousness. Won Kun Jun, Soo Jung Park, and Andy Harwood expand the visual realm of color into the realm of synesthesia. Through the three-person exhibition, The Abstract Field of Color; Color Beyond the Radiance, feel the contemplative experience created by color and light.

name: The Age of Digital Transformation: Meeting Nam June Paik Again
summary: The Seoul Museum of Art is holding an academic symposium The Age of Digital Transformation: Meeting Nam June Paik Again, to commemorate the 90th anniversary of Nam June Paik’s birth
description_html: The Seoul Museum of Art is holding an academic symposium The Age of Digital Transformation: Meeting Nam June Paik Again, to commemorate the 90th anniversary of Nam June Paik’s birth. This event, co-hosted by the Nam June Paik Art Center and the Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST), is a place where, with Nam June Paik in mind, from where we stand, we imagine ourselves and what’s coming next. The creative future that Nam June Paik imagined a long time ago is always welcoming us anew through his work and matching with the approaching times. In this symposium, contemporary scientists and artists at the forefront of art and science will be invited to gauge the "future drawn by technology" and "vision contained in art practice" in the digital transformation era.

summary: It is a festival where you can experience Yukuijeon, six exclusive stores located in the Cheonggye area of Jongno during the Joseon Dynasty. The king granted exclusive commercial rights for them to procure goods for national demand.

The king granted exclusive commercial rights for them to procure goods for national demand. Yukuijeon represents Jijeon (Korean paper goods shop), Eomuljeon (seafood shop), Jeopojeon and Pojeon (linen hemp fabric shop), Shenzhen (silk shop), Myeonpojeon (cotton fabric shop), and Myeonjujeon (silk fabric shop).


The Yukuijeon Festival, which marks its 17th anniversary this year, is an event created to share the particularities and experience the characteristics of each store. The festival will feature traditional Yukuijeon exhibitions, modern Yukuijeon exhibitions, experiences of the traditional life of the Joseon Dynasty, various traditional performances, Korean traditional music performances, cultural and artistic performances, and special performances.

summary: Based on the cultural resources of Pyeongchang-dong, Buam-dong, Hongji-dong, Sinyeong-dong, and Gugi-dong and with love from the people who love art, the Jamunbak Cultural Festival has been a leading festival every fall since 2013. description_html:
Our daily life needs food for survival and living, but we also need roses for emotions and sensitivity. Access Jamunbak’s art life through exhibitions with local galleries, concerts and busking by various participants, forums for sharing past-present-future journeys and inspiration, art markets prepared by artists and local workshops, Jamunbak healing retreats, art experience programs for elementary school students and adolescents, and performances by 30 independent performing artists. Thank you.

name: 2022 Picksgood Gallery Opening Exhibition [The New WAVE]
summary: The first opening exhibition of Picksgood is with four major active artists of Korean contemporary art. The opening exhibition title is ‘The New Wave.’ In this era where the boundaries between cyberspace and reality are increasingly blurring with the advent of the new Web 3.0 era, it will be an exhibition where established artists find their way to meet the flow of the new generation.
description_html:
■This is the first opening exhibition with four contemporary artists dealing with various media originating from NFT art. The New WAVE exhibition will be an exhibition where established artists find their way to meet the flow of the new generation in this era where the boundaries between cyberspace and reality are increasingly blurring with the advent of the new Web 3.0 era. The exhibition included Geum Min-jeong, who majored in sculpture and deals with video media. She infinitely expands the scalability of sculpture. Her critical perspective reflects on contemporary events and accident sites and the attitude of the mass media delivering the news to the general public. There is also artist Ha Tae-beom, who expresses himself through photography, video, and sculpture, Jang Hee-jin, who expresses abstract colors and beautiful landscape images on canvas with a unique technique; and lastly, Han Seung-gu, with roots in sculpture, which adds engineering techniques to his video work In this exhibition of The New WAVE, people will feel the flow of contemporary Korean art, and the clues to find the direction of contemporary art in the works created.

Part I. 1st floor
■Artists involved: Geum Min-jeong, Jang Hee-jin, Ha Tae-beom, and Han Seung-gu, four young active contemporary artists, are exhibiting in the main exhibition space on the first floor, including the entrance to the exhibition hall. These artists have established their unique world in contemporary art using a unique medium in their work and respective spheres. In addition, as artists at the center of the Korean art world, attracting attention from contemporary art, they were selected as the leading artists of this Picksgood opening exhibition. As you enter the exhibition hall, you can enjoy various photos, videos, paintings, and sculptures, as well as their latest new and recent NFT works.

Part II. Basement multipurpose hall
■What will be introduced:
This section will mainly introduce NFT works by newcomers and artists with great potential and artistry, which are listed in the Picksgood NFT platform project. In addition, it will be a space for exhibiting various NFT project works, such as Steel Troop 2 NFT conducted jointly by KT Skylife and PICKSGOOD, NFT by rapper Koonta, and NFT works by Electro Pixel Kongz that combines music and fashion.

Part II. 2nd floor above ground (limited open)
■ What will be introduced:
You can see paintings by Oh Se-young, the primary collection of Starkey Hall CEO Shim Sang-don. CEO Shim Sang-don, the longest-running professional manager of a domestic company, has been running Starkey Group, the Korean branch of Starkey, the largest hearing aid company in the United States, for 26 years. The first meeting between CEO Shim Sang-don and artist Oh Se-young, a major national exhibition artist in Korea, began 25 years ago when painter Oh Se-young, suffering from hearing loss, visited Starkey headquarters, and a meaningful relationship between the entrepreneur and artist began. Shim Sang-don was deeply impressed by the artist's dedication to his artistic creation despite financial difficulties and has continued to support the artist's work through sponsorship. Shim Sang-don, who currently owns many works of artist Oh Se-young, shares the value of artist Oh Se-young's work in this space and strives to raise the status and interest of the senior.

name: Seoul 100K
summary: Seoul 100K, an iconic competition with the world's only ultra-trail running race, is where you can encounter Seoul’s natural, historical, and cultural attractions, from the Dulle-gil that wraps around Seoul along with famous mountains such as Inwangsan Mountain and Bukhansan Mountain, the forest of buildings that cross the city center, and the Hangang River.
description_html:
Seoul 100K, an iconic competition with the world's only ultra-trail running race, is where you can encounter Seoul’s natural, historical, and cultural attractions, from the Dulle-gil that wraps around Seoul along with famous mountains such as Inwangsan Mountain and Bukhansan Mountain, the forest of buildings that cross the city center, and the Hangang River.

The 2022 Seoul 100K race includes the trail behind the Blue House, which opened for the first time in 54 years. By adding the Baegakjeong - Gokjang - Bugaksan Mountain Palgakjeong Pavillion section, participants will be given a new experience while looking down at the panoramic view of downtown Seoul.

name: 2022 Photographic Arts Center, Seoul Museum of Art Pre-opening Program - The Printed World
summary: 2022 The Photographic Arts Center, Seoul Museum of Art Pre-opening Program - The Printed World introduces the main collections of the Photographic Arts Center (the 1950s to the 1980s) and contemporary artworks (the 2010s to the 2020s.) Let's listen to the voices of photographers who have used their photos as a medium between the past and the present.
description_html:
The Photographic Arts Center, a branch of the Seoul Museum of Art and the first public art museum specializing in photography in Korea, is under construction with the goal of opening in 2024. The purpose is to establish a balanced Korean photographic history, flexibly respond to the rapidly changing characteristics of photographic media, and encompass expertise, popularity, internationality, and locality.


Before its inauguration, through a pre-opening program every year, the Photographic Arts Center, SeMA, shares the development and construction process and asks questions about the role and function of the museum. Furthermore, it explores the possibility of harmoniously connecting the region-medium-topological peculiarity of the Korea-photography-art museum. 2022 Photographic Arts Center, Seoul Museum of Art Pre-opening Program - The Printed World introduces the main collections of the Photographic Arts Center (the 1950s to the 1980s) and contemporary artworks (the 2010s to the 2020s.) Let's listen to the voices of photographers who have used their photos as a medium between the past and the present.


The Printed World began with several questions raised during the artwork-collecting process. Fixing is a photo phenomenon. It is a technical term referring to the photochemical stage of settling an image onto support during the printing process. Printed World expands the meaning of ‘printed’ to fixing, a word that refers to the process in which the artist’s experiences and perceptions are imaged. This three-part pre-opening program focuses on the diversity and heterogeneity of photographic media caused by changes in technology and media environment from analog to digital. The hope is that this will serve as an opportunity to think about the meaning and role of photography recontextualized in the 'history of Korean photography' and 'Art Museum.’

name: Kim Young-Eun 《Frames of Sound》
summary: From July 8 to August 13, 2022, Kim Young-Eun, the 17th Songeun Art Grand Prize winner, will be hosting her solo exhibition 《The Frame of Sound》. In this exhibition, she pays attention to our auditory experiences as a basic sense we can easily miss and the relationship with our surroundings.
description_html: From July 8 to August 13, 2022, Kim Young-Eun, the 17th Songeun Art Grand Prize winner, will be hosting her solo exhibition 《The Frame of Sound》.In this exhibition, she pays attention to our auditory experiences as a basic sense we can easily miss and the relationship with our surroundings.. Through this exhibition, the artist looks at sound as an area that can be interpreted from a physical, psychological, and historical perspective and looks at the process of building an existing system that shapes the music, questioning the criteria for individuals' recognition of sound. By reconstructing historical events based on various records, the artist pays attention to the clash of meanings that occur within the existing musical ‘frame’ and the production of new acoustic realism.

name: Yukjo Street: The Symbolic Street of Hanyang
summary: Yukjo Street, which has maintained its status as a key government office since Hanyang was established, and the footsteps of officials who traveled between them.
description_html: Yukjo Street refers to a boulevard that runs from Gwanghwamun to Sejong-ro intersection. On this boulevard, there was also Uijeongbu, Yukjo, Saheonbu, and Hanseongbu, the core streets of Hanyang. It was a place where major policies were made. In the back, there were lower-level government offices that gathered goods or supported key government offices within the palace. In this exhibition, follow the footsteps of Yukjo Street, which has maintained its status as a key government office area since Hanyang was established 600 years ago, and learn about the officials who traveled between them.

name: Seoul as Envisioned by a Scholar of Urban Design
summary: Donated items from the late Professor Kahng Byong Kee will be displayed and shed light on the history of urban development in Seoul.
description_html: Professor Kahng Byong Kee is deemed as a person who laid the foundation for the field of urban planning and design in Korea. After receiving his doctorate in 1970, he was invited as a professor of urban engineering at Hanyang University, served as president for the first generation of the Korea Planning Association, and was invited to be the president of the Urban Design Institute of Korea. He also practiced urban planning from the bottom up and was involved in different social movements. He was the representative of the "Citizens' Solidarity for Creating a Walkable City" and implemented citizen-led urban planning through civic movements such as "Pedestrian Plaza In Front of Seoul City Hall" and "Enacting a Basic Ordinance on Securing Walking Rights and Improving Walking Environments."

name: 2021 Seoul International Buddhism Festival
summary: This festival allows visitors a chance to experience traditional Korean culture while also shedding light on how Buddhism is in the center of the Korean cultural industry.
description_html:
The 2021 Seoul International Buddhist Festival sheds light on how Buddhism is in the center of the traditional Korean cultural industry and showcases exhibits containing philosophical themes. It's a festival that allows visitors to experience traditional Korean culture while also promoting businesses related to the Buddhism industry in Korea.

 

On and Offline Seoul International Buddhism Fair Exhibits

The Seoul International Buddhism Fair will be held online and offline in accordance with pandemic regulations.

 

The Pandemic Era, Experience Live Commerce at Home

As exhibits will be held on and offline, view products from the exhibition in the comfort of your own home!

 

2021 International Buddhism Fair Businesses

Architecture : Environmentally friendly companies and traditional architecture businesses will provide exhibits including, but not limited to, traditional architecture, modern architecture, interior design, Korean traditional building painting, eco architecture, alternative energy, indoor gardening, and zen gardening.

Crafts : Handmade crafts artists and companies will provide exhibits including but not limited to Buddhist, traditional, modern, ceramic, metal, environmentally friendly furniture, and horticultural crafts.


Food : Health food companies will exhibit items such as temple and traditional foods, vegan/vegetarian products, and many others.

Tea : Various tea related companies will exhibit products such as green tea, fermented tea, traditional Korean tea, white tea, puer tea, and tea tools.

Performance Ceremony : Companies and businesses will exhibit things such as temples, meditation organizations, performance NGOs, funerals, IT and services, etc.

Cultural Items and IT: Traditional and eco-friendly companies will have exhibits such as traditional and Buddhist design products, travel, publishing, media, web, eco-friendly beauty products, zero waste, upcycling, smart farms, electric vehicles, refill stores and more.  


Clothing :  Natural clothing and fabric companies will have exhibits such as kasaya, hanbok, natural fabric dye, modern hanbok, upcycled clothing, vegan fashion, accessories and more. 

 

Exhibition of superb traditional cultural products

 

The 9th Buddha Art Festival!

Traditional Korean and Buddhist art exhibit : A comprehensive exhibition of works ranging from traditional Korean and Buddhist art to contemporary Buddhist art including Buddha statues, Buddhist paintings, and dancheong (traditional Korean wood building painting).

name: Hongneung Forest (Arboretum)
summary: Hongneung Forest used to be the grounds of the tombs of King Gojong (the 26th king of Joseon) and Empress Myeongseong. It is a historical place as the first-generation arboretum in Korea.
description_html: The nation’s first arboretum was created in Hongneung Forest in 1922. Currently, there are the coniferous garden, deciduous garden, herbaceous plant garden, and shrub garden covering a wide area. There are various indigenous animals and plants in the forest as well. In 2020, the forest was designated as a Seoul Future Heritage as it was acknowledged historically as the nation’s oldest arboretum.

name: Nighttime Fancies that Disappear in the Morning
summary: The fourth special exhibition to open at the Hotel Imaginary.
description_html:
The Nighttime Fancies that Disappear in the Morning special exhibition is the fourth exhibition taking place at the Hotel Imaginary located on the hill in Seongbuk-dong, Seoul, from November 20, 2020, to February 28, 2021. All visitors are required to make a reservation in advance.


Serving as both the exhibition planner, and the guide, visitors are told the story of light & dark surrounding the life of the main protagonist, Xiao Si’r, from the story, A Brighter Summer Day. You can also see the video artwork of artist, Hwang Min-gyu, as well one of his earlier works, I Protect You [2015], and a more recent work, Into the Wild [2020]. 


Centered around the concept of the word "fancy," referring to the process of drawing the image of an object or event inside one's mind that has little to no possibility of actually coming to pass in reality, this exhibition aims to break away from the dichotomy of "darkness" that blinds us and "light" that opens our eyes. The result is the storytelling of a color produced within the boundaries of where light and dark coexist.


※ In order to abide by social distancing measures in protection from the spread of COVID-19, all visitors are required to observe the exhibition by individual only with a maximum of four visitors allowed in the exhibition at any given time.


※ All visitors are required to make a reservation in advance and are available online via Naver Booking services [ https://booking.naver.com/ ].

name: Namsan Park & World Cup Park Archives
summary: This exhibition displays the archives of Namsan & World Cup Parks and is set to take place online.
description_html:
Come visit this special exhibition to see the archives of two of Seoul's most signature parks: Namsan Park and World Cup Park. Namsan Park maintains its standing as one of Seoul's most noteworthy landmarks, having transformed over the years from being just a beautiful mountain to becoming a popular and thriving public park. World Cup Park has gone through its own share of changes as well, after initially having been used as a landfill and then being turned into an ecological park. Visitors from all around the world stop by these parks to explore their magnificence. 


As a part of the "Our Park" exhibition series ran by the Park Archives division, a part of the Seoul Metropolitan Government, this year's exhibition is the final exhibition following the Namsan Botanical Garden and the Seoul Forest Story exhibitions held last month on October 13 and 27, respectively. It is the first time for an event of its kind to be held online, allowing for any and everyone to access the event via the Seoul Mountains & Parks (http://parks.seoul.go.kr) and Seoul Archives  (http://archives.seoul.go.kr)  websites.

name: 41st Seoul Dance Festival
summary: Earned a satisfactory evaluation to receive the honor of being the top domestic performance festival of 2019!
description_html:
The Seoul Dance Festival, sponsored by the KoreaDance Association, with Professor Cho Namgyu as the Standing Director, first commencedin 1979 as the "Korean Dance Festival" so as to contribute to the development of danceart in Korea through quality creative dance performances. By 2019, the festivalhad solidified itself as the best domestic dance festival around. From two yearsprior to that in 2017, with the beginnings of widespread changes to the program,each year witnessed the festival team take to new challenges and push for furtherprogram development. It was in 2019 when the festival finally earned itself a satisfactory("S") evaluation in the Korean Arts Assessment Program, winning over bothdancers and the public with its standard of excellence.


Without limiting itself to a particular genre,denomination, or age group, the Seoul Dance Festival involves the active participationof middle-aged and senior dancers, as well as that of public arts organizations. This has led to the continual planning and development of various dance contentand genres, spawning the tireless effort to innovate and advance Korean dance. Asa result, the festival has become the signature dance festival of Seoul, featuringover 500 dancers performing amid as many as 20,000 spectators.


The festival has now been around for the last41 years shaping the dance community of Korea, and with its surpassing the 40-yearmark, it has become the perfect opportunity for the festival to carry on its tradition, while also pushing the envelope on the art of dancing for even greater success and advancement.

name: 2020 Insadong Culture Festival
summary: A collaborative festival featuring the 2020 Insadong Culture Festival and the Asia Hotel Art Fair Seoul 2020.
description_html:
As the premier culture festival of the Jongno-gu District in downtown Seoul and having reached its 33rd annual celebration after its humble beginnings as the Insadong Traditional Culture Festival, the 2020 Insadong Culture Festival is set to commence its exhibition together with the Asia Hotel Art Fair Commission. This year's collaborative festival is comprised of two special exhibitions, the Leaving Insadong documentary and the Asia Hotel Art Fair, with the former scheduled to run from October 15-22 in the Central Museum of the 1st basement floor of the Anyoung Insadong Cultural Complex, and the latter slated to operate from October 15-18 on the 10th, 12th, and 14th floors of Insadong's Nine Tree Premier Hotel.


At 5 p.m. on the 15th at the Central Museum exhibition hall, the festival will kick off with Insa Open and follow with a slew of other programs and exhibitions over the course of eight days that go on to include the Leaving Insadong documentary, an exhibition featuring old artistry, galleries, and crafts; Insa Chwihaeng & In Sense, two programs with tours of historical, cultural, and lifestyle content, as well as hands-on actitivites; Insa Site H & Insa Lounge, a couple of special lectures on Insadong culture that are led by well-known figures and field specialists; and In Sound, a unique experience of the Insadong area through music. 


Motivated by a sense of empathy for proceeding with such festivals that deliver much needed economic activity to the local community alongside the opportunity to satiate the public's thirst for cultural events, even during these trying times, this year's joint event was planned to fit within the constraints of the pandemic, resulting in a festival of a smaller scale that is operated in separate parts in the form of an exhibition and other programs. All festival operations will observe safety and social-distancing procedure and are available for the public to attend in small groups by way of advanced reservation. Also, the festival content will be available for viewing online as an alternative during the festival period.
description_text: As the premier culture festival of the Jongno-gu District in downtown Seoul and having reached its 33rd annual celebration after its humble beginnings as the Insadong Traditional Culture Festival, the 2020 Insadong Culture Festival is set to commence its exhibition together with the Asia Hotel Art Fair Commission. This year's collaborative festival is comprised of two special exhibitions, the Leaving Insadong documentary and the Asia Hotel Art Fair, with the former scheduled to run from October 15-22 in the Central Museum of the 1st basement floor of the Anyoung Insadong Cultural Complex, and the latter slated to operate from October 15-18 on the 10th, 12th, and 14th floors of Insadong's Nine Tree Premier Hotel. At 5 p.m. on the 15th at the Central Museum exhibition hall, the festival will kick off with Insa Open and follow with a slew of other programs and exhibitions over the course of eight days that go on to include the Leaving Insadong documentary, an exhibition featuring old artistry, galleries, and crafts; Insa Chwihaeng & In Sense, two programs with tours of historical, cultural, and lifestyle content, as well as hands-on actitivites; Insa Site H & Insa Lounge, a couple of special lectures on Insadong culture that are led by well-known figures and field specialists; and In Sound, a unique experience of the Insadong area through music. Motivated by a sense of empathy for proceeding with such festivals that deliver much needed economic activity to the local community alongside the opportunity to satiate the public's thirst for cultural events, even during these trying times, this year's joint event was planned to fit within the constraints of the pandemic, resulting in a festival of a smaller scale that is operated in separate parts in the form of an exhibition and other programs. All festival operations will observe safety and social-distancing procedure and are available for the public to attend in small groups by way of advanced reservation. Also, the festival content will be available for viewing online as an alternative during the festival period.

It is scheduled to take place both on and offline over the two-day course of October 9 & 10 (Friday & Satuday).

description_html:
※ Online: 10.10.2020 - 11.08.2020 / Offline: 10.10.2020 - 10.18.2020


The Royal Culture Festival is Korea's largest cultural heritage festival that is inclusive of the country's most infamous historical grounds, from the five major Seoul palaces to Jongmyo and the Sajikdan Altar. The creative cultural and arts programming based on the geographical and historical significance of the palaces help advocate a greater awareness among the public of the value that these heritage sites hold.
