name: Opening of Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music
summary: A museum offering a rich collection of sounds of Korea, along with exhibition halls, listening rooms, and educational spaces.
description_html:
A petite hanok building located on the site of the Border Defense Council of Joseon at the junction in front of Changdeokgung Palace on Donhwamum-ro. The building is Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music where everyone can experience and enjoy the melodies of Korean folk music. The sound of farmers singing through strenuous farm work, the sound of fishers yanking fishing nets wishing for a full load of fish, the sound of women humming softly as they weaved hemp clothes, and the folk songs that have been passed from mouth to mouth. This is a place where you can listen to the unfamiliar yet comforting sounds to your heart's desire.


The Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music was established for Korean citizens and tourists visiting Korea from overseas to enjoy the sound of Korea that the Seoul Metropolitan Government has collected so far including 20,000 pieces of Korean folk music and 5,700 pieces of musical instruments. If Seoul Donhwamun Traditional Theater which is located not far from the museum is the center of the traditional Korean court music, this place offers a comprehensive view of Korean folk music in a systematic manner. Through the Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music, the preservation of Korean oral folk songs, which are harder to hear these days, is now possible.

name: 11th Annual World Coffee Leaders Forum
summary: A knowledge-sharing forum that gathers the world's top coffee scholars in one sitting
description_html:
As the world's first international conference to be officially sponsored by the International Coffee Organization (ICO), an organized body operated under the UN, and the leading conference of its kind in Asia, the World Coffee Leaders Forum (WCLF) was first held in 2012 and has since continuously provided a platform for specialists in the field to provide their insight on a number of select issues to aid in the sustainable growth of the global coffee market. The forum also offers the chance to pursue the search for a new paradigm focused on the future of the industry that takes a look at the changes that are in store.


There are several issues facing the global coffee industry that must be overcome. Some of those issues include the expansion of the specialty coffee market due to the increased demand for high-quality coffee; the price increase of basic costs and the coffee itself that result from such an expansion; the damage caused by plant-attacking bugs on top of inadequate temperatures for farming coffee plants due to global warming; the relationship between coffee producers and countries of consumption; the changes in the coffee market following the pandemic as well as the required solutions needed as a response to such change; and so on. The guest speakers from both home and abroad help break some ground regarding these issues in order to offer new possibilities while those in attendance help brainstorm global market trends and the challenging, new directions to take the market.



Program Details:


1. Global Session


The Global Session gives a voice to educated leaders from different fields to share their perspectives on the future of the global coffee industry while offering novel and innovative ideas to business owners in need of solutions for managing their coffee shops and brands during the post-Corona era. There will also be a panel discussion to promote discourse and debate that will be open to communication with the audience.


2. Professional Session


The Professional Session provides a platform for specialists around the globe to share the technology and knowledge of the industry. The various demonstrations and presentations allow attendees to come away with a better understanding of some of the advanced technology along with other helpful information.


3. Origin Adventure Session


The Origin Adventure Session holds a coffee "cupping" session featuring premium coffee tastings for partnered producers, including buyers, retailers, and importers, that seek to try the coffee beans and their flavors for themselves.


4. SCA Training Program


The SCA Training Program, consisting of the Coffee Skills Program, a popular program of the SCA Certification Program, and the Coffee Technicians Program, newly launched in 2021, builds upon the passion attendees have for coffee and helps promote the advancement of industry technology. After completing courses on proven theory and field training geared toward coffee connoisseurs, professional baristas, and those looking to obtain a SCA international certification, participants may then take the online written exam for an opportunity to get officially certified.

name: Touch Me Tell, A Children's Exhibition at Seoul Museum of Art by Melanie Bonajo
summary: How many people do we interact with each day? Is holding hands an act of intimacy? You are invited to perceive your emotions in this Touch Me Tell exhibition. This exhibition is about realizing and ac
description_html: How many people do we interact with each day? Is holding hands an act of intimacy? You are invited to perceive your emotions in this Touch Me Tell exhibition. We live in a cerebral world, spend too much time online, and often turn ourselves off, says Touch Me Tell artist Melanie Bonajo. Emotional intelligence can be developed by listening to your current emotional state, so this is your chance to know how you truly feel. Bonajo deals with the meaning of contact and intimacy in an increasingly marginalized and commodity-centric experience. This work also emphasizes contact and intimacy, given the limited physical contact and isolation during the pandemic. The exhibition hall was designed in a circular shape to allow people to hold hands and spin around. The circular shapes of the hall and the people inside it were designed to fit together like puzzle pieces. The placed structures are made in the form of flat pillows and rounded islands. The tactile sensation is activated in a soft space, encouraging thinking through touch. This exhibition is about realizing and acknowledging what makes you feel comfortable returning your body to a state of self-regulation and agency. When we feel safe in that comfort, we can be more empathetic and kinder to each other.

name: Reflective Space: Void Towards The Realm of The Mind
summary: The Vivian Choi Gallery has been holding the Reflective Space: Void Towards The Realm of The Mind exhibition since March 16th
description_html:
The Vivian Choi Gallery has been holding the Reflective Space: Void Towards The Realm of The Mind exhibition since March 16th. This exhibition began with a fundamental question: what is an artistic act? Artist Kim In-gyeom has said that his work begins when he escapes from the consciousness of making something new and discovers what has already been made.

“I collected the discarded plywood scorched by the sun and scratched by the wind and rain for a long time. I cut out the deeply damaged areas and trimmed and burned the areas that could be salvaged, and began to incorporate them into my work. I feel happy and moved as if I was dealing with a life that was saved as I watched the discarded things that had to go to the garbage dump be transformed into a vivid and confident work amidst the pain of planting a new life.”
Kim In-gyeom (1945 – 2018)

Artist Kim In-gyeom placed importance on the beginning and process of artwork because he believed that “work left behind is not meaningful, but that the artist’s mental movement, judgment, and the action itself have important value.” Participating artists in the Reflective Space: Void Towards The Realm of The Mind exhibition, Kim In-gyeom, Kim Dong-hyung, and Jeong Min-hee, rather than focusing on the creation of the work itself, see what already exists with new eyes. The meaning of work is found in infusing new values into the spiritual realm of self-reflection beyond the material realm of the work.
As Kim In-gyeom said, “Drawing, expressing, and erasing are all expressions in painting.” Through Reflective Space: Void Towards The Realm of The Mind, a three-person exhibition by Kim In-gyeom, Kim Dong-hyeong, and Jung Min-hee, who look at existing things with new eyes and infuse new values into them, the hope is that you understand the work as much as you erase the ideological framework.

name: Ai Weiwei : Defend the Future
summary: Ai Weiwei's solo exhibition focusing on the themes of freedom of expression and world refugees.
description_html:
Explore the themes of freedom of expression and world refugees through Ai Weiwei: Defend the Future, the first individual exhibition in Korea within an art museum from world-renowned artist Ai Weiwei. The original name of the exhibition in Chinese combines the terms for "man" and "future that is better than the present". The aim of Ai Weiwei's works is to encourage visitors to live in a dignified way, enjoy life, and freely express joy and anger. Furthermore, these actions should be done for the benefit and happiness of all humanity beginning now and continuing to future generations. Visit Ai Weiwei's exhibition to learn more about his ideals and experiences.

name: Project Hashtag 2021
summary: An exhibition that leaves behind the traditional visually focused forms of art and experiments with new platforms and creations produced through collaboration amongst different mediums.
description_html:
Project Hashtag, hosted by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea and Hyundai Motors, is an exhibition that leaves behind the traditional visually focused forms of art and experiments with new platforms and creations produced through collaboration amongst different mediums. This is to show how, through the use of hashtags, random and unrelated texts and media can be woven into one common theme. Visitors can see the creations from the two selected teams at Project Hashtag 2021- After New Order... and The Duck Among Us. This exhibition focuses on the human experience of life on the internet and how humanity shapes the environment of the web. It also looks at the expansion and distortion of human values that occurs in virtual spaces and how it has changed since after the pandemic began.

name: Obsidian, roll over and over
summary: Shinhan Young Artist Festa writers Bae Soyoung and Song Da Seul's <Rolling Black Stone: Obsidian, roll over and over> exhibit.
description_html:
Shinhan Gallery will host "Rolling Black Stone: Obsidian, roll over and over" by artists Bae So Young and Song Da Seul, selected for the 2021-2022 Shinhan Young Artist Festa Group Contest which will run from November 10 to December 21. The exhibit begins with the creation of a space with different elemental properties. Bae So Young creates a "tropical forest where lava boils", while Song Da Seul makes a "glacial and arctic sea." The two artists gradually approach each other in the middle and show the energy, atmosphere, and byproducts created in the process of intertwining the two different elements through various forms of media in the exhibition hall.

The process of melting and solidifying each other when the heat and flowing lava of the rainforest meets the frigid cold and glaciers of the sea generates steam, creating a new substance, obsidian, in the smoke.The smooth surface of this black stone reflects external reality. Furthermore, the original heat it had becomes a five-colored energy that radiates from the inside.The black stone, which was born from the collision between lava and glaciers, cannot stay sedentary. From the desires and impulses in it, it rolls over and over again and becomes a new shape every time. Black stones record their journey by leaving traces behind them with their bodies. This journey ends when it is completely exhausted.

name: Flowers on the Border
summary: Neo Rauch & Rosa Loy's two-person exhibit
description_html: Flowers on the Border focuses on the two artists who pioneered the New Leipzig Style of painting in post-reunification Germany. Married couple and artists Neo Rauch and Rosa Loy have undoubtedly influenced each other's own works intentionally and unintentionally by serving as advisors and mentors to one another. In this exhibit, one can only notice the similarities and differences of the artist's imaginations and the fantastic atmosphere that presents various metaphors about human nature. Despite the couple sharing a similar cultural background and experiences, there is a difference between their perspectives and opinions on different subjects. Neo Rauch focuses on incidents and collects historical fragments which are then presented through mysterious themes and narratives in a surreal way, while Rosa Loy explores women's contemporary role in society structured within magical worlds such as fairy tales and fantasies. The exhibit's title, Flowers on the Border, represents exploration of the boundary between the two subjects. Boundaries always serve as a point of contention, uneasiness, and anxiety. However, they can also become dynamic, mixed, and anew.

summary: An exhibition that introduces various forms of art.
description_html: The 11th Seoul Media City Biennale focuses on themes of escape in today's mass media and invites 41 creators and teams from within Korea and abroad to introduce various forms of artistic content inside and outside of the exhibit. The exhibition, which opens at the Seosomun Main Building and stretches out to all over downtown Seoul, works to expand the concept of media through various works that experiment with a variety of perspectives and attitudes around the theme of "new relationships with escapism." This Biennale hopes to suggest a fresh perspective on the reality of escapism, and while self-reflecting, use these works as tools for navigation in the world experiencing a pandemic today.

name: Jane Jin Kaisen: Community of Parting
summary: Jane Jin Kaisen's Solo Exhibition focusing on the topics of history, memory, translation and migration.
description_html: Community of Parting is a solo exhibition by Jane Jin Kaisen, an artist who travels back and forth between Korea and Denmark, that focuses on the themes of history, memory, translation and migration. The exhibition introduces three recent works: a three-channel video installation, "Community of Parting," (2019), a six-piece light box installation, "At the Moon," (2020), and a two-channel video installation, " Braiding and Fixing" (2020). All of these works are based on the artist's hometown of Jeju, its natural environment, her years of research on Jeju shamanism, and the voices of oppressed and marginalized communities. The images and materials of historical events related to these topics are juxtaposed to provide multiple perspectives and multiple narratives.

Although these buildings are no longer in operation, the impact of these places is still felt to this day. This exhibition introduces and recalls the history of these landmarks as well as remembers those involved.

name: Heritage of Seoul's Traditional Crafts
summary: This exhibition tells the story of 25 artisans who have dedicated their lives to inheriting traditional techniques, spreading their skills and passing them on to future generations.
description_html: According to the "Gyeongguk Daejeon," a legal code from the Joseon Dynasty, there was always a craftsman who produced the best goods necessary for the royal family and the nation active in Seoul (Hanyang). During the Japanese colonial period and the industrialization period, the number of places available for craftsmen was greatly reduced, yet still today there are craftsmen in Seoul who carry out tradition and craftsmanship from the factories that historically produced the best products. This exhibition tells the story of 25 artisans who have dedicated their lives to inheriting traditional techniques, spreading their skills and passing them on to future generations.

description_html: From July 7 to October 31, the National Palace Museum of Korea is holding a special exhibition titled Hello Peony, which examines the culture of the Joseon Dynasty through peony flowers. 120 pieces of various relics featuring peony flowers, which were often depicted in various household items and ceremonial items such as screens, palace bowls, furniture, and clothes, will be unveiled at this exhibition. name: Gwangtonggyo: The Capital's Primary Bridge
summary: An exhibition on the  600-year long story of Gwangtonggyo Bridge, the first bridge in the city, which has maintained its place since the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html: Gwangtonggyo Bridge was constructed during the early Joseon Dynasty and became known as the "capital's primary bridge," located near the center of the city wall, connecting the palace and Namdaemun Gate. This exhibition presents a total of 80 documents and artifacts including maps, paintings, modern photographic materials, excavated relics, documents related to various restoration projects, reports, and drawings. The exhibition reflects on the way of life of people during the Joseon Dynasty and the evolution of the Gwangtonggyo Bridge starting from the Joseon Dynasty, through its restoration project in 2005, and how it stands today.

summary: Explore the significance of human existence and interactions between human beings and other living species in the evolutionary process.
description_html: Some say that we, who wandered around the meadows seven million years ago, have evolved into omnipotent beings comparable to gods. However, the recent global pandemic has shed light on just how helpless humans are in coping with natural disaster and the force of nature. This special exhibition seeks to portray homo sapiens in an unexaggerated way using various perspectives. An additional aim of this exhibition is to provide an opportunity for us to reflect on our relationship with the various species that have been stablished in the process of evolution and to look into our future.

name: Icons and Identities [from National Portrait Gallery]
summary: As 2021’s first large-scale special exhibition from overseas, seventy-eight masterpieces housed at the National Portrait Gallery, London will be introduced to the Korean public for the first time through this exhibition!
description_html: A portrait is both simple and multifaceted, and unfamiliar yet immediately engaging at the same time. Viewing a portrait involves a visual and mental dance between looking at an image and engaging with the person represented, because they reflect our own selves. This exhibition introduces you to the lives of seventy-six people and tells you stories on the genre of portrait.We live in an age in which images overpower words. Sometimes, just one image can tell everything about the person. Today's selfies and 16th century's portrait paintings share the same goal fundamentally. We would like for you to rediscover the tradition of 'presenting myself' through this exhibition.

name: Life Exhibition: The Last Print
summary: The organizers of the exhibition, "Life: The Last Print," have carefully selected 100 photos from the most touching moments of the 20th century.
description_html: The exhibition "Life: The Last Print" is based on the archives from "Life" magazine, which holds a vast collection of 10 million photos. The "Life" magazine was considered to be one of the most influential magazines in the world ever since it was first published in 1936. Photographers of the magazine captured precious moments from a very turbulent historic period during the pre-war and post-war eras. The organizers have carefully selected 100 photos of the most touching moments from the 20th century. Using these powerful images, "Life" magazine aroused people's curiosities, discussed the major issues of the time, and made both art and science approachable for the masses.

name: Andy Warhol: Beginning Seoul
summary: A special exhibition on the art of Andy Warhol, an icon of the pop art movement.
description_html: Andy Warhol: Beginning Seoul, is a large-scale exhibition hosted by Hyundai Seoul, featuring a wide spread of the works by the world-famous pop-art icon, Andy Warhol. This exhibition comes to Seoul after touring some of Italy's most popular museums, and while there have been other Warhol exhibitions that have been presented in Seoul before, this is the largest one to-date. The exhibition boasts over 150 works, including the infamous prints of Marilyn Monroe and the Campbell's Soup cans. There will also be private collections displayed at this exhibition along with various artifacts from Warhol's life, which will allow for a more in-depth and intimate study of Warhol and his art.

name: Day Travel
summary: This special exhibition, located at the Ttukseom Museum of Art, is influenced by the themes of "Travel" and "Environment."
description_html: This special exhibition, located at the Ttukseom Museum of Art, is influenced by the themes of "Travel" and "Environment." The exhibition was formed as a response to people's burning desire to travel during this past year of quarantine and sacrifice. Visitors can immerse themselves into this simulation-like experience, which recreates the feelings and emotions that come along with travelling to new places. The artwork on view features popular tourist destinations as well as interactive displays and props. Additionally, this exhibit brings forward the sad reality that many of the world's most beautiful destinations are quickly deteriorating due to environmental catastrophes caused by the current climate crisis. This unique exhibition, while indulging its guests to the world of travel, promotes the important message that travel can only be preserved when nature is also preserved.

name: A Climate Crisis Come
summary: An exhibition on the world's current climate crisis
description_html: The exhibition "A Climate Crisis Come," which can be translated as the "Arrival of Climate Crisis" at the Seoul Energy Dream Center is held with the goal of informing residents and visitors about how the climate has changed and how it affects our daily lives. The exhibition consists of three parts. In the first section of the exhibition, visitors will have a chance to learn about the impact of the climate crisis on humanity. Finally, in the last section of the exhibit, the organizers call for the fight against climate crisis. After the exhibition, all visitors can take part in various interactive and education programs offered by Seoul Energy Dream Center.

As a form of street art, graffiti is characteristic in demonstrating the energy and creative powers of younger generations. Event-goers will get a chance to witness magnificient installations that capture the street vibe and unique traits of the streets of South Bronx, NY, the home of graffiti. 


Considering the growing consumer demand for warm consolation and originality in the midst of the COVID pandemic, P/O/S/T is anticipated to provide an all new form of culture consumerism within this lifestyle space abundant with brand identity.

TeamLab's latest exhibition, Life, is an attempt to recreate life's beauty through a variety of bold and entrancing artworks that utilize the facilities and features of the Dongdaemun Design Plaza culture complex to the utmost. The dichotomies of nature's blessing and threatening force, alongside that of the benefits and risks of a growing civilization, are harmoniously intertwined with one another. There may not be any absolute evil to specifically pinpoint, yet there are some aspects of nature and civilization that are too cruel to simply succumb to and accept. This dynamic and overall sentiment is not something that can be understood or defined in a conventional way. However, people find a way to continue onward, which speaks to the beauty life itself.


As an interdisciplinary group having launched operations in 2001, TeamLab seeks out common ground between art and science & technology through mass creative projects and activities. The group is comprised of several field specialists from artists and programmers to engineers, CG animators, mathematicians, designers, and more, while searching for a new dynamic existing between humans, nature, and the world we live in through art. People naturally create boundaries between the world they live in and experience and the world as it is, leading to a false awareness that depicts everything to be separate from one another and therefore we place ourselves at a distance from everything. And TeamLab works to find a way to go beyond that level of awareness, the boundaries created between ourselves and the world, as well as the awareness that time is simply continuous to ultimately convey that we all miraculously exist by a thread within a connectivity of life free of time-defined boundaries.

name: Meak: Soul, Elements & Sound
summary: Meak: Soul, Elements & Sound is currently open for viewing at Gallery Kuzo.
description_html:
The three veteran artists featured during this exhibition, Suk Chuljoo, Kwon Daesup, and Lim Dongchang, cover three primary themes of modern art in this day and age: conversation, "objet" (an object meant for viewing that holds aesthetic value), and music. They are able to accomplish this through conducting their own expansive creative process while simultaneously carrying on the aesthetic elements of Korean tradition. The aim of this project was to pose the question of "What are we made of?" This question refrains from being entrapped within the confines of aesthetic constructs created in line with ideologies of western culture.

* Lim Dongchang: Formulates his very own world of music that covers a vast, sweeping spectrum by deconstructing the boundaries set between east & west and the traditional & modern musical art forms

name: 2021 CRE8TIVE REPORT
summary: A beautiful exhibition featuring new works from the eight resident artists of the OCI Museum.
description_html:
Currently being held at the OCI Museum, the 2021 CRE8TIVE REPORT features newly-released works from resident artists of the museum's Creative Studio. The featured artists, including GR1, Kim Minho, Kim Jeongeun, Son Seungbeom, Lee Hoeok, Jeon Juyeon, Jeong Cheolgyu, and Cheon Changhwan, were very carefully selected during an open recruitment. For the last year, they have been actively at work while taking residency at the Creative Studio located in Hagik-dong of Incheon since April 2020. The exhibition has as many as 60 works on display that are being released for the first time ever.


The studio operates a variety of events and programming apart from providing creative space for the artists. Some of which include a resident artist workshop that allows each artist to discuss their projects in depth with one another; an art critic pairing program that matches a resident artist with an art critic to help better develop the level of artistry; a visiting artist program that invites a currently active, more experienced artist to act as a mentor and talk over potential directions to take a certain project; as well as a virtual open studio. This helps encourage the creative process and promote a better exchange between the artists.


All of the artists came together in one mind and body to make this exhibition happen despite the struggling art world amid the pandemic. Built upon the originality and methodic detail of each artist, it is hoped that the 2021 CRE8TIVE REPORT is able to promote a greater awareness of the creative process of each artist.

name: 2021 Delight Seoul
summary: An immersive media art exhibition that puts a spin on the image of Seoul!
description_html:
2021 Delight Seoul is the first exhibition of its kind that implements Korea's immersive, media art experience centered around the theme of Seoul, and it's scheduled to run until October 25 of this year at the Insa Central Museum. The creator behind this exhibition, Design Silver Fish, presents its immersive content in line with the topic of "the dynamic transformation of Seoul," a city that stands out as the beating heart of K-Culture itself! And Design Silver Fish being able to ground the content of this exhibition in it's internationally-recognized skillset in planning and technology is what made this all possible. 


2021 Delight Seoul features artists from a variety of fields that are currently active in purely media-based exhibitions centered around Seoul. The exhibition's aesthetic utilizes several kinds of media that captures the culture and daily life of Seoul. There are total of 11 different themes ranging from images capturing Seoul's potential to welcoming exhibits that enable viewers to experience the retro trend of the city, street scenes that emanate the energy of Hangul embedded within the soul of Koreans and their everyday lives, metaphorical exhibits, and much more! This exhibition allows you to discover something new within the familiar in a space that rearranges what you already know in a way that feels different. The barcode technology incorporated in each themed exhibit allows for a distanced yet interactive experience that is sure to stimulate your senses while sparking an imagination that blurs the line between the past and the future.

name: 2021 Doosan Art Lab
summary: An exhibition featuring five new artists selected by the Doosan Art Center
description_html:
The Doosan Gallery at the Doosan Art Center opens this year's very first exhibition, 2021 Doosan Art Lab, from January 13 (Wednesday) to February 20 (Saturday), 2021. The exhibition serves as a program of the art center that has been around since 2010 to help discover and support new and rising artists in the art and performance industry. From this year, the exhibition was decided to be held on a yearly basis, rather than biennially as it had been previously, while the five artists, all under the age of 35, were selected for this year's event through an open contest. The Doosan Art Lab features a variety of different works, from paintings and pictures to installations and more, from the premiering artists that include Kim Se-eun, Park Jeong-hye, Oh Yeon-jin, Oh Hui-won, and Lee Jun-ah.


Rather than basing the selection on a particular form of media or subject matter, the Doosan Art Lab contest based its selection on artists that were determined to invoke an interest in their creative world while also being worth observing for a prolonged period of time. The final five artists that were selected are all women with the work of each artist sharing the commonality of having worked on a flat surface of their choice, be it painting, photography, prints, or any of similar 2D art form. The exhibition was created in a such a way so as to discover and get a feel for the common areas between each artist, as well as the specific traits they each have. 


The 2021 Doosan Art Lab is anticipated to set the stage for expo-goers to enjoy the various and intriguiing approaches of each artist despite their similiarity in age.

name: Yudam Solo Exhibition: What I Felt
summary: A solo exhibition of the artist, Yudam, opening at the Like Thiz Gallery.
description_html: From January 5 to February 19, 2021, the Like Thiz Gallery presents "What I Felt," or "간직해온 마음들,  a special solo exhibition from the artist, Yudam. A native to Korea utilizing the art form of digital drawing to illustrate works of landscape, Yudam incorporates emotions she had felt and wishes to feel in her artwork. Her work is grounded in actual memories of hers, as well as things she has seen, and creates something reminiscent of the emotions and ambiance she experienced at those exact moments. Her style primarily gives off a comfortable and balanced feel that emanates a quaint, peaceful vibe from a flat, landscape angle. Some of her other works, however, take on a more aerial view from above to accentuate a more wide, sweeping overlook that portrays a sense of depth. Another facet of her work is that she relies heavily on using colors from the blue spectrum, of which she then skillfully manipulates the lightness and saturation according to the theme of the work or the current season, to convey an array of various tones and emotions from warmth and cold, to sadness, melancholiness, happiness and more. This exhibition provides the opportunity for visitors to reflect on their own experiences and memories as they peer into the openness of personal moments from her life out on display.

name: Ocragela: Sustainable Design
summary: A design exhibition of the artist, Chae Soowon, opening at the Eyelove Art Center in Gangnam.
description_html:
The artist, Chae Soowon, launched this exhibition with the hope of bringing about a reflection on human behavior toward the environment, while also demonstrating the possibilities for a sustainable tomorrow using more traditional materials from days passed. Focusing on the use of four ingredients, including red clay, gelatin, glycerin, and water, Chae illuminates upon the process of creating new, eco-friendly materials that are both sustainable and ecological and becoming more familiar with their possibilities and future application. This project, in essence, partly pays hommage to the "wiser ways" of ancient civilizations that were able to survive within nature by extracting a number of functions and possibilities for application from red clay. It's part of an effort to invoke a sense of curiosity and creativity through a repitition of spontaneity and planning using as few materials as possible.


The countless process of trial and error helped enable the ability to better manipulte thickness and flexibility, as well as color and texture, by constantly adjusting the different variations of the temperature, ratio, and production of materials. After creating a variety of samples, Chae was able to offer new solutions in material development that are both realistically feasible and applicable in the present day. For one of the ingredients, gelatin, Chae contacted a company called Estonia, a gelatin specialist, to collaborate and share on any findings within their respective research, which led to the exhibition here today. 


All expo-goers are free to sample the various materials that Chae created through a series of trail and error during the research.

name: Shooting the Pulitzer
summary: Welcome to the Shooting the Pulitzer exhibition featuring Pulitzer prize-winning photography!
description_html:
The encore edition of the Shooting the Pulitzer exhibition presents the opportunity for visitors to awe at the Pulitzer Prize-winning photography from 1942 up through 2020. The exhibition drew significant attention among expo-goers for putting the work of 2019 Pulitzer Prize winner and Reuter photographer, Kim Kyung-hoon, on public display and his achievement for becoming the first Korean ever to win the prize. Kim covered the story of the migrating caravans on route toward the United States' border from Latin America and captured amazing footage of the phenomenon in progress, including one of a mother and daughter, native to the country of Honduras, trying to escape the incoming tear gas being released into the migrating crowd at the U.S. border. The exhibition has as many as 130 photos on display that also feature an accompanying excerpt from interviews with the photographer of each picture. It's as if visitors are able to witness a history textbook come to life before their eyes! Actual interview footage is also on display in the exhibition hall.


Shooting the Pulitzer is scheduled to run through February 28, 2021, in Seocho-dong's Seoul Arts Center.

name: On Guard in Hanyang
summary: An exhibition shedding light upon the Samgunyeong military base during the Joseon Dynasty and a particular family who had served for generations as officers.
description_html: "On Guard in Hanyang" sheds light on Samgunyeong by observing Lee Ji-geon, who was a yangban (an aristocrat) in Yeongsan, Gyeongsang-do (today’s Yeongsan-myeon, Changnyeong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do), and his family. Samgunyeong is a central military base formed while retrofitting a city wall system in the late Joseon period. Soldiers in Samgunyeong were stationed in Hanyang and played a key role in guarding the king, protecting palaces, defending the city wall, and maintaining public security. The family register documents and commands that Lee's family left behind show not just their duties but also small stories like passing the national exam or house ownership. This exhibition is an opportunity for visitors to look into the lively city of Hanyang in the late Joseon period and the lives of soldiers who played their part.

name: The Abstract with Mr. Kandinsky
summary: This exhibition enables today's younger generations to have a visceral, sensory experience.
description_html:
Following the success of the "Mr. Kandinsky and the Psychology of Color in Yeonnam-dong" exhibition at Yeonnam-dong's 19.8 Art Gallery, The Abstract with Mr. Kandinsky began from November 14 as a tailored program for children. Simply walk out of exit 3 of Hongdae University Station and follow along the Gyeongui Line Forest Park area and you're sure to run into not only his artwork, but also the different embodiments of his life, world, and philosophy. If you stop by to explore just why the reviews of the exhibition describe it as being "refreshing" and "useful," you'll find an impressive and unique line-up of docents at the ready that go on to include a musical actor, professor, young artists, designers, and other specialists in each field. They help provide commentary on his works through their perspective and collectively work to provide a comprehensive take on the exhibit.


Kandinsky is a native artist of Russia and art theorist that is most often described as being the "Father of Abstract," and is known to stand among the main artists of the 20th century, alongside Picasso, Matisse, and more.

If you stop by to explore just why the reviews of the exhibition describe it as being "refreshing" and "useful," you'll find an impressive and unique line-up of docents at the ready that go on to include a musical actor, professor, young artists, designers, and other specialists in each field. They help provide commentary on his works through their perspective and collectively work to provide a comprehensive take on the exhibit. Kandinsky is a native artist of Russia and art theorist that is most often described as being the "Father of Abstract," and is known to stand among the main artists of the 20th century, alongside Picasso, Matisse, and more.

name: Day Travel
summary: Ttukseom Art Museum's all new exhibition, showcasing new ways to enjoy traveling in a time when the idea of traveling has become so unfamiliar.
description_html:
The number of daily travelers passing through Incheon Airport saw a drastic decrease from an average of 230,000 to 7,000 travelers, the equivalent of 1/30th the number from last year. It's hard enough to carry out simple conversations on a daily basis with our masks on, let alone think about trying to travel abroad, but this year's Day Travel exhibition is here to provide a little bit of respite from the these difficult times. 


Rather than maintaining the traditional vibe of an art gallery, the Day Travel exhibition seeks to provide an ambiance similar to that of an airport interior that seemingly boards expo-goers on a plane before "arriving" in the departure terminal where people can enjoy the feeling and excitement as if ready to embark on a distant travel abroad.


Once everyone has "disembarked," they will have arrived at a gallery area featuring the works of artists that captures their impressions of personal travels and daily life, while sharing their experiences traveling so as to remind visitors of the intrinsic value of traveling and provide a sense of consolation for those nostalgic for the days heading out on an adventure abroard.


The exhibition offers yet another message to its visitors, besides simply portraying the theme of traveling. And that message has to do with the environment. Perhaps we are stuck in quarantine within our homes and country borders due to the pandemic, but we might see a day when the idea of travelers themselves might become a thing of the past amid worsening environmental pollution. The exhibits on display offer the opportunity to think over and put into practice the issues and solutions concerning the environment, while participating environment organizations will be operating a campaign in tandem with the exhibition to ensure the environmental protection of travel destinations.


It is hoped that Day Travel will serve as a meaningful opportunity to partake in activity to protect these areas of travel. Feel free to stop by and make an adventure of the exhibition and all the wonderful content and themes on display! 


All visitors are required to scan their QR code or sign an attendance sheet upon entry at the information desk so as to ensure the observance of proper safety procedure. The number of visitors allowed into the exhibition at any given time is limited to 40, and it is asked that everyone maintain their distance from one another while enjoying the exhibition.

name: Breath of Earth
summary: A special exhibition featured at the Choi Manlin Museum of Art in the Seongbuk area of Seoul.
description_html: The Choi Manlin Museum of Art in the Seongbuk area of Seoul, located in the neighborhood of Jeongneung, was once the residence of the sculptor, Choi Manlin (b. 1935), for over the 30 years where he had worked on his artistry. This exhibition is the first of its kind in this particular location. Breath of Earth is a dedication to Korea's signature abstract sculptor and his source of inspiration to the art of Korean abstract sculpturing that all began from the early 1960s up through the present time. Visitors can experience Choi's artistic motivation first hand that was deeply rooted in an interest in living things and an exploration into the source of Korean sculpturing. This motivation of his lasted throughout his entire life and can be observed in each of his works on display, all of which were created using the very earth beneath our feet.

name: The Radio Our Family Listened To - 1978
summary: This exhibition features the radio-listening culture at its height during the 1970s having recaptured the interior of a family residence in Mia-dong.
description_html:
※ The exhibition is currently closed due to the recent rise in COVID-19 cases.


The Radio Our Family Listened To - 1978 is a splendid exhibition that takes expo-goers back to the time in the 1970s when the culture of radio listening was at its height. The exhibition features a recreation of the times designed around the idea of a typical family residence interior. You can even get a taste of what it was like by having a listen to one of the hit programs at the time, "Night Owl Radio," led by the once popular DJ, Hwang In-yong. Families and friends are encouraged to come visit and hear Seoul as it was in the 1978, amid the myriad of sites and sounds, including the beginnings and history of radio in Korea, the display of nearly 120 different artifacts related to radio broadcasting at the time, a children's photo zone and hands-on area.

name: Between Dreamy and Dreary
summary: Between Dreamy and Dreary is an exhibition that aims to introduce the varied research of the sentiment tied to mainstream futuristic science, especially that of databases for emotion analysis. At 6 p.m. on August 22, Owen Wells and Soomi Park are scheduled to conduct a live-stream of their lecture at the Eye Love Art Hall of the Eye Love Art Center, where the Céline Park Gallery is located.
description_html: Currently active as overseas designers in England, Soomi Park and Owen Wells respectively conduct lectures at the London College of Communication (LCC) at both the Goldsmiths, University of London, and the University of the Arts London. Their collective work, Between Dreamy and Dreary, has been showcased via a number of exhibitions and mediums, including the Design Museum in London and the Victoria and Albert Museum, as well as in the New York Times and Vogue Magazine. The work focuses upon the cultural, political, and ethical issues that arise from technological development using "design" as the artistic medium. The exhibition ultimately offers the opportunity to view societal issues through a different light, while providing a time to reflect on the current times, be it from an either utopian or dystopian perspective.

name: Rise Up Rim Dong Sik
summary: The Seoul Museum of Art opened the Rise Up Rim Dong Sik exhibition from August 19, 2020, on the 1st floor exhibition hall of the Seosomun Main Building.
description_html:
Rise Up Rim Dong Sik is an exhibition solely featuring the nature artist, Rim Dong Sik (b. 1945), who illustrates the artistic world grounded in an intense love affair with nature itself.


Since 2018, Rim has donated collective art resources to the Culture HQ in Seoul over the course of four stages so as to contribute to the Seoul Museum of Art Archives, scheduled to open by December of 2021. In collaboration with the Culture HQ, the Seoul Museum of Art looks to put the artistic works of artists ranging from the 1970s up through the 2000s up on display to reevaluate the said artists as artists that function as lifelong performers and meticulous archivists from a comprehensive perspective that unifies nature, life, and the arts.

name: This Event
summary: The Seoul Museum of Art opened the This Event exhibition from August 12, 2020, on the 2nd and 3rd floor exhibition halls of the Seosomun Main Building.
description_html: The This Event exhibition was created with the purpose of exploring the various attempts and methods of communication of visual artistry embedded within set performances through a multi-layering of unique characteristics. This idea runs in connection with an explorative search portrayed through the exhibition of artistry that is largely finite. Amid the stumbling about for a way for society to continue onward while avoiding unnecessary face-to-face contact during the widespread pandemic, we are faced with the task of responding to such circumstances that would allow us to capture the same value rewarded to live audiences by way of an exhibition. This exhibition includes an exploration into the genre of art performance, the method in which abstract artistry can be reinterpreted into an exhibition, and the different ways in which performances can be enjoyed during the current state. Ultimately, the goal is to overcome the limitations of time and perhaps even recategorize the identity of a performance so as to suggest various alternatives through which performances during such pressing times can be understood and enjoyed.

name: Goods For You
summary: D Project Space opens its inaugural exhibition since relocating to Gwanghwamun
description_html:
• * Relocated to Gwanghwamun to further spread the vision of D Project Space throughout various fields and generations

  • * Transformed into a cultural leisure space downtown for office workers to find some respite from everyday life

  • * Offers a new lifestyle experience through various works and goods from 12 artist teams dealing with numerous art genres that include illustrations, graphic design, art installations, and more


Operating as the inaugural exhibition since D Project Space relocated to Gwanghwamun, Goods For You will run during the entirety of the month of July as a part of the Daelim Cultural Foundation's "Goods" series. Having launched with the successful run of the 2019 special exhibition, Goods is Good, this series depicts the general climate where the culture of "goods" can be freely experienced without being restricted by time or place through the use of a newly-conceptualized, collaborative platform that covers lifestyle trends centered around goods, or product culture. This exhibition employs a comprehensive reinterpretation of lifestyle by utilizing spatial design and different products while focusing on familial and/or social events that create a stronger bond between people. The young, domestic artists with their work on display here are among the most popular in the art community, and are active in a number of art forms, including illustration, graphic design, and art installations. The exhibition especially works to capture the transient moments, both big and small, of our lives where we express such sentiment as congratulations, gratitude, and consolation with those that are closest to us through a singular space, similar to that of a home. This enables the artwork and intended message behind each piece to be naturally conveyed through the familiar objects that comprise our homes, be it furniture, fabrics, or lighting.

name: My Name is Green
summary: A wondrous green-themed special exhibition
description_html:
* Featuring Kim Won-jung, Choi Sun-nyung, Kim Bong, and Kim Ji-soo
* Also featuring the audience-participatory program, "Hey Cactus. You Know What? It's a Secret," by Project C in collaboration w/ Ku So-yung

The color green generally signifies positivity. Some feel a sense of calmness from the color, while others associate it with vitality and recovery. In the meantime, we all live our lives experiencing a vast range of sensations. The ability to see, hear, and touch also serves as a marker that immediately awakens us to the fact that we are alive and existing in each and every single moment of our lives.

The exhibition was created so as to enable audience viewing and participation having adorned the white walls of the exhibition room in green to conjure up the motif of a "forest that awakens the senses," while also utilizing various sensations. Artists participating in the exhibition all work to formulate a reenactment of the color green through their own artistic voice and use the color to rationalize or express their view of the world. Also, the artists, at times, try to draw attention to the color as a entity that can communicate.

Sometimes we grow numb to our value as beings in existence the moment we become accustomed to our actual being and regard it as nothing more than a matter of fact. This exhibition offers a connection of the senses, from that which is visual to that which is aural, olfactoral, and more. It also functions as both an attempt to feel the calmness and recovery power of the color green and a recollection of a memory of having already experienced those sensations once before.

name: Monet to Cezanne
summary: An exhibition featuring the masterpieces of impressionists and post-impressionists of the Israel Museum in Jerusalem.
description_html:
Monet to Cezanne: An exhibition of masterpieces from impressionists and post-impressionists of the Israel Museum in Jerusalem


Rather than featuring the collected artworks of Europe-based galleries that have been accessible in Korea, the Monet to Cezanne exhibition distinguishes itself with its carefully-selected curation from the globally-renowned Israel Museum, located in Jerusalem. From a non-European viewpoint, their collection offers some insight into the kind of impact of impressionist artwork and artists, a movement centered in France during the late 19th century, had on modern art.


Culture & I Leaders had initially held the exhibition this past January 17, however, they decided to reopen the exhibition for those that missed out on the January opening due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The exhibition is set to run from June 20 to August 30 at the Hangaram Art Museum on the second floor of the Seoul Arts Center. There are a total of 106 pieces of artwork set to be on display, all of which were carefully hand-selected from the globally-renowned Israel Museum's collection, located in Jerusalem.


With the rise of the plein-air, or open-air, painting trend among the Barbizon school of painters, the exhibition aims to explore the genre from the birth and maturing of the impressionist movement up through the post-impressionist era through five distinct themes - waterscape and reflections, nature and landscapes, cityscapes, portraits, and still life. In particular, among Water Lilies: Green Reflections, a renowned collective artwork of one of the founders of impressionism, Claude Monet, the piece titled, Pond with Water Lilies [1907], will be featured for the first time domestically, alongside other formative artworks of other impressionist and post-impressionist artists, including Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Paul Gauguin, and Paul Cezanne.

From a non-European viewpoint, their collection offers some insight into the kind of impact of impressionist artwork and artists, a movement centered in France during the late 19th century, had on modern art. Culture & I Leaders had initially held the exhibition this past January 17, however, they decided to reopen the exhibition for those that missed out on the January opening due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The exhibition is set to run from June 20 to August 30 at the Hangaram Art Museum on the second floor of the Seoul Arts Center. There are a total of 106 pieces of artwork set to be on display, all of which were carefully hand-selected from the globally-renowned Israel Museum's collection, located in Jerusalem. With the rise of the plein-air, or open-air, painting trend among the Barbizon school of painters, the exhibition aims to explore the genre from the birth and maturing of the impressionist movement up through the post-impressionist era through five distinct themes - waterscape and reflections, nature and landscapes, cityscapes, portraits, and still life. In particular, among Water Lilies: Green Reflections, a renowned collective artwork of one of the founders of impressionism, Claude Monet, the piece titled, Pond with Water Lilies [1907], will be featured for the first time domestically, alongside other formative artworks of other impressionist and post-impressionist artists, including Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Paul Gauguin, and Paul Cezanne.

name: Little China Town
summary: The Chinatown centered around the Chinese Embassy located in Myeongdong.
description_html: Little China Town, the Chinatown in Myeongdong, centers around the Chinese Embassy and has been home to Chinese cuisine restaurants, Chinese elementary schools, and Chinese culture for over 100 years. It is considered the oldest Chinatown in South Korea. The Seoul Overseas Chinese School, located next to the Seoul Central Post Office, has been there since 1909, along with some imported bookstores, Chinese food specialty stores, Chinese product specialty stores, and currency exchange shops. The Hansung Chinese Association handles various tasks such as issuing and processing documents for the Chinese community. This Chinatown developed naturally and is not managed comprehensively. It is one of the places where you can feel an exotic atmosphere in the city.

description_html: Jeong-dong Observatory is located on the 13th floor of the Seosomun Building at Seoul City Hall. Photos depicting the old appearance of Jeongdong are displayed on the cafe walls, allowing visitors to appreciate the historical aspect of the area. There are bar tables by the windows, providing a perfect spot to admire the stunning view while spending time, and there are also group seats, making it ideal for visiting with friends or colleagues. On clear days, you can see Gwanghwamun and the Blue House from the window seats, which are always popular. The cafe at the observatory offers not only coffee but also a variety of drinks like aids and teas at relatively affordable prices, making it a popular spot for many visitors.

name: Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education Namsan Library
summary: Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library
description_html:
Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library, originally opened in 1922 as the Gyeongseong Municipal Library in Myeong-dong. Situated in the heart of Namsan, the current building was constructed in 1965 following a public design competition. It has since been recognized as a Seoul Future Heritage building. The library boasts a collection of invaluable resources, including three volumes designated as Seoul City Tangible Cultural Properties and 227 volumes of 30 registered cultural properties.

With a collection of around 500,000 books, 16,000 non-book materials, and 800 serial publications, Namsan Public Library is committed to preserving and sharing knowledge. In collaboration with the National Library of Korea, it has created a digital archive of rare and valuable materials, including ancient books and East Asian texts. Additionally, the library serves as a specialized resource center for Seoul's residents, offering various programs designed to enrich their cultural and intellectual lives.

name: Changsin-Sungin Quarry Observatory
summary: In the era of Japanese colonial rule, the Changsin-dong quarry was active, and atop its peak lies an observation deck, offering breathtaking night views.
description_html:
The quarry observatory is built atop the summit of Changsin-dong quarry, providing a panoramic view of the city and natural landscapes at a glance.


During the Japanese colonial period, a quarry was located in Naksan, Changsin-dong, to supply stone for the exterior of large buildings such as the Government-General of Korea, the old Seoul Station, and the Bank of Korea. After the Korean War, the quarry's use was discontinued, but the quarry observatory was located where immigrants and refugees settled to form a village.


From the quarry observatory, with nothing obstructing the view, you can enjoy the skyline of Seoul at a glance. The second floor houses a coffee shop (Café Nakta), and the third floor features an outdoor observation deck, allowing you to appreciate the scenery of Seoul's cityscape and nature from any vantage point. Especially renowned is the breathtaking view that unfolds alongside the sunset. 


Enjoy the best panoramic view, a reasonably priced cup of coffee, and homemade ggangjeong and Nakta rice cakes. Small music concerts featuring historical and cultural stories, exhibitions, and live guitar performances are held occasionally.

name: Changsin-dong's Cliff Village
summary: A village built around a rock cliff used as Korea's only quarry
description_html:
Changsin-dong Cliff Village, located in Changsin 1, 2, and 3-dong in Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, has undergone various transformations over the years. It was a quarry village in the 1960s, a wooden village in the 1970s, a sewing factory in the 1990s, and finally a sewing village in the 2000s. It is situated around the rocky cliffs once used as the nation's only quarry. Changsin-dong Cliff Village is divided into densely packed, dilapidated, aged homes built on cliffs and precipices and homes formed beneath rocky hills.


*Please Note: When visiting, please refrain from making excessive noise, as actual residents live there.

name: Insadong
summary: Nowhere exudes more local and traditional charm than Insa-dong, a quaint neighborhood in the center of Seoul
description_html:
Nowhere exudes more local and traditional charm than Insa-dong, a quaint neighborhood in the center of Seoul that transports visitors back to a time when women wore hanbok and men rode horses. With its wooden tea houses, boutique galleries and street vendors selling traditional snacks, a stroll through Insa-dong is mandatory for all visitors, especially on Sundays when the streets become traffic free and come alive with street performances, buskers and throngs of young and old who have come to experience one of Seoul’s most fascinating and creative neighborhoods. While the entertainment here is free, Insa-dong is also one of the best places in Seoul to purchase traditional Korean art, products, and other souvenirs, as it is filled with antique shops, art galleries, traditional stationery shops, handicraft shops, pottery and porcelain shops, bookstores, and art supply stores. Insa-dong is also home to many traditional restaurants and tea houses.

name: Hongdae
summary: Lit up by neon signs that buzz late into the night, evenings in Seoul have a creative energy that sucks people in crowds.
description_html:
Hongdae is the scene where Korean culture, both pop and indie, manifests, especially at night. More information on planning a Sangam day trip can be soon found at K-stars and their K-style if the Korean Wave has washed over you, then there’s no better place to tread the path of such tastemakers as Hongdae, the live-wire district of music and art culture. Whether you’ve come on your own or with equally eager friends, the ever-trending university area remains the only place in Seoul where you can transitionfrom daytime exploring to nighttime adventures just as easily as you shuffle through your K-Pop playlist.


Shopping in Hongdae

Across the street and around the corner is a three-story store aptly named Around the Corner, Its multi-designer displays only cover two floors, but the smaller selection gives customers room to consider the subtler hip-hop motifs and mixed prints that punctuate the street wear-filled racks. Remember, just because Hongdae is more casual and “free” than, say, Gangnam or Apgujeong, doesn’t mean fashion doesn’t matter. The vibe you can see from the stores and the people on the streets, is effortless withan edge of the true Hongdae touch. You can see more of that in the quintessential Hongdae institution Aland, and the up-and-coming company Understar.

The name "Samcheong" is derived from the words "sam" meaning “three", and "cheong" meaning "fresh" or "pure", because the mountain, water and the heart of the people in this area are all very fresh and pure. name: Itaewon
summary: Located smack-dab in the center of Seoul, Itaewon is home for the majority of expats that reside in Korea, making Itaewon a mini melting pot of cultures and religions from all over the world.
description_html:
Korea is one of the most ethnically homogeneous countries in the world, but you'd never know that walking down the streets of Itaewon. Located smack-dab in the center of Seoul, Itaewon is home for the majority of expats that reside in Korea, making Itaewon a mini melting pot of cultures and religions from all over the world. The Seoul Central Mosque is also located in Itaewon along with a number of halal food stores, and large numbers of US military personnel can be seen here as the Yongsan Garrison that is stationed nearby. Due to the area’s diverse inhabitants, Itaewon has become one of the most cosmopolitan areas in Seoul boasting restaurants, shopping and nightlife that are equally diverse and cater to international tastes, attracting many other foreigners and tourists. It is safe to say that Itaewon is almost better known by foreigners and non-Korean residents than Koreans. 


Itaewon is known as the place to go when you want to get your foreign food fix. Restaurants featuring cuisine from all over the world can be found here including Indian, Thai, Pakistani, Greek, German, French, Italian, Australian, English, American, and Mexican, cuisines which are not easily found in Korea.  Itaewon is also famous for its nightlife. Among foreigners, it is often considered the most popular area  of Seoul for bars and clubs other than Hongdae. A range of drinking establishments can be found here including pubs, wine bars, hip-hop clubs, salsa clubs, lounges and cafes. 


Most stores in Korea offer clothing that fit Asian builds well but are unfortunately too small to fit those with “Western builds”. This leaves many of those with bigger and taller builds struggling to find clothing that fit. Fortunately many of the stores in Itaewon offer imported clothing in sizes that are difficult to find elsewhere in Korea. And if you still can’t find what you want, experienced tailors can create customized clothing. Itaewon also specializes in leather and fur goods, luggage and handbags, as well as jewelry and antique furniture. Trinkets and souvenirs can also be found here.


Itaewon boasts some 100 antique stores clustered together on a single street. Originally these stores only dealt with second-hand U.S. Army furniture, but nowadays the selections at the stores have expanded to include antique furniture from around the world.

Every October, the 'Itaewon Global Village Festival' is held on the streets of Itaewon. The Itaewon Global Village Festival is Seoul's main global street culture festival where people from all over the world gather and can enjoy unique and various cultures.

name: National Jeongdong Theater Cecil
summary: The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, operates a 232-seat performance hall.
description_html: The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, is a historic performance hall in Jung-gu, Seoul. Originally opened in 1976 as Cecil Theater, it’s a small yet iconic venue with a capacity of 232 seats. During the late 1970s, it became the heart of Korea's theater scene, hosting the Korea Theater Festival from 1977 to 1980. Despite its prominence, financial difficulties led to its closure in 2018 after being operated by private theater groups 'Madan' and 'Rodem.' In April 2018, the Seoul Metropolitan Government spearheaded a cultural regeneration project to reopen Cecil Theater and handed its management to a non-profit organization. Designed by renowned architect Kim Joong-up, the theater has long been a cornerstone of Korean performing arts and cultural heritage. In 2022, the theater was revitalized under the management of the National Jeongdong Theater, taking on the new name 'National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil.' Today, it serves as a vibrant space for artists and audiences to connect through innovative and experimental performances, upholding its legacy and creative core values.

name: Seoul Namsan Gugakdang
summary: Situated in the Namsangol Hanok Village, Seoul Namsan Gugakdang, which opened in 2007, is a traditional Korean music venue on three levels, two of them below ground.
description_html:
Situated in the Namsangol Hanok Village, Seoul Namsan Gugakdang, which opened in 2007, is a traditional Korean music venue on three levels, two of them below ground. In addition to the 330-seat main auditorium, the venue also features a traditional music experience chamber, a practice room and a food court. The main performance space on the first basement level is the only music venue in Korea equipped with a specially-designed solid wood interior which does not absorb sound, allowing the audience to experience natural unamplified acoustics. The wide repertoire features different recitals every day from a variety of traditional music genres, and the venue also runs free experience programs including a traditional tea tasting event and traditional painting classes.

Its location in a hanok (traditional Korean house) makes Seoul Namsan Gugakdang the perfect venue for traditional Korean music, equally suited to both the grandeur of royal court music and to pansori, a genre of traditional Korean music which is performed with the participation of the audience. Since it opened in 2007, Seoul Namsan Gugakdang has hosted a number of traditional Korean events designated as Intangible Cultural Heritages, and the leading figures of traditional Korean music have also performed here. There is also a special program of events for newcomers to traditional Korean music.

name: HiKR Ground
summary: A multi-cultural complex to enjoy Korean Wave culture
description_html:
Located in Euljiro, HiKR Ground is a multi-cultural complex that brings together everything about globally popular K-content. The name "HiKR Ground" carries the meaning of “a warm greeting (Hi) from Korea (KR)” and “a playground for global travelers.”

On the 1st floor is "HiKR Wall," a large media wall exhibition space centered on Korean cultural tourism. The 2nd floor is "K-POP Ground," where visitors can experience live studios and music video sets and become the main characters of Hallyu content. The 3rd floor features "HiKR Atrium," a special K-art exhibition hall. The 4th floor includes "HiKR Cave," where you can experience Korea's major tourist attractions with all five senses, and the "Festival Experience Center" introducing local festivals.

The 5th floor includes the "HiKR Lounge" with a view of Cheonggyecheon and a "Tourist Information Center." HiKR Ground also offers various regular programs that can be reserved through the official website.

name: Big Issue Korea
summary: The magazine Big Issue aims to create a society where no one has to experience homelessness, and everyone is guaranteed the right to appropriate housing
description_html: Big Issue Korea is a non-profit social enterprise that publishes a magazine that develops solutions to help homeless, marginalized, and disadvantaged people positively transform their lives. The company operates to support the independence of the homeless, a housing-vulnerable group. If you walk around the streets of Seoul, you may often encounter homeless individuals selling Big Issue magazines. Through these sales, they earn a legitimate income to sustain their lives. Big Issue is currently published in countries such as the UK, Australia, South Africa, Japan, Taiwan, and Korea, and it has significantly impacted many lives since its establishment. The organization is now developing new projects to expand job opportunities for homeless women and disabled individuals. Additionally, as part of its mission expansion, Big Issue is involved in publishing, printing, design, and public relations businesses.

name: Supsok Hanbang Land
summary: A charcoal kiln Jjimjilbang (Korean Spa) located in Sinchon, the heart of the city
description_html: This charcoal kiln, jjimjilbang (Korean spa) in Sinchon, is popular throughout the year. Featured in numerous Korean dramas and media, it attracts foreigners eager to experience jjimjilbang culture. Visitors can enjoy traditional snacks like sikhye (sweet rice punch), eggs, roasted rice cakes, and sweet potatoes cooked in the charcoal kiln. The facility includes Gamagol Charcoal Grill, which offers grilled pork belly, and Gamagol Korean Restaurant, which serves traditional Korean dishes perfect for a post-sauna meal. Additionally, it boasts a playroom for children, gaming consoles, a nail art station, and a sky garden for diverse entertainment options. A unique aspect of this jjimjilbang is the hearth room, where heated charcoal is placed in a brazier, providing direct warmth to guests.

description_html:

name: Graphic
summary: A Giant Alley Decor, Graphic
description_html: The building is in the shape of white cylinders stacked in layers with some cut-out sections, alomost like a multi-tiered cake covered in whipped cream. It is almost impossible to guess the purpose of this three-story high windowless building just by looking at it from the outside. Despite the mysterious appearance from afar, with a closer look one can see the bumpy lines that run vertically along the structure's facade. These lines represent the grain of a book's pages, implying Graphic's identity as a bookstore. Just like the mysterious exterior, the interior is surrounded  by magnificent walls that makeit impossible to guess the interior space is also secretive. Approximately 100new books are brought in every month, providing a new experience each time you visit.  The fact that only adults overthe age of 19 are allowed to enter makes the space even more secretive. A spacewhere you can read books without time constraints becomes a haven for one toshake off the weariness of life while having a light drink with a book.

name: Sojeonseolim
summary: A forest of books surrounded by plain white bricks.
description_html: Sojeonseolim, which means "a forest of books surrounded by white bricks," is a place where books and art coexist. It’s a space where visitors can read and discuss literature together, while also growing and relaxing through the books. Although there is a private space where visitors can fully fall into the story they’re reading, there is also an area called yedam, or “a place to discuss art.” Here, visitors can view arts and humanities texts and experience book-related events such as theme exhibitions, lectures, and performances. Reservations are needed and there is a fee, yet if you want to experience deep relaxation surrounded by books in a private space, visit Sojeonseolim.

name: Zero World Gangnam
summary: Zero World Gangnam Branch is an escape room location where visitors can challenge themselves with with various games and themes unique to Zero World.
description_html: Zero World Gangnam Branch is an escape room location where visitors can challenge themselves with with various games and themes unique to Zero World. Zero World's themed rooms have realistic interiors, fresh puzzles and tricks that are accompanied with solid and exciting stories, allowing visitors to enjoy their time while immersing themselves in the game. name: Gocheok Skydome
summary: Gocheok Skydome is the largest capacity stadium in South Korea. In addition to sporting events, arts events such as concerts and awards ceremonies are also often held here.
description_html:
Gocheok Skydome is the largest capacity stadium in South Korea. In addition to sporting events, arts events such as concerts and awards ceremonies are also often held here.


The stadium was completed in September, 2015 and is a cultural sports complex that is open year round. During the baseball season, visitors can watch exciting games and enjoy Korean baseball culture. During the off-season, there are concerts and other cultural events held at Gocheok. The stadium's design is dome-shaped and there are 2 basement levels and 4 above-ground levels. Thanks to its ceiling cover, games and events are unaffected by weather conditions. There are baseball facilities, a swimming pool, gym, soccer field, basketball field and many other facilities open for public use. The stands have 18,000 seats, but for cultural events like concerts, audiences of 20,200 can be accommodated. Gocheok Skydome is the home stadium for the Nexen Heroes from 2016 to 2017. 


G ocheok Skydome's size makes it one of the largest indoor concert venues in South Korea.  The stadium has hosted many K-pop concerts and awards shows such as the KBS Music Awards and more.



Frequently Asked Questions about Gocheok Skydome

What is the nearest subway station to the Gocheok Sky Dome?

The nearest subway station to Gocheok Sky Dome is Guil Station (Subway Line 1).

Is there a cafeteria at the Gocheok Sky Dome?

There are thirty-two shops inside the Gocheok Sky Dome serving chicken, snack food, and pizza, and a convenience store. Outside, there is a management building with one store, so you can use it when watching baseball. (As of 2024)

Can I bring food inside the Gocheok Sky Dome?

Bringing food and drinks to the Gocheok Sky Dome may be restricted depending on the nature of the event. Food and beverages in plastic bottles of 1L or less may be brought in during professional baseball games. However, alcoholic drinks, cans, and beverages in glasses are not permitted. In addition, according to Kiwoom Heroes' regulations, food cannot be brought into the stadium when re-entering.

name: Lotte World Adventure
summary: Opened in 1989, Lotte World is a major recreation complex located in downtown Seoul.
description_html:
Opened in 1989, Lotte World Adventure is a major recreation complex located in downtown Seoul. It consists of Indoor Adventure, the world's largest indoor theme park, an outdoor theme park called Magic Island, a luxury hotel, the Korean Folk Museum, shoppingmalls,departmentstores,sportsfacilities and a movie theater, all in one place. 

Indoor Adventure is the world’s largest indoor theme park and hosts a dazzling variety of seasonal festivals and parades all year round and features 22 different rides. Magic Island, the outdoor theme park of Lotte World, is an artificial island locatedinthemiddleofSeokchon Lake and boasts 17 different rides including the high-altitude free-fall thrill ride, the Gyro Drop.


Frequently Asked Questions about Lotte World Adventure

Where do I get the tickets for Lotte World Adventure after purchasing them online?

For mobile/online reservations, tickets are issued on the app. You can enter the gate by scanning your ticket through the app without printing a separate ticket.

Are Lotte World Adventure Magic Island amusement facilities operating regardless of the weather?

Magic Island's amusement facilities are subject to weather conditions. In case of heavy rain or snow (if it rains continuously, even if it is a small amount), if the temperature drops to 5 degrees below zero, or if there is a strong wind of 7 m/s or more, operations may be stopped for safety reasons. However, indoor attractions such as Comet Express and Fantasy Dream can be used regardless of the weather.

What types of tickets are available at Lotte World Adventure, and what do they include?

Lotte World Adventure tickets are divided into a general pass, a park pass, and an annual pass.

  • • General pass, annual pass: Park admission + access to attractions + access to the folk museum

  • • Park pass: Park admission + access to attractions

  • However, you will have to pay separate fees for paid facilities.


Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting near Lotte World Adventure?

The following tourist attractions are around Seokchon Lake Park.

  • • Seokchon Lake Park

  • • Lotte World Tower

  • • Lotte World Ice Rink

  • • Lotte World Folk Museum

name: BANKSY: Still Here
summary: A symbol stronger than identity, Banksy's unending message!
description_html: The street artist Banksy, who operates while concealing his identity, is one of the world's most famous artists, yet his true identity remains shrouded in mystery. Nevertheless, people are captivated by the powerful messages he leaves on street walls. The exhibition <BANKSY: Here Still> introduces his artistic world through images and major projects that represent Banksy. By following works that contain messages of war and peace, satire and humor, as well as hope and solidarity, we aim to examine why so many people still discuss Banksy today. The questions posed by the anonymous artist remain ongoing. While his identity remains a mystery, the messages he left behind continue to live on beside us today.

description_html: Co organized with the Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation, 《Proximities》 introduces more than forty artists across three generations connected to the United Arab Emirates, a Gulf nation shaped by migration, abundant natural resources, and rapid urban transformation over the past half century since its founding. Expanding from the most intimate and imaginative realms to geopolitical and foundational dimensions, the exhibition asks how relationships can remain close without collapsing into sameness.
