name: SeMA Omnibus - I Want to Love Us
summary: The 2024-themed exhibition “Connection” aligns with the community-oriented direction of the Seoul Museum of Art's Buk-Seoul branch.
description_html:
The SeMA Omnibus is a largescale collection-based exhibition presented at the main branch and three branches of the Seoul Museum of Art under the theme of the museum’s 2024 institutional agenda, “connection.” The exhibition SeMA Omnibus: I Want to Love Us, at the Buk-Seoul Museum of Art, reflects the diverse stories of minorities that cannot be reduced to a collective narrative and envisions a new community connected by individuals who are all unique in their own right.  This exhibition is focused on social minorities oppressed and/or discriminated against due to various reasons, such as race, nationality, gender, age, physical condition, sexual orientation, sociocultural environment, and/or economic status. In any highly competitive neoliberal society, the problems faced by minorities are often treated as secondary or not recognized as problems at all, and attempts at collectivization frequently fall apart. On the other hand, even when minorities are collectivized through social welfare policies or collectivized to assert their rightful place in society, individual lives are overlooked, and only the aspects of the collective identity that society expects are reduced to “a single story.” Minorities need collectivization to eliminate oppression and discrimination, but they face the paradox in which individual diversity is erased during the process of unification in and among minority groups. This exhibition aims to demonstrate ways to include the diversity of individuals without collectivizing minorities. Through art, it seeks ways for vulnerable individuals to affirm themselves and find love for the “us” composed of individuals with unique bodies and minds. Instead of categorizing the works by specific identities, the exhibition focuses on the shared experiences of social minorities. Furthermore, it explores the possibility of individuals uniting while respecting each other's diversity.


* The title of this exhibition is borrowed from the book Minor Feelings, with permission from Cathy Park Hong and Jeff Chang.

name: Kylie Manning: Yellow Sea
summary: Space K Seoul will host a solo exhibition titled "Yellow Sea" by Brooklyn-based international artist Kylie Manning (b. 1983) from August 9 to November 10. This exhibition presents a unique opportunity
description_html: On view from August 9 to November 10, Space K Seoul is pleased to present "Yellow Sea", a solo exhibition of works by Kylie Manning. Informed by coastal experiences from her upbringing in Alaska and Mexico, the works combine seascapes and ambiguous figures, moving between moments of clarity and abstraction. In a technique employed by Dutch Baroque painters, the artist builds up layers of thin paint, refracting light through the oils in each layer to create a self-luminous effect. The result is a lush harmony of radiant textures and delicate colors. This exhibition features the artist’s most ambitious project to date, submerging viewers in the rippling compositions of a new installation created specifically for Space K. Three large paintings on silk scrim will cascade through the exhibition space like film strips of the surrounding compositions. Measuring nearly 7 meters wide, three silk scrims by Manning are suspended in the center of the exhibition space, creating a stage-like effect. Each scrim is divided into five individual strips, acting as live gridded capsules. This allows the audience to traverse the oscillating vistas of Manning’s work alongside her represented figures. Manning draws inspiration from the tides of the ‘Yellow Sea’ that joins China and the Korean peninsula, meditating on ‘what is distilled after a tide removes excess debris, noise, and marks’. This exhibition will be an exciting opportunity to immerse visitors in the majestic seascapes alchemized by ‘Kylie Manning'.

name: Open-Air Museum - Pungnap
summary: An exhibition that utilizes the spatial resources around Pungnaptoseong to host outdoor displays, aiming to create a city where tradition, the present, and the future coexist while expanding cultural
description_html:
Open-Air Museum_Pungnap 
Welcome to Open-Air Museum_Pungnap. 
Here is Pungnaptoseong, an earthen mound built by the people of the Hanseong Baekje period to defend their city along the windy Han River. Over time, a city has been built within the fortress, burying traces of past eras underground. With relics buried one to two meters below the surface, the inside of the fortress itself becomes a vast, hidden museum. Now, please take a moment to imagine this immense museum, and remember that a museum has exhibition halls where relics or artworks are displayed. This exhibition envisions the excavation sites within the fortress as exhibition halls. That said, these halls come to be sites where visitors encounter contemporary artworks while walking along the streets or turning a corner, thus blending the past with the present. So, what kind of works would you expect to encounter in such a museum? This exhibition consists of “reappearing” works that can metaphorically represent the characteristics of space and time. You will encounter the emergence of traditional media experiments, historical works, images, and others. In today’s time of immense interest in nonlinear temporality, the exhibition showcases works by artists who have meticulously experimented with and restructured the content, form, and structure of traditional media in the Korean art scene; these works metaphorically and materially represent the layers of time and space in contemporary Pungnap-dong. Additionally, it explores the spatial boundaries of art and museums by installing mediums such as Korean painting, painting, video, photography, and ceramics, which are usually exhibited indoors, outdoors. These works by the mound are realized like small openings to a portal to another time and space, with even the flow of the wind between them becoming visible. Artist Seung-taek Lee, who has established a unique artistic practice through the concept of “non-art,” presents another track in this exhibition by circulating through the city. Lee’s bicycle carrying the earth symbolizes the reappearance of historical works and becomes a ritual of circulation. To add, Lee’s wind extends beyond the city to the fortress; the red cloth flying across the wind, along with the earth running through the fortress, reaches back to a time older than the Hanseong Baekje period, older than ancient times, making one perceive the planet Earth and its life. How did you feel after walking through this vast museum and discovering the hidden artworks? We hope this exhibition provides an opportunity for you to transform your view of Pungnaptoseong, a historical yet everyday space, and discover new possibilities within the city. 

□ Performance information
Open Air Museum_Pungnap is pleased to present renactments of Seung-taek Lee's iconic reproduced works, Wind-Folk Amusement (1971) and Earth Play (1994). These are visualizations of ""Wind,"" a red cloth that forms the shape of a bicycle and wind carrying an PVC balloon.
It will be held four times on August 24, August 31, October 4, and October 11, and anyone can watch Earth, Let's Play from 15:00 to 16:00 and Wind, Let's Play from 16:00 to 16:30 at the Pungnaptoseong Namseong-Wall.

name: Shunita, Oh Jeisung, Dokkaebi: Multi Persona
summary:
"New Interpretation of Korean Fantasy"  
Gallery Jiwooheon Presents Dokkaebi Multi Persona

This exhibition expands the concept of “Korean Fantasy,” which emerged in the early 2000s in the Korean lite
description_html:
Gallery Jiwooheon is pleased to announce a two-person exhibition titled Dokkaebi: Multi Persona by Shunita and Oh Jeisung from 22 May to 22 June. 
This exhibition extends and reinterprets the concept of ‘Korean fantasy’ that emerged in the domestic novel scene in the early 2000s into the realm of art. Through a perspective that encompasses both tradition and modernity, it aims to present a new form of visual fantasy by combining Korea's unique cultural elements with an exploration of identity in contemporary society. Unlike the typical images seen in media, Dokkaebi with unclear origins and sources, and Multi persona referring to an individual's diverse identities in digital culture, these two concepts evoke something mysterious and unpredictable. In this context, two artists, Shunita and Oh Jeisung, who approach fantasy structures in their own ways, collaborate. Shunita's Moomyeong(nameless) is the artist's signature character that reflects the empty inner self of modern people. Moomyeong, an alien who came to Earth, takes on various appearances in relationships with humans. Its simple yet ambiguous gestures, colorful monochrome fur, round body, and flexible limbs give a strange sense of familiarity. Moomyeong dramatically represents the empty emotions in one corner of the young generation who use multiple identities in the digital world as a breakthrough in life, while simultaneously reflecting some substance behind the Multi persona. Oh Jeisung is an artist who has gained attention for his research-based sculptural work that investigates and archives undesignated cultural properties across the country. Various folk sculptures such as animals from Folktales, Dokkaebi, Abandoned dolmens, and Stone Maitreyas are reinterpreted in a contemporary context in his works, gaining contemporary forms. In this exhibition, he presents works that newly adapt the attributes of Dokkaebi from folk tales, which have been around humans, sometimes helping and sometimes hindering, but still with unclear forms, by grafting them onto the belief in the twelve zodiac animals. His work, which commemorates marginalized folk sculptures and revives folktales and legends as modern sculptures, offers a new interpretation of Korean fantasy. 
Dokkaebi: Multi Persona is an exhibition that calls upon imaginary beings infused with human life history from a modern perspective and loosely sketches the past and present of Korean fantasy. Through this, we aim to provide an opportunity to contemplate together the unique imagination of our culture and the identity of modern society

name: crosswalk
summary: Gallery Planet will host a two-person exhibition 《Crosswalk》 featuring artists Kim Jung-in and Cho Hyun-seo from August 8 to September 13, 2024.
description_html: Gallery Planet will host a two-person exhibition 《Crosswalk》 featuring artists Kim Jung-in and Cho Hyun-seo from August 8 to September 13, 2024. 《Crosswalk》 begins by examining the perspectives of two artists who set out from different directions, meet, and diverge at an intersection. Through Kim Jung-in's images, which actively reveal subjective judgments uniquely human through a mixture of internalized and externalized memories, and Cho Hyun-seo's works, which seek to define aesthetic taste through the judgments of trained artificial intelligence, we ultimately find ourselves contemplating the paintings of our current era. As the exhibition title 'Crosswalk' suggests (a place where paths cross or meet), following the viewpoints of the two artists standing at the intersection leads us to a time of selected memories that have become filters. We experience numerous moments of (un)conscious choices as internal and external memories mix, pass through external memory, and reappear before our eyes. Based on their unique qualities, reflecting innate senses and learned tastes, the artists technically preserve images in their own memory vessels. The divergent perspectives of the two artists, which this exhibition highlights, are revealed at this point.

name: 50th Anniversary of Seoul Metropolitan Subway <Subway in Seoul>
summary: Seoul Museum of History X Seoul Metro Joint Special Exhibition <Subway in Seoul>
description_html:
On August 15, 1974, marking the 29th anniversary of Korea's liberation, the country's first subway line, the 'Jongno Line,' opened. Since then, Seoulites have lived in the “Subway Age” for five decades. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway is familiar to everyone who has traveled to and from Seoul. It was not just a convenient public transportation system that eases commutes to school and work; it was a vehicle for a ‘new era of modern life.’ Back then, the subway was a new experience for everyone in Seoul. Over time, as we adapted to this new era, the subway gradually changed our mindset, lifestyle, culture, and the city itself. It has served as a commuter train for the city’s many workers, a transportation service that makes it easy for everyone to get around and keep appointments, a meet-up point, and a venue for consumption. The subway also provided a social space where people could mingle, fostering both a sense of community and deep aloneness. Furthermore, it has reshaped urban spaces and living areas, and as a comfortable cultural space accessible anywhere, it has expanded people's cultural enjoyment.
The Seoul Metropolitan Subway has been “connecting” Seoul through its underground network and to the outlying areas, shaping the capital city as we know it today. To mark the 50th anniversary of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway, the Seoul Museum of History and Seoul Metro have partnered to present this commemorative exhibition. We cordially invite you to this exhibition, which we hope will offer an opportunity to reflect on Seoul’s story, created by the subway and its people, and to envision what the future holds for the city.

name: A Stroll Through Records: Seoul’s Parks
summary: An exhibition exploring the history and transformation of Seoul's parks through records
description_html: The exhibition "A Stroll Through Records: Seoul's Parks" showcases over 90 related records, highlighting Seoul's green space policies, stories of its prominent parks, park records categorized by keywords, and photographs of Seoul's parks taken by residents. Part 1, "The Path of Seoul's Parks," showcases the historical evolution of Seoul's park and green space policies through various documents, blueprints, photos, and videos. Part 2, "Parks Through Records," delves into the histories of notable parks like Namsan Park and Hyochang Park, utilizing records preserved by the Seoul Archives. Part 3, "Park Records Through Keywords," investigates the history and policies of parks, focusing on themes such as children, ecology, and urban regeneration. Additionally, the exhibition features 20 photos collected from a public event, allowing residents to share their personal memories of Seoul's parks.

name: MINSEONG KIM: False Alarm
summary: Dynamically explosive scenes are arranged randomly, capturing attention and representing the endless, unilateral information cycle
description_html:
The artist explores the screens and boundaries we encounter in today's digital age, delving into the temporal nature and reconfiguration of images through various painterly experiments. In this exhibition, dynamically explosive and attention-grabbing scenes are arranged randomly to depict the endless, one-way cycle of information. Images selected from platforms like YouTube and Instagram are visually arranged using a 'dendrogram' method, which pairs and merges similar attributes based on algorithmic data.

Through this exhibition, artist Kim Min-seong aims to highlight the paradox of displayed images and invites us to reflect on how we consume algorithm-driven images on these platforms.

name: Bosingak Pavilion: Echoes of Time
summary: Bosingak Pavilion: Echoes of Time
description_html:
Bosingak Pavilion is a well-known landmark that can be easily spotted by anyone passing through Jongno Street. The street's name, Jongno, which means "Bell Street," is derived from the presence of this historic bell. The chime of the Bosingak Bell, especially during the transition to the new year, has become a cherished tradition. Historically, Bosingak Pavilion functioned as a public clock maintained by the government. When the water clock at Borugak indicated the time, the bell at Bosingak would be rung to announce the time throughout Hanyang. During the Joseon Dynasty, the residents of Hanyang began and ended their days with the sound of the Bosingak bell.
The exhibition "Bosingak Pavilion: Echoes of Time" delves into the history and evolution of the Bosingak Pavilion. Through this exhibit, visitors can explore the daily lives of Joseon-era Hanyang residents, who lived according to the rhythmic chimes of the Bosingak bell.

name: Yoonkee & Guhong's Guhong & Yoonkee
summary:
"An Interesting Proposal on the Future of AI Technology and the Role of Artists"
From July 3, Gallery Jiwoohun will host Yoonkee & Guhong's Guhong & Yoonkee
description_html:
Paintings created under rules and conditions such as "Draw 9 circles on the canvas and fill each circle with a different color" and "Play acoustic guitar for the canvas to hear" will be exhibited. This exhibition, titled Guhong & Yoonkee, opens on July 3rd at Gallery Jiwooheon.
'Yoonkee and Guhong' is the name of a web-based music duo formed in 2023 by Kim Yoonkee and Min Guhong. Kim Yoonkee (hereafter Yoonkee), who debuted in 2000, has been actively working internationally as a musician, painter, and poet in countries including the UK and Japan. Min Guhong (hereafter Guhong) works as an editor and programmer at Ahn Graphics and Workroom, while also running his company Min Guhong Manufacturing and a coding language course called New Order. For over a decade, they have been supporting each other's activities by filling in the 'gaps' beyond their individual abilities, collaborating on performances and designs. Recently, they formed a duo and are presenting Guhong & Yoonkee as their first step. Yoonkee and Guhong prepared this exhibition out of curiosity about what would happen if artists, following the development of AI technology, designed rules and conditions like prompt engineers and created works accordingly. Guhong, a programmer, reveals his primary form of expression, coding, while Yoonkee candidly displays the painting format he has approached simply and comfortably. The process of creating the works is simple. Guhong creates 20 arbitrary rules and conditions, and Yoonkee combines the items he likes to personally paint 20 pieces. Notably, Guhong's rules include not only 'codes' for brush strokes but also actions like playing music for the canvas or discussing economics with it. Here, the coding method leads to a human twist that amplifies the analog aspect. Can the audience discern which canvas listened to Yoonkee's music? Can the canvas confess that it had a sincere conversation about economics with Yoonkee? Their attempt, which makes one imagine personified canvases, is also an optimistic thought experiment about the coexistence of digital and analog. This is why music or stories can be read in Yoonkee's paintings mediated by Guhong's coding. Additionally, four paintings by Yoonkee and two media works by Guhong will be exhibited. One of Guhong's works, Twenty Ways to Fall in Love with Canvas, shows the codes applied to Yoonkee's paintings flickering through kinetic typography. Visitors can deduce how these codes were applied to each of Yoonkee's paintings. Meanwhile, in the exhibition space, music first released on 'Yoonkee and Guhong's' website (https://www.yoonkeeguhong.com/) will be played randomly along with unreleased music. Yoonkee and Guhong described this exhibition as "improvised melodies drawn on a score of rules, twenty variables created by one algorithm." It sounds like an incantation suggesting that conforming to the inevitable technology of AI will open up possibilities for rich enjoyment rather than creating humans with submissive selves without will. This premise raises the fundamental question of "what questions to ask and what to enjoy in the face of rapidly changing technological environments." Thus, Guhong & Yoonkee presents results born more humanly within a mechanically generated framework, offering a light-hearted outlook on the future of art.

name: Kim Jihee’s Solo Exhibition: DIVINITY
summary: Museum Wave is celebrating its first anniversary with its inaugural full-scale exhibition, featuring the solo exhibition “DIVINITY” by Kim Ji-hee.
description_html: Museum Wave is celebrating its first anniversary with its inaugural full-scale exhibition featuring Kim Ji-hee's solo exhibition “DIVINITY.” Known domestically and internationally for her imagery of girls wearing glasses and animals, Kim Ji-hee has gained significant popularity, particularly in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. This exhibition will showcase the 10-meter masterpiece "Eternal Golden," first presented at the K11 Art Museum in China earlier this year. This work, debuting in Korea, was meticulously created over four years using traditional Korean paper (jangji) and fine brush techniques. It depicts the finite nature of life, likening it to a single day, and portrays humans' desires and adventures from dawn to night. This exhibition provides a rare opportunity to view one of the artist's most significant works. This exhibition, spread across four galleries, begins on the first floor with the 10-meter masterpiece "Eternal Golden," exploring the theme of “desire.” On the second floor, the Dongja Gallery features traditional paintings inspired by the Museum Wave's predecessor, the Old Stone Museum, unveiling the artist's first digital work themed around divinity. The main exhibition hall on the second floor will host the Trunk Show series, which has garnered immense domestic and international popularity. On the third floor, visitors can watch videos showcasing the artist's creative process and international blockbuster exhibitions and explore new works depicting various scenes of a girl, symbolizing the possibility of hope.

name: Kim So-jin's Complete Performance of Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga
summary: The first complete performance of Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga by a female singer showcases the traditional and classical essence of Gojesori.
description_html: Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga is a precious form of traditional Korean music that retains the old-fashioned charm of Gojesori. It is characterized by its robust and dignified sound, primarily in the Ujo mode. This musical lineage, which began with Park Yu-jeon and continued through Jeong Jae-geun, Jeong Eung-min, and Jeong Gwon-jin, was on the brink of extinction until it was revived by Yoon Jin-cheol, who was recognized as a holder of the National Intangible Cultural Heritage. Recently, it has been actively performed again. This performance is particularly notable as it marks a female singer's first complete rendition of Boseongsori Jeokbyeokga. Audiences will experience Kim So-jin's unique interpretation and color.

name: Celestial Whisper
summary: The exhibition, centered on the “angels” theme, seeks to make contemporary art more approachable and familiar to children and general visitors. Lowering the barriers to contemporary art offers a multi
description_html: Celestial Whisper is an exhibition by sculptor Meekyoung Shin, who has built a unique body of work using soap as her main material. The theme of the exhibition, angels, is a religious symbol that connects God and humans. More than that, however, angels serve as symbolic beings that have become a natural part of our perception. Visualizing the image of angels as those that lie somewhere between what exists and what is absent, the artist first became interested in angels when she came across a fragrance called “Angel.” In this exhibition, Shin highlights the meaning of angels, something that everyone knows of yet has never seen. Her angel is a being in the realm of illusion, hovering between heaven and earth, life and death, body and soul, and is presented metaphorically through the material properties of soap. The artist has used soap as a material for her sculptures for more than 30 years. For Shin, soap also has a materiality to it that wavers between transparency and opacity. Still, it is destined to wear down over time, while its scent can only be experienced by those who have come in contact with it in person. These characteristics of soap are connected to the symbolism of angels, who are intermediate beings between heaven and earth. In particular, the transparency of soap, the light that maximizes its transparency, and its many different scents allow visitors to experience the presence of angels that oscillate between existence and absence. Visitors can draw closer to contemporary art by appreciating sculptures made from everyday soap, allowing their imagination to run wild through angels, a familiar yet unseen entity. We hope that this exhibition, which is filled with the light and fragrance of angels that evoke a kind of fantasy across generations, will inspire you to rediscover the very same angels you have always felt are familiar.

name: Childhood under the shield
summary:
Bosnia War Childhood Museum International Exchange Exhibition
Stories of Children Who Lived Through the War
CHILDHOOD UNDER THE SIEGE_Sarajevo 1992-1995
description_html: What was your childhood like? This exhibition begins with that question. The international exchange exhibition, “Stories of Children Who Lived Through the War: Childhood under the Siege,” aims to convey the preciousness of peace through 38 stories of children who endured the longest siege in modern history, which took place in Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia, from 1992 to 1995. For 1,425 days, children in Sarajevo lived isolated from the world, experiencing a different daily life than ordinary children. Their lives, filled with the pain of war and the preciousness of everyday moments, are told with quiet resilience. These deeply personal stories are not just about Sarajevo, a city 8,465 kilometers away from Seoul. They are stories of families, friends, and neighbors, resonating deeply with the audience. Through this exhibition, the hope is for you to feel that "people are strong, and children are strong!"

name: A Walk Around the City Wall: Hanyangdoseong through the Eyes of 19th-Century Literature
summary: A Walk Around the City Wall: Hanyangdoseong through the Eyes of 19th-Century Literature
description_html:
After the cold winter passes and spring arrives with its budding flowers, many people visit Seoul City Wall. Originally, "Soonseong" referred to the patrols conducted by Joseon soldiers along the fortress walls to defend and manage the Seoul City Wall. In the late Joseon period, however, the term also came to refer to the leisurely activity of springtime visitors walking along the fortress walls to enjoy the scenery.
Additionally, Soonseong was a tradition for scholars who traveled to Hanyang to take the state exams and walked around the fortress walls, hoping for success. Here, we have a record of a Soonseong journey left by a scholar over 100 years ago. This writing, which describes his experience of walking the Soonseong path with a light heart after passing the exam, captures the image of the Seoul City Wall as it was in the past. This exhibition aims to follow the journey of Soonseong as documented in the record and reflect on how the tradition has continued to the present day. Today, why not walk along the fortress path in ancestors’ footsteps?

name: Make a Wish
summary: An exhibition showcasing how shamanism, superstitions, and ancestral rites, from traditional folk paintings to contemporary art, continue to influence not only the past but also our subconscious
description_html: "Make a Wish" is an exhibition that focuses on what we have lost and need to reclaim while living in an era of lightness. Unlike the past, when unchanging universal values prevailed, in the era of lightness, where only constant change becomes the sole truth, unstable daily life has become the “new normal.” People feel the lightness of existence more than ever, drifting by clicking on links as algorithms lead them through another new normal in the digital world. In this reality, we find ourselves pondering what we can rely on to alleviate anxiety and prevent ourselves from being consumed by sadness and emptiness. We inevitably contemplate how to reclaim important things like communication, symbiosis, peace, and happiness that we are losing. Perhaps now is the time to summon the genie from the lamp and make a wish. This exhibition, presented as a kind of “spiritual journey,” aims to demonstrate the belief that humans can still uphold conditions for dignity and spiritual freedom even amidst the scattering of life's lightness. Stories initiated by the artists evolve into the audience's narratives, creating their tales, myths, and earnest prayers. These interconnected narratives are hoped to become wisdom passed down through generations.

name: DMAU Project "Init"
summary: Director Kim Sung-yong's latest work, "InIt," is the first piece of the DMAU (Dance Makes Asia become the Universe) project, planned by the Korea National Contemporary Dance Company based on the aspir
description_html:
Director Kim Sung-yong's latest work, "Init," is the first piece of the DMAU (Dance Makes Asia become the Universe) project, planned by the Korea National Contemporary Dance Company based on the aspiration to expand the exchange of Asian dance and lead the world of contemporary dance.
Based on the paradoxical keywords of "complexity within simplicity," "depth within repetition," and "coexistence of unconsciousness and consciousness," “Init” unfolds intricate traces focusing on the unique history of the dancer's body and the essence of dance, together with the top dancers in Asia.
Developed from choreographer Kim Sung-yong's methodology, "Process InIt," aims to evolve, removing barriers between choreographer and dancer, as well as between dancer and audience. Stage design, geared towards highlighting the individualistic movements of the dancers, is crafted in collaboration with Yoo Jae-heon (YouJam Studio), with whom the choreographer has shared a long-standing creative partnership. Meanwhile, musician Yoo Ji-wan of the band “Alligators” joins as the music director to present a more innovative stage.

name: Takahata Isao  Exibition
summary: Takahata Isao, is known as the rival and collaborator of Miyazaki Hayao, the luminary of Studio Ghibli. His works encapsulate the history he has crafted over 50 years in the animation industry.
description_html:
This exhibition showcases the entire production process of all the works directed by the master of animation, Takahata Isao, from his debut to his masterpieces. It includes works such as “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)”, “Anne of Green Gables (1979)”, “Grave of the Fireflies (1988)”, “Only Yesterday (1991)”, “Pom Poko (1994)”, and “The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013)”.
His directorial materials include layouts, which can be likened to blueprints for animated film production, and sketches and handwritten notes that he wrote and drew.
In addition, it is packed with previously unreleased materials from Miyazaki Hayao, who was responsible for the layouts during Takahata Isao's directorial era at Zuiyo Video, including “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)” and “Anne of Green Gables (1979).”

name: Eddie Martinez 《To Be Continued》
summary: Space K Seoul presents a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based artist Eddie Martinez (b.1977).
description_html:
Space K Seoul presents a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based artist Eddie Martinez (b.1977). The exhibition, titled 《to be continued》, sheds light on the artist’s oeuvre, which effortlessly fuses figuration and abstraction, from 2005 to the present, arranged both chronologically and thematically. His paintings are characterized by swift lines and bold colors, while everyday found materials add a unique texture to the flat canvases.
The exhibition features about 30 drawings and paintings, including a new series, focusing on Martinez's practice of 'constant drawing'. Surrounding objects that catch his eye are transferred onto paper and canvas and transformed into entirely new landscapes, while repeated motifs give a sense of coherence to unfamiliar landscapes. The familiar objects of everyday life that are gradually revealed among the shapes which may be difficult to interpret at first glance stimulate our imagination through the artist’s personal experience.

name: Weaving Relations
summary: Weaving Relations is an exhibition that explores the fundamental attributes of architecture as a process of creating value and experience through relationship building.
description_html:
Weaving Relations is an exhibition that spans the theme of "Architecture" for the 2024 Seoul Museum of Art exhibition. It delves into the essential attributes of architecture as a process of creating value and experience through relationship building and examines this process through various conceptual approaches.
Weaving Relations induces a shift in perspectives on life by exploring various ways of relationship building, facilitated by physical spaces that serve as fundamental conditions for self-recognition. Through the works of seven artists, the exhibition prompts contemplation on the transformations in how we perceive life.
Through this, the aim is to awaken modern individuals to the dynamic value of relationship building, which can counter feelings of isolation and identity loss.
The exhibition title, Weaving Relations, borrowed from Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's literary work "The Little Prince," encapsulates the essence of relationship building.
Weaving Relations refers to forming relationships based on temporality, repetition, and process while also being grounded in communal nature, which is the essence of architecture. What are we weaving, and what are we being weaved by? The exhibition aims to produce various narratives that accumulate deep relationship moments.

name: Euphoric Proliferation
summary: From March 27th to May 4th, Gallery Jiwooheon will host an exhibition of two talented young artists who have attracted considerable attention in the art world.
description_html:
Gallery Jiwooheon will host Euphoric Proliferation, an exhibition featuring Yi Young-uk and Jojae, from March 27th to May 4th. Both artists have recently received attention by winning awards for young artists at prominent domestic art museums. The exhibition focuses on their work, which is similar in the context of fragmenting, distorting, and amplifying images but differentiated by the abstract and figurative nature of the results.
Since 2018, Yi Young-uk has been boldly exploring methods of redefining the concept of the subject. His distinctive theme revolves around creating bizarre patterns by repetitively distorting parts of human and animal bodies, which have become a hallmark of his work.
JoJae's work originates in the virtual realm. Since 2016, she has been sculpturally translating digitally rendered images and their original analog counterparts. By shaping the gap between digital images and their unprocessed originals, she constructs a new sense of connection between the virtual and the real worlds.
In this exhibition, Jojae presents works that extend from his ongoing “Crumbs Series,” which involves the reconstruction of urban landscapes and byproducts of digital images collected over time.

name: Architecture, Space Time Scenarios
summary: “Space Time Scenarios” is an exhibition planned to explore in depth the internal and external changes surrounding the Seoul Museum of Art to consider the museum's architecture with a focus on ‘time.’
description_html:
The Seoul Museum of Art, including the upcoming new building, operates its branches throughout Seoul in various ways, in line with the flow of time and art trends.
“Architecture, Space Time Scenarios” is an exhibition planned to explore in depth the internal and external changes surrounding the Seoul Museum of Art at this point and to consider the museum's architecture with a focus on ‘time.’
Various discussions regarding architectural deterioration have taken place at national public art museums, including the Seoul Museum of Art, in response to national events and policies since the 1980s.
Furthermore, witnessing urban redevelopment and reconstruction sites altering the city's landscape, this exhibition focuses on the 'life cycle of architecture' implied within art museums' special and symbolic public architecture.

The exhibition features a refreshed arrangement and staging of over 22 varieties of content, including both acclaimed existing works and newly created pieces.

name: From unfamiliar gaze
summary: In this exhibition, invited artists Manwook (b.1975) and Kimi Jaak (b.1976) discuss their respective relationships based on deep contemplation of unfamiliar subjects that have long captured their atte
description_html:
Forming a relationship begins with sensing the subject. Among these senses, sight, or our eyes’ path, is the easiest and fastest way to establish a relationship. A gaze that doesn't stray from everyday life is conducive to forming connections. However, if the subject is unfamiliar, desire becomes entwined with the gaze. To start a relationship with that subject, one might actively explore it, desperately avoid forming a connection, or even experience frustration in their desire.

In this exhibition, invited artists Manwook (b.1975) and Kimi Jaak (b.1976) discuss their respective ways of forming relationships based on their deep contemplation of unfamiliar subjects that have long held their attention. The results of their gazes are fundamentally different. In the case of artist Manwook, an active exploration of the subject ultimately leads to the erasure of boundaries with the unfamiliar subject. On the other hand, the unfamiliar gaze of artist Kimi Jaak results in narratives that revolve around and observe from the periphery, unable to be integrated.

summary: This exhibition features the works of three artists, Kang Min-sung, Kim Kyung-hee, and Jo Sung-hyun, who are furthering the tradition and evolving it into contemporary art.
description_html:
Superior Gallery has organized an exhibition titled 'Super Moon on My Hand: Moon Jar' featuring the artists Kang Min-sung, Kim Kyung-hee, and Jo Sung-hyun, who are furthering the tradition while evolving it into contemporary lifestyle art. Showcasing works that reinterpret traditional techniques and imagery in a modern way, these pieces fuse contemporary images with various materials and forms, embodying unique stories crafted by the artists. Their creations capture the personal joy, wishes, and happiness evoked by moon jars while incorporating diverse perspectives through subjective creativity.

The three artists are forging a new wave in tradition, harmoniously blending inherited values with contemporary narratives. Using moon jars as a medium, each artist conveys their unique artistic value and cultural expression, infusing unchanging values with new emotions to deliver their distinctive messages. Amid rapid changes, we invite you to fully experience the jars created by three artists at Superior Gallery, where they skillfully blend their unique realms into the living, breathing fabric of everyday life.

name: Yuichi Hirako <Travel>
summary: This exhibition proposes to view nature from an equal standpoint rather than as a subject of exploration and conquest, aiming to refresh the human-centered attitude towards nature.
description_html: Hirako, who studied painting at Wimbledon College of Art in London and continues to work internationally based in Tokyo, seeks the coexistence of man and nature. He created a hybrid character as a medium to connect human with nature. The character, who has a human body and tree head, travels with dogs, cats, and various plants in the exhibition. Sometimes by the river, sometimes in the forest, and other times in a room, these scenes with flora and fauna are transformed into a variety of media, including painting, sculpture, and installation, to give the viewers a more sensory understanding of nature. Through this, Hirako questions anthropocentric attitudes toward nature, suggesting that nature be viewed on an equal footing rather than as an object to be explored and conquered.

name: 2023 Sejong Museum Special Exhibition《 'Ink and Brush Transformation: Song Soo-nam and Hwang Chang-bae》'Two Perspectives on Contemporary Ink Painting'
summary: An exhibition showcasing the era's spirit and artistic worlds of two masters, Song Soo-nam and Hwang Chang-bae
description_html:
Namcheon Song Soo-nam (1938-2013) and Sojeong Hwang Chang-bae (1947-2001), who liberated themselves from the traditional use of ink and brush at the end of the 20th century, marked a milestone in their times through change and innovation and had a great influence on later generations. We present the spirit of the times and the world of work.

This exhibition offers an opportunity to encounter the works of Namcheon Song Soo-nam and Sojeong Hwang Chang-bae, who departed from tradition and always aimed for contemporary reality, firmly rooted in a pragmatic space-time for Korean painting. This exhibition conveys the messages of the two masters regarding the visual resonance and their perspective on life, which their works uniquely emit directly to the audience.

name: The Shape of Touch
summary: This exhibition represents how materials in our surroundings are shaped into forms, all crafted by the skilled handiwork of the artist.
description_html:
As in a sculpture park, how about strolling through the art gallery?

The shape of touch started from a desire to share the fun and the value of work derived from using the hands and the body to make art in the era where all materials are digitalized. This exhibition represents how materials in our surroundings are shaped into forms, all crafted by the skilled handiwork of the artist.

Artist Lee Eun-woo starts her day by heading to her studio for work. The artist sets a one-hour timer and engages in her 'drawing' without a specific purpose, simply allowing her hand to create whatever it desires. It's a repetitive habit that resembles a daily routine. Various shapes combine and accumulate by connecting dots with lines, forming interesting patterns. The finished work is transferred onto grid paper and complemented with textures and colors that suit the shapes.

The entire space of the Children's Gallery has been structured using a square grid. For the artist, the grid serves as a crucial tool for quantifying the size of objects and is the fundamental framework for her drawings. The drawing results that have become part of a regular daily routine are visualized in various ways in a grid-standardized exhibition space. Lines and shapes in a drawing may go beyond the ground and become three-dimensional as a sculpture or may be enlarged into an architectural form and pass through the structure.

Large and small sculptures throughout the exhibition hall are made from various materials around us. The artist has molded her sculptural world by spending a long time cutting and shaping materials by hand, harmonizing them with everyday objects. The sculptures' visuals reminiscent of furniture and toys, can evoke one’s favorite object.

Could there be significance in doing something 'just because' without a specific purpose? The Shape of Touch results from accumulating simple and repetitive acts of 'drawing' and 'creating' over a long period. The hope is that this exhibition serves as an opportunity to contemplate the value of the immersive experience and the sense of peace that comes from the ordinary labor of starting a day well and finding inner tranquility.

name: Park Hyunsung, Yoon Sukone: The rest of today going to tomorrow
summary: This is an exhibition by two artists, Park Hyunsung and Yoon Sukwone, connecting the ever-changing times of modern society.
description_html:
Recently, the art market, hosting grand festivals like never before, has been saturated with similar and repetitive works, overshadowing its dazzling spectacle. The era is marked by a lack of contemporary spirit, with image-based works that depict an era devoid of its essence. The selection of artists and artworks based on investment value, as well as exhibition planning focused on leisure activities and social media, are rapidly departing from the unique path of art. In this context, Park Hyunsung and Yoon Sukwone's work centers on recreating the mimetic experiences from the inception of art and challenging the categorization within the art world. Gallery Jiuhun presents the exhibition "The Rest of Today Going to Tomorrow," where the two artists connect the ever-changing time of modern society, bridging yesterday with today.

What the two artists create through "relationships" is the restoration of the space of mimetic experience. "Mimesis" is the practice of capturing the object’s appearance as it is without alteration. Amidst the absence of the subject, in a world teeming with splendid objects, their work will restore a space where more flexible relationships can be formed, taking us back to the beginning of the vivid moments of thought.

name: Joke: Spreading from Me, Passing to You
summary: This exhibition features three artists who begin by expressing their own solitude through the nuanced shades of blue, ultimately seeking the smiles and greetings of others.
description_html:
Joke: Spreading from Me, Passing to You is a three-artist exhibition by Lee Jeong-hee, Lee Fero, and Joo Yoo-jin, which was curated with a focus on the multiple meanings of "농담" (pronounced "nongdam" in Korean). The exhibition encompasses both the notion of a small gesture or playful act intended to make someone feel good and the concept describing the degree of lightness and darkness in color and shading in art. This exhibition is divided into three spaces: "Spreading Deeply," "Gently Passing By," and "Anticipating a Smile."

In the first part, "Spreading Deeply," artists Lee Jeong-hee and Joo Yoo-jin explore their personal solitude. With various shades of blue accumulating, Lee Jeong-hee reflects on her solitude in the paradise of Arcadia, where despair coexists. Joo Yoo-jin expresses her contemplation of her solitude through the color blue.

In the second part, "Gently Passing By," you can encounter the works of artists Lee Jeong-hee and Lee Fero. Lee Fero's distinctive approach involves delicately drawing desserts and then pushing them away with swift strokes to reshape their forms. In her works, the subjects become distorted, and the original shapes are briefly touched upon and then become ambiguous, much like the concept of "swipe to unlock" on a mobile phone. It reveals hidden elements, and paradoxically, the intention to reveal becomes clearer, according to the artist.

Finally, in the innermost section, "Anticipating a Smile," artist Joo Yoo-jin creates a small garden. In this bright and colorful garden filled with blooming flowers, the artist positions someone other than themselves. Unlike the spread of their own loneliness through the blue light, they hope that the loneliness of others will not be lonely and that they will experience the spread of various colors.

name: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
summary: This exhibition explores the concept of gardens as both artists' responses and symbolic representations of the world surrounding nature and us.
description_html: The Seoul Museum of Art will hold the exhibition "The Hanging Gardens of Babylon" from August 30th to November 19th. The Hanging Gardens of Babylon is an exhibition exploring the concept of 'gardens' as both artists' responses and symbolic representations of the world surrounding nature and us. The exhibited works attempt methodological experiments, referencing and reproducing issues of reality and fiction, imitation and replication, and various ways to address the contemporary environment and ecosystem. Through the independent ecosystems created by participating artists Kohui, Kim Joon, Yang Seungwon, Cho Leesop, and Hyun Nahm, it examines the sensitive perspectives and senses of the artists toward the world.

name: SeMA Anthology: Ten Orders
summary: This exhibition, featuring ten artists, celebrates the 10th anniversary of the opening of the Seoul Museum of Art, envisioning new landscapes that transcend the past and future.
description_html: In celebration of the 10th anniversary of its opening, the Seoul Museum of Art presents an exhibition titled "SeMA Anthology: Ten Orders," featuring ten artists who envision new landscapes transcending the past and future. Rather than organizing the present through an archival listing of the Seoul Museum of Art's trajectory, this exhibition attempts to actively sense the coming time by focusing on imagination as an active, creative act that connects the past and the future. To explore how the formal and thematic essence of imagination connects with art, the exhibition examines the unique grammar inherent in the language of imagination and replaces it with the particularity embedded in contemporary artworks. This will serve as a kind of aesthetic exploration and creative experiment about how our present embraces the past, anticipates the future, and pioneers the constantly emerging unknown world.

description_html:
LOCA: Walking Through New York.

LOCA embarks on a journey to New York. Strolling through alleyways, riding the subway, shopping, taking photos, and meeting various people.

In 1950, while dining at a restaurant in Manhattan, USA, an idea sparked to make payments solely through credit. This marked the birth of the first-ever credit card. In a similar vein, LOCA focuses on a card's essence. Inspired by the birthplace of credit cards, Manhattan, New York, LOCA has launched a card designed with the motif of the Manhattan map. To commemorate LOCA's 3rd anniversary, LOCA cards are embarking on a journey to New York, capturing everyday life and iconic landmarks in photos to convey a sense of inspiration and emotion.

In commemorating Kwon Jin Kyu's 50th anniversary, Seoul Museum of Art's Nam Seoul Museum is launching the "Kwon Jin Kyu's Forever Home" exhibition in 2023. Having received the Kwon Jin Kyu collection in 2021, the Seoul Museum of Art has transformed five exhibition rooms on the 1st floor of Nam Seoul Museum into a permanent exhibition space dedicated to Kwon JinKyu's valuable works and materials.

This exhibition succinctly presents Kwon Jin Kyu's entire artistic realm, where he continuously observes and studies the subjects around him, capturing only their essence to manifest an enduring soul and eternity that never fades away.

Kwon Jin Kyu (1922–1973) navigated through the Japanese colonial era and post-liberation during the severed diplomatic ties between Korea and Japan. Despite the challenges, he engaged as a sculptor, shuttling between the two countries. He established a unique artistic realm. For him, true art was incessantly observing and studying the subjects around him, capturing only their essence. He pursued not realism or beauty but an enduring soul, an eternity that never fades away. Seoul Museum of Art's Nam Seoul Museum aims to be both a perpetual resting place for his works and a nurturing ground for new research.

Please explore his works in the exhibition inspired by the architectural structures, wooden furniture, shelves, and more from Tokyo Musashino Art University, where Kwon Jin Kyu dedicated himself to his work and the Seoul studio.

name: Collection of Moments
summary: This exhibition illuminates the subtle relationship between memory and the subconscious through works that artistically express nostalgic scenes using the writer's distinctive visual language.
description_html:
From September 1st to October 13th, 2023, the Vivian Choi Gallery will host a three-person exhibition titled 'Collection of Moments,' featuring artists Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil. In this exhibition, three artists who have collaborated in the realm of painting techniques come together to illuminate the subtle relationship between memory and the subconscious through artworks that uniquely express inner landscapes preserved within the time and space of the past, using their distinctive visual languages.

Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil, the artists, capture moments unconsciously stored in memory within spaces they casually overlook. The subtle emotions of the artists, intertwined with the current inner consciousness, intersect with the spaces and objects that once existed in the subconscious. This unique painterly expression by the three artists highlights their ability to capture this delicate relationship as they reconfigure it in a dreamlike manner. The works of Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil do not spotlight any particular events, figures, or objects as protagonists. Instead, they breathe life into places and objects that often go unnoticed, like the modest roofs of an obscure neighborhood, a secluded and unnamed beach, or a small potted plant guarding a desk corner. These surroundings, taken for granted yet filled with the artists' momentary feelings and emotions, are reconstructed to become unique landscapes with different memories, offering a special perspective.

Through the three-person exhibition "Collection of Moments" by Kim Yeon Soo, Rosie Park, and Lim Jin Sil, the hope is that you'll experience the opportunity to observe the infinite world unfolding around you. Ordinary objects that go unnoticed, places casually passed by, elements of life that remain inconspicuous in the periphery, and those that construct life with simplicity come together. Gain the experience of seeing the limitless world that surrounds you.

name: Keep Calm and Give a Shit
summary: Keep Calm and Give a shit introduces the paintings and animations of four artists who are gaining attention in the domestic and international art scene with their cuteness and familiarity. The common
description_html:
Keep Calm and Give a Shit introduces the paintings and animations of four artists, Hun Kyu Kim, SOON.EASY, Tala Madani, and Wong Ping, are gaining attention in the domestic and international art scene with their cuteness and familiarity. The common point among these four artists is their ability to capture the audience's attention through cute characters, comic elements, and techniques and that they tell stories about various social issues through imaginative, fairytale-like images and satirical wordplay.

The canvases and screens, which depict characters and events from refined comics or animations, seem to remind us of the LCD frames of media that we gaze at all day. The subjects and images in each work are also filled with familiar imagery that feels like something we've seen somewhere before, whether through various repetitive feeds on our mobile devices or well-known memes. However, these familiar images and characters do not simply remain cute. They embody the sharp sense of humor and insightful interpretation of the four artists regarding the acute issues that surround us here and now - including the Ukrainian war, political problems in Hong Kong, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and media, surveillance symbolized by panopticon, and ideologies. As such, they demand active engagement from the audience in their interpretation. The narratives that traverse excessive narratives and broad topics in the paintings of Hun Kyu Kim and SOON.EASY and the stories depicted in Wong Ping's animations that resemble his own diary are similar to stories about the absurdities of our daily life and the world around us. These stories concocted by the artists feel as if they are our own experiences because the artists delve into universal themes to such an extent. Moreover, as we lead similar lives in an information-driven city, rather than experiencing the world firsthand, we perceive the world through symbols and images that have been edited and reconstructed beyond the glass screens, as evident in the artists’ works. Tala Madani sharply exposes in "Fan" how we rely entirely on the constant feed of unreliable information. Madani states, "We need art that triggers shifts in consciousness and new ideas, rather than art like morphine that weakens reality with beauty or alleviates pain.

At this juncture, the art we need should be cute and familiar, presented smoothly without any aversion, yet above all, it should be art capable of revitalizing our paralyzed perception, like our sense of smell during the pandemic. Through this exhibition, the hope is for the viewers to contemplate whether, like the artists, they construct their daily lives with a sensitive perspective that reflects their own thoughts and emotions or if they are inundated with indiscriminate assaults of superficial images and information. The hope is to become more sensitive and connected to the present "here and now" of life.

name: The 4th Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism
summary: Land architecture refers to a city that connects the flow of land, water, and wind. Envisioning Seoul 100 years from now, it presents a master plan for an eco-friendly compact city, proposing a vision
description_html:
The Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism, which began in 2017, addresses various issues stemming from rapid urban growth. As one of the world's prominent high-density cities, Seoul aims to rediscover the vision of a human-centered, eco-friendly city under the "Urban Architecture" theme.

The 4th Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism presents the theme "Land Architecture and Land Urbanism: City of Mountain Ranges, Waterways, and Wind Breezes- drawing of Seoul’s Next 100 Years," aiming to connect the past, present, and future by illustrating Seoul's blueprint.

name: NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK
summary: This exhibition creates a harmonious blend of seemingly disparate works through the combination of various arts such as visual arts, digital art, and dance.
description_html: Character pop artist Lemar Kim and hop-funk artist Yakgwa present innovative works, seamlessly navigating between physical and digital mediums. Choreographer Kim Se-ryung and painter Hwang So-young also create their works with entirely different palettes and methods, focusing on canvas works. This exhibition, through collaborations across various arts like visual arts, digital art, and dance, creates a harmonious blend of seemingly incompatible works. Through the "NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK" exhibition, we invite you to experience the distinctive works and collaborations of NUMAZ members firsthand. The NUMAZ WHOLESALE WEEK exhibition will run until August 27th.

name: 2023 Autumn Seoul Light DDP
summary: "Artistic Exploration of New Nature Achieved Through Digital Technology" - Seoul Light DDP
description_html:
Global pandemics and climate change have brought about significant changes in our daily lives. We have grown accustomed to encountering artificial nature within residential and commercial spaces, and through devices equipped with video systems like TVs and smartphones, we experience virtual nature on screens. As a result, our desire for a real nature has been fulfilled. Virtual Reality (VR) has also enabled us to immerse ourselves in vivid nature experiences within virtual spaces previously only accessible in reality.

In 2023, Seoul Light DDP began with the question, "Can real nature, which has existed since the beginning, coexist with the technological nature created by humans?"

Our current focus is exploring the "sensation of coexistence," where humans and nature coexist in harmony instead of attempting to control or dominate nature. By harnessing the power of 'light (projection),' which is one of the earliest phenomena in the world, achieved through scientific technology, we have curated an encounter with nature using advanced technology. We aim to transcend the sense of coexistence and evoke the profound feeling of biophilia – a deep affection and love for nature.

name: Kim Byung-gu Solo Exhibition: 7 am Green pew
summary: Pause for a moment and immerse yourself in the presence of artworks that capture the essence of both existence and non-existence within 7 am Green pew
description_html:
One early morning in early April, while strolling in the corner of Paju as usual, I unexpectedly came across a certain scenery.

The dense fog gradually cleared, revealing a place filled with dew-covered grass awakening from sleep, permeating the air with freshness. The sounds of footsteps on the ground and leaves rustling harmonized. Finding a space where I could be free brought me great joy.

Since then, I found myself returning to that spot even when the grass grew wildly uncontrollable during the torrential rains of the monsoon season or when the snow piled up thickly.

Around the middle of April, a week with the most rapid changes occurs there. The same plants grow in different locations each year, and accordingly, the impressions of the place change each time. Although they quickly disappeared, it was an attempt to capture the most beautiful week.

Pause for a moment and immerse yourself in the presence of artworks that capture the essence of both existence and non-existence within 7 am Green pew.

name: GanaArt Collection Permanent Exhibition《80 Urban Reality》
summary: This exhibition showcases the GanaArt collection and the Seoul Museum of Art collections under the keyword 'urban reality and urban people in the 1980s'.
description_html: The curated exhibition 《80 Urban Reality》 in the GanaArt Collection at the Seoul Museum of Art explores the realities surrounding cities in the 1980s from various perspectives through the collection and artworks. The 1980s in Korean society marked a significant era of rapid industrialization and economic growth, ushering in a new phase of urbanization. During that time, artists had their own attitudes towards cities and created various artworks reflecting their perspectives. This exhibition is organized into three sub-themes: ‘The Other Side of Urbanization,' 'Urbanites,' and 'Beyond Urban Surroundings: Origin of Life,' based on a common thematic consciousness that runs through the exhibited works. Through the artists' perspectives from that era, we hope this exhibition provides an opportunity to empathize with the realities of that time and contemplate their significance in our present lives.

name: Diffusione
summary: Park Eunsun's new work, Colonna Infinita, features a lighting installation composed of various colored marble beads, forming a pillar-shaped light artwork.
description_html:
Park Eunsun, as an artist, primarily engages in works where he breaks and stacks marble slabs of two different colors and alternately or repetitively constructs unit structures in cylinders or spheres that extend endlessly toward the sky. His geometric and abstract sculptures, reaching infinitely towards the sky, demonstrate humanity’s boundless potential. Simultaneously, through the cracks in the marble slabs, his works symbolize the inner wounds of the human condition. By alternating and stacking these fractured marble slabs, Park Eunsun expresses the process of healing and reconciliation, where wounded hearts come together.


The cracks in Park Eun-sun's artworks embody his distinctive sculptural characteristic and are the central philosophy behind his creations. This is precisely why his sculptures have captivated the hearts of people worldwide. While Western sculptors often aimed to represent marble in its natural state as a solid mass, Park Eunsun's unique approach involves cutting and stacking layers of marble. These cracks also serve as the channels that touch our hearts. By intentionally breaking the strong marble and juxtaposing rough and smooth stones and stones of different colors within a single artwork, Park Eunsun's creations reflect the artist's experiences of striving fiercely to survive in a foreign country.


It is said that art reaches a higher level of completeness when there is a harmonious unity between form and ideology, and when the spirit idealizes nature and creates a faithful image of itself. Park Eunsun's works, which evoke images of ancient Egyptian obelisks or traditional stone towers in Korea, transcend time and cultural boundaries, achieving the perfect harmony between the ancient and the modern, the East and the West. These works have been born beautiful masterpieces, representing the artist perfectly internally and externally.


Park Eunsun's new work, Colonna Infinita, features a lighting installation composed of various colored marble beads, forming a pillar-shaped light artwork. With the subtitle diffusion, these works aim to convey a message of hope, particularly during the challenging times of the COVID-19 pandemic. They symbolize the infinite hope that lies ahead, offering us a message of boundless optimism for the future.


The upcoming Park Eunsun exhibition at Stellar Gallery is the artist's first solo exhibition in five years in South Korea. It serves as a celebration of the artist's world, past achievements, and honors. The exhibition will showcase Park Eunsun's works, which contain messages of infinite human potential, unity, and hope.

name: Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
summary: Harmony Between East & West, Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
description_html: Built in the 1970s, this two-story detached house was remodeled in 1986 by Kim Joong-up, who added exotic elements to every corner of the house based on traditional Korean architecture. This is a place where you can get a glimpse of the housing culture of the middle class at the time, and was designated as a Seoul Future Heritage in 2017. The KimJoong-up House of Architectural Culture harmoniously integrates Korean and Western architectural styles. The second-floor living room has an umul-maru, rafter structure, and windows covered with changhoji paper, which are mainly used in hanok, but with a modern interpretation. In contrast, the bathroom was designed in a European style. The dry bathroom with a dressing room attached, something that wasn’t common in Korea during the '70s and '80s, has a vintage jade-colored interior that stands out. Stepping out to the elegantly decorated garden, a water element, a characteristic of Kim Joong-up's architecture, is located on one side of the yard. Even equipped with its own small greenhouse, the Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture contains immense nature in the garden.

name: National Meteorological Museum of Korea
summary: It is the first meteorological science and history museum that researches and preserves the meteorological culture of Korea from the Joseon Dynasty to modern times. The museum owns the world's last surviving rain gauge instrument, known as the Rain Gauge of the Chungcheonggamyeong Provincial Office, Gongju, invented 200 years earlier than the West.
description_html:
It is the first meteorological science and history museum that researches and preserves the meteorological culture of Korea from the Joseon Dynasty to modern times. The museum owns the world's last surviving rain gauge instrument, known as the Rain Gauge of the Chungcheonggamyeong Provincial Office, Gongju, invented 200 years earlier than the West.
The Seoul Meteorological Observatory (52 Songwol-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul), where the National Meteorological Museum was established, is the center of Korea's modern and contemporary meteorological history. The modern meteorological observation started in Wonnam-dong, Gyeongseong, in 1907 and moved to Songwol-dong via Nakwon-dong. The building at the time of its establishment in 1932 and extension in 1939 have been maintained and served as the Korea Meteorological Administration until the administration moved to Dongjak-gu, Seoul, in 1998. For this continuity, it was selected as a ‘100-year observatory’ by the World Meteorological Organization in 2017. In 2016, when the museum was being built, the Seoul Meteorological Observatory was restored to its original form based on the architectural drawings of the 20th-century meteorological station kept at the National Archives. Please enjoy the change of weather and history at the National Meteorological Museum, the heart of Korea's meteorology.

name: Seoul Hall of Urbanism & Architecture
summary: Come share and experience in the exhibitions and events in store for the public to explore the urbanism and architecture industry while enjoying some leisure in the city.
description_html:
In honor of the 70th anniversary of the nation's liberation from Japanese rule, the Seoul Hall of Urbanism & Architecture was erected as a part of the Sejong-daero Historic Culture Space Design Competition in the very spot where the annex to the tax office during the Japanese Occupation, one of the last remnants of the period, once stood. The competition had been held as a social contribution project to help restore the historical significance of the location. As Korea's very first urbanism and architecture specialized exhibition hall, it houses a total area of 2,998 m², spread between the first floor down to the third floor basement level. The first floor is comprised of a citizen's space, or public area, while the lower three basement levels are home to extensive galleries and have an underground walkway connecting with Seoul Citizens Hall. In accordance with Seoul's process of urban development and vision for the future, the hall is intended to be a platform for the urbanism and architecture industry so as to promote the value and public awareness of the industry as a cultural asset. Additionally, the hall is sought to bolster the city's capacities on a global scale as a metropolis with a ten million-plus population through becoming that of an influential city, as well as through an exchange of policy and culture. Being grounded in the aim to also establish the hall as both a communal and cultural space, the hope is to encourage the understanding of Seoul's origin and background, in addition to its historical and geographical value; while also establishing the hall as a public space that enables the sharing and appreciation of the city's true significance and value as an architectural feat among both specialists and everyday people.


The Seoul Hall of Urbanism & Architecture currently operates special, permanent, and general exhibitions focused on the city, architecture, the urban environment, and policy, and runs several public programs that pertain to issues concerning the collection and archiving of such information, as well as theme-based events about the seasons, holidays, and much more.

name: Seoul Sewerage Science Museum
summary: A space centered on on-site experience comprised of a science exhibition hall that displays the history, technology, and future of the industry.
description_html: Established in 2017 to promote the history and science of sewerage, the Seoul Sewerage Science Museum is the nation's first science museum specializing in sewerage. It was constructed at the site of the Cheonggyecheon Sewage Treatment Plant, the country's first sewage disposal plant, to continue the historical significance and values of the facility. The museum is also a space that is centered on on-site experience, comprised of a science exhibition hall that displays the history, technology, and future of domestic and overseas sewerage, as well as a water reclamation center where visitors can take a look around sewerage facilities. As the center of environmental education, the Seoul Sewerage Science Museum offers various programs to teach the process of sewage purification and the significance of water.

name: Seoul Museum of Art Buk Seoul Branch
summary: A cultural communication space where the museum and park meet, and people, nature, and art live and breathe together
description_html: Opened in 2013, the Buk Seoul branch of the Seoul Museum of Art is the first and largest branch of the Seoul Museum of Art. As a contemporary art space representing northern Seoul, it is a cultural landmark where art and everyday life naturally meet. It was designed as a cultural communication space where the museum and park come together, and where people, nature, and art live and breathe in harmony. Reflecting the place name Nowon, which is derived from the meaning 'Reed Hill', the museum is located on a small hill that appears to bring the beautiful natural scenery of Suraksan and Bulamsan, once hidden behind apartment complexes, into the heart of the city. All exhibitions, except for special exhibitions, can be viewed free of charge, making it a beloved and accessible destination for tourists as well.

name: 2Gil29Gallery
summary: 2Gil29 Gallery, located in Garosu Gil
description_html:
Located in the vibrant Garosu-gil area of Sinsa-dong, Gangnam, where diverse interests and dynamic Seoul culture converge, 2Gil29 Gallery has been actively introducing contemporary art to the public since its opening in 2015. The gallery has fostered active exchanges with prominent Korean artists such as Hong Jung-hee, Choi Sun-ho, Nam June Paik, Lim Young-kyun, and Kang Suk-young while also showcasing works by artists like Kwon Young-ho and Charlie Han to diversify the Korean art market.

The gallery’s curatorial approach is based on a wide range of creative works, fostering a more positive and progressive discourse on art. Through deeper communication and interaction with art, it transcends mere visual and auditory engagement, offering meaningful aesthetic and spiritual exchanges with artists. This, in turn, enhances the value of their creative endeavors.

In addition, 2Gil29 Gallery is committed to discovering and nurturing emerging talents such as upcycling artist Hong Ji-hee, singer-turned-painter Yoo Hyun-suk, and Kwon Jae-hyuk, a graduate of the University of the Arts London (UAL).

name: Kimdaljin Art Archives & Museum
summary: "Art Posters Outliving Their Exhibitions"
description_html:
All posters featured in the exhibition:

  

  ○ Have been archived within the museum after either being donated, or created on museum grounds

  ○ Encapsulate a form of artistry that appeals primarily to the human senses 

  ○ Maintain significant usability as a visual symbol that beckons memories of the past, as well as history

  ○ Offer a chance for expo-goers to further expand their view of cultural history through provided commentary that pinpoints the artistic significance of each poster


The Kimdaljin Art Archives & Museum opens its exhibition, Art Posters Outliving Their Exhibitions, which is grounded in the idea of the "art poster." As the oldest form of media used to market and advertise for exhibitions and galleries within the art community, the art poster is something that, once a certain period has passed, loses its practical use, leaving only its artistic and archival value intact. Especially for a solo exhibition, art posters are viewed prior to works displayed at an exhibition and uniquely function as the first impression of the artist among the public.

name: Arario Gallery Seoul
summary: The Arario Gallery is one of Seoul's renowned art galleries. New or prominent, Korean or international, the gallery exhibits the best there is.
description_html:
Over the years, Arario Gallery Seoul has led the way in curating a harmonic fusion and variety of different art forms in Korea's art community through bold collaborations with international artistry that have never been attempted before. Also, the gallery takes the forefront in introducing artwork from today's more modern Korean artists having implemented an ongoing and structured system of exclusively-contracted artists. Currently, a wide range of artworks from artists native to India and Southeast Asia, who have yet to come to Korea despite having already experienced China's art community, are finally getting some spotlight in Korea. What's better is that with the help of continued promotional activity, the search and funding for up-and-coming talent in the respective regions is ongoing as well. Thanks to the gallery's efforts grounded in a system of exclusive artists displaying excellence; various collaborations with other galleries, both at home and abroad; introductions of varied artworks from numerous places around the world; and more, the Arario Gallery is set to play out its role as Asia's signature gallery that expands upon the possibilities for the future of Korea's art community while leading the market as well.


Since its first opening in Sogyeok-dong, Jongno-gu, in 2006, Arario Gallery Seoul has been leading the contemporary art scene based on its solid artist system and bold exhibition planning capabilities. name: Seoul Museum of Art (Seosomun Main Building)
summary: A leading public art museum in Seoul, offering a variety of exhibitions and cultural programs centered around contemporary art.
description_html:
The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) opened in 1988 and has earned a reputation as one of Korea’s leading art venues with a series of world-famous exhibitions. Situated in the center of Seoul, its convenient location and outstanding collections attract large numbers of locals and tourists. The specially-designed building features large windows that fill the interior with natural light. This attracts not only tourists but also artists and even movie directors, some of whom have used the location for filming.


Since it was established in 1988, the main museum building has been relocated to Seosomun-dong in Seoul. The museum has a variety of annexes such as SeMA Gyeonghuigung, located on the historic site of Gyeonghuigung Palace, and the Nam Seoul Annex Building, which is situated in a building that was once the Belgian Embassy. The museum also runs the Naji Art Studio which offers workshops and financial support to new generations of Korean artists to nurture their creativity.


The beautiful Renaissance façade which forms the entrance to the museum was originally part of the Supreme Court, built in 1928. Today it is better known as the iconic image of the Seoul Museum of Art. In March 2006, the arch and the beautifully constructed museum building were designated as Cultural Property No. 237 in recognition of their great historical and architectural value.
