name: Leeum Museum of Art
summary: Leeum Museum of Art is the perfect place to enjoy traditional and contemporary art created by Korean and international artists.
description_html:
The Leeum Museum of Art is the perfect place to enjoy traditional and contemporary art created by Korean and international artists. Most of the exhibits on display at the museum are based on the large collection of the founder, the late Lee Byeong-cheol, once president of the Samsung Group. Three world-renowned architects, Maria Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas, were commissioned to design the outstanding museum complex. The name Leeum is the acronym of the family name of its founder, “Lee” and an abbreviated word for museum, “um”. The museum is composed of three individual buildings linked together as a composite complex. Museum 1 showcases traditional Korean arts and crafts such as calligraphy, ceramic arts and metal craft work, while Museum 2 displays dynamic modern and contemporary art by domestic and international artists, this section includes the Samsung Child Education & Cultural Center which offers cultural education for children.  In the museum basement, a sunken garden and Gabion wall, which is a cylindrical metal container filled with stones, can be found. Art, architecture and nature exist together in perfect harmony.





Frequently Asked Questions about Leeum Museum of Art
Do I need to make a reservation to visit the Leeum Museum of Art?
Leeum Museum of Art operates under a reservation system. Reservations can be made 14 days before the visit. The maximum number of people per reservation is four. On-site ticketing is possible and limited to remaining tickets per reservation time (As of 2025)
Is the Leeum Museum of Art digital guide available for free?
Digital guides that automatically provide explanations when one approaches the exhibits can be borrowed free of charge. The devices are available to elementary school students and anyone older. You must present an identification card such as a passport or resident registration card. The digital guide is available in Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese. (As of 2025)
Can I visit the Leeum Museum of Art permanent exhibitions for free?
Yes. Permanent exhibitions are free. They are also operated under a reservation system, so please make a reservation before visiting. (As of 2025)

name: National Folk Museum of Korea
summary: Exhibits Korean culture and folk history from prehistoric times to the late Joseon Dynasty
description_html: The National Folk Museum of Korea displays the culture and folk history of the Korean people from prehistoric times to the end of the Joseon Dynasty. Since its establishment, the museum has dedicated itself to studying and researching the folk history of Korea, and collecting artifacts from different Korean regions in order to pass on an insight into the lifestyle and culture of Koreans. The museum achieves this by offering visitors various seminars, exhibitions, performance art, concerts and hands-on activities.   Located on the grounds of Gyeongbokgung Palace, the National Folk Museum of Korea is well known for its beautiful architecture. The building was constructed in the traditional Korean style comprising several stories with a pagoda on top. The three main exhibition halls at the museum cover different aspects of Korean life, as well as displaying various local costumes, musical instruments and festivals.

name: Itaewon Books
summary: Seoul's oldest secondhand foreign bookstore
description_html:
Itaewon Books, which has been around since 1973, is the oldest foreign used bookstore in Seoul. It was founded in 1967 by a U.S. military unit that collected and delivered used books to bookstores and operated a stall with leftover books. At the time, foreign books were rare, especially those in color. A few years later, in 1973, he opened his own bookstore, where he has remained for over 40 years. It mainly deals with used books in English and American languages, and its categories are as diverse as a large bookstore, including poetry, fiction, philosophy, psychology, travel, religion, dictionaries, and history.

 

• This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

name: Seongwoo Barbershop
summary: A barbershop that has kept its place for over a century
description_html:
Seongwoo Barbershop is the oldest barbershop in Seoul, opened around 1927 and passed down through three generations of the family. It has remained in the same location for nearly 100 years and still retains its traditional culture. They pride themselves on using only scissors and combs to give each customer a haircut that best suits their head and face shape. Seongwoo Barbershop was transformed into its current form through a project supported by the Seoul Metropolitan Government to prevent the loss and damage of Seoul's future heritage after the building collapsed due to a typhoon in 2019.

name: HONGIKMUNGO
summary: A popular hangout in Sinchon and Seoul's oldest bookstore
description_html:
Hongik Books started as a street vendor in 1957 and has become a Sinchon landmark for over 60 years, making it South Korea's oldest bookstore. It was once a popular meeting spot in Sinchon. The bookstore moved to its current building in 1978, initially using only the first and second floors, and expanded to occupy the entire building in 1984. Now in its second generation of family operation, Hongik Books takes its name from the Hongik Ingan philosophy, which means "to benefit humanity broadly." The bookstore is dedicated to serving customers, partners, employees, and family. In front of Hongik Books is "Literary Street," which features the handprints of 15 prominent Korean writers and hosts romantic street piano concerts.

name: Tongmungwan
summary: The Korea’s oldest bookstore with national treasure-level cultural artifacts
description_html:
Tongmungwan is an old bookstore that opened in 1934, and has been opening for three generations. It is a bookstore that discovers, evaluates, analyzes, distributes, and publishes ancient Korean books, and has discovered numerous cultural assets such as "Wolin Seokbo" and "Independent Newspaper." It is currently run by Lee Jong-un, the grandson of founder and first director Lee Geom-ro. The main customers are those who study and study ancient books, collectors who invest in the value of ancient books, and Japanese and Chinese tourists who are familiar with Chinese characters, according to the commission.

name: Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street
summary: Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street, located in Jongno, a central district of Seoul, is well known nationwide. It is estimated to house between 2,000 and 4,000 jewelry stores of every size and packed close together in one district.
description_html:
Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street, located in Jongno, a central district of Seoul, is well known nationwide. It is estimated to house between 2,000 and 4,000 jewelry stores of every size and packed close together in one district. Jongno district has always had a large floating population and has been a well-developed commercial area since olden times. The jewelry street in its current form has existed since the 1960s. Even though the area has repeatedly undergone major changes to its academic and entertainment venues, the jewelry street continues to be as lively as ever. At present, about 70 percent of the domestic jewelry market is traded on Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street.


The first thing that catches the eye is the number of wholesale and retail stores lining the street (Jongnodaero), which now form a new commercial zone in the area. Here, customers can purchase jewelry at around 20 to 40 percent cheaper than market prices, since most stores have close connections with jewelry-makers and can lower prices. Proof of this is the number of gold-and-silver workshops nearby, in an area slightly bigger than 3.3 square meters. Jewelry Street is especially popular with lovers and soon-to-be-married couples, and overseas tourists frequently visit looking for Korean jewelry at low prices.

description_html: Kwanchenru Street is an unofficial cultural district located in Myeong-dong that is home to incredible Chinese restaurants and stores. Kwanchenru is the Chinese pronunciation of the Korean word "gwancheonga", which means the street in front of a government office. At one of end of Kwanchenru is the Chinese Embassy. Authentic, delicious Chinese food can be had here and there are several famous restaurants here such as Din Tai Fung. There are also several shops selling Chinese antiques, souvenirs, and books. summary: Many visitors trek from afar in order to search for limited editions and rare books, nostalgic of the smell of ink and the increasingly rare sight of books piled from floor to ceiling, wall to wall.
description_html:
Book Street at the Peace Market


When you hear "Dongdaemun" you may immediately think of the Doosan Tower and the Migliore Fashion Mall, or you may not. Upon close inspection, Dongdaemun is easily one of the most difficult places to categorize in Seoul. New shopping alleys are spawning around the vicinity, alley to street, street to alley. The Cheonggyecheon Peace Market's Secondhand Book Street is one of these hidden jewels. Growing steadily since the 1960s, many collectioners trek from afar in order to search for limited editions and rare books, nostalgic of the smell of ink and the increasingly rare sight of books piled from floor to ceiling, wall to wall.


One Man's Trash is Another's Treasure
Living history seems to seep out of these books that can be found here. Limited editions of Korean masterpieces, hard to find foreign comics and magazines, and even stores specializing in design and home interiors can be found here. Some of the stores are so small and so full of books that you will most likely be shoulder-to-shoulder with other bibliophiles searching for lost treasures. You could easily spend hours just looking at titles here until an entire day has gone by. In general, prices for books cost 30% lower than elsewhere. Of course, price will also depend on the condition and the rarity of the item you are seeking to purchase.

name: Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market
summary: Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market is famous for its “dokkaebi sale” held three times a week. The market sells various agricultural and marine products, including fruits and vegetables at low prices, attracting many shoppers.
description_html:
Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market is famous for its “dokkaebi sale” held three times a week. The market sells various agricultural and marine products, including fruits and vegetables at low prices, attracting many shoppers. In particular, the market offers great value bargains in sales leading up to New Year's Day and Chuseok (Korean harvest festival). The market has 87 stores and 13 street vendors equipped with modern facilities, making it a convenient place to browse.  The origin of the market dates back to 1982 when unlicensed street vendors began gathering here one by one, selling their goods in the evenings to avoid police patrols. Whenever officers came to the market to crack down, the vendors would disappear in an instant, earning the nickname, “dokkaebi”. Dokkaebi is a mythical being that appears in many old Korean folktales and is similar to a hobgoblin. During the early 2000s, the market faced crisis and risk of closure when a number of major discount supermarkets opened. In spite of this, since the market was renovated in 2004 it has grown to become one of the busiest traditional markets. 


Many items in Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market are priced 30 to 40 percent cheaper than in the major supermarkets. In the middle of the market, displays of the most popular items can be found in every shop at 20 to 30 percent cheaper. The market also holds huge bargain sales before the festive seasons.  Traditional Korean banchan (side dishes) can be purchased at very reasonable prices in Banchan stores. It is very common to see overseas visitors in the market buying different types of banchan. These include Kimchi and Tteok, traditional Korean cakes. The market also has sections for fruit and vegetables, seafood and meat. Cosmetics and confectionery are also sold in the market at cheap prices. Seafood and meat are delivered directly from their place of origin, so customers can be sure they are buying fresh produce.

name: Garosu-gil Road
summary: Garosu-gil has quickly became one of Seoul's hottest neighborhoods in recent years.
description_html:
Garosu-gil has quickly became one of Seoul's hottest neighborhoods in recent years. 20 years ago, this place was once a densely populated area filled with galleries and packed with designer shops. At one point, many film companies spotted the area, and at other times, various artists set up shop here. So there plenty of neat, older shops in the Garosu-gil area. Additionally, there are many fashion stores that have become quite popular. The stores in the area are diverse, from antique furniture stores to bookstores selling foreign books. It is also a good walking area. It's also very easy for visitors to come across their new favorite cafes while strolling around the neighborhood. In addition to clothing stores, visitors can find plenty of exhibitions and galleries to check out.

name: Dongdaemun Shopping Complex and Shopping Town
summary: Opened in 1970, Dongdaemun Shopping Complex is the largest single market in Asia as well as one of the oldest with over 40 years of history.
description_html:
Opened in 1970, Dongdaemun Shopping Complex is the largest single market in Asia as well as one of the oldest with over 40 years of history. In 1985 Dongdaemun Shopping Town was added to the complex bringing the total to four buildings altogether (A, B, C and Shopping Town). This traditional market houses many wholesale and retail stores specializing in various fabrics, materials, accessories, and wedding products. As much as eighty percent of all the fabric traded in Korea goes through here, allowing for goods to be sold at reasonable prices. Dongdaemun Shopping Complex first opened with over 5,000 shops crammed into three separate buildings. Recently the market was extensively refurbished and extended to include outlets selling quilts, corsages and handmade toys.

  • • Food Court in Building N, Restaurant District : 07:00 ~ 18:00 (Saturday: 07:00 ~ 17:00 / Closed on Sunday)

  • • Building B, Restaurant District : 08:00 ~ 19:00 (Closed on Sundays)


※ 2nd and 4th Sundays are all closed days.

Where can I park my car when visiting Dongdaemun Market?

You can park your car in the rooftop parking lot and underground parking lot of Dongdaemun Market.

For shoppers there is a mixture of street stalls and retail outlets selling everything from high fashion to casual attire, as well as many Korean cosmetics stores offering high-quality products at competitive prices.


Myeongdong is very popular with international visitors and fills with Japanese and Chinese tourists during the holiday period known as “Golden Week” which takes place in spring and is called golden week due to the week-long holiday period that takes place in Japan and China. Part of Myeongdong’s popularity stems from relatively affordable prices here, especially compared to the other shopping meccas of Apgujeong-dong and Cheongdam-don g.

name: Nagwon Instrument Arcade
summary: Wind instruments, string instruments, percussion, pianos, electric instruments, amps, speakers, karaoke machines, audio equipment, and other music equipment can be found there.
description_html:
Nagwon Instrument Arcade has traditionally been Korea's largest collection of music stores and is very close to Insa-dong. The second and third floors of the Nagwon building has a few hundred music stores clustered together. Wind instruments, string instruments, percussion, pianos, electric instruments, amps, speakers, karaoke machines, audio equipment, and other music equipment can be found there. Countless people are there to sell or repair instruments for beginners and experts alike.


Built in 1968, the Nagwon building is a uniquely constructed pillar based complex. On the first floor, there are hundreds of pillars with a four lane road going through them and a market below. Above the shopping area, there are apartments. On the fourth floor, there's a theater that used to premiere films and was called the 'Hollywood Theater'. Now, it has turned into the 'Seoul Art Cinema' and 'dance musical private theater' which play 'Silver Theater' films for senior citizens, independent films, and other specialty films.

name: Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street
summary: The street is packed with home and foreign brand-name stores targeting all ages from teenagers to the older generations and offering good quality products at very moderate prices.
description_html:
Located at subway line 8 Munjeong station, Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street is considered to be Korea's first outlet shopping district. The street began when shops selling off excess clothing stock opened here one by one. After walking about 500 meters from exit 1 of Munjeong Station, a cowboy statue first welcomes visitors. From here, the 2.5 kilometers of Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street begin, also known as the first fashion avenue.  Both sides of the street are full with over 200 brand-name shops, making it easy to browse several famous brands at once. Always popular with shoppers are the 100 individual shops, as well as the multi-fashion malls such as Modes, Dump etc. or the outlet shops such as Cheil Industries Inc. and LG Fashion. 


When you start to feel tired from shopping, Zelkova Park, situated just behind Munjeong-dong Office is the perfect place to take a rest. The park has a 600-year-old zelkova tree and provides refreshing rest areas. There are many restaurants, cafes, amusement arcades, food courts etc. located nearby, providing lots of interesting things to see, do and eat.  As the nation's oldest outlet street, various festivals and cultural events are frequently held on Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street.

summary: Mangwon Market is a traditional market in Seoul
description_html: Mangwon Market, which has been around for over 40 years, is a traditional market in Seoul where visitors can fill their stomachs with delicious food at a low price. Visitors at the market should seek out Q's Dakgangjeong, which sells various kinds of chicken gangjeong, including spicy chicken gangjeong and fruit dakgangjeong, as well as Hwanginho Croquette, which sells spicy croquettes and donuts, which are famous at Mangwon Market. In addition to these options, there are many food items that are unique to Mangwon Market such as various snacks, tteokgalbi, and traditional alcohol. There are many restaurants to choose from, so it has become known as a hot spot in Mangwon-dong, which is commonly visited by many people in their 20s and 30s. Mangwon Hangang Park is also nearby, so it's recommended to pack delicious food from the market and then enjoy a picnic in the park. A paradise of cheap and varied food! Let's visit Mangwon Market.

name: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street
summary: The first place in Korea to sell antique furniture.
description_html: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street is the first place in Korea to sell antique furniture. Back in the 60s, American soldiers would put out their furniture and sell them on the street before they headed back home to the US, leading to the formation of Itaewon Antique Furniture Street. At the present, there's close to 100 stores selling and renting out vintage and antique furniture. After Chungmuro, it's the next most frequented place by people working in the film and advertising industry. Hosting an "Itaewon Antique Festival" every October and "Weekend Flea Market" every weekend, this street is always attracting new visitors. It's a must-visit place for those interested in walking through a medieval European-like street in Seoul.

name: Seoul Folk Flea Market
summary: Korea’s largest flea market. Shop owners sell the second-hand goods which they gathered with efforts from everywhere.
description_html:
Seoul Folk Flea Market is the largest flea market in Korea. The market sells typical Korean items, everyday goods, souvenirs, traditional goods and traditional food, allowing visitors to enjoy shopping and eating all under one roof. These days, the market has become one of the city's main attractions among local people as well as overseas visitors. Seoul Folk Flea Market is filled with Korean traditional goods and foods that reflect the simpler lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market  opened in April 2008 and is a place alive with typical Korean folk items, souvenirs, traditional food and everyday goods that reveal the lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market holds performances of "Pungmulpae" (pungmul band, traditional Korean percussion band) all year round. Regional specialties and traditional and modern crafts are also bought and sold here. In this two-story building, everyday miscellaneous goods, antiques and clothing are found on the first floor, and restaurants are situated on the second floor. 


Seoul Folk Flea Market is divided into seven zones; red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet, the colors of rainbow. The red zone is a food court. The orange zone is for regional specialties such as squid from Ulleungdo Island, traditional crafts like crockery, and bits and bobs such as smoking pipes etc. The yellow zone deals with secondhand vintage goods, such as typewriters, telephones etc. The green zone is for antiques, such as traditional antique furniture and art. The blue zone sells fashion accessories and the indigo zone sells clothing, paintings, calligraphy, hanji (traditional handmade Korean paper) and so on. name: Seoul Yangnyeong Market

description_html:
Seoul Yangnyeong Market is one of the most famous oriental medicine markets in Korea. The market slowly started to establish itself in the late 1960s when small medicinal herbs stores started opening one by one. Today, the market has grown to become the nation's largest oriental medicine market, and 70 percent of the oriental medicine traded in Korea goes through here. Because the market is able to minimize distribution costs, the medicinal herbs sold here cost around 30 percent cheaper than elsewhere.


When you enter Seoul Yangnyeong Market, you are immediately struck by the unique fragrances of oriental medicine. All Korean medicinal herbs can be found here including several types of ginseng, dates, milk vetch roots, as well as a variety of herbal medicine preparations for maintaining good health. More than 800 oriental medicine shops and clinics are located in this area.

name: Gwangjang Market
summary: Gwangjang Market is one of Korea's largest traditional markets and is renowned for its quality silk goods, linen bedding and hand-made goods.
description_html:
As one of the most vibrant traditional markets in Seoul, Gwangjang Market is based in the center of the city so it can easily be located by even first-time visitors. This historic market opened in the early 20th century and is home to a number of clothing and food stalls, offering tourists a taste of traditional Korean cuisine. Starting with "addictive gimbap," one of Koreans’ all-time favorite snacks, and nokdujeon (mung bean pancake), visitors can sample a range of Korean delicacies. Other traditional treats such as tteok-bokki (stir-fried rice cake) and eomuk (fish cake) are also available. It is worth visiting the food stalls since most dishes are reasonably priced. If you have a keen interest in clothing, we recommend that you visit the hanbok stores and vintage clothing shops on the 2nd floor. 


Frequently Asked Questions about Gwangjang Market

What is the famous food in Gwangjang Market?

Favorite foods at Gwangjang Market include Bindae-tteok (Mung Bean Pancake,) Modum-jeon (Assorted Savory Pancakes,) Mayak Gimbab, Sundae (Korean Sausage) and Head Meat, Yukhoe (Beef Tartare ), and Korean style meatballs.

Where can I park my car when visiting Gwangjang Market?

When visiting Gwangjang Market, please use the Jongno 4-ga Jongmyo parking lot.

Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting Gwangjang Market?

There are the following tourist attractions around Gwangjang Market.

  • • Sewoon Shopping Center

  • • Jongmyo Shrine

  • • Dongdaemun Design Plaza

name: Namdaemun Market
summary: Namdaemun Market is the largest traditional market in Korea with over 10,000 stores that line the streets around Namdaemun (Gate), the main southern gate of the old city wall.
description_html:
Namdaemun Market is the largest traditional market in Korea with over 10,000 stores that line the streets around Namdaemun (Gate), the main southern gate of the old city wall. Namdaemun Market first started under the reign of King Taejong (1367 – 1422, the third Joseon king) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392 – 1910), when the government built shops around Namdaemun and rented out the shops to traders. It boasts one of the largest distribution structures in Korea, providing local products, daily living essentials, food products, medical supplies and more to retailers and consumers across the country.


Due to the wholesale nature of the market, shoppers can comparison shop for the lowest prices on all sorts of goods. Namdaemun Market is also packed with interesting things to see and eat, making it a popular destination for both locals and international visitors alike. So whether you’re looking for traditional oriental medicine or imported drugs, traditional Korean food or imported snacks, hanbok attire or a Halloween costume, Namdaemun Market is the place to go.


Namdaemun Market is renowned for its vast size and the variety of goods it offers. With the exception of construction materials, the market sells nearly every item under the sun including clothing, food, living essentials, etc. So it comes as no surprise that Namdaemun Market is always bustling day and night. Retailers from all over the nation flock to the market at night and local consumers flock to the market during the day. Many tourists come during the day as well to experience the charm of a traditional Korean market. The market's success is largely due to its independent distribution system. Although the shops are small, most of them produce the goods they offer themselves, allowing for customers to purchase goods directly from the manufacturers at wholesale prices.

The nearest subway station to Namdaemun Market is Hoehyeon(Namdaemun Market) Station (Subway Line 4).

Namdaemun Market is open from 00:00 to 23:00 on weekdays, and opening hours may vary per stall.

Namdaemun Market has the following tourist attractions.

  • • Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun)

name: Dongdaemun Market
summary: Dongdaemun Market is a large commercial district comprised of traditional markets and shopping centers that covers the entire area around Dongdaemun Gate, a prominent landmark in Korea.
description_html:
Dongdaemun Market is a large commercial district comprised of traditional markets and shopping centers that covers the entire area around Dongdaemun Gate, a prominent landmark in Korea. It is Korea’s largest wholesale and retail shopping district, featuring 26 shopping malls, 30,000 speciality shops, and 50,000 manufacturers. All kinds of goods can be found here including silks and fabric, clothes, shoes and accessories, electronics, leather goods, sporting goods, office supplies, pet products, and toys.

Although Dongdaemun Market is traditionally famous for its night market, this popular shopping district attracts hordes of shoppers and tourists at all times of day. Like Namdaemun Market, Dongdaemun Market sells a variety of products, but unlike Namdaemun Market, it is open 24-hours a day. The powerful appeal of Dongdaemun Market stems from the fact that you can buy everything you need at a reasonable price, in one convenient location and at anytime. Most major wholesalers and retailers are here along with specialist outlets focusing on the youth market, making Dongdaemun Market the best place to find the latest fashions at bargain prices. Dongdaemun’s famous food alley, Mukja Golmok, is also essential for anyone wanting to check out the latest trends in Korean cuisine.

In addition to selling everything under the sun, large shopping malls such as Good Morning City and Freya add an extra dimension to the shopping experience with their own multiplex cinemas, while Doota features a huge outdoor concert hall hosting a range of events including outdoor fashion shows, concerts, modeling contests and classical Korean music for tourists.

name: Dongmyo Flea Market
summary: Dongmyo Flea Flea Market started life in the late 1980s.
description_html:

The main items bought and sold here are antiques of every type, including items such as wallets, electronics, old books, film posters etc. Recently vintage clothing and shoes have become the main area of interest. Prices are normally around 1,000 won, but leather items or furs reach around 10,000 won. Designer labels can reach over 100,000 won. The best time for shopping is on weekend afternoons.

name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
summary: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market is the best place in Seoul to get fresh seafood at competitive prices.
description_html: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market (or Noryangjin Fish Market for short) is the best place in Seoul to get fresh seafood at competitive prices. The market is both a wholesale outlet, trading in daily catches that arrive from every possible location, and also a retail market, where the public can get seafood at very low prices. The market is easily reached since it is conveniently connected to the subway station. The market is the largest fish market in Seoul. There are many restaurants ready to slice any fish bought at the market into hoe (raw fish) for their customers. During lunch and supper times, the market is bustling with customers browsing for fresh seafood. Nearby restaurants are ready to slice the fish that customers buy directly from the market into hoe. The usual arrangement is that the customer pays the fishmonger for the fish and the restaurant owner for the side dishes, vegetables or sauces. Daily auctions also take place from 1 am to 4 am. Among merchants, competition is fierce to get the freshest seafood, and tourists as well as citizens of Seoul like to come down to see this unusual scene. It is great fun to see and taste a wide range of seafood at the market, and everything bought and sold here comes fresh from the ocean.

description_html:
Dongwha Duty Free Shop, opened in 1973, is the oldest duty-free shop in the heart of Seoul. The shop features around 250 of the world’s most famous brands such as Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Bvlgari, Salvatore Ferragamo and Ermenegildo Zegna, and over 300,000 different imported goods are on display and sale. 

Dongwha Duty Free Shop is a convenient place for international tourists to enjoy sightseeing and shopping. It is within easy reach of the ancient palaces of Gyeongbokgung and Deoksugung (from the era of the Joseon Dynasty), and tourist attractions such as the Seoul Museum of Art and Cheonggyecheon (a stream running through Seoul and popular as a waterside walking route), making it the ideal place to enjoy both shopping and sightseeing at the same time.

The first floor features traditional Korean products including Korean ginseng, red ginseng, dried laver and kimchi (a traditional fermented Korean dish, made of vegetables with varied seasonings). In addition, there are various Korean cosmetics brands, and separate alpine clothing and jeans counters.  They also carry wide variety of imported designer brands, such as Rolex, Omega, Gucci, Dior, Hermès and Celine, and is divided into different sections, such as a watches, sunglasses, bags, including LeSportsac and Furla, accessories & jewelry including Swarovski and Tateossian. However, visitors should note that there are no liquor or tobacco products in the shop.

name: Garden of Gratitude
summary: A space to reflect upon the gratitude toward Korean War veterans, as well as the achievements and prosperity of the Republic of Korea.
description_html: Newly established in Gwanghwamun Square, the Garden of Gratitude is a space designed to reflect upon the gratitude toward Korean War veterans and the achievements and prosperity of the Republic of Korea, which has transitioned from an aid-recipient country to a donor country. The "Light of Gratitude 23" comprises 23 symbolic sculptures situated quietly yet magnificently at the center of Gwanghwamun Square. It stands as a symbol of the deepest respect and gratitude dedicated to the noble devotion of the participating nations that willingly extended their hands to safeguard the freedom and peace of the Republic of Korea. "Freedom Hall," situated underground at Gwanghwamun Square, is an immersive multimedia space where visitors can multi-dimensionally experience the sentiments of freedom, sacrifice, peace, and gratitude toward the nations that participated in the Korean War.

name: Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path
summary: A serene stone wall path stretches along the west wall of Jongmyo Shrine
description_html: The Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path is a tranquil walkway that stretches along the western wall of Jongmyo Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Unlike well-known historical and cultural spots like Bukchon and Insadong, this pathway is a hidden gem that has recently gained popularity. Strolling along the pristine, elegant stone wall, visitors can leisurely explore nearby cafes, craft studios, and shops and cafes housed in renovated hanok buildings along the side alleys. The path is beautifully framed by the historic stone wall and lush trees, offering scenic views throughout the seasons. In spring, cherry blossoms and fresh leaves embrace the wall, creating a bright and cheerful atmosphere. In autumn, the wall is transformed into a picturesque setting draped in warm hues, perfect for a romantic walk. This peaceful spot offers an ideal escape from the busy pace of everyday life. Traditional architecture and nature are in harmonious balance, providing a calming ambiance. Jongmyo Stone Wall Path is a fantastic photo spot for capturing traces of Korea’s traditional culture. Walking along the path, visitors can conveniently explore nearby attractions, such as Changgyeonggung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, Insadong, and Samcheong-dong, where tradition meets modernity, allowing for a well-rounded cultural experience.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace Jibokjae
summary: A pavilion located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace, used as King Gojong's study
description_html: This building is located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace. It housed about 40,000 books on Western artifacts purchased from the Qing Dynasty and was mainly used as King Gojong’s private library. Additionally, it served as a venue for enshrining portraits of kings or receiving foreign envoys. Originally constructed as a secondary building of Hamnyeongjeon Hall in Changdeokgung, it was relocated to Gyeongbokgung in 1891. The building was opened to the public in 2006, and the books previously housed there are now kept at Seoul National University's Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies and the Jangseogak Archives of the Academy of Korean Studies. In 2016, Jibokjae was transformed into a library and opened to the public. It is open from April to October, except for July and August, making it a great place to visit if you're in Gyeongbokgung during this period.

name: Cheongjeon Yi Sang-beom House
summary: Yi Sang-beom’s House located in Nuha-dong
description_html: The house and studio of Cheongjeon Yi Sang-beom, an artist recognized for pioneering new directions in Korean Southern School painting, are located west of Gyeongbokgung in Nuha-dong. Built-in 1929, the Yi Sang-beom House is an urban hanok featuring an L-shaped main house and straight-line servant quarters. It is distinguished by its rare kitchen with a cool wooden floor. Yi lived in this small, renovated hanok in Nuha-dong for 43 years. In his studio, known as Cheongjeon Hwasuk, he produced many artworks and mentored exceptional students such as Bae Ryeom and Park No-soo.

name: Gwanghwamun Square
summary: King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty moved the capital to Hanyang in 1394 and built Gyeongbokgung Palace, the official residence of the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html: King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty moved the capital to Hanyang in 1394 and built Gyeongbokgung Palace, the official residence of the Joseon Dynasty. In addition, on both sides of the road in front of the palace’s main gate, the Street of Six Ministries, including Uijeongbu (State Council), was built. It was the best road in Hanyang. In 2009, that road opened again. Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Plaza were built. The square is mostly “a square that restores the history of Gwanghwamun,” “a square that recreates the scenery of the Street of the Six Ministries,” “an emblematic square of Korea,” “an urban culture square where citizens mingle,” “a square in the city center,” and “a connection to the Cheonggyecheon Stream.” It functions as a space for history, culture, and relaxation. The focal point of this emblematic square in Korea is the statue of King Sejong the Great. The “downtown square” around the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin is also a space appreciated by city dwellers. In addition, artificial ponds and fountains are installed to cool off people from the summer heat. Also, the Haechi statue and Grass Plaza, which are symbols of Seoul, were also created.

name: Changdeokgung Secret Garden
summary: A garden of a Joseon Dynasty located inside Changdeokgung Palace
description_html: The Secret Garden (Huwon) at Changdeokgung Palace, once used for royal entertainment and ceremonies, is a significant heritage site showcasing traditional landscaping. Covering around 446,943 square meters, this expansive royal garden still has restricted areas that remain inaccessible to the public. Historically, it was off-limits to commoners, reserved only for the Joseon royal family. Nestled against Maebong Peak of Bugaksan Mountain, the garden features several ponds, including Buyongji, home to Buyongjeong Pavilion, Aeryeonji, Jangbangji, and Banwolji. The arrangement of pavilions and buildings reflects traditional Korean architecture, demonstrating a masterful harmony between structures and nature.

name: Gyeonghuigung Palace
summary: One of the five grand palaces, Gyeonghuigung Palace was also called "Seogweol" (which means "palace of the west") because it's located west of the main palace, Gyeongbokgung.
description_html:
One of the five grand palaces, Gyeonghuigung Palace was also called "Seogweol" (which means "palace of the west") because it's located west of the main palace, Gyeongbokgung. In its heyday, it was part of a vast complex, with 100 buildings in total, but most of these were destroyed during the Japanese occupation. Following intensive restoration work, it reopened to the public in 2002. On its grounds stand the Seoul Museum of History and the Gyeonghuigung Annex Building of the Seoul Museum of Art.  The palace was originally constructed by order of King Gwanghae, the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty, and was completed in 1623. From the beginning, it was much-loved and served as a secondary palace for some ten kings of the Joseon Dynasty. 

A variety of Korean art can also be seen in the Gyeonghuigung Annex building of the Seoul Museum of Art, which is situated on the Gyeonghuigung site. Also, the Seoul Museum of History, one of the foremost tourist attractions in the city, houses a permanent collection allowing visitors to see how Seoul has developed and transformed from prehistoric times to the present day.

name: Jongmyo Shrine
summary: Jongmyo is a royal shrine dedicated to the performance of ancestral rites for the deceased kings and queens of the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html: Jongmyo is a royal shrine dedicated to the performance of ancestral rites for the deceased kings and queens of the Joseon Dynasty. Being the place where the royal ancestral tablets are enshrined, Jongmyo's atmosphere is solemn and sacred rather than splendid like the royal palaces. The simple and elegant buildings of this shrine have faithfully kept their original forms since the 16th century. Jongmyo is made up of Jeongjeon (the main hall), Yeongnyeongjeon (the hall of eternal peace), and auxiliary buildings such as Jeonsacheong, Eosuksil, Hyangdaecheong and Sindang. Jeongjeon, the main hall of Jongmyo, is a place steeped in royal history and is highly esteemed for its outstanding architecture. It is said to be the world's longest single wooden structure with a length measures 109 meters. The main hall is an outstanding example of traditional Korean architecture. Jongmyo was designated as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site together with Jongmyo Jerye and Jongmyo Jeryeak. Jongmyo Jerye is the royal ancestral ritual and has been performed for 600 years. The court music performed during the ritual is the Jongmyo Jeryeak.

name: Unhyeongung Palace
summary: Unhyeongung Palace is one of Seoul's smaller palaces and it is an important historic site that is open to the public.
description_html:
Unhyeongung Palace is one of Seoul's smaller palaces and it is an important historic site that is open to the public. The palace was formerly the private residence of Emperor Gojong's father, the prince regent Heungseon Daewongun. The young Gojong lived here before he assumed the throne and his wedding to Myeongseong took place here. An annual re-enactment of the royal wedding ceremony between Emperor Gojong and Empress Myeongseong takes place here at the palace.


During the reign of Emperor Gojong, Unhyeongung was as grand as any other palace in Seoul, but over time, many of the palace buildings were heavily damaged and destroyed. Today, visitors can see what has been preserved of the palace and take part in traditional cultural activities and crafts experiences. On weekends, visitors can watch Seoulites get married in traditional Korean wedding ceremonies at the palace.

name: Changgyeonggung Palace
summary: Changgyeonggung Palace was built in 1483 by King Seongjong (the ninth king of the Joseon Dynasty) to take care of the wives of the preceding kings.
description_html:
Changgyeonggung Palace was built in 1483 by King Seongjong (the ninth king of the Joseon Dynasty) to take care of the wives of the preceding kings. Compared to other palaces, the size of the palace is compact and simple. Changgyeonggung Palaceis connected with Changdeokgung Palace. It's located east of the primary palace of Gyeongbokgung, so it is also referred to as "Donggwol," the "East Palace."

Myeongjeongjeon is the main hall of the palace, where state affairs were held, such as meetings with officials and the reception of foreign envoys. In particular, Myeongjeongjeon represents an outstanding example of seventeenth century Joseon architectural style and is the oldest main hall of any palace. While visiting Changgyeonggung Palace, it is recommended you visit nearby Changdeokgung Palace as well.

Most of the palace buildings were destroyed by the Japanese during the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592. The main buildings such as Myeongjeongjeon, Munjeongjeon (council hall), Hwangyeongjeon (Hall), Inyangjeon (Hall), Gongsacheong, and Honghwamun (Gate) were rebuilt by King Gwanghaegun (the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty). During the Japanese occupation, the Japanese built a zoo on the site and renamed the palace "Changgyeongwon," meaning "Changgyeong Garden." Since 1987, the palace has been reconstructed and now resembles its original form.

name: Changdeokgung Palace
summary: Changdeokgung Palace is also known as Donggwol, the Eastern Palace, because of its location to the east of Gyeongbokgung.
description_html:
Changdeokgung Palace is the second UNESCO World Heritage Site in Seoul. It was selected as a representative palace for its notable beauty in the history of palace architecture in East Asia and for its excellent arrangement with the surrounding naturalenvironment. Changdeokgung Palace was built by King Taejong in 1405.


During the Imjin War, Joseon lost both Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace. Reconstructed in the 2nd year of Gwanghaegun (1610), Changdeokgung was used as the royal palace of Joseon for about 270 years.


Changdeokgung Palace has two major tour programs. The first is the general tour, which is a basic tour that covers Injeongjeon (仁政殿), the main hall, and Nakseonjae (樂善齋). The second is a special tour of Howon, which runs from Buyongji, the entrance toHowon, to Okryucheon. The conservation of the ecosystem is absolutely stunning and includes various ponds and gardens.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
summary: Gyeongbokgung Palace was the first and largest of the royal palaces built during the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html:
Gyeongbokgung Palace was the first and largest of the royal palaces built during the Joseon Dynasty. Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung Palace was located at the heart of the newly appointed capital of Seoul (then known as Hanyang) and represented the sovereignty of the Joseon Dynasty. The largest of the Five Grand Palaces (the others being Gyeonghuigung Palace, Deoksugung Palace, Changgyeonggung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace), Gyeongbokgung served as the main palace of the Joseon Dynasty.


The Korean government has invested much time and effort into rebuilding, restoring, and maintaining the palace for future generations. These efforts include work to rebuild and restore the buildings that were destroyed during the Japanese occupation. Visitors to Gyeongbokgung can also visit the National Palace Museum of Korea and the National Folk Museum of Korea as they are located on the palace grounds.

 

To increase ease of accessibility from Gyeongbokgung Palace to Seochon and vice versa, the palace's western gate, Yeongchumun, was opened to the public on December 2018. For the past 43 years, there were only 3 entrances to Gyeongbokgung Palace - the southern gate Gwanghwamun, the northern gate Sinmumun, and the eastern entrance of National folk Museum of Korea. However, with the opening of the western gate Yeongchumun, entry to the palace from all directions has been now made possible.


Frequently Asked Questions about Gyeongbokgung Palace
When is Gyeongbokgung Palace closed?
Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed every Tuesday.
If a public holiday and a closed day overlap, the doors will be opened. As a result, the first non-holiday following the open holiday will be the closed day. (As of 2025)
Can I visit Gyeongbokgung Palace for free if I wear a hanbok?
Yes, you can. You can enter Gyeongbokgung Palace for free if you wear a complete hanbok.
Please refer to the guidelines regarding detailed hanbok regulations. (As of 2025)
How can I participate in the Gyeongbokgung Palace guided tour?
Groups of less than ten individuals can participate in the guided tour without reservation. Groups of 10 or more people need to make a reservation, and up to 30 people can participate in the tour. You can participate in the regular guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace without any reservations. During the tour, you'll hear the storyteller's narration as you explore the main pavilions of the palace. English tours are available daily at 11:00, 13:30, and 15:30 (except on Tuesdays.) (As of 2025)

name: Deoksugung Palace
summary: Deoksugung Palace is unique among Korean palaces in having a modern seal engraving and a western style garden and fountain.
description_html:
Deoksugung Palace is unique among Korean palaces in having a modern seal engraving and a western style garden and fountain. Medieval and modern style architecture exists together in harmony in Deoksugung Palace. The Changing of the Royal Guard can be seen in front of Daehanmun (Gate) and is a very popular event for many visitors. During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guard was responsible for opening and closing the palace gate as well as patrolling around the gate area. Outside the palace is a picturesque road flanked by a stone wall which is much loved by visitors.


Originally, Deoksugung Palace was not a palace. The Imjin War (the Japanese invasions in 1592) left all the palaces in Korea severely damaged. When King Seonjo (the fourteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty) returned to Seoul from his evacuation, the primary palace Gyeongbokgung Palace had been burnt to the ground and other palaces were also heavily damaged. A temporary palace was chosen from among the houses of the royal family. This is the origin of Deoksugung Palace. King Gwanghaegun (the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty) named the palace Gyeongungung, formalizing it as a royal palace. Since then it has been used as an auxiliary palace by many Joseon kings. In 1897, Emperor Gojong (the twenty-sixth king of the Joseon Dynasty) stayed here and expanded it. The modern buildings such as Seokjojeon (Hall) were constructed during this period. In 1907, the palace was renamed Deoksugung.

name: Gyeonggyojang
summary: The final headquarters of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea and the momentous historical site of the assassination of Baekbum Kim Gu.
description_html: Designated as Historical Site No. 465, Gyeonggyojang served as the operational headquarters of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea following national liberation and marks the solemn historical site where Baekbum Kim Gu passed away. The Seoul Metropolitan Government has meticulously restored the interior and transformed it into an exhibition venue, utilizing the space to educate citizens on domestic modern and contemporary history. Currently operating as an official branch of the Seoul Museum of History, Gyeonggyojang offers visitors a deep exploration of the Provisional Government's legacy through historical artifacts, archival videos, and interactive information terminals.

name: Shina Memorial Hall
summary: This place serves as a memorial to honor the founder, Jang Ki-bong and Shina Ilbo, after its forced closure.
description_html: Located in Jeong-dong, this building is notable for its uniquely stacked red bricks. It was constructed in the 1930s as a reinforced concrete building with one basement level and two above-ground floors. The structure, finishes, and facilities reflect its nearly 100-year history. Initially used as the Korean branch of the American sewing machine brand “Singer,” it was purchased by Shina Ilbo, Korea's first commercial newspaper, in 1963. Shina Ilbo expanded the building by adding the third and fourth floors in 1975, using it as an annex. Following the forced shutdown of Shina Ilbo, the building was transformed into a memorial to commemorate the founder, Jang Ki-bong, and the newspaper. Today, it houses various businesses, including memorial halls, a café, and boutique shops, on each floor.

name: Wongudan Altar
summary: Wongudan was built during the Joseon Dynasty to be an altar for performing divine harvest rituals.
description_html: Wongudan was built during the Joseon Dynasty to be an altar for performing divine harvest rituals. Located in central Seoul right near City Hall, it was designated Historic Site No. 157 in 1967. Through the past few centuries the altar was once called Hwandan and more recently Hwangudan. Now officially known as Wongudan Altar, Wongudan is located in close proximity to other major Seoul tourist attractions so it's convenient and easy to add a stop to Wongudan on a Seoul travel itinerary. The current Hwangudan Altar is a complex established in 1897 on the site of the old Nambyeolgung Palace. Its altar was built for Emperor Gojong's enthronement ceremony and rituals. The Japanese demolished the original complex in 1913, and a railway hotel was built on the site, reducing its size. Today, only the Hwangungu, the stone drum, and a stone gate with three arches remain preserved within the grounds of the Joseon Hotel.

summary: A garden that was tended to by the ruling class during the Joseon Dynasty
description_html: The name of this historical complex, "Seokpachon," translates into English as "surrounded by water, soaring above the clouds" and was given in honor of the great Heungseon Daewongun, the regent of the Joseon Kingdom. The Seokpachon complex is more than 600 years old, but it has been able to maintain its original appearance through careful preservation. This place is remarkable for its extraordinary beauty and it displays a combination of traditional Korean and Chinese architecture. This historic garden is currently under the authority of the Seoul Museum, which celebrates traditional and contemporary Korean art throughout the world.

name: Seosomun Historical Park
summary: Seosomun Historical Park includes a total area of 46,000 m².
description_html:
Formerly Seosomun Neighborhood Park, Seosomun Historical Park is a park which underwent renovation in 2019 to include 4 basement levels, totaling an area of 46,000 m². The ground level features the park and its facilities while the basement levels feature memorial halls, Sky Square, educational centers, facilities, and parking lot.


During the park's renovation process, the mausoleum built back in 1984 was preserved on ground level and a plaza was placed in the center of the park surrounded by plant life, including 45 different species of trees (pine, oak, rose bush), and 100,000 stems of 33 different species of grass and reed such as iris, pink mulley, and silver grass, transforming the site into a cultural "healing" space.


The basement levels of the park are consist of a memorial hall, a historical memorial hall, convenience facilities, education centers, and a parking lot. Specifically, the B1 level holds a library, seminar rooms, memorial souvenir shop and cafe, facility, and amenities for visitors. The B2 - B3 level is made up of a Sky Square and an exhibition hall. Although Sky Square, a memorial hall to commemorate the martyrs who've sacrificed themselves, is located on the basement floor, it has no ceiling so that visitors can look up to see the sky.

name: Manhae Han Yong-Un Simujang
summary: Manhae Han Yong-un Simujang was the residence of the Korean Buddhist, poet and independence activist Han Yong-un.
description_html: Simujang, the residence of Manhae Han Yong-un, was built in 1933 during the Japanese occupation. Unlike typical hanok homes that face south, this house faces north. As an independence activist, Manhae chose a north-facing site on the hillside to avoid facing the Japanese Government-General of Korea. The house has a rectangular layout with a hip-and-gable roof and features four front rooms and two side rooms. Inside, you’ll find Manhae's personal room with preserved artifacts such as his calligraphy, research papers, and court records from his time in prison. After his death, his only daughter, Han Young-sook, lived there. However, when the Japanese Embassy moved across from the property, she relocated to Myeongnyun-dong, and Simujang was transformed into a research center dedicated to Manhae's philosophy.

summary: Heojun Neighborhood Park is located in Gayang-dong, Seoul. The neighborhood is the birthplace of Heo Jun, a famous Joseon-era doctor and scholar.
description_html: Heojun Neighborhood Park is located in Gayang-dong, Seoul. The neighborhood is the birthplace of Heo Jun, a famous Joseon-era doctor and scholar. Next to the park is a museum dedicated to Heo Jun. His name is known in Korea to this day, more than 4 centuries after his death, in part because of his definitive text on Oriental medicine, "Dongui Bogam." There is a large, shrubby rock big enough to accomodate 20 people in the park. Known as Heogabawi Rock, during times of conflict such as the Imjin War and the Second Manchu Invasion of Korea, the rock was used as a refuge.

category_path: History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
name: Baek In-je House
summary: Baek Inje's House is a museum and cultural heritage site located in Bukchon Hanok Village's Gahoe-dong.
description_html:
The Baek Inje’s House, located in Gahoe-dong, Bukchon, is a representative traditional house that well preserves the style of modern hanok architecture. Although built during the Japanese occupation period, it has been designated as a Seoul Metropolitan Folklore Cultural Heritage due to its good condition and its blend of traditional hanok beauty with modern adaptations. Situated on a plot overlooking Bukchon, the property features a spacious Anchae (main living quarters) and a large garden centered around the Sarangchae (men's quarters), with a small Byeoldangchae (detached quarters) on the highest point. In this quiet, traditional setting, visitors can glimpse the lifestyle of the wealthy class of that era and observe features that distinguish it from typical upper-class homes of the time. Detailed information on the Baek Inje’s House, including its history, context, and characteristics, is available in the Haengnangchae (servants' quarters) and small Sarangbang (guest reception room). While general tours don't require reservations, entry to some areas like the Sarangchae and Byeoldangchae is only for those with guided tour bookings.
※ Baek In-je (1898 - Unknown): Baek In-je was a Korean patriot who fought for Korean independence during the Japanese colonial era. Baek was also a doctor who devoted much of his time to studying rickets and blood disorders. He made great contributions to the body of research on these medical issues.

name: The War Memorial of Korea
summary: Established to remember the Korean War (6. 25. 1950 - 7. 27.1953) and symbolize the desire for peaceful reunification of Korea.
description_html:
The War Memorial of Korea was established to remember the Korean War (6. 25. 1950 - 7. 27.1953) and to symbolize the desire for peaceful reunification of Korea. The museum consists of 6 individual exhibition halls and a combat experience room, a screening room and an outdoor exhibition area with memorial statues.  The Statue of Brothers located in the south-west corner of the outdoor exhibition area at the museum symbolizes the Korean War and the hope for reunification. The statue depicts a scene where a family’s oldest son, a South Korean soldier and his younger brother, a North Korean soldier meet on a battlefield. Their embrace expresses reconciliation, love and forgiveness.

There is also an extensive garden area around the memorial with an artificial waterfall, and a lake where visitors can picnic whilst enjoying the beautiful landscape. The museum houses more than 10,000 artifacts in the indoor and outdoor exhibition areas. It takes visitors about three hours to complete the tour. The first floor exhibition hall features a history of war from prehistoric times up to the Korean War. The combat experience room on the third floor offers visitors a special opportunity to experience a simulated life and death situation on the battlefield through special effects.

name: Namsangol Hanok Village
summary: Namsangol Hanok Village is a collection of five hanok (traditional Korean houses) from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910).
description_html: Namsangol Hanok Village is a collection of five hanok (traditional Korean houses) from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910), recovered from different parts of the city and relocated to the northern foot of Namsan Mountain. The interiors of each of these five houses reflect owners from different walks of life, from the middle class to high government officials, noblemen and aristocrats. At Namsangol Hanok Village, visitors can see the hanok of important figures from the Joseon era including the house of Queen Yun's parents, who was the Queen Consort to King Sunjong, the 27th king of the Joseon Dynasty; the jaesil (study) of Yun Taekyeong, King Sunjong's father-in-law; the house of Min Yeong-hui, a relative of Empress Myeongseong; the house of Lee Seungeop, who was in charge of constructing Gyeongbokgung Palace and the house of Kim Chunyeong, a military official of the Joseon Dynasty. At the hanok village, international visitors can participate in traditional Korean activities such as archery and enjoy traditional Korean performances as well. Anyone who is curious about Korean wedding culture should visit the village on the weekend when traditional wedding ceremonies take place.

name: Hanyangdoseong (Seoul City Wall)
summary: The Seoul City Wall was originally built in 1396, surrounding Seoul (then known as  Hanyang) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1897).
description_html: The Seoul City Wall was originally built in 1396, surrounding Seoul (then known as  Hanyang) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1897). The wall stretches for 18.6km along the ranges of Bugaksan Mountain, Naksan Mountain, Namsan Mountain, and Inwangsan Mountain. The wall stands at average heights of 7 - 8 m high. Along the Seoul City Wall, there once stood eight gates that were originally built between 1396-1398, but only six remain standing. The North, South, East, and West gates of the wall are known as the “Four Great Gates” (Sukjeongmun, Heunginjimun, Sungnyemun, Dongeuimun), while the Northwest, Northeast, Southwest, and Southwest gates are known as the “Four Minor Gates” (Changuimun, Hyehwamun, Gwanghuimun, Soeuimun).

The memorial hall opened on October 14th, 2012, marking the centennial anniversary of Son's birth. The memorial hall was once a school and was in fact Son's alma mater. Son Kee Chung was a gold medalist in the 1936 Berlin Olympics Marathon. Though Son Kee Chung was registered as a Japanese athlete, due to the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula, his victory was cherished and praised by Korean nationals. Visit the memorial hall to learn more about Son's life and how he won his gold medal. Admission is free and there are sometimes special exhibitions.

name: Bonghwanggak Pavilion
summary: Bonghwanggak Pavilion was constructed in 1912 by Son Byeonghui. In 1969, Bongwhanggak was designated Tangible Cultural Property No. 2 by the Seoul Metropolitan Government
description_html: Bonghwanggak Pavilion was constructed in 1912 by Son Byeonghui, the Korean independence activist. Bongwhanggak was built to be an educational facility that taught students the doctrines of Cheondogyo and educated leaders of the Korean independence movement. Cheondogyo is a Korean religion founded by Choe Je-U and its main tenet is that life and death are one, and all things in the universe repeat in an endless cycle. "Bonghwang" is the Korean word for the phoenix and it appeared often in Choe's writings, which is how the pavilion came to be named Bonghwanggak. The pavilion is considered the main shrine of Cheondogyo. In 1969, Bongwhanggak was designated Tangible Cultural Property No. 2 by the Seoul Metropolitan Government.

name: Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well
summary: Jang Huibin’s Well has been associated with Yeonhui Palace, a detached palace since the early Joseon Dynasty. It has been associated with palace grounds, courtyards and main buildings.
description_html:
The area of the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well has been associated with Yeonhui Palace, a detached palace since the early Joseon Dynasty. It has been associated with palace grounds, courtyards, main buildings, and the royal family's first mulberry orchard. It has been passed down by the name Seojamsil, known as the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well.
The first palace in this area was used as a refuge palace by King Jeongjong, who abdicated the throne to his younger brother, King Taejong, in the 3rd year of King Jeongjong's reign (1400). Later, in August of the 7th year of King Sejong's reign (1425), the palace was renamed Yeonhui Palace. It is said that there were wells in various places within the palace grounds due to the presence of palace officials and palace women. Among them, the preserved well is called the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well.
During the reign of King Sukjong (1674-1720), Huibin Jang (1659-1701), who followed Queen Inhyeon, who was deposed, briefly stayed at this place as a concubine, but there is no proof she drank from the well. Over time, oral tradition in Yeonhui-dong has perpetuated the belief that "this well is where Huibin Jang drank water," upheld by generations of elders. Consequently, it was chosen for restoration as a part of the community's treasure-hunting initiative.

name: An Jung-geun Memorial Hall
summary: The An Jung-geun Memorial Hall was established to memorialize the Korean patriot An Jung-geun.
description_html: The An Jung-geun Memorial Hall was established to memorialize the Korean patriot An Jung-geun. An fought for Korean independence from Japan and was ultimately executed by Japanese authorities for assassinating Ito Hirobumi in 1909. Ito was a major force behind the Japanese annexation of Korea. The memorial hall is composed of 12 exhibition halls and galleries, an auditorium, a reference library, and a rest area. In addition to exhibition information about An's life and some of his calligraphy, the memorial hall also hosts the An Jung-guen Academny and other events each year. Events include visits to historic sites abroad that were important to independence movements and calligraphy contests. Admission to the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall is free.

name: Seodaemun Prison History Hall
summary: The Seodaemun Prison was used to intern Korean patriots during the Japanese Occupation.
description_html: Seodaemun Prison was used to intern Korean patriots during the Japanese occupation. Until the Liberation of Korea on August 15, 1945, it was known as a clandestine mecca for the anti-Japanese resistance fighters, where they were tortured and executed. The Seodaemun Prison History Hall opened in November 1998 in Seodaemun Independence Park to commemorate the patriots who sacrificed their lives in the fight for Korean independence during the Japanese occupation. name: Space C
summary: A cultural complex established by Coreana Cosmetics
description_html:
Space C is a venue created and run by Coreana, a Korean cosmetics company. It spans 10 levels comprising a museum, gallery, beauty shop, café, and rooftop garden. On the 5th and 6th floors, visitors will find Korea’s largest cosmetics museum where visitors can learn about the history and development of Korean cosmetics. Space C also houses a large number of cosmetics-related artworks and other artifacts.


The Cosmetics Museum is Space C’s main exhibition hall, presenting the history of Korean cosmetics through a collection of more than 5,300 beauty-related items used by women in the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). The C Gallery on the first basement level is a traditional exhibition hall that displays fine art while C Cube on the second basement level plays host to more experimental work. The museum café on the 1st floor reflects the nature of its setting with art exhibits created from everyday objects, giving visitors the chance to continue their cultural odyssey even as they relax. The Beauty Space on the 2nd to 4th floors is a peaceful haven where women can consult a beauty therapist in the skin clinic and indulge in a range of body treatments. The Outdoor Cosmetics Museum on the rooftop of Space C is a garden featuring a collection of important plants which provide key ingredients for the cosmetics industry. From here, visitors can also enjoy spectacular views of the Seoul skyline.

summary: A nostalgic baths and a retro-style café housed in a repurposed inn
description_html: Opened in 1972, Samyangtang was a state-of-the-art bathhouse with over 130 pyeong when it opened. In the old days, bathhouses often mixed groundwater and tap water to fake the appearance of tap water, but Samyangtang was famous for using 100% tap water. Nowadays, public bathhouses with memories of those days are gradually disappearing, but Samyangtang has been maintaining its old appearance for 50 years.

name: My Friend Seoul, Seoul Gallery
summary: A complex cultural space where you can experience the future and present of Seoul.
description_html:
'My Friend Seoul, Seoul Gallery' is a complex cultural space created to share Seoul's vision and values with its citizens, located in the basement of City Hall in the center of Seoul. It has excellent accessibility to nearby attractions such as Gwanghwamun and Deoksugung Palace, and is also connected to City Hall Station and Euljiro 1(il)-ga Station, allowing tourists to comfortably stop by, enjoy various contents, and take a rest.


Hall 1 of My Friend Seoul, which consists of a 1:1600 scale model of the entire map of Seoul, the media-interactive 'Play Hangang', and the 'Media Wall' screening media art, and Hall 2 of My Friend Seoul, consisting of a 2-meter diameter globe-shaped 'Media Sphere' and the 'World City Wall' showing the world's top 5 cities and Seoul, are popular spots where you can overlook the future of Seoul and Seoul within the world.

Also, the 'Kids Lounge', a space for children that explains Seoul's policies through play, and the 'Performance Hall', where cultural performances are held and Haechi animations are screened, can be comfortably enjoyed by family visitors. In addition, it features contents that offer various experiences for tourists visiting Seoul, comprising the 'Seoul My Soul Shop' where you can be the first to meet representative Seoul goods, the 'Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall' displaying artifacts discovered during the City Hall construction, 'Haechi Photo Zones' arranged throughout, and the 'Wishing Tree' where you can write and hang your wishes.

Starting in 2007, it was reimagined into a cultural production space for creative minds, and in 2017, it evolved into BOAN 1942 from Boan Inn. It is a cultural arts complex, featuring an exhibition space, a bookstore, and a cafe. The place explores contemporary art and the possibilities of diverse media, with the goal of presenting a new cultural ecosystem through artistic practice. Boan Stay, located on the third and fourth floors, offers a lodging space for cultural nomads with panoramic views of the unique scenery of Seochon, including Bukaksan Mountain, Gyeongbokgung Palace, and traditional hanok homes..

name: Hangang Eland Cruise
summary: One of the best ways to enjoy the Hangang River.
description_html:
The ultimate way to experience the Hangang River is by embarking on a cruise. Feel the refreshing breeze as you enjoy the picturesque views along both banks. Various cruises are available day and night, allowing you to appreciate the river’s beauty in a different light. The "Hangang Tour Cruise" runs daily during the day, offering a chance to explore Seoul's cityscape while enjoying live entertainment. Every evening at 6 PM, the "Sunset Cruise" provides a romantic view of the setting sun. For those who prefer evening or night outings, the "Moonlight Music Cruise" and "Starlight Cruise" offer stunning nighttime views of the Hangang River. Special options like the "Fireworks Music Cruise," featuring dazzling displays, and the "Dinner Cruise," which includes a buffet or champagne, add an extra luxury to your river experience.


Aboard the cruise, you can enjoy live music while soaking in the sights of Seoul's iconic landmarks, including Sebitseom Island, Nodeul Island, Yeouido, the National Assembly Building, and Jamsil. It’s an ideal way to spend quality time with a partner, friends, or family, and offers a serene setting for those who wish to enjoy some peaceful reflection alone. Since schedules and routes vary by course, checking the official website for detailed information is advisable.

Adellain Jewelry Studio is a one-day Korean craft experience workshop located in Jongno, Seoul, where traditional and modern cultures coexist. Visitors can experience traditional Korean craft techniques in a calm and comfortable studio environment and directly make one-of-a-kind silver jewelry.

All classes are conducted as 1:1 personalized sessions with a professional jewelry designer, allowing even beginners with no prior craft experience to participate easily and enjoyably.

By referring to over 250 sample designs, you can choose various forms of jewelry, not only silver rings but also bracelets, pendants, silver clay jewelry, wood rings, etc. Depending on the design, you directly select the thickness, texture, gemstones, engraving, and plating (optional) to complete your own artwork.

All jewelry uses high-quality silver clay made of 99.9% pure silver. Completed works can be worn immediately on the same day or beautifully packaged for a gift. This experience, conducted amidst the historical atmosphere of Jongno, Seoul, provides a meaningful souvenir of a trip to Korea and long-remembered memories to overseas travelers, families, and solo travelers alike.

name: Deoksugung Palace Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony
summary: A traditional cultural reenactment event that realistically revives the changing scene of the royal guards who guarded the palace gates during the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html:
The ‘Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony’ is a representative traditional cultural reenactment event hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, which realistically revives the changing scene of the royal guards who guarded the palace gates during the Joseon Dynasty. The royal guard commander (Sumunjang) was an official of the junior 6th rank, who, along with the subordinate officers (Chamha) and guards (Sumungun) belonging to the royal guard headquarters (Sumunjangcheong), guarded the palace gates, controlled access, and conducted patrols. The changing ceremony is structured based on actual historical records and unfolds centering on Deoksugung Palace in the late Joseon Dynasty. The event is held six days a week, excluding every Monday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in front of Daehanmun Gate at Deoksugung Palace. To add to the interest of general citizens and foreign tourists, various experience programs are also operated. The ‘Gaesiktago (Opening Drum Beating) Experience’ is an experience where one directly beats a drum to announce the start of the ceremony. ‘I am also a Royal Guard Commander’ is a program where one experiences the role while wearing the royal guard commander's uniform. The ‘Traditional Costume Experience’ is a popular experience where one can take pictures wearing Joseon Dynasty attire.


[Event Details]


- Main Program: Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony

- Side Events and Programs: 'I am also a Royal Guard Commander' Experience / 'Gaesiktago' Experience / Traditional Costume Experience / 'Special Day of My Life' Photography Experience


[Detailed Information on Side Events and Programs]


1.  I am also a Royal Guard Commander


-Operating Period: Every Tuesday~Sunday (During the changing ceremony time)

-Number of Participants: 1 person per session

-Main Contents: Royal guard role experience / Wearing attire / Role education

-Remarks: Advance reservation required / Arrive at the waiting room 1 hour before the experience date


 2. Gaesiktago (Opening Drum Beating)


-Operating Period: Every Tuesday~Sunday (During the changing ceremony time)

-Number of Participants: 1 person per session

-Main Contents: Drummer (Eomgosu) role experience / Wearing attire / Role education

-Remarks: Advance reservation required / Arrive at the waiting room 30 minutes before the experience date


3. Traditional Costume Experience


-Operating Period: Weekends and public holidays 10:30~15:30

-Number of Participants: No limit

-Main Contents: On-site costume wearing experience

-Remarks: Operated free of charge


4. Special Day of My Life


-Operating Period: Every Tuesday / Wednesday / Friday (10:00, 13:00, 15:00)

-Number of Participants: 1 team per session (up to 5 people)

-Main Contents: Commemorative photo shoot with the royal guard commander / 1 instant photo provided

-Remarks: No duplicate applications by the same person / Photography equipment, costumes, props, makeup, etc., are not provided / Moving the royal guards for photography is prohibited

name: 2026 Yeowoorak Festival
summary: This summer! Dive into the sea of our music! The National Theater of Korea's representative summer festival.
description_html:
The comeback of the National Theater of Korea's representative summer festival, !

The Yeowoorak Festival, meaning ‘Here is our music (樂)’, is a festival participated in by musicians based on our traditional music and artists from various fields.


Since its first showcase in 2010, it has heated up every summer as Korea's representative traditional music festival, meeting with approximately 88,000 audiences and 'our music' to date. The Yeowoorak Festival, which has opened a new horizon for our music through encounters with artists crossing various genres and bold musical experiments, celebrates its 17th anniversary this year. Not settling for achievements so far, it attempts changes differentiated from existing festivals and plans to present another world of our music to the many audiences waiting for the festival.


This summer, discover your own taste on 12 islands over the sea of our music along with Lee Han-chul, Kang San-eh X Jung Bo-kwon, Sunwoo Jung-a X Chae Ji-hye, Lip J X Yoo Hee X Park Dong-seok, Dongyang Gozupa X Choi Ye-rim, Hareem X Gu I-im, Samsan X Seo Eui-chul Gadan, Sangjaru X Ahn Ye-eun, Country Gongbang X Jung Yoon-hyung, Kim Su-in X Richiman and Groove Nice, Kim Baek-chan X Kim Ban-jang and Saenggi Bokdeok, and Yoo Tae-pyung-yang!

name: 2026 Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony
summary: Breathing life into our proud cultural heritage embraced by the historical city of Seoul! The 'Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony' guarding Sungnyemun.
description_html: Pasu (Guarding) refers to defending the capital city and was one of the important military ceremonies during the Joseon Dynasty. Defending the capital city was the most critical issue during the Joseon Dynasty, and it emerged as a serious problem, especially after experiencing the Imjin War (Japanese invasions) and the Byeongja Horan (Manchu invasion) during King Seonjo's reign. The Guard Ceremony is a military ceremony of the Joseon Dynasty that connects the capital gate opening and closing ceremony,opening and closing the gates at Injeong (curfew) and Paru (lifting of curfew), with the patrol ceremony. Considering its position and role within the central military system, it can be viewed as a ceremony no less important than guarding the royal palace.

description_html:
<<The Seoul Light: Hangang Bitseom Festival>> is Korea’s largest waterfront laser art festival, held against the scenic backdrop of the Han River in Seoul. This festival, which takes place annually across six islands along the Han River, offers visitors a unique experience where nature, art, and technology come together. The Bitseom Festival is hosted sequentially across Seoul’s three islets (Nanjido, Yeouido, Seonyudo) and three islands (Nodeulseom, Seoraeseom, Ttukseom), presenting diverse programs under the key themes of 'Bitseom 3L (Laser Art, Light Run, Lecture).'


Now in its third year, the 2025 Bitseom Festival will be held under the theme 'Spectra of Light' from Friday, October 3 to Sunday, October 12, 2025, for a total of ten days at Ttukseom Hangang Park.
