name: Global Art & Tech Festival: FuturaCanvas 2025
summary: A global Art & Tech conference exploring the intersections of art and technology, raising questions about the future of art, technology, and humanity.
description_html:
The global Art & Tech conference FuturaCanvas 2025 will be held from Thursday, September 25 to Saturday, September 27, 2025, at Aube Studio in Seongsu-dong, Seoul. This year’s theme, Revival Avatar: Algorithmic Mythology, explores the new identities and belief systems created by artificial intelligence and blockchain.


[Program]


1. Synference (Main Conference, After Session, Talk Show, Art Screening, etc.)

From 2025, the expanded key program enables closer connections between speakers, artists, and participants. Comprising talks, discussions, screenings, and workshops, the program is designed to create synergy and synchronization among art, technology, and people.

Key Line-up: Hwang Seok-hee (film translator of K-pop Demon Hunters, Deadpool, Pachinko), Hyun Min-a (creative technologist at SM Entertainment subsidiary Studio Realive, researching generative AI and producing K-pop idol music videos), Lionclad (world-renowned beatmaker known for IU’s Square Dream).


2. Extended Futura (Futura Showroom, Collaborative Exhibitions, etc.)

An expansion program featuring showrooms of brands, satellite exhibitions, and workshops in collaboration with partner institutions, illustrating the art and technology ecosystem centered in Seoul.


3. Art Tour (Professional Docent Art Tour, Art Insider Tour)

A deep and unique program combining guided visits to major museums, galleries, and studios with networking opportunities with artists, curators, and collectors.

name: 22nd Experimental Film & Video Festival in Seoul EXIS 2025
summary: Experimental Film & Video Festival in Seoul (EXiS) is Asia's most significant and Korea's only experimental film festival, illuminating experimental film theory and issues while operating educational
description_html: The competitive section EX-Now screening works of Experimental Film & Video Festival in Seoul were selected through preliminary committee reviews from among approximately 2,300 works from 82 countries submitted through open calls over four months, as well as works from domestic and international distributors. Selecting more meaningful works is a continuous process of contemplation, questioning, and confirmation, resulting in a total of 34 selected works being screened through 8 sections, divided into international (EX-Now 1-5) and domestic (EX-Now 6-8) categories. The final three award-winning works will be determined through jury evaluation. The Moving Image Forum, which hosts the Experimental Film & Video Festival in Seoul (EXiS), re-examines experimental film theory and issues while establishing the foundations for their utilization. It operates programs in collaboration with art museums, alternative spaces, and cinematheques, and provides workshops and curricula through connections with media education. Moving Image Forum is dedicated to archiving domestic and international experimental film works and materials, and expanding the influence of experimental films by supporting the artist community.

description_html:
From the Rediscovered Uijeongbu Site, All Together in Yeominrak (Harmony with the People)

At the Uijeongbu site where state affairs were discussed during the Joseon Dynasty,

we bring back to life the meaning of Yeominrak, “to enjoy together with the people.”

A special beauty of gugak (Korean traditional music) enjoyed by all citizens in daily life,

now unfolds as our era’s Yeominrak at the newly rediscovered Uijeongbu site.


From dynamic performances by gugak musicians to participatory stages with citizens including foreigners, people with disabilities, and gugak enthusiasts,

from diverse traditional experiences that awaken the senses to one-day classes where you can learn and feel gugak firsthand,

the 2025 Seoul Gugak Festival invites you to experience the charm and depth of tradition interpreted through the emotions of today.
description_text: From the Rediscovered Uijeongbu Site, All Together in Yeominrak (Harmony with the People) At the Uijeongbu site where state affairs were discussed during the Joseon Dynasty, we bring back to life the meaning of Yeominrak, “to enjoy together with the people.” A special beauty of gugak (Korean traditional music) enjoyed by all citizens in daily life, now unfolds as our era’s Yeominrak at the newly rediscovered Uijeongbu site. The “Seoul Garden Festa” is a pop-up store festival held in Seoul's magnificent parks. As part of a deregulation policy initiative which now allows commercial activities in parks, Seoul City has created a festive space where visitors can enjoy pop-up stores such as markets and food trucks alongside cultural events—all previously prohibited in parks. The festival features activities that are a treat for all five senses, including the Book Garden (an open-air library), busking performances, and gardening programs. Under the slogan "A Healthy Chapter in My Life," each park offers uniquely themed pop-up stores to enhance the visitor experience. Running throughout April, the Seoul Garden Festa will allow visitors to fully enjoy spring in parks filled with cherry blossoms, tulips, daffodils, and other spring flowers alongside exciting content.

name: Gwanak Starlight Walk
summary: Gwanak Starlight Walk: A Three-Month Event
description_html: In its fourth year, the Gwanak Starlight Walk, the only lighting festival in Seoul that uses a river within a self-governing district, decorates the section of Byeoblit Naerin Stream from Bongnim Bridge to Silim Bridge for three months. This year, the Gwanak Starlight Walk will be themed "Starlight Garden in the City," decorating Byeoblit Naerin Stream with warm-colored lights and sculptures. Especially utilizing the riverside terrace, completed this May, to install lights and decorate Byeoblit Naerin Stream. Starting with the main gate decorated with butterflies and flowers, the space also features a 10-meter tall Christmas tree, a golden carriage that seems to float through the galaxy, and bear sculptures, creating a warm exhibition space that contrasts with the cold winter air. Additionally, for the first time this year, lights will be installed on the riverside terrace, where small trees will be set up to give residents a feeling of being in a forest garden as they take a rest.

name: 2024 The Winter Solstice Festival <Dongji Seotdal>
summary: The Winter Solstice Festival will be held at the Namsangol Hanok Village.
description_html: Dongji is a traditional holiday in Korea, celebrated on the winter solstice—the shortest day and longest night of the year. People observe this day to prepare for the New Year and to chase away evil spirits. Historically, Dongji was regarded as the starting point of a new annual cycle, considered as ‘the small lunar new year’s day’. Join the variety of Dongji programs prepared by Namsangol Hanok Village, reflect on the past year, and welcome the upcoming 2025. From 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM, various experience programs will be offered, and from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM, there will be red bean rice cake and calendar giveaways. These events may end early if supplies run out.

In celebration of the 5th anniversary, the Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music is hosting a special event week, "Yesterday's Stories, Today's Sounds, Tomorrow's Memories," from Thursday, November 14 to Saturday, November 23. 

As part of ongoing giveaways, visitors can receive a Dianthus Seed Kit and Korean Folk Music terrazzo soap through an on-site, first-come-first-served basis and a social media upload verification event. All programs are free to join, but reservations are required for performances and hands-on experiences through the Seoul Public Service Reservation System, which opens on November 14 at 10:00 AM for performances and 10:30 AM for experiences. 

Please visit the Seoul Museum of Korean Folk Music website for further details. We hope many people will come and enjoy the essence of traditional Korean folk music in a relaxed setting.

name: Autumn and Winter of the lake and the Luminaries
summary: The Luminarie Festival will be held around Seokchon Lake in Songpa-gu, showcasing the beauty of the lake in autumn and winter.
description_html: The 2024 Seokchon Lake Luminarie Festival will be themed “Dream, Universe & Love.” As one of Songpa's signature seasonal festivals representing autumn and winter, the Luminarie Festival transforms the natural beauty of Seokchon Lake with various illuminated displays, light sculptures, and photo zones, creating a dazzling spectacle of light. The term “Luminarie” refers to a festival where buildings or spaces are decorated with lights, often referred to as "light art" or "light sculptures." From the main gate at the entrance to the east side of Seokchon Lake, visitors will encounter large and small Luminarie gates, a Luminarie tunnel, a bridge gate, and a series of dreamy and mystical illuminated displays and photo zones. One unique feature is the “Lake I Create” installation, where messages based on the theme “Dream, Universe & Love”—selected through a prior public contest—are brought to life in LED lights, brightening the lake through community participation. The festival starts with an opening ceremony and fireworks on Friday, October 25, followed by cultural performances, experience booths, and a flea market. On Saturday, October 26, the Lotte World Marching Band will perform a special performance alongside Songpa's mascot, HaHa HoHo. From October 26 to November 24, various cultural performances, including busking, mime shows, magic performances, and breaking dance shows, will take place every weekend, along with the flea market, offering a wide range of entertainment for visitors.

name: Baek Inje's House “Bukchon Music Concert – Abstraction”
summary: Originally launched in June 2016 and warmly embraced by audiences, the "Baek Inje’s House Bukchon Music Concert" hosts three performances annually.
description_html: On Saturday, October 19, at 4 PM, a concert with the theme of "Abstraction" will be held at Baek Inje’s House, a 100-year-old modern hanok located in Bukchon, Gahoe-dong, Jongno-gu (16 Bukchon-ro 7-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul). Designated as Seoul Metropolitan Folklore Cultural Heritage No. 22, Baek Inje’s House was built in 1913 and represents modern hanok in Bukchon. It was opened to the public as a museum in November 2015 and has since become a popular tourist destination. This concert will feature a performance of the famous pansori scene from "Chunhyangga," where Chunhyang’s mother meets the royal inspector, performed by master singer Song Jae-young. Attendees will also enjoy a harmonious blend of various Western classical pieces featuring instruments such as the cello and flute.

name: 2024 Seoul Battleship Festival: Fall Edition
summary: A fall festival will be held at Seoul Battleship Park in Mangwon Hangang Park
description_html:
Seoul Battleship Park, located in Mangwon Hangang Park in Mapo-gu, is Seoul's first naval-themed park. It features a permanent exhibition of three decommissioned naval ships, including the Frigate Seoul, which served for 30 years protecting the nation's seas, the Patrol Killer Medium, and the Dolphin-class submarine. Visitors can view naval vessels in person and enjoy a picnic in the grassy park, serving as both an educational site for peace and security and a relaxing space for citizens. 
This fall festival celebrates the 40th anniversary of the Seoul Battleship. It will feature a variety of activities, such as a “Naval Culture Experience” reflecting the park's unique theme, a “Dance Contest” and a “K-POP Culture Concert” for the MZ generation, and a “Dokdo is Our Land” flash mob with citizens. We hope you enjoy a special day at Seoul Battleship Park, filled with exciting things to see and do!

Unhyeongung is a historic site No. 257 in Seoul. It was the residence of King Gojong, the 26th king of the Joseon Dynasty, and the private residence of Heungseon Daewongun. name: 2024 Namsangol Wedding Banquet: Autumn Edition
summary: We invite you to the Autumn Wedding Banquet at Namsangol Hanok Village!
description_html:
You're invited to the Autumn Wedding Banquet at Namsangol Hanok Village!  
In the elegant setting of a traditional hanok, a bride and groom, dressed in beautiful traditional Korean wedding attire, will celebrate their marriage. Join us in congratulating the couple as we witness this meaningful and heartwarming traditional wedding ceremony, filled with the wisdom of our ancestors and accompanied by rich Korean music. You can enjoy a guided viewing of the traditional wedding and a reenactment of an actual ceremony at Namsangol Hanok Village.

Namsangol Traditional Wedding Procedure
Jeonanrye: The groom visits the bride's home and offers a wild goose to the bride's leading family representative.  
Gyobaerye: The bride and groom bow to each other (In the past, this was the first time the bride and groom met and bowed as part of the formal introduction).  
Seocheonjirye: The couple vows before the spirits of heaven and earth to live diligently as husband and wife.  
Seobaewoorye: The bride and groom pledge to be good partners to each other.  
Geunbaerye: The couple shares a drink from each other's cups, symbolizing their union.

name: 2024 Changdeokgung Palace Moonlight Tour
summary: The 2024 Changdeokgung Palace Moonlight Tour invites visitors to light traditional cheongsachorong lanterns and discover the hidden stories of the palace as they explore.
description_html:
We invite you to Changdeokgung Palace, the most beloved palace of Joseon dynasty kings. Under the soft glow of moonlight and the lush greenery, you can explore the palace's hidden stories illuminated by traditional cheongsachorong lanterns.

During the Moonlight Tour, stroll through the palace grounds and listen to expert-guided tales of the royal family. You can also enjoy a traditional art performance paired with traditional tea. Starting at Donhwamun Gate, the tour takes you through Geumcheongyo Bridge, Injeongjeon Hall, Huijeongdang Hall, Nakseonjae Hall, Buyongji Pond, and the secret garden forest path, offering stunning views of Changdeokgung Palace at night. Additionally, through special programs, you’ll have the chance to meet actors portraying the kings and queens of the Joseon dynasty. Participants who wear hanbok during the tour will receive a small commemorative gift.

summary: The ZERO+ Ttukseom Sharing Market is a beloved secondhand market that promotes the circular use of resources by increasing the value of forgotten items through reuse.

We look forward to your interest and participation.

description_html:
This fall, immerse yourself in Korea's premier art festival, Kiaf SEOUL 2024! Celebrating its 23rd edition, Kiaf SEOUL 2024 will take place at COEX from Wednesday, September 4th, starting with a VIP preview day, until Sunday, September 8th. This year's event will feature 206 major galleries from 22 countries across the globe, organized into the GALLERIES/PLUS/SOLO sections. Kiaf SEOUL 2024, a global art festival, is ready to welcome you again at COEX.

name: Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony and Traditional Cultural Events
summary: Events where you can experience traditional Korean culture
description_html:
Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony and Traditional Cultural Events is a project hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government. It aims to recreate the communication methods of the Joseon Dynasty, allowing residents and domestic and international tourists to learn about and enjoy Korea's unique traditional culture. These events are held year-round, excluding Mondays, and provide opportunities for people of all ages to experience traditional culture together. 

[Bosingak Pavilion Bell-Ringing Ceremony]
Experience the sound of a millennium with the Bosingak Pavilion Bell-Ringing Ceremony! This interactive program, held daily at noon, allows residents and tourists to participate in the bell ringing. You can apply to join the program and experience the moving sound of the bell with family, friends, and loved ones.
(*Closed every Monday. On Tuesdays, there is an on-site participation program specifically for foreigners.)

[The Namsan Beacon Lighting Ceremony]
The Namsan Beacon Lighting Ceremony was a crucial communication tool during the Joseon Dynasty, where beacons from across the country were gathered to relay information to the capital. Visitors can watch the Namsan Beacon Lighting Ceremony and listen to historical explanations at the Namsan Beacon site.

[Traditional Cultural Performances]
At the N Seoul Tower Palgakjeong Pavilion Plaza, you can enjoy Samulnori (traditional Korean percussion music) performances and traditional martial arts demonstrations. Additionally, there are hands-on experience programs such as the Daily Guard Experience and the Daily Beacon Keeper Experience.

name: K-Food Festival Knock Knock
summary: The 2024 K-Food Festival Knock Knock is a Korean food-themed festival where you can enjoy and experience Korean cuisine's diversity and unique flavors
description_html:
The 2024 K-Food Festival Knock Knock is a Korean cuisine-themed food festival where you can enjoy Korean food's diversity and unique flavors while having a great time. Following the success of the Hangang Moonlight Market in 2023, this year, it returns as the “Knock Knock Festival,” specializing in Korean cuisine. Especially after sunset, the “Outdoor Night Library” opens, allowing visitors to enjoy reading in the cool evening breeze. They can savor an emotional and unique night of reading under the stars or watch various genres of movies at the Grass Theater, which screens films on the last Sunday of every month.

name: The 21st Seoul International Experimental Film Festival EXiS2024
summary: A film festival dedicated to exploring new formats, embracing challenges, and seeking inspiration
description_html: The EX-Now competition section at the 21st Seoul International Experimental Film Festival (EXiS2024) features a selection of 32 films chosen from over 2,000 submissions from 79 countries and works from domestic and international distributors. These selections were made after careful review by the preliminary jury, focusing on meaningful and impactful works. The films are divided into eight categories: five international (EX-Now 1-5) and three domestic (EX-Now 6-8) categories. The panel of judges will decide the final three award-winning films. The Moving Image Forum, which organizes EXiS, reexamines experimental film theories and issues, creating a foundation for their utilization. Collaborating with museums, alternative spaces, and cinematheques, the forum operates programs and offers workshops and curricula linked to media education. Additionally, the forum archives experimental films and materials, supports filmmakers, and strives to expand the influence of experimental cinema both domestically and internationally.

name: Seoul Fringe Festival 2024
summary: The Seoul Fringe Festival is an independent arts festival that supports the free experimentation and autonomy of artists.
description_html: The Seoul Fringe Festival, the only festival in the country that allows open participation without screening or selection, started as an independent arts festival in 1998. It has occurred in various locations, including Daehak-ro, the Seoul Arts Center, Hongdae, the Seoul World Cup Stadium, and the Oil Tank Culture Park. It collaborates with various cultural and artistic spaces in Mapo-gu and Seodaemun-gu, Seoul. In an arts ecosystem where numerous factors influence the presentation of artists' works, the Fringe does not restrict artists based on qualifications or genres, supporting all experiments and attempts. The Seoul Fringe Festival aims to continue as an independent arts festival that connects artists and audiences. Every summer, experience new attempts, unique challenges, and free artistic presentations from artists across various fields, such as theater, dance, music, performance, visual arts, and video.

summary: K-Food Festa in Seoul: A place where you can taste a variety of foods, including Tteokbokki and traditional liquor.

name: 2024 Seoul International Book Fair
summary: South Korea's Largest Book Festival for Both the Publishing Industry and the General Public
description_html: The Seoul International Book Fair, which began as a national book exhibition in 1954, has been South Korea's largest book festival for nearly 70 years. It brings together publishers, authors, and readers in one place. The fair serves as a joyful gathering where those who create and read books—authors, scholars, artists, editors, and readers—come together to share knowledge and information. Since 1995, the fair has expanded its international scope, becoming a festival that promotes the exchange of books and culture and a hub for diplomacy and trade. It has grown alongside Korea's cultural, artistic, and academic development, establishing itself as one of Asia's leading book fairs recognized worldwide. In addition to the Seoul International Book Fair event, the fair organizes a Korean Pavilion at overseas book fairs and oversees guest country events. It brings together participants from around the globe to exchange ideas in Seoul and introduces Korean books and culture to the world.

name: 2024 Maker Faire Seoul
summary: The joy of turning imagination into reality! Join the fun at Maker Faire Seoul! The festival for creators, "Maker Faire Seoul 2024," is held at the Seoul Science Center.
description_html: The joy of turning imagination into reality! Join Maker Faire Seoul! The festival for creators, "Maker Faire Seoul 2024," will be held at the Seoul Science Center. Maker Faire Seoul introduced the maker movement to the public in 2012 as Korea's first maker event. The 8th event in 2019, the last before the pandemic, was the largest, with over 700 makers showcasing over 150 projects and over 16,000 visitors. The 9th Maker Faire Seoul will resume this year at the Seoul Science Center through an exclusive contract with the U.S. maker community. Maker Faire is a festival where makers gather to showcase and explain their creations. First held in San Mateo, California, in 2006, it now occurs over 220 times annually in 45 countries. Maker Faires are categorized into three types: Flagship Maker Faires directly organized by Maker Media, Featured Maker Faires hosted by O'Reilly Media's foreign branches or partners, and independently organized Mini Maker Faires under Maker Media's license. Most are held once a year regularly.

name: Weekly Classic Festival
summary: Classical festivals held across the country
description_html: Starting in 2022 in Osan, Gyeonggi Province, with the slogan "Enjoy a Classical Music Concert at Our Local Theater," the Weekly Classical Festival, which has been well-received by audiences, will be held at eight venues nationwide from March to July 2024. A total of 210 performers from 68 teams, selected through a public contest, will perform 92 concerts in Seoul, Gyeonggi, Cheongju, Daegu, and Jeju. In addition to traditional classical music, various genres such as jazz, Korean traditional music, new age, and Latin American music will be showcased using classical instruments. The participating venues are Gyeongbokgung Classic (Jongno, Seoul), Gallery Onue (Dongjak, Seoul), Meister Klang (Gwangmyeong, Gyeonggi), MEG Art Hall (Osan, Gyeonggi), AG Art Hall (Cheongju, Chungbuk), Franz Hall (Nam-gu, Daegu), Auditorium (Aewol, Jeju), and Claude Art Hall (Seogwipo, Jeju). The seating capacity of each venue ranges from a minimum of 30 to a maximum of 100 seats. With the stage and seats close enough for the audience to feel the performers' breath and with commentary provided by the performers at every concert, this festival promises an extraordinary experience where the barrier between audience and performers naturally breaks down. Through this festival, you can experience classical music's emotion, joy, and unique energy and expand its artistic influence. Tickets can be purchased on the classical performance booking site “Finestage” (www.finestage.co.kr)

name: Seoul K-Family Festival
summary: A festival where you can experience and immerse yourself in Korean family culture will be held at Seoul Children's Grand Park
description_html: The K-Family Festival is held to revive the essence of the traditional Korean extended family culture based on the spirit of Hongik Ingan. It promotes universal values and ethics related to love, gender, marriage, and family, advocating for value-centered policies on low birth rates and aging populations and proper sex education. The festival's primary goal is to spread the proud Korean family culture (K-Family) worldwide. "K-Family" refers to the extended family culture embodying the founding philosophy of Hongik Ingan in Korea. Various civic organizations collaborate and unite to prepare the festival to promote the values and culture of the Korean extended family. The festival features a range of activities for all family members, including contests, family song competitions, policy exhibitions, talk concerts, diverse cultural performances, and interactive booths for parents and children to enjoy together.

name: ASSITEJ International Summer Festival
summary: Korea's largest nationwide performing arts festival for children and youth, featuring outstanding domestic and international productions.
description_html: The ASSITEJ International Summer Festival is Korea's largest performing arts festival for children and youth, showcasing outstanding domestic and international productions. Launched in 1993 as the “Seoul Children's Theatre Festival,” it invited exceptional international children's plays starting in 1995, transforming into an international performing arts festival. It evolved into the “Seoul International Children's Performing Arts Festival”' in 1997 and the “Seoul Children and Youth Performing Arts Festival” in 2001. Following the 17th 'ASSITEJ Summer Festival' in 2009, the “ASSITEJ International Summer Festival” was renamed in 2013, expanding its international participation and solidifying its status as a global festival for children and youth. Over the past 25 years, the festival has attracted a total audience of 300,000, featuring a variety of genres such as dance theatre, music theatre, and object theatre, as well as workshops and exhibitions. From 2014 to 2017, the festival received an A grade in the Korea Arts Management Service’s Performing Arts Event Support Project evaluation for four consecutive years. In 2018, it was awarded an S grade in the regional representative performing arts festival evaluation, establishing its reputation as Korea's leading performing arts festival.

name: Seoul International Writers' Festival <Particles & Waves>
summary: The Seoul International Writers' Festival is a global literary festival that was founded in 2006 to create a platform for Korean and world literature interaction in Seoul. Celebrating its 13th edition
description_html:
The Seoul International Writers' Festival is a global literary festival that was founded in 2006 to create a platform for Korean and world literature interaction in Seoul. Celebrating its 13th edition this year, the Festival presents various literary events such as discussions, performances, and exhibitions with the theme 'Particles & Waves,' featuring writers worldwide.

1. Opening Ceremony/Open Lecture: Domestic and international writers will give lectures on the theme of “Particles & Waves,” along with an opening ceremony and celebration performance featuring various speakers.
2. Writer Conversations: Two domestic and one international writers will have a conversation focusing on subtopics related to social issues and their literary works.
3. Thematic Discussions: Panels of 2-3 writers, both domestic and international, will discuss subtopics related to literary themes and language.
4. Convergence Sessions: Audience participation programs and crossover events with other genres.
5. Exhibitions: Throughout the festival, media art exhibitions and a book sales zone for participating writers will be open.

name: 2024 Jeongdong Culture Night
summary: The Jeongdong Culture Night Festival will be held on May 24th (Friday) and 25th (Saturday) for two days around Jeongdong-gil and Deoksugung-gil.
description_html:
Jung-gu, Seoul (led by the head of district Kim Gil-sung) will host the "Jeongdong Culture Night" on May 24th (Friday) and 25th (Saturday), bringing the dream of the Korean Empire to Jeongdong. Jeongdong Culture Night, the first cultural heritage night event in Korea, was initiated in Jung-gu, Seoul, in 2015. This year marks the 10th edition of Jung-gu's signature festival. The Jeongdong Culture Night Festival will be held in the Jeongdong-gil and Deoksugung-gil areas, which are known for their rich modern cultural heritage. During this event, visitors can experience historical and cultural facilities open specifically for night viewing, attend a palace concert in Deoksugung, and participate in modern history programs.

3. Experience Programs: Appointments using the imperial seal, solving the Deoksugung of the Korean Empire in 3D puzzles, and making personalized LED Hanji lamps.
4. Other Features: Food trucks, art markets, and more.

summary: As the representative festival of Dongdaemun-gu, it aims to expand the platform for cultural communication and offer a more diverse and vibrant array of programs.
description_html: The Seonnongdaeje is a ritual held in Seonnongdan from the Silla Dynasty to the Joseon Dynasty. It involves ceremonies for Sin Nong, the god of agriculture, and the king's Chingyeong. Chingyeong refers to the ritual of the king personally performing agricultural activities to show an exemplary model and pray for a good harvest.) Although discontinued during the Japanese colonial period, the Seonnongdaeje was restored in 1979 and has been hosted by the Dongdaemun Foundation for Arts and Culture under the auspices of the Seonnongdan Preservation Society since 2019. We invite you to the Seonnongdaeje, which preserves history and tradition. Enjoy traditional cultural experiences and delicious seolleongtang (Ox Bone Soup) on a warm spring day.
description_text: The Seonnongdaeje is a ritual held in Seonnongdan from the Silla Dynasty to the Joseon Dynasty. It involves ceremonies for Sin Nong, the god of agriculture, and the king's Chingyeong. Chingyeong refers to the ritual of the king personally performing agricultural activities to show an exemplary model and pray for a good harvest.) Although discontinued during the Japanese colonial period, the Seonnongdaeje was restored in 1979 and has been hosted by the Dongdaemun Foundation for Arts and Culture under the auspices of the Seonnongdan Preservation Society since 2019. We invite you to the Seonnongdaeje, which preserves history and tradition. Enjoy traditional cultural experiences and delicious seolleongtang (Ox Bone Soup) on a warm spring day.

description_html: The K‑Royal Culture Festival is Korea's largest cultural heritage festival, set against the backdrop of beautiful palaces. Celebrating its 10th anniversary this year, it will run for nine days starting on April 27th, with the opening ceremony on April 26th. Various programs, including performances, experiences, and participatory events, will take place in Seoul's five major palaces (Gyeongbokgung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, Deoksugung Palace, Changgyeonggung Palace, and Gyeonghuigung Palace) and Jongmyo Shrine area. Permanent programs have been expanded in this festival so visitors can easily participate on‑site without separate reservations. Additionally, a global reservation system allocates separate program sessions for foreigners, thus widening opportunities for their participation.

name: 2024 Seoul Spring Festival of Chamber Music
summary:
The 19th Seoul Spring Festival of Chamber Music will be held in 2024 under the theme “All in the Family.” 
The daily theme includes musical styles according to musical trends.
description_html:
The 19th Seoul Spring Festival of Chamber Music will be held in 2024 under the theme “All in the Family.”

The daily theme includes music schools according to musical trends, performances by SSF musician couples, 

veteran ensembles that are not related by blood but have worked together for a long time like family, 

composers of the same nationality and ethnic background, and ahead of their time. 

Pioneering composers, composers with similar personal histories, and performances featuring only works from the same instrument group are presented on stage. 

The House Concert is the center of attention every year, with compositions with special significance (commemoration of death, birth, etc.) in 2024. 

Additionally, the Family Concert, directed by pianist Joo Hyungki, will feature a series of short musical theater performances in a format called "Humoresque." This omnibus style performance will mark the debut of SSF musicians and will be the first of its kind in South Korea.

name: Bulgwangcheon Stream Cherry Blossom Festival ‘Spring of Eunpyeong’
summary: As cherry blossoms bloom and Bulgwangcheon Stream turns pink, the Bulgwangcheon Stream Cherry Blossom Festival is held.
description_html: The Bulgwangcheon Stream Cherry Blossom Festival is held as cherry blossoms bloom and Bulgwangcheon Stream turns pink. This festival offers diverse cultural and artistic programs highlighting the scenic beauty of Eunpyeong. It is a festival where you can enjoy cherry blossoms while walking along the beautiful Bulgwangcheon Stream. It celebrates the beauty of spring, hope, and vitality, overcoming the cold winter and enjoying the beauty of blooming cherry blossoms. The festival will be held for three days, from April 4th to 6th. You can enjoy performances by Kim Bum‑soo, Koyote, Jin Sung, H1‑KEY, and Kim So‑Hyun, as well as traditional cultural performances such as Cheoyongmu and Cheonggomu and media art performances. In addition, historian Choi Tae‑seong will give a special lecture on Yun Dong‑ju's poetry, which embodies the hope and vitality of spring. Near Eungam Station to Saejeol Station, various promotional, exhibition, and experiential booths are set up, and visitors can also enjoy delicious food from food trucks.

name: Seoul Winta (Seoul Winter Festa) 2023
summary: The Seoul Metropolitan Government is hosting Seoul Winta Festa 2023, themed "Fresh new light, shining across Seoul," connecting seven prime attractions across Seoul.
description_html:
Seoul is set to rival New York's Times Square and Sydney's Opera House as a premier New Year's Eve countdown destination and a festival of lights. From December 15, 2023, to January 21, 2024, a grand 38-day urban winter festival, 'Seoul Winter Festa 2023,' will connect seven of Seoul's prime attractions.

Centered around the theme of 'Fresh New Light, Shining Across Seoul,' this festival, celebrating the essence of 'light,' will offer a range of spectacles and activities in seven central Seoul locations, such as DDP, Bosingak Pavilion, Sejong-daero, Gwanghwamun Square, Yeolrin Songhyeon Green Plaza, Cheonggyecheon Stream, and Seoul Plaza. Leveraging advanced light illumination techniques, including media facades and projection mapping, the festival is set to showcase ten diverse events and celebrations, promising an enjoyable experience for all attendees.

The New Year's Eve bell-ringing ceremony at Bosingak Pavilion, known as "Joya no Kane," will be a 'Global Event' celebrated by both Seoul locals and international visitors. For a more relaxed and spacious viewing, the event will be live broadcasted from Bosingak Pavilion, Gwanghwamun Square, and DDP.

The Seoul Winter 2023 festival kicks off at 6 PM on December 15th, marked by the simultaneous illumination of the Seoul Light Gwanghwa (Gwanghwamun Square), the Seoul Lantern Festival (Gwanghwamun Square, Cheonggyecheon Stream, and Seoul Plaza), and the Songhyeon-dong Light Festival (Yeolrin Songhyeon Green Plaza). Don't miss this chance to make unforgettable memories during the festive year-end and New Year season!

Seoul Winter 2023 Major Events

○ Seoul Light Gwanghwamun, Seoul Lantern Festival, Gwanghwamun Square Market
- Dates: Dec 15 (Fri) to Jan 21, 2024 (Sun)
- Location: Gwanghwamun Square

○ Songhyeon-dong Light Festival
- Dates: Dec 15 (Fri) to Jan 21, 2024 (Sun)
- Location: Yeolrin Songhyeon Green Plaza

○ Seoul Lantern Festival
- Dates: Dec 15 (Fri) to Jan 21, 2024 (Sun)
- Location: Cheonggyecheon Stream

○ Seoul Light DDP, SeoulCon (until Jan 1, 2024)
- Dates: Dec 21 (Thu) to Dec 31 (Sun)
- Location: DDP

○ New Year's Eve Bell-Ringing Ceremony
- Dates: Dec 31 (Sun) to Jan 1, 2024 (Mon)
- Location: Bosingak Pavilion

○ Countdown Event 'Midnight Sun'
- Dates: Dec 31 (Sun) to Jan 1, 2024 (Mon)
- Location: Sejong-daero

○ Seoul Plaza Skating Rink
- Dates: Dec 22 (Fri) to Feb 11, 2024 (Sun)
- Location: Seoul Plaza

name: Seoul Downtown Hiking Tourism Center's Traditional Games Event in Celebration of Chuseok
summary: A traditional games event for domestic and international visitors visiting the Seoul Downtown Hiking Tourism Center is taking place during the Chuseok holiday.
description_html:
· Happy Chuseok Event! ·


Happy Chuseok Event ! : Event 1. Tuho Play (투호놀이), Event 2. Jegichagi (제기차기), Event 3. Yutnori (윷놀이)


■ Event 1. Tuho Play (투호놀이)




Tuho is a traditional Korean game played by the royals since ‘Samguk-period(A.D 5C)’.

Players should throw arrows or sticks into the pot, and the one who gets the largest number of arrows into the pot wins the game.

How to Play : Score points by landing arrows in three pots!

Get ready at the preparation line and throw the arrows towards the pots.

How to Win Special Gift : throw 10 Tuho arrows, and if you succeed in 7 or more, you will get a Knee Support Brace !


- Tip : Put some power into your arm and throw lightly !


■ Event 2. Jegichagi (제기차기)




Jegichagi is a traditional Korean folk game enjoyed during the Lunar New Year and Chuseok Holidays.

The exact origin of the game is unknown;

However it has been played in Korea in some form for thousands of years.

How to Play : Score points by kicking the Jegi many times without letting it drop to the ground.

How to Win Special Gift : When you successfully achieve 10 consecutive wins, you will get a pair of Hiking Socks !


- Tip : Ease off on your leg strength and kick swiftly in the shape of a 'ㄱ' !

■ Event 3. Yutnori (윷놀이)



Yutnori is a popular traditional Korean folk game,

often enjoyed by families during Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays.

It involves throwing four yut sticks, with the outcome determining the course of the competition.


In the game, rolling 'Do' allows you to move 1 block, 'Gae' lets you go 2 blocks, 'Gul' takes you 3 blocks, 'Yut' advances you 4 blocks, and rolling 'Mo' lets you go 5 blocks.


Head & Tail : Do (3 heads 1 tail), Ge (2 heads 2 tails), Gul (1 head 3 tails), Yut (4 tails), Mo (4 heads).

How to Play : Throw the four sticks (Yut) together upward (from a sitting position) as high as your shoulder and let them fall down on the ground, resulting in six possible outcomes.

How to Win Special Gift : Throwing four giant Yuts, you will get a Multifunctional Headwear upon rolling Yut or Mo (Four of the same side).


- Tip : Leave it to luck !


* Game Rules : One opportunity per player, unlimited practice allowed, but please use an appropriate amount of time, considering others. 
* Limited to 30 gifts a day per game



For the Chuseok holiday, we run a traditional game event that can be experienced at all times for domestic and foreigners visiting the Mountaineering Tourism Center in downtown Seoul. You can experience a total of three traditional games: Tuho Nori, Jegichagi, and Yut Nori, and if you succeed in the missions given for each game, you can win prizes for safe hiking.

※Provides 30 people on a first-come, first-served basis by mission every day

name: 2023 King Jeongjo’s Royal Parade
summary: In the late Joseon Dynasty, the 22nd king, King Jeongjo, brought about the greatest revival of politics and literature. The procession of filial piety and benevolence begins anew in 2023!
description_html: King Jeongjo, the 22nd king who led the late Joseon era into a cultural golden age and achieved great revival, will be commemorated through the joint reenactment of King Jeongjo’s Royal Parade, which took place during the Eulmyo year (1795, 2nd lunar month). This reenactment will be even closer to the actual procession day and will take place in October 2023. Based on the heritage record 'The Royal Journey of Eulmyonyun,' the reenactment of 'Eulmyonyun Hwaseong Royal Procession,' also known as King Jeongjo's Royal Parade, refers to the grand royal journey that took place over eight days, from the 9th to the 16th day of the 2nd lunar month in 1795, to commemorate the 60th birthday of King Jeongjo's mother, Queen Heongyeong. The joint reenactment of King Jeongjo's Royal Parade is a festival in which Seoul City, Gyeonggi Province, Suwon City, and Hwaseong City collaborate to recreate the original procession in modern times splendidly.

name: Seoul International Writers' Festival, Crossing the Bridge of Language
summary: he Seoul International Writers' Festival is a global literary festival that has been held since 2006 to expand readers' opportunities to appreciate literature and create a platform for the exchange of
description_html:
The Seoul International Writers' Festival, held since 2006, is a global literary festival aimed at expanding readers' opportunities for literary enjoyment and creating a platform for the exchange between Korean literature and world literature on Seoul’s stage. Celebrating its 12th edition this year, the festival presents various literary events such as talks, performances, and exhibitions with the theme of "Crossing the Bridge of Language," featuring the participation of writers worldwide.

[Event Highlights]
- Opening Ceremony/Performance: Domestic and international writers deliver lectures on "Crossing the Bridge of Language," followed by an opening ceremony and celebratory performance with diverse speakers.
- Writer, Face to Face: Dialogue sessions between two domestic and international writers, focusing on social issues and their literary worlds.
- Writers' Chit-Chat: Panel discussions featuring 2-3 domestic and international writers on literary topics and language-related sub-themes.
- Exhibition: "Reader's Perspective" from September 2, 2023, to September 13, 2023.

name: 2023 Seoul B-Boy Festival
summary: In the upcoming summer, a breakdance and street culture festival will be held against the backdrop of the Hangang River.
description_html:
▶ Festival Date: 2023. 6. 3. (Sat) 12:00-20:30 KST
▶ Festival Venue: Around Nodeulseom Island
▶ Admission fee: Free
▶ Festival Inquiries: 02)758-2044 (Festival Planning Team, Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture)
▶ Festival Introduction


In the upcoming summer, a breakdance and street culture festival will be held against the backdrop of the Hangang River. The Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture, which has been supporting the breakdance culture through performances, education, and production, by operating the representative B-Boy Group of Seoul City for the past ten years, conveys the freedom and powerful energy unique to street culture through the Seoul B-Boy Festival.
There are various things to see and enjoy, such as the Seoul Metropolitan B-Boy Selection Competition, Hip Hop Musician Performances, 3-on-3 All Style Dance Battles, 2-on-2 Break Dance Battles, a Large Graffiti Art Wall Exhibition, and Street Culture Experience Zone.


▶ Program


□ Contests
- Seoul Metropolitan B-Boy Group Selection
- 3-on-3 All-Style Dance Battles
- 2-on-2 Break Dance Battles

□ Performances
- Seoul Metropolitan B-Boy Group Selection
- Judge show and celebratory performance, event battles

□ Exhibitions
- Large Graffiti Art Wall Exhibition
- Seoul B-Boy Festival_Archive

□ Experience/event
- Street culture experience zone

□ Training/Workshops
- B-Boy Art Play Education
- Overseas breaker movement workshop 


About Seoul B-Boy Festival

The Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture, which has supported breakdance culture through performances, education, and work production by running the Seoul Metropolitan Government's Representative B-Boy Group for the past ten years, has held the Seoul B-boy Festival since 2022 to deliver the unique freedom and powerful energy of street culture to people. 
This festival, which marks its second anniversary this year, is the representative summer festival of the Seoul Cultural Foundation's four-season brand, Art Festival_Seoul. It is designed so that anyone can experience the vibrant breaking culture in the early summer by the Hangang River.


Introducing Seoul’s representative B-Boy Group

The Seoul’s Representative B-Boy Group is a project initiated by the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture in 2013 to promote the breakdance culture and encourage healthy leisure activities for citizens. The project selects a representative B-Boy team for Seoul City, which actively performs various shows on domestic and international stages.
01 Production
The Seoul Representative B-Boy Group, in collaboration with artists from various genres, has the opportunity to create new works based on creative workshops. From 2015 to 2023, the team produced six bodies of work, establishing a foundation for breakdancing to be recognized as an art genre. The team is preparing for their latest production's premiere, scheduled for June 30th this year.

02 Performance Activities
The Seoul Representative B-Boy Group showcases their domestic and international breakdancing performances at prestigious festivals and events, engaging with diverse audiences. They serve as cultural ambassadors, traveling to cities worldwide such as Paris, Sydney, Beijing, San Francisco, and Angola, acting as mediums for cultural exchange.

03 Training/Workshop
The program is designed to combine play and breakdancing artistically and educationally, aiming to enhance the creativity of children and teenagers. Through this program, participants can experience an art-based play education that integrates breakdancing, fostering their imaginative thinking. Additionally, workshops are conducted to share methods and insights for breakdancers who are interested in exploring career opportunities as educational instructors. Moreover, the team operates breakdancing workshops for professional artists, promoting collaboration and synergy among various artistic genres.

name: Yeon Deung Hoe, The Lotus Lantern Festival
summary: Yeon Deung Hoe lights up the lanterns to brighten one's heart and the world
description_html:
'Gandeung' during the Unified Silla dynasty, 'Yeon Deung Hoe' during the Goryeo dynasty, 'Gwandeungnori' during the Joseon dynasty, it's form has changed throughout history however the festival's identity and essence of illuminating both the spirits of the people and the world have persisted. The Lotus Lantern Festival, which has a long history and has been passed down as a living cultural heritage, is a National Intangible Cultural Heritage and a UNESCO Intangible Heritage of Humanity recognized for its value as an intangible heritage.

We invite you to the beautiful festival that blends tradition and light.

＜Yeon Deung Hoe Festival Information＞
-Traditional Lantern Exhibition (4/16 ~ 5/6)
Hanji paper filled up with light transforms into a variety of lanterns, brightening people's compassion and wisdom and warmly illuminates the world.

- EoulimMadang (April 26 4:00 PM ~ 6:00 PM)
A Buddhist ceremony and service, followed by a lively Buddhist Cheer Rally (Yeonhuinuri) to enliven everyone's spirits

- Lantern Parade (4/26 7:00 PM ~ 9:00 PM)
The lantern of Wisdom and Mercy, the lantern of Happiness and Peace, the lantern of Prayer and Hope; The majestic waves of peace packed with our hearts and souls embroider the city.

- Daedong Hanmadang (4/26 9:00 PM ~ 11:00 PM)
The flowerly rain of joy falls and happiness can be found with every hand that holds ours in the post-parade celebration.

- Traditonal Culture Madang (4/27 11:00 AM to 6:00 PM)
Memories for parents, new experiences for childern, and Korean culture for foreigners!
A street festival with traditional cultural experiences and performances such as drawing traditional patterns, making lanterns, and experiencing temple food! Fun experiences await!

- Performance Madang (4/27 11:00 AM ~ 6:00 PM)
Enjoy a joyful Madangnori performance where performers and the audience come together on a stage of traditon and passion

-Yeondeungnori (4/27 7:00 PM ~ 9:00 PM)
If only the Lantern Festival was every day! It's a shame the festivities has to come to a close, so let us signal the finale with one final Parade from Insa-dong and one last Dance together, hand-in-hand with one another.

- Buddha's Birthday (5/5 10:00 AM)
April 8th according to the lunar calendar is Buddha's Birthday.
Temples across the country will light lanterns filled with the hearts and souls of the people and hold ceremonies to commemorate the birth of Buddha.

Let your spirits become as radiant as the lantern lights!

name: The Great Rite of Sajik Daeje
summary: The great rite of Sajik Daeje is a ritual dating back to the Joseon Dynasty. Sajik Daeje lives on today in Seoul and a historical re-enactment of the ritual is held once a year.
description_html:
Sajikdaeje (社稷大祭), a national ritual from the Joseon Dynasty, praying for national peace and a bountiful harvest, will be reenacted in downtown Seoul.


Sajikdaeje (社稷大祭) is a traditional ritual in which the king and all civil and military officials of the Joseon Dynasty participate, offering offerings directly to Sasin (社神), the god of land, and Jikshin (稷神), the god of grain, to pray for national peace and a bountiful harvest. Designated Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 111 in October 2000, this precious cultural heritage is a precious cultural heritage.
For our people, who have long relied on agriculture for their livelihood, land and grain were the foundation of their nation. The nation held Sajikdaeje to pray for the well-being of the people who relied on agriculture for their livelihood. Abolished in 1908 (the second year of King Sunjong's reign) under Japanese colonial rule, Sajikdaeje was restored to its original form in 1988 and has been held annually since then under the auspices of the Jeonju Lee Clan Association's Sajikdaeje Preservation Committee. Departing from Deoksugung Palace, the tour takes approximately 50 minutes via Gwanghwamun Gate to Sajikdan Altar.

name: Changing of the Royal Guard at Gyeongbokgung Palace
summary: A must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions, this ceremony is a great opportunity to experience a rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments.
description_html:
During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guards were responsible for guarding and patrolling the gates of the capital city and the royal palaces. The royal palace guards, who were known as the "Wanggung Sumunjang", had the very important duty of protecting theking by guarding the entrance gates of the primary royal palace where the king resided. They were in charge of opening and closing the palace gates, inspecting all visitors, and maintaining a close surveillance of the palace. They were divided intodayand night shifts, and the Changing of the Guard ceremony took place whenever the shifts changed over. 


In the early period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Changing of the Guard ceremony was conducted at Gyeongbokgung Palace as at that time Gyeongbokgung was the primary royal palace and the king then resided there. However, in the late period of the Joseon DynastywhenGyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Waeran (Japanese Invasions of 1592 - 1598), Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace and the Changing of the Guard ceremony was then conducted at Deoksugung. 


After some extensive historical research, this splendid and elegant traditional Korean royal court cultural ceremony was first re-enacted in 1996 and has been a must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions ever since. This ceremony is a great opportunity to experiencea rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments. A tradition comparable to the Changing of the Guards atBuckingham Palace, this ceremony takes place twice a day in front of Gwanghwamun, the main gate of Gyeongbokgung at 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. (except on Tuesdays).

name: Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony
summary: The Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony is a re-enactment of Bongsu, a communication system that was once used to notify the government of urgent military matters occurring at the city borders. After being reconstructed in 2007, a re-enactment of how the Beacon Mound was used during the Joseon Dynasty has been held from 11:30 to 12:30 daily (except Mondays).
description_html:
The Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony is a re-enactment of Bongsu, a communication system that was used to notify the central government of urgent military matters (e.g. the approach of enemy forces, etc.) from the borders during ancient times. Bongsu was used to send messages across the peninsula by using smoke during the daytime and torchlights at night, a more convenient and rapid messaging method than horse or messenger. "Bongsu" is a combination of the words "bong" meaning torchlight, and "su" meaning smoke.

Namsan Beacon Mound was established after moving the capital city to Hanyang (present day Seoul) during the third year of King Taejo's reign (1394) during the Joseon Dynasty period. To protect the city from invasions, castle walls were built on the four major mountains located within the city: Bugaksan, Inwangsan, Naksan, and Namsan. On Namsan, five beacons were built at its peak to report political and military information to the king. One beacon was lit at normal times, two when an enemy appeared, three when an enemy approached the border, four when an enemy invaded the border and five beacons were lit when a battle with an enemy had begun at the border.

Namsan Beacon Mound served as the central destination point for all beacons in the peninsula because of its proximity to the King. At the peak of the Chosun dynasty, 673 beacon towers transmitted military and political information from around the peninsula to the capital Seoul. Historical records state that it took 12 hours for a message to travel from Busan to Seoul, two cities approximately 500 kilometers apart. Namsan Beacon Mound was used for approximately 500 years until 1894, the year after Gabo Reformation. Namsan Beacon Mound was also called "Mokmyeoksan Beacon Mound" as Namsan was once called Mokmyeoksan, and was even called "Gyeong Beacon Mound" as it was located in Seoul.

Originally there were five different beacon mound stations located on Namsan, but they were destroyed over the course of time. The current beacon mound was reconstructed in 1993 based on historical records in one of the five locations, near Namsan Palgakjeong Pavilion), and has been designated Seoul Monument No. 14. 

Starting from 2007, a re-enactment of how the Beacon Mound was used during the Joseon Dynasty has been held from 11:30 to 12:30  every day except on Mondays. The event starts with a patrolling ceremony and a ceremony of the guards. At around noon, the bongsugun (beacon tower soldiers) sound the bugle and conch horn to signify that the lighting ceremony is about to begin. Then at exactly noon, Bosingak Belfry located in Jongno rings twelve times, and the lighting ceremony begins. Only one beacon is lit in accordance with the rules that were used in ancient times.   

Although the lighting ceremony itself is great to see, the patrolling ceremony and ceremony of the guards that occurs before and after the lighting ceremony are very interesting to see as well. Although smaller in size than the Changing of the Guards ceremony that takes place at Deoksugung Palace, these ceremonies offer the opportunity to witness a different aspect of traditional Korean culture. Once the event has concluded, visitors may take photos with the bongsugun.

summary: Seoul Museum of History will be showcasing a lobby exhibition titled "Korea in 1908 Through the eyes of a Hungarian Medical Doctor, Dezső Bozóky" from Oct. 1st to Dec. 1st, 2019.
description_html: Seoul Museum of History will be showcasing a lobby exhibition titled "Korea in 1908 Through the eyes of a Hungarian Medical Doctor, Dezső Bozóky" from Oct. 1st to Dec. 1st, 2019. name: Changuimun in Jeong Seon’s Paintings : Special Exhibition
summary: Taking place from Sept. 10th to Dec. 15th, a special exhibition titled "Changuimun in Jeong Seon's Painting" will display paintings of Changuimun by famous artist and painter Jeon Seon, allowing visitors to view the rich detail and history surrounding this particular gate of Seoul City Wall during the Joseon Dynasty.
description_html:
Taking place from Sept. 10th to Dec. 15th, a special exhibition titled "Changuimun in Jeong Seon's Painting" will display paintings of Changuimun by famous artist and painter Jeon Seon, allowing visitors to view the rich detail and history surrounding this particular gate of Seoul City Wall during the Joseon Dynasty.

 

Changuimun Gate is a gate located in the northwestern section of Seoul City Wall on top of the ridge connecting Baegak Mountain and Inwangsan Mountain. The oldest gate to be preserved in Seoul City Wall, Changuimun Gate was drawn in two paintings by Jeon Seon, a prominent painter and artist in the Joseon Dynasty. Through his paintings, visitors can glimpse the past life and history of the people and its surrounding areas back in the Joseon Dynasty.

name: Seoripul Festival 2019
summary: A music festival featuring a night music parade and various other performances throughout 51 venues in Seocho-gu, Seoripul Festival 2019 will take place from Sept. 21st to Sept. 28th, 2019.
description_html:
A music festival featuring a night music parade and various other performances throughout 51 venues in Seocho-gu, Seoripul Festival 2019 will take place from Sept. 21st to Sept. 28th, 2019.

Celebrating its 5th year, the festival will run under the theme of “music”. Transforming the entire district of Seocho-gu to a music and performance venue, the festival will also have a car-free zone along Banpodae-ro Street on Sept. 21st for a fantastical parade of lights and music celebrating the opening of the festival.

Running under the slogan, “With Music, We are Together”, the festival will become a great way for visitors to enjoy all kinds of music including classic, jazz, 70s and 80s folk music, EDM, opera, music, etc. The festival will also become a stage for over 238 new and young artists and musicians to showcase their music to the public. On Sept. 28th, the last day of the festival will feature performance by artists like 2PM’s Junho, Kim Bum-soo, Park Myung-soo’s EDM Fantasy, and more, bringing a close to the 8-day festival. Visitors will be able to also enjoy the vibrant fireworks show and EDM party on Banpodae-ro Street..

Collective City 

 

Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2019 will run from Sept. 7, 2019 to Nov. 10, 2019. name: Gwanghwamun International Art Festival 2020
summary: An arts festival open to the public that welcomes any and every one to come and join the fun!
description_html:
Gwanghwamun Plaza is a symbol capturing that of democratization amid the background of Korea's vast history. Gwanghwamun has solidified itself as the stage for impassioned demonstrations and communication from the Korean people. It even served as the battleground for volunteer street rallies that take place during each World Cup event! Rather than functioning as a cultural asset of sorts, it's a cultural that's very much alive with voices of the people, making itself known as a place of gathering on the global stage.


As a public cultural festival, the Gwanghwamun International Art Festival has traditionally held several accompanying events with the purpose of promoting different exhibitions. Numerous performances have taken place in an attempt to further garner even more interest from artists and attendees from around the globe, while it also has a plethora of sites and sounds in store without limiting itself to simply providing visual exhibitions. Coloring psychological tests, ceramics making, silversmithing, leather-crafting, and other experiential booths are available for event-goers to try their hand at various hands-on activities to ensure everyone enjoys a well-rounded experience!

description_html:
Deoksugung Doldam-gil Music Concert 

 

In celebration of opening up the entire stonewall walkway surrounding Deoksugung Palace to the public after 59 years, Deoksugung Doldam-gil Music Concert will be held on Friday, May 10,2019.

 

By opening up a path along the interior of Deoksugung's stonewall, the stonewall walkway once obstructed by the British Embassy was connected and made whole again. The special concert held to celebrate this event will start marching from Daehanmun, the main gate, and move along the wall to a main stage prepared next to Jeonggwanheon. The performance team will be Kwanggaeto Samulnori, the same team that collaborated and performed together with BTS at the 2018 MMA.

○ Visitors can follow the march into the palace or wait in front of the stage next to Jeonggwanheon. Following along the march will give you free admission into the palace. However, visitors who opt to wait in front of the main stage will have to enter the palace and pay the admission fee.

○ Performance Team: Kwanggaeto Samulnori

○ Performances: Samulnori, B-boy, Beatbox, Fusion Gugak Concert

name: 1890 Hanyang Exhibiton : Namsangol Yangtang-guk
summary: Located inside Namsangol Hanok Village, Seoul Namsan Gukakdang will showcase an exhibition/experience program titled “Namsangol Yangtang-guk” from Mar. 15, 2019 to May 15, 2019.
description_html:
Korean Empire's First Coffee, Yangtang-guk 

 

Located inside Namsangol Hanok Village, Seoul Namsan Gukakdang will showcase an exhibition/experience program titled “Namsangol Yangtang-guk” from Mar. 15, 2019 to May 15, 2019. A chance to make, sample, and experience the coffee culture which existed back in the period of the Korean Empire, this program will take place inside the exhibition hall and educate visitors on how to make and differentiate between various Korean coffee (Yangtang-guk, Naeng Yangtang-guk, Tarak Yangtang-guk, etc.)

 

Yangtang-guk, literally meaning “Western broth”, was named so due to the similarity it had to the bitter, dark-colored Korean oriental herbal medicine. Boiled and drunk from porcelain bowls like an herbal medicine, this yangtang-guk (Korean coffee) program will be sure to provide visitors with a unique experience where they can learn more about the Korean Empire period.

name: 2019 Seoul Rose Festival
summary:
An annual rose festival at the Rose Tunnel (5.15km) in Jungnang-gu, where thousands of roses bloom every May. 
The most beautiful festival in Seoul.
description_html: An annual rose festival at the Rose Tunnel (5.15km) in Jungnang-gu, where thousands of roses bloom every May.This year's theme is ROSE GARDEN & ROSE PICNIC, inviting families, couples and friends to visit together and enjoy the Garden of Love, as well as the beautiful flowers. The opening ceremony will feature a night-time lighting ceremony and a flower petal rain, while the ending ceremony will be a multimedia light performance with flashy fireworks, laser beams and music.This festival is recommended to Korean and foreigner tourists alike, as the garden theme changes by date, offering special programs centered around roses, as well as the beautiful Rose Garden and rose photo zone. This year's mascot, Miss Rose, was created by Artist Baek So Young, a Korean floral illustrator. Miss Rose looks lovelier than ever, buried in beautiful roses in the Rose Garden. She wears hanbok, a Korean traditional dress, and the dress code for the festival is rose crowns, which will add to the aesthetics of the festival. There will also be a performance by the people of Kazanlak, Bulgaria (a city that has been hosting rose festivals for 114 years) like last year, as well as parades and other cultural exchanges of flowers with other countries.

name: Changdeokgung Palace : Injeongjeon Hall Tour
summary: The inside of Injeongjeon Hall will be open for viewing from Mar. 6, 2019 to Mar. 30, 2019.
description_html:
The inside of Injeongjeon Hall will be open for viewing from Mar. 6, 2019 to Mar. 30, 2019. Meaning "Hall of Benevolent Rule", Injeongjeon Hall is the throne hall of Changdeokgung Palace (National Treasure No. 225). A building with a magnificient dignified atmosphere, Injeongjeon Hall was where major state events such as coronation ceremonies, reception of foreign envoys, and the greetings of his officials took place.

The interior of Injeongjeon Hall is only accessible through guided tours taking place 4 times a day.

name: Dilkusha and Chain of Amber : Special Exhibition
summary: Seoul Museum of History will be showcasing a special exhibition of donated relics called “Dilkusha and Chain of Amber” from Nov. 23, 2018 to Mar. 10, 2019.
description_html:
Seoul Museum of History will be showcasing a special exhibition of donated relics called “Dilkusha and Chain of Amber” from Nov. 23, 2018 to Mar. 10, 2019.

 

In 1919, an American journalist by the name of Albert Taylor made great effort to report the events of the March 1st Movement, Jeam-ri Massacre, and the brutalities of Japanese imperialists to the world. For the first time, records of his life in Korea such as photo albums of him and his wife living in their house “Dilkusha” and first drafts of his wife’s autobiography “Chain of Amber” will be up for public display.

 

Through this exhibition, visitors will be able to see how Taylor and his family lived in Seoul (Gyeongseong) from1917 to 1942.

name: Jongmyo Daeje (Autumn) 2018
summary: A royal ancestral ritual to honor the past kings and queens of the Joseon Dynasty, Jongmyo Daeje 2018 will take place in Jongmyo Shrine on Saturday, Nov. 3, 2018.
description_html:
Jongmyo Daeje (Autumn) 2018

 

A royal ancestral ritual to honor the past kings and queens of the Joseon Dynasty, Jongmyo Daeje 2018 will take place in Yeongnyeongjeon Hall (Hall of Eternal Peace) and Jeongjeon Hall (Main Hall) of Jongmyo Shrine on Saturday, Nov. 3, 2018. Designated as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site, Jongmyo Daeje (or Jongmyo Jerye) is the biggest memorial rite ceremony to be held in Jongmyo Shrine. Since 1969, Jongmyo Daeje has been preserved with support from the Jeonju Lee Royal Family Association and consists of an  Eoga Haengnyeol (Royal Procession) and anestral ritual (including Jongmyo Jeryeak performances).

name: King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment 2018
summary: In memory and celebration of the filial piety of the famed 22nd Joseon king who made annual journeys to his father's tomb, King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment 2018 will take place from Saturday, Oct 6, 2018 to Sunday, Oct 7, 2018.
description_html:
King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment 2018

 

In memory and celebration of the filial piety of the famed 22nd Joseon king who made annual journeys to his father's tomb, King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment 2018 will take place from Saturday, Oct 6, 2018 to Sunday, Oct 7, 2018.

 

The city of Seoul, Suwon, and Hwaseong will come together again this year to recreate a perfect reenactment of the famed royal procession. In Seoul, a temporary bridge called Baedari will be set up across the Hangang River from Noryangjin using the same techniques the people used back in Joseon dynasty, connecting a way and leading festival-goers towards Hwaseong and Suwon as everyone celebrates the reenactment of King Jeongjo's royal procession.

name: Seoul Street Arts Festival 2018
summary: Celebrating its 16th year, Seoul Street Arts Festival 2018 will take place for 4 days at Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun Square, Donuimun Museum Village, and other areas located within central Seoul from Thursday, Oct. 4, 2018 to Sunday, Oct. 7, 2018.
description_html:
Seoul Street Arts Festival 2018

This festival will showcase close to 46 performances of various genres from 10 different countries and acknowledge the differences yet unity of cultures under the theme “Separate, yet together”.

 

The opening program, also titled “Separate, yet together”, will showcase aerial performances by Spain’s La Fura dels Baus and Korea’s Creative Dandi, where close to 200 performaners will color and shape the streets and sky with their brilliance. 

 

The festival will also feature interactive programs open to people of all ages such as “Domino Parade”, “Asphalt Gallery”, “Bus Theatre”, and more.

name: Yukuijeon Festival 2018
summary: Yukuijeon Festival 2018 will take place at  Jongno Cheonggye Special Tourist Zone from Sept 13th to Sept 14th and feature exhibitions, performances, special experience programs, tours, and more for its visitors.
description_html:
Yukuijeon Festival 2018


As an area where Yukuijeon (Joseon merchant monopolies) and Sijeonhaengrang (Joseon market) prevailed back in the Joseon dynasty, Jongno Cheonggye Special Tourist Zone will host the annual Yuijeon Festival along the streets of Sejong-daero Street and Sungin-dong. Following along the Cheonggyecheon Stream, there exist close to 14,000 different stores and shops in various specialty markets, some of which includes the jewelry district selling award plaques and gold, a district selling medical equipments, Sewoon Shopping Center, Gwangjang Market, and Changsin-dong Toy Wholesale Market.
This festival will not only recreate the marketplace during Yukuijeon's reign, but feature exhibitions, performances, special experience programs, and tours of the Sijeonhaengrang for its visitors.

- Date : Sept 14, 2018 (Fri) - Sept 15, 2018 (Sat) 13:00 – 18:00

             ※ Opening Ceremony: Sept 14 (Fri), 15:00 

- Location: Sept 14, 2018 (Fri) Sewoon Shopping Center, Gwangjang Market 

             Sept 15, 2018 (Sat) A section of Changsin-dong’s Stationery Store Street

Celebrating its 13th year, Yukuijeon Festival 2018 will aim to spread awareness and educate visitors about the many different markets and sectors like the jewelry district, Sewoon Shopping Center, Jongno medical equipment market, Gwangjang Market, Changsin-dong Toy Wholesale Market, printing district, aquarium market, etc. existing within the district of Jongno.

name: Made in Cheonggyecheon: Era of Pirated Pop Culture - Special Exhibition
summary: A special exhibition titled “Made in Cheonggyecheon: Era of Pirated Pop Culture” will be on display in Cheonggyecheon Museum from Friday, Aug. 24, 2018 to Sunday, Nov. 11, 2018.
description_html:
Made in Cheonggyecheon: Era of Pirated Pop Culture - Special Exhibition

 

A special exhibition titled “Made in Cheonggyecheon: Era of Pirated Pop Culture” will be on display in Cheonggyecheon Museum from Friday, Aug. 24, 2018 to Sunday, Nov. 11, 2018.

 

This exhibition is going to be the first of many in a series to examine the impact Cheonggyecheon Stream played on the history of pop culture in Seoul. The 1960s to the 80s was an era where pirated media reproduction and distribution happened frequently within the Sewoon Shopping Center due to the growing popularity and demand of pop culture. In this exhibition, visitors will be able to see some of the pirated tapes, books, and game devices that were distributed during this particular era.

summary: A special exhibition which highlights the history and transformation of Sinchon, “Frontier of Korean Youth Culture, Sinchon” will be put on display at Seoul Museum of History from Wednesday, Aug. 22, 2018 to Sunday, Oct. 21, 2018.
description_html:
A special exhibition which highlights the history and transformation of Sinchon, “Frontier of Korean Youth Culture, Sinchon” will be put on display at Seoul Museum of History from Wednesday, Aug. 22, 2018 to Sunday, Oct. 21, 2018.

 

“Frontier of Korean Youth Culture, Sinchon” will focus on the past youth community and culture that was prevalent in Sinchon district from the 70s to the 90s.

 

It will also focus on the geographical and spatial transformation of Sinchon starting from the Joseon dynasty to the present and bring attention to the sociocultural characteristics of the area as it became influenced by the arts, Western culture, and democratic ideals.

name: The Great Rite of Sajik Daeje 2019
summary: The great rite of Sajik Daeje is a ritual dating back to the Joseon Dynasty. Sajik Daeje lives on today in Seoul and a historical re-enactment of the ritual is held once a year.
description_html:
The Great Rite of Sajik Daeje 2019
 

The great rite of Sajik Daeje is a ritual dating back to the Joseon Dynasty. 

 

Sajik Daeje continues to live on today in Seoul as a historical re-enactment of the ritual is held once every year. Efforts to preserve this piece of Korean cultural heritage have lead to the preservation of Sajik Daeje.

 

On October 19, 2000, the Sajik Daeje, or "Great Rite for the Gods of Earth and Agriculture",  was designated as Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 111. This annual ceremonial rite was held to honor the ancestors and pay homage to the great gods of the land and grains. It was also held as a prayer for peace and prosperity of the people throughout the land. At present, the Sajik Daeje Ceremonial Committee strives to preserve the tradition of this important historical rite.

 

For generations, Koreans were people who heavily relied on agriculture and the harvest. Thus, Sajik Daeje was an extremely important ritual that held a significant place in society. However, Japanese powers forced the abolishment of Sajik Daeje in 1908 (the 2nd year of Sunjong’s reign). The rites were not carried out again until 1988, when the Jeonju Lee Royal Family Association came to restore the practice of Sajik Daeje again. The members of the association are descended from the Korean royal family, and the association continues to presides over the ritual to this day.

 

The Sajik Daeje was a ritual of utmost importance and solemnity in the Joseon era. The rites were carried out by the kings, civic officials, and military officials. Today, the procession departs from Deoksugung Palace at 11:00 a.m. The 50-minute procession winds its way past Sejong-ro, Gwanghwamun, and Sajik-ro to arrive at the Sajikandan Altar. Upon arrival of the procession, the Sajik Daeje ritual is immediately carried out at the Sajikandan Altar around 12:00 p.m. The preservation and reenactment of Sajik Daeje has allowed for an increased recognition of Korean culture and heritage among Koreans and foreign visitors alike. The great rite of Sajik Daeje is an experience that should not be missed.

 

※ This is a 2019 event. Further information about this event in 2020 will be updated at a later date.

The Day Seoul Went Underwater : Exhibition

 

Taking place from Tuesday, Jul. 24th to Friday Aug. 31st, 2018, “The Day Seoul Went Underwater : Exhibition” shines a spotlight on ordinary everyday places like the 1970 Hangang relaxation areas, urban swimming pools, and bathhouses.

 

A joint project between Seoul Museum of History and university students, this exhibition will focus on water-related places like the swimming pools and bathhouses in Seoul.

 

The exhibits will depict the daily lives of people living in “underwater” Seoul and will portray the culture of “bathing” in a new light. Visitors are encouraged to step inside, away from the blistering summer heat, and enjoy these wonderfully creative and unique exhibits.

name: The 1988 Olympics: Momentum of Changes in Seoul Exhibition
summary: In celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Seoul Olympics, an exhibition titled “The 1988 Olympics: Momentum of Changes in Seoul” will be held in Seoul Museum of History from Saturday, Jul. 28th to Sunday, Oct. 14th, 2018.
description_html:
The 1988 Olympics: Momentum of Changes in Seoul Exhibition

 

In celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Seoul Olympics, an exhibition titled “The 1988 Olympics: Momentum of Changes in Seoul” will be held in Seoul Museum of History from Saturday, Jul. 28th to Sunday, Oct. 14th, 2018.  

 

The exhibition will be divided into three parts: "Part 1: 1988, the Olympics and Seoul", "Part 2: The 1988 Olympics and spatial change in Seoul", and "Part 3: The Olympics and Seoul culture of the 1980s". 

 

This exhibition will look back on how Seoul got to host the 1988 Olympics 30 years ago and show how hosting these events led to the rapid growth of Korean society and urban development of Seoul.

summary: Summer of Seoul 2018 will take place on Friday and Saturday, from Aug. 10th to Aug. 11th, 2018.
description_html:
Summer of Seoul 2018 

 

Summer of Seoul 2018 will take place under the theme of “taking a cultural vacation in Seoul” on Friday and Saturday, from Aug. 10th to Aug. 11th, 2018.

 

Celebrating its 11th year, Summer of Seoul 2018 will feature both “outdoor” and “indoor” programs. Outdoor programs will take place at Seoul Plaza, Cheonggye Plaza, and Gwanghwamun Square while indoor programs will take place in the 6 different cultural facilities located around Seoul.

 

This year, Seoul Plaza will host “Cinemusic Vacance”, a film festival featuring movies screening and movie soundtrack, and a media art show. In Cheonggye Plaza, a graphic art contest and hip-hop performances and breakdancing is scheduled to take place. In Gwanghwamun Square, a big tree decorated with summer vacation products and giant ice sculptures will be on display among other things. 

 

※ This is a 2018 event. Further information about this event in 2019 will be updated at a later date.

name: The Election Climate in Seoul : Exhibition
summary: From Jun. 5th to Jul. 15th, 2018, Seoul Museum of History will hold an exhibition titled “The Election Climate in Seoul” to showcase the political climate surrounding past elections in Seoul.
description_html:
The Election Climate in Seoul : Exhibition

 

 

From Jun. 5th to Jul. 15th, 2018, Seoul Museum of History will hold an exhibition titled “The Election Climate in Seoul” to showcase the political climate surrounding past elections in Seoul.

 

Photos and various records depicting the election of the first mayor of Seoul, their campaign processes, voting booths, and the polling and counting of votes will be put on display. Videos of the first Seoul mayoral election of 1960 and the subsequent regional elections that happened in 1995 will also be shown, allowing visitors an opportunity to see how the political climate was like in Korea's history.
