name: Marie Laurencin : Special Exhibition
summary: Dec. 9th, 2017 to March 11th, 2018. Visit the largest-ever retrospective of Marie Laurencin in Asia at the Hangaram Art Museum.
description_html:
Life through the Eyes of Marie Laurencin 

Visit the largest-ever retrospective of the French artist Marie Laurencin in Asia at the Hangaram Art Museum. The exhibition will run from Dec. 9th, 2017 to March 11th, 2018. It is Korea's first large-scale Laurencin retrospective and the largest ever held in Asia. 

More than 160 pieces of Laurencin's work will be on display. Among the artworks there will be 70 oil paintings, several lithographs, many watercolors and even photographs for visitors to enjoy. The retrospective is a rare opportunity to take a look at Laurencin's life and artworks from her time as a struggling artist to finding success and acclaim. Take in Marie Laurencin's unique style and see how she made her mark on the Parisian art.

name: Drawn by the Wind Exhibition: Shin Yun-bok & Jeong Seon
summary: Nov. 24th, 2017 to May 24th, 2018. "Drawn by the Wind" is a Joseon-themed media art exhibition that will take place at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).
description_html:
"Drawn by the Wind"

"Drawn by the Wind" is a Joseon-themed media art exhibition that will feature a modern exploration of artworks by the artists Shin Yun-bok and Jeong Seon. The exhibition will take place in the Design Museum at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) from Nov. 24th, 2017 to May 24th, 2018.

Shin Yun-bok and Jeong Seon were major artists of the Joseon dynasty. This exhibition will take some of their major works and expand on the imagined, hidden stories within the artworks. Shin Yun-bok, also known by his pseudonym Hyewon, was famed for his depictions of everyday life. His famous series of paintings, Hyewon Jeonsipchub, served as inspiration for some of this exhibition's displays. Art displays span a range of mediums and genres. Visitors can look forward to colorful art and creative staging, animated videos, and other media art.

name: Taehwagwan-gil 2017 : Culture and History in Seoul
summary: Nov. 10th (Fri) to Nov. 24th (Fri) 2017. The Taehwagwan-gil festival will take place to commemorate the March 1st Independence Movement. Learn about Korea's independence movement and history through exhibitions, activities, and performances!
description_html:
March 1st Independence Movement

The Taehwagwan-gil festival will take place to commemorate the March 1st Independence Movement. The festival will run from Nov. 10th through Nov. 24th, 2017. Learn about Korea's independence movement and history through exhibitions, activities, and performances! On March 1st, 1919, 33 leaders of the Korean independence movement gathered at the Taehwagwan restaurant in Seoul to read aloud the Korean Declaration of Independence from imperial Japan. The Taehwagwan-gil festival will take place along the street next to where the Taehwagwan restaurant stood. 

Visitors will be able to take part in a range of activities and there will be exhibitions, special talks on a range of subjects, live music, and hands-on experiences.

Locals and tourists alike can learn about the hidden history of Seoul and Korea while honoring the March 1st Independence Movement at Taehwagwan-gil 2017.  

※ March 1st Movement: The March 1st declaration of independence in 1919 was the earliest major display of independence against the Japanese colonial authorities.

name: King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment 2017
summary: Sept. 23rd and 24th, 2017. The King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment will take place over 59.2km and include 4,391 participants in its reenactments and processions.
description_html:
See History Come Alive on the Streets of Korea

The King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment will take place over 59.2km and include 4,391 participants in its reenactments and processions. Taking place in Seoul, Suwon, and Hwaseong, visitors will be able to watch the procession and take part in related activities on September 23rd and 24th, 2017. 

King Jeongjo was the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty and he is considered one of the greatest Joseon kings for his visionary politics and his role in supporting the literary and cultural arts. King Jeongjo was known for his devotion to his parents and after his father's death, he would often make the journey from Seoul to Hwaseong to visit his father's tomb. The reenactment follows the same route that the king took over two centuries ago and the participants will be dressed in historically accurate 18th century clothing. In addition to the royal procession, there will be other activities and events for visitors to enjoy. Have fun and see history in action at the King Jeongjo Tomb Parade Reenactment!

○ Parade Events
- Seoul Course : Changdeokgung Palace Leaving Ceremony, Assassin-Warrior Baek Dong-su, Baedari Opening Ceremony, etc. 
- Suwon Course : Welcome Ceremony for King Jeongjo Entering Suwon, Flash Mob by the Joseon People,Daedongnori and Gijeopnori, etc. 
- Hwaseong Course : Reenactment of Rites at the Royal Tomb, Reenactment of Funereal Service, Greetings, etc.

name: Storytelling Street Performance at Dongdaemun : HADOGAM LEESAENGJEON
summary: Sept. 8th through Oct. 21st, 2017. A traditional martial arts performance will take place at Dongdaemun every Friday and Saturday evening. See the story of Hadogam Leesaengjeon!
description_html:
See a Traditional Story Performed at Dongdaemun!

A traditional martial arts performance will take place at Dongdaemun every Friday and Saturday evening from Sept. 8th through Oct. 21st, 2017. See the story of Hadogam Leesaengjeon as performed on the Outdoor Stage in front of Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial in Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).

Though Dongdaemun is best known today for being a fashion and design mecca, during the Joseon Dynasty, the area was once home to a famed barracks and martial arts training center called Hadogam. Hadogam Leesaengjeon tells the story of a fabric merchant known as Leesaengjeon who is fascinated by martial arts and soldiers. He dreams of becoming the nation's finest warrior but achieving that dream seems out of reach. Then one day, he overhears a band of robbers talking about their plan to kill the king. See what happens next at Dongdaemun! The performance is an exciting blend of martial arts and theater!

DDP will also be hosting many other online and offline events during the performance period. The Seoul Bamdokkaebi Night Market will also be taking place at this time. Have fun and catch a performance at Dongdaeum! 

※ Hadogam: A major military martial arts training center and barracks during the Joseon Dynasty.

name: Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2017
summary: Sept. 2nd to Nov. 5th, 2017. Enjoy events and exhibitions on architecture and urban issues  at the Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism. Events and exhibitions will be held throughout Seoul.
description_html:
"Imminent Commons"

The Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism will open on September 2nd and run until November 5th, 2017. Visitors will be able to enjoy events and exhibitions on architecture and urban issues at locations throughout Seoul as part of the biennale. Unlike arts biennales, the Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism will go beyond a simple exhibition-viewer format. The Seoul biennale will be an experimental platform that explores issues relating to architecture, urban planning, and urbanism.

The theme of "imminent commons" will be explored in depth as it relates to sustainable cities. In particular, the concept of nine commons will (nine ecological and technological factors) and their impact on the future of cities and humanity will be engaged during the biennale. There will be educational programs, attend movie screenings, tour programs and more for visitors to enjoy.

name: Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival 2017
summary: Sept. 21st to 24th, 2017. The Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival will take place at Olympic Park in Seoul.
description_html:
Experience Hanseong Baekje Culture in Seoul!

The Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival will take place at Olympic Park in Seoul from Sept. 21st to 24th, 2017. This year's festival theme is "Ancient Seoul! Meet the kings of Hanseong Baekje." 

The Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival is a fun, interactive festival that highlights the ancient Hanseong Baekje kingdom and culture! Festival-goers will be able to learn about an important era of Korean history while enjoy hands-on activities and experiences. The festival will feature a recreation of a period village called the Hanseong Baekje Experience Village where visitors can see traditional games and military barracks. The festival will also have a wide range of Korean and international food on offer. 

The three day festival will be jam-packed with events. There will be a cultural parade, a Hanseong Baekje gala parade, fireworks, concerts, and much more at Olympic Park in Songpa-gu! 

※ Hanseong Baekje Kingdom: An ancient Korean kingdom founded in 18 BCE in the region now known as Seoul. The Hanseong Baekje kingdom endured for about 475 years.

summary: Aug. 14th and Aug. 15th, 2017. Celebrate the 72nd anniversary of Korea's independence at the Seodaemun Independence Day Festival.

Learn about fight for freedom undertaken by Korean activists and patriots and how the road to democracy and peace was paved with supression, resistance, and ordeals.

The 2017 Yeo Woo Rak Festival will take place at the National Theater of Korea. The festival's name is shorthand in Korean for, "our Korean music is here." name: "Unbuttoning French Fashion" Exhibition
summary: May 30th through Aug. 15th. 2017. See a special exhibition on the history of buttons in French fashion from the 18th to 20th centuries at the National Museum of Korea.
description_html:
"Unbuttoning the French Fashion from the 18th to the 20th Century" 

See a special exhibition on the history of buttons in French fashion from the 18th to 20th centuries at the National Museum of Korea. The exhibition will run from May 30th through Aug. 15th. 2017. 

Learn about French fashion throughout the ages as seen through buttons. Buttons are often thought of as small, unimportant adornments. Through this wide-ranging exhibiton, visitors can see how buttons reflect human history and society. The exhibition has 1,800 pieces on display. In addition to buttons, the exhibition will also display garments, paintings, drawings, photographs, and artwork.

Visit the National Museum of Korea to see how a small item can have an outsized impact on the world.

name: Storytelling Performance at Cheonggyecheon Stream : Fly, Ishimi
summary: June 3rd to July 23rd, 2017. A traditional fusion performance will take place at Cheonggyecheon Stream every Saturday and Sunday
description_html:
See a Traditional Story Performed at Cheonggyecheon Stream!

A traditional fusion performance will take place at Cheonggyecheon Stream every Saturday and Sunday from June 3rd through July 23rd, 2017. See performance artists tell the story of "Fly, Ishimi" at Gwangtonggyo Bridge. 

Traditional Korean puppetry plays, known as "kkokdugaksi noreum" are intangible cultural asset no. 3 and "Fly, Ishimi" is best known as a traditional Korean puppet play. The performance at Cheonggyecheon Stream is a reimagination of that play. It turns a puppet play into a dance-focused street performance. The charms and merits of puppetry can be seen on a larger scale at the Cheonggyecheon performances. There will be a giant Ishimi figure that will dance among the crowd as part of the performance. "Fly, Ishimi" is a fun, interactive performance that suitable for all ages. 

July 23rd is the closing day for "Fly, Ishimi" and there will be special events to mark the occasion. Performance-goers who bring along a paper cup will receive a free seedling as a gift. Foreign visitors can also write out a postcard and have the postcard mailed to any location of their choice. 

※ Isimi : Also sometimes called imugi, is a mythical creature from Korean folklore. Before a dragon becomes a dragon, it was sometimes said to have taken the form of a giant serpent, which was also called ishimi.

History, Culture, and Atmosphere

Jeong-dong Culture Night will take place on May 26th and 27th, 2017 in the Jeong-dong neighborhood. Take part in themed activities and enjoy the romantic atmosphere at the festival. Jeong-Dong Culture Night will have 6 themes, Night Blooms, Night Alleys, Night History, Night Stories, Night Scenery, Night Delicacies. name: Roads of Arabia Special Exhibition
summary: May 9th to Aug. 27th, 2017. The National Museum of Korea will hold a special exhibition titled, "Roads of Arabia"
description_html:
The Archaeological Treasures of Saudi Arabia

The National Museum of Korea will hold a special exhibition titled, "Roads of Arabia" from May 9th through Aug. 27th, 2017. The exhibition will feature 466 different artifacts from throughout the ages. The oldest piece in the exhibition is a stone figure in the shape of a man that is roughly 4,000 years old. A gate from the Great Mosque of Mecca (where the Kaaba stands) will also be on display. See archaeological treasures from Saudi Arabia and more at the National Museum of Korea!

name: Taekwondo in Namsangol Hanok Village 2018
summary: "Taekwondo Performance in Namsangol" will run every Thursday to Sunday (Thurs 15:00 - 15:25 / Fri - Sun 13:00 - 13:25, 15:00 - 15:25) from May 4th, 2018 to October 2018 at Namsangol Hanok Village.
description_html:
Internationally Beloved, Korea's Representative Cultural Sport Taekwondo
 
"Taekwondo Performance in Namsangol" will run every Thursday to Sunday (Thurs 15:00 - 15:25 / Fri - Sun 13:00 - 13:25, 15:00 - 15:25) from May 4th, 2018 to October 2018 at Namsangol Hanok Village. Performances will be held every week, Friday through Sunday with two performances each day (May will only have one daily performance). The city of Seoul has held annual Taekwondo performances since 2007 so that Korean and foreign visitors alike may enjoy Taekwondo. See the inner strength and spirit of Taekwondo through Taekwondo demonstrations and nonverbal performances. Admission is free.  
 
[Traditional Taekwondo Demonstration Performances]

Korea's best demonstration performance teams will show off Taekwondo's long history. There will be board breaking, attack and defense technique demonstrations, and team demonstrations. On the stage, see Taekwondo as an art and experience the dynamism and spirit of Korea's national sport. Be witness to the strength and brilliance of Taekwondo's techniques. 

- Korea's finest Taekwondo demonstration performance team: Kukkiwon Demonstration Performance Team
- Korea's finest children's Taekwondo demonstration performance team: Midong Elementary School Children's Demonstration Performance Team 

- Military-specific combat demonstration team: 3rd Unit Taekwondo Demonstration Team
 

[Original Cultural Taekwondo Performances]

See Taekwondo in combination with K-POP, traditional music, musicals, traditional dance and other genres. The performances will tell original stories that are both Korean and global. Teams who have created original content will be participating! Korean and international visitors alike will have fun and see Korean culture through these nonverbal performances.

 -  NOLJA Taekwondo Team + Heung Cultural and Artistic Cooperative:  A collaboration performance of different Korean cultural and artistic elements  
 -  Mireume Taekwondo Team: A light, fun Taekwondo performance

 -  K.U.T.D Taekwondo Team: Traditional demonstration and dance
 

[Taekwondo Experience Program]
After the performances have concluded, there will be activities and experiences open to those who reserve in advance. Try board-breaking or self defense lessons for females! After the activities finish, participants can get a commemorative photo taken and the photo will be made into a postcard as a souvenir. An additional souvenir will be given as a gift for 3 participants each session.

▶2018 Namsangol Taekwondo Experience Program  - Application Form  
 
2018 Namsangol Taekwondo Experience Program


Wear a uniform, learn the basics, and break some boards in this 60 minute Taekwondo class! Learn about Taekwondo culture and spirit with the Namsangol Taekwondo Experience Program.
Foreign visitors to Namsangol Hanok Village can learn about the Korean spirit and culture through the national sport of Taekwondo. Take this chance to learn about Taekwondo in Seoul!

▶2018 Namsangol Taekwondo Experience Program - Application Form
(Only foreigners are eligible to apply for this program.)


- Eligibility : Foreign nationals
- Duration : May 10th til October 2018. Wednesdays and Thursdays 10:30-11:30        
- Location : Namsangol Hanok Village, Cheonwoogak Stage
- Capacity : 15 participants (Selection will be based on order of application submission)
- Program Fee : Free (uniforms can be purchased at the venue for 30,000)
- Application Deadline : 3 days before your desired participation date
- Inquiries : +82-2-6674-4303, sugary2001@gmail.com


* Classes will be conducted in English.

summary:
May 3rd to May 7th, 2017. Seoul's global culture festival C-Festival will take place at COEX in
 Samseong-dong, Gangnam.
description_html:
A Culture Festival in the Heart of Seoul!

Seoul's global culture festival C-Festival will take place at COEX in Samseong-dong, Gangnam from May 3rd to May 7th, 2017.

This year's festival concept is "an urban playground in the heart of the city" and the festival's highlight will be the C-Festival parade and the fireworks display. The C-Festival will be divided into three themed sections: Dream Theater, Dream Garden, and Dream Agit. There will be many diverse cultural activities and experiences on offer! Festival-goers will be able to enjoy craft beer and food at the Dream Garden, and the Dream Agit will feature exhibitions with art from popular artists. The parade and street art shows will take place at Dream Theater.

The Art Toy Culture event and the Cook Festa event will also be a part of this year's C-Festival. The young at heart can view and purchase an array of figurines and toys at the Art Toy Culture event. Cook Festa will feature food exhibitons and food stalls operated by famous restaurants across the country.

Enjoy the warm spring weather at the global culture festival C-Festival! There will be something for everyone at this large and fun cultural event.

name: Hangeul Design Exhibition at the National Hangeul Museum
summary: Feb. 28th to May 28th, 2017. The National Hangeul Museum will be celebrating the 620th anniversary of the birth of King Sejong the Great with an exhibition on the Hangeul script.
description_html:
Prototypes and Future of the Korean Alphabet

The National Hangeul Museum will be celebrating the 620th anniversary of the birth of King Sejong the Great with an exhibition on the Hangeul script. The exhibition will run from Feb. 28th until May 28th, 2017.

23 teams of designers have re-imagined the Hangeul alphabet drawing inspiration from the Hunminjeongeum. The Hunminjeongeum was published during King Sejong's reign and the manuscript was both the king's declaration of a new writing system and it explained the principles and purpose of Hangeul. The designers have created artistic interpretations of the original form of the manuscript and excerpts from the manuscript.

There are 30 works on display in formats such as video, models, and graphic design. This exhibition will give visitors a chance to appreciate the original forms of Hangeul and its potential applications in people's lives.

※ King Sejong the Great : The fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty, Sejong reigned from 1418 to 1450. He is known as the creator of Hangeul.
    Hunminjeongeum : Published during Sejong's reign, this manuscript was the king's promulgation of the Korean alphabet. Though now known as Hangeul, the alphabet was once referred to as hunminjeongeum. The Hunminjeongeum is a registered UNESCO heritage property.

name: Saimdang, Her Garden Exhibition
summary: Jan. 24th till Sept. 3rd, 2017. See a special exhibiton of Shin Saimdang's artworks at the Seoul Museum.
description_html:
Shin Saimdang, Painter and Poet

The Seoul Museum in Buam-dong will be hosting a special exhibiton of Shin Saimdang's artworks from Jan. 24th till September 3rd, 2017. The exhibition, "Saimdang, Her Garden," marks the 5th anniversary of the museum's opening. Shin Saimdang, also known simply as Saimdang, was a famed Joseon-era painter and poet who lived during the 16th century. There has been growing modern interest in her life and art and Hallyu fans may be familiar with the K-drama series about Shin's life, "Saimdang, Light's Diary."

Visitors will be able to see an array of Shin's work and appreciate her artistic aesthetic through the exhibition. Shin's artwork tends to have clean lines and a natural symmetry. The works on display are superb examples of Eastern art and visitors will be able to see the kind of art that was popular during the Joseon era.

※ Shin Saimdang : Shin Saimdang lived during the middle of the Joseon period and she is best known as being the mother of the famed Confucian scholar Yulgok. Though Shin's image mostly revolves around her reputation as a wise mother, she is also notable for her achievements as an artist and writer during a highly patriarchal era. Shin appears on the 50,000 won note.

name: SeMA Green 2017 : Nalgae.PaTI
summary: March 14th through May 14th, 2017. The biannual SeMA Green 2017 exhibition will take place at the Seoul Museum of Art.
description_html:
A Meeting of Hangeul and Design

The biannual SeMA Green 2017 exhibition will take place at the Seoul Museum of Art from March 14th through May 14th, 2017.

The exhibition will highlight the Hangeul (Korean alphabet) typography pioneer Ahn Sang-soo, whose pen name is Nalgae, and the Paju Typography Institute (PaTI). The exhibition will display the ways that Ahn de-constructed, arranged, and styled the letters of Hangeul through different art mediums, calligraphy, and performance. Ahn's love of the Korean alphabet has resulted in a continuous search for ways to express himself through design and art.

Exhibition-goers will also be able to learn about PaTI and the design and educational work that they do. Projects designed by some of the institute's students will allow visitors to see the issues that interest young people and think about different forms of design in contemporary society.

summary: March 20th to April 14th, 2017. Take a nighttime tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace and tour Sojubang, the royal kitchen. Visitors will also be provided with a dinner of 12 royal dishes to enjoy!

name: Year of the Rooster - Lunar New Year's First Full Moon Events
summary: The first full moon of the Lunar New Year has customarily been considered an important occasion in Korea.
description_html:
Ring in the Year of the Rooster!

The first full moon of the Lunar New Year has customarily been considered an important occasion in Korea. As the first one of the year, the full moon carried great significance. The day of the first full moon was thought to be able to foretell fortunesfor the year ahead.

The first full moon signifies a chance to wish for good luck and good health. Accordingly, Lunar New Year customs to celebrate the first full moon signal ways for people to wish for good luck and good health. Celebrations for the first full moon of theLunar New Year will take place at several locations in Seoul and visitors will be able to enjoy fun events and activities. Nut cracking, drinking liquor (drinking during the first full moon was thought to make your ears sharper and better able toreceive good news), eating ogok-bap (five grain rice), and tal (mask) performances are just some of the traditional Lunar New Year's first full moon activities that visitors will be able to enjoy. Have fun and wish for good health and good luck inthe new year at these Seoul events!

name: Renoir : Images of Women Exhibition
summary: Dec. 12th, 2016 to Mar. 26th, 2017. The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) will host a special exhibition of works by the French Impressionist, Pierre-Auguste Renoir.
description_html:
Renoir, a Leader of the Impressionist Movement

The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) will host a special exhibition of works by the French Impressionist, Pierre-Auguste Renoir in celebration of 130 years of Korean-French diplomatic ties and the 70th anniversary of the Korean newspaper, the Kyunghyang Shinmun. The exhibition, Renoir : Images of Women, will run from Dec. 12, 2016 until March 26th, 2017.

Renoir thought art should portray the pleasant and beauty of life, and he enjoyed focusing his artwork on women. Fittingly, the theme of this exhibition is women. Exhibition-goers will be able to appreciate Renoir's technical skills, genius, and artistry through his depictions of women and everyday life. Don't miss this opportunity to see the work of a French master in person at the Seoul Museum of Art!

name: Father of Modern Architecture : Le Corbusier Exhibition
summary: Dec. 6th, 2016 to Mar. 26th, 2017. The Seoul Arts Center's Hangaram Art Museum will host a special exhibition of Le Corbusier's works.
description_html:
Father of Modern Architecture

The Seoul Arts Center's Hangaram Art Museum will host a special exhibition of Le Corbusier's works from Dec. 6th, 2016 until March 26th, 2017. The exhibition celebrates the 2016 addition of 17 Le Corbusier projects to the UNESCO World Heritage List, and it is the largest Le Corbusier exhibition ever held.

Le Corbusier's contributions to modern architecture are historic, and his influence in the field is immense. Le Corbusier sought to remedy social problems through architectural solutions. He may be most famous for creating the modern apartment building, thought up as a solution to urban overcrowding. Exhibition-goers will be able to see the work and thought behind Le Corbusier's creative processes, from conception to construction. As a retrospective of Le Corbusier's life, from his youth until his death, the scale of the exhibition is truly expansive. Many of the pieces on display have never been exhibited before, and visitors will be able to appreciate Le Corbusier as an artist as well as an architect. 

※ Le Corbusier : Le Corbusier is the only architect on the Time Magazine 100 Persons of the 20th Century list. He is credited with creating large-scale apartment buildings and was a revolutionary pioneer of modern architecture.

name: "Northern Seoul, Now a Forest of Apartment Buildings" Exhibition
summary: Dec. 17th, 2016 to March 5th, 2017. A special exhibition about the history of Northern Seoul, "Northern Seoul, Now a Forest of Apartment Buildings," will run at the Seoul Museum of History.
description_html:
Journey through the History of Northern Seoul

A special exhibition, "Northern Seoul, Now a Forest of Apartment Buildings," will run at the Seoul Museum of History from Dec. 17th, 2016 until March 5th, 2017. The exhibition is the first-ever exhibition about the history, geography, and urban development of Northern Seoul. Learn about Northern Seoul and its importance as a major residential area for the middle class of the city as well as its role as the former gateway to Seoul during the Joseon Dynasty.

Visitors will be able to see images of Northern Seoul from the Joseon Dynasty up through modern times. In addition to images, there will be 18 video displays and 65 artifacts and items on display. Display items include a neighborhood periodical for Mangu-dong that dates back to 1760, photographs of the old Gyeongwon Railway Line, gilt bronze Buddhist artifacts from the Dobong Temple. With this exhibition, people will be able to areas of Northern Seoul and the history of the city.

※ Today, the following areas are considered Northern Seoul: Gangbuk-gu, Dobong-gu, Nowon-gu, and Jungnang-gu.

name: 2017 Seol Festival for Year of the Rooster
summary: Jan. 27th to Jan. 30th, 2017. Celebrate the Lunar New Year at the National Folk Museum with fun activities and performances.
description_html:
The Rooster, Welcoming the New Dawn

Celebrate the Lunar New Year at the National Folk Museum from Jan. 27th to Jan. 30th, 2017. There will be performances and fun activities to enjoy!

Just as roosters welcome in the new dawn, visitors will be able to welcome in the new year at the museum. There will be traditional arts performances with music, a Buddhist prayer corner, and crafts activities to partake in. Visitors will also be able to experience Lunar New Year customs that take place in Korean homes. A charye table (a major part of holiday celebrations) will be set up on the museum's grounds so that visitors can observe holiday rituals. There will be a hanbok dress-up experience and great photo opportunities throughout the festival's duration. 

For a bit of light-hearted fun, visitors can have their fortunes read read as part of the museum's Yutnori Fortunes event. Yutnori is a traditional Korean game that uses sticks rather than dice. Fortunes will be read with yutnori sticks!

name: Egyptian Treasures from the Brooklyn Museum Exhibition
summary: Dec. 20th, 2016 to April 9th, 2017. This special exhibition, Egyptian Treasures from the Brooklyn Museum, will take place at the National Museum of Korea. See artifacts from one of the world's great ancient civilizations!
description_html:
"For an Eternal Life" : Artifacts from Ancient Egypt

Special exhibition, Egyptian Treasures from the Brooklyn Museum, will take place at the National Museum of Korea from Dec. 20th, 2016 until April 9th, 2017. Visitors will be able to see artifacts from one of the world's great ancient civilizations.

The exhibition's pieces are on loan from the Brooklyn Museum, located in the United States. The exhibition's theme is "for an eternal life" and it is comprised of 229 pieces. The exhibition includes human and animal mummies, sarcophogi, sculptures, jewelry, and more. The artifacts are not mere objects, they provide a window into the minds and beliefs of ancient Egyptians regarding death and the afterlife. 

Visitors to the exhibition can enjoy the artistry, creativity of ancient Egyptians as well as learn about the hopes they held for eternal life. Take a special journey back in time at the National Museum of Korea.

name: Fornasetti : Practical Madness Exhibition
summary: Nov. 22nd, 2016 to Mar. 19th, 2017. See Asia's first-ever showcase of the artist Piero Fornasetti at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).
description_html:
Practical Madness

In 2013, for the occasion of the 100th anniversary of artist Piero Fornasetti's birth, the Triennale Design Museum in Milan organized the exhibition, "Practical Madness." The exhibition began to tour internationally in 2015 and its arrival in Seoul marks the first-ever showcase of Fornasetti in Asia. The exhibition will take place at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) from Nov. 22nd, 2016 until March 19th, 2017.

There are over 1,300 pieces in this vast exhibition, the Triennale pulled items from their archives. The pieces were selected by Barnaba Fornasetti himself, an artist in his own right and the son of Piero Fornasetti. Piero Fornasetti's work spans across different mediums, from designs and drawings, to sculptures and painting.

Fornasetti's influence can be felt in modern art even today, and visitors to the exhibition can enjoy his artwork and learn about the artist. "Practical Madness" has crossed the entire world; see what has made exhibition has so popular by visiting DDP!

name: Alphonse Mucha Exhibition : Pioneer of Modern Graphic Design
summary: Dec. 3rd, 2016 to March 5th, 2017. An exhibition of works by the great Alphonse Mucha will run at the Seoul Arts Center's Hangaram Art Museum.
description_html:
Alphonse Mucha the Artist, the Pioneer 

An exhibition of works by the great Alphonse Mucha will run at the Seoul Arts Center's Hangaram Art Museum from Dec. 3rd, 2016 till March 5th, 2017. Alphonse Mucha is most famous for his intricately drawn advertisements and posters featuring graceful women surrounded by flowers, but he was also one of the fathers of modern graphic design.

Mucha's artwork and style became representative of Art Nouveau in Europe and the United States. Art Nouveau was an artistic style and movement that took place during the late 19th century and early 20th century. His influence continues to be felt today as new generations of artists continue to be inspired by Mucha's work. Mucha's influence can be seen in diverse fields of art; from comic artists to commercial designers, and more.

This exhibition will showcase Mucha's artworks and the breadth of his influence in graphic design. Alongside works by Mucha, there will also be displays from modern Korean and Japanese graphic artists that were influenced by Mucha. Visitors will be able to enjoy Mucha's works as well as modern pieces at the Seoul Arts Center.

※ Art Nouveau - Art Nouveau was an artistic style and movement that dominated the decorative arts, fine arts, and architecture during the late 19th century and early 20th century in Europe and America.

name: Five Nobleman's Lunar New Year Feast
summary: Jan. 28th and 29th, 2017. Ring in the New Year at Namsangol Hanok Village and take part in this special event!
description_html:
Celebrate the Lunar New Year at Namsangol Hanok Village!

Ring in the New Year at Namsangol Hanok Village at the Five Nobleman's Lunar New Year Feast; taking place on Jan. 28th and 29th, 2017. The concept for this special holiday event is a feast at homes of noblemen. Visitors will be able to tour the homes of Korean noblemen while enjoying Lunar New Year festivities. There will be folk games, traditional performances, and hands-on activities for visitors to participate in.

The charye ceremony, which is a memorial ceremony that honors one's ancestors, is an integral part of the holiday. An elaborate charye table is prepared with food as part of the charye ceremony.  At Namsangol, there will be a communal charye table, set up for all who were unable to prepare a charye table at home, accompanied by a guided explanation so that visitors will be able to learn about charye. 

Tteokguk (sliced rice cake soup) is the representative dish of the Lunar New Year. There will be free tteokguk for visitors to enjoy, as well as fun activities such as writing wish notes, making crafts, and much more. Enjoy the Lunar New Year holiday at Namsangol Hanok Village!

name: Musee d'Orsay Exhibition
summary: Oct. 29th, 2016 to March 5th, 2017. The Musee d’Orsay, located in Paris, France, is home to countless masterpieces and historically important works of art. The Musee d'Orsay exhibition will take place at the Seoul Arts Center’s Hangaram Museum.
description_html:
Oct. 29th, 2016 to March 5th, 2017. The Musee d’Orsay, located in Paris, France, is home to countless masterpieces and historically important works of art. The Musee d'Orsay exhibition will take place at the Seoul Arts Center’s Hangaram Museum.

The Musee d’Orsay exhibition commemorates two anniversaries. 2016 marks 130 years of Korean-French diplomatic ties and this exhibition is one of several events that mark this special anniversary. 2016 is also the 30th anniversary of the founding of the Musee d’Orsay. There will be many works on display from many world-famous artists. Two of the most well-known works that will be exhibited are The Gleaners by Jean-François Millet and Meridian by Vincent van Gogh.

There are 131 pieces in this exhibition. Visitors will be able to see masterpieces from the great artists of the 19th such as Millet, Van Gogh, Monet, Gauguin, Cezanne, Degas, and Delacroix.

summary: Nov. 8th through Nov. 13th, 2016. The Turkic Culture Festival will take place at the National Museum of Korea. The festival will celebrate mutual cultural ties between Korea and Turkic countries, as well as feature cultural showcase performances from the 5 Turkic countries.

The Turkic Culture Festival will take place at the National Museum of Korea starting on Nov. 8th through Nov. 13th, 2016. The Turkic Culture Festival will also feature cultural showcase performances from the 5 Turkic countries, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, and Turkmenistan.

It's not every day that people get a chance to learn about and experience Turkic cultures in Seoul! The arts performances that are scheduled to take place are sure to impress festival-goers but the festival has even more to offer. name: The City in Art, Art in the City
summary: Oct. 5th to Nov. 23rd, 2016. This special exhibition at the National Museum of Korea will display Korean masterpieces pertaining to urban culture from the 18th century onward.
description_html:
A special exhibition, "the City in Art, Art in the City," will take place at the National Museum of Korea from Oct. 5th until Nov. 23rd, 2016. The exhibition will display Korean masterpieces pertaining to urban culture from the 18th century onward. The exhibition has many superb and famed pieces, including some that have been loaned to the museum. The artworks' themes will portray the urban landscape and deal with sentiments and aesthetics of the late Joseon period through modernity.  

Korean institutions such as the Kansong Art and Culture Foundation, Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art, and the Seoul Museum of History loaned works. Internationally, the Liaoning Museum of China, the National Museum of Japanese History, and the Hamburg Museum of Ethnology also loaned works to complete this fascinating exhibition of life in a growing urban space.

name: ST-BOMB 2016
summary: Nov. 17th though Nov. 30th, 2016. ST-BOMB 2016 is a chance to see new forms of theater and performance. Catch performances from Korean and international artists at venues throughout Seoul.
description_html:
They're the Bomb! Performances with Style and International Flavor

Nov. 17th though Nov. 30th, 2016. ST-BOMB 2016 will take place from Nov. 17th through Nov. 30th. The festival is a chance to see new forms of theater and performance in Seoul from domestic and foreign artists. There will be 6 plays and performance pieces by artists and troupes from 5 different countries. Performances will take place at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts' M Theater, CJ azit Daehak-ro, and Ellim Hall.

"Aquatique" is a mask-dance performance from a Chinese dance troupe, with a French director. "Burq Off!" is a one woman show about living life through madly opposing worlds: the glowing promise of modern London versus the glum realities of a conservative Pakistani Muslim home. "1969: A Space Odyssey? Oddity!" part homage, part reinterpretation of Jean-Paul Sartre's famous play "No Exit," the performance is set in the near future in outer space. "Oedipus-Those who want to know" is based on the classic play by Sophocles, "Oedipus" and it is about a human's will to know the truth. "Furtuna" (the word for storm in Russian) is from a Russian playwright and director. It is a show about human, hope and desire, faith and religion, and false attitudes towards others.

In addition to the performances, there will be events such as artsts' panels with discussion of the plays and performances from the festival, lectures on the humanities and opportunities to the performers at other events.

Transformation through light does not refer to simple change of lights or to the lighting industry. The event theme refers to a larger transformation in the culture of Euljiro (Seoul's lighting district), and future changes that may come to fruition. Though the event is focused primarily on light and its uses, in the evening, there will be fusion jazz and classic music playing at DDP’s Oullim Square. It will also be possible for visitors to purchase the novel and innovative light installations on exhibit.

name: 3rd Seoul Kimchi Festival
summary: Nov. 4th through 6th. The 3rd Seoul Kimchi Festival will take place at Seoul Plaza. Experience kimchi and kimjang culture, a designated UNESCO intangible cultural heritage asset!
description_html:
Let's Make and Enjoy Kimchi Together!

The 3rd Seoul Kimchi Festival will run from Nov. 4th through Nov. 6th, 2016. The festival will take place at Seoul Plaza and nearby streets, Sejong-ro and Mugyo-ro.  Visit the festival and experience kimchi and kimjang culture, a designated UNESCO intangible cultural heritage asset! Take part in kimjang (making kimchi) and learn all about kimchi at Seoul Plaza. 

The festival first began in 2014 and the festival's aim was to share and preserve the thousand-year-old kimjang culture.  Every year, people come together at Seoul Plaza and make kimchi while grooving to music of all kinds. The kimchi is donated to low-income families. The music, festivities, and the welcoming atmosphere means the festival feels more like a giant party. A citizens' parade is also part of this year's festivities!

※ Kimjang : The process of making and sharing kimchi in large enough quantities that a family will be sustained through the harsh winter. It is emblematic of Korean sharing culture and kimjang is a designated UNESCO intangible cultural heritage asset.

See Jeong-dong bloom at night and learn about history while seeing great street performances and eating great food.

summary: Oct. 7th to Oct. 16th. Every October, visitors gather to the World Cup Haneul Park to enjoy the crisp fall weather and welcome the blooming of the park's silver grass.
description_html:
Finally, it's Fall - Seoul Silver Grass Festival 2016
Every October, visitors gather to the World Cup Haneul Park to enjoy the crisp fall weather and welcome the blooming of the park's silver grass. The Seoul Pampas Grass Festival will run from Oct. 7th until Oct. 16th this year.
 
Though near the heart of Seoul, visitors will find themselves surrounded by nature when at Haneul Park. The blooming of the pampas grass marks the beginning of fall, so for the month of October, take the time to enjoy the outdoors! The beautiful muted colors of the silver grass, against the blue sky makes for a relaxing atmosphere. By night, the green space is decorated with multi-colored lights. From the highest points of Haneul Park, visitors will be able to enjoy stunning views of the Han River.
 
A walk around Haneul park is highly recommended, especially during October and the festival, for a day of family fun, or quality alone time.

summary: It's the perfect season to enjoy the outdoors and good weather! Organized by the Seoul Tourism Marketing Office, the 2016 Discover Seoul 'Eco Walking Tour' event will be held on October 2nd.
description_html:
2016 Discover Seoul - Eco Walking Tour

It's the perfect season to enjoy the outdoors and good weather! Organized by the Seoul Tourism Marketing Office, the 2016 Discover Seoul 'Eco Walking Tour' event will be held on October 2nd. 

Discover the greener side of Seoul on the Eco Walking Tour around the Saetgang Ecological Park. Home to many migratory birds, and a host of different gardens, the park is a beautiful location to enjoy the fall weather.  During the walk, various events and activities, like an AR (Augmented Reality) Experience, Saetgang Catch and other games, and non-verbal performances, will make this a memorable Sunday afternoon. 

○ Event Name: 2016 Discover Seoul (Eco Walking Tour)
○ Time: Sunday, October 2nd – 1pm to 6pm (5 hours)
○ Place: Building 63~Seoul Marina, Irwon Saetgang, Yeouido-dong
○ Website: www.discoverseoul.kr    

How to Participate
○ Step 1: At 1pm, all participants will meet at Building 63, Hangang Park, Saetgang Ecological Park (Yeouido Garden). To get there, get off at Yeouinaru Station, take Exit 3 and walk for approximately 15 minutes. 
○ Step 2: Before departing, follow the instructions indicated on the main booth and download the Saetgang Catch app. 
○ Step 3: Let the Eco Walking Tour begin! Enjoy the relaxing walk through the Ecological Park, and try to spot 14 different kinds of animal friends. 
○ Step 4: When you arrive at the final destination (the Seoul Marina), check and record your steps on the the Saetgang Seoul app. 
○ Step 5: On stage there will be a non-verbal performance to enjoy and entertain!

summary: Around 2,000 years ago, for around 500 years, Songpa was the capital during the Hanseong-Baekje period. From October 6th to October 9th, 2016, the Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival will revive and celebrate the spirit of the ancient capital.
description_html:
Experience Korean history at the 2016 Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival!

Around 2,000 years ago, for around 500 years, Songpa was the capital during the Hanseong-Baekje period. From October 6th to October 9th, 2016, the Hanseong Baekje Cultural Festival will revive and celebrate the spirit of the ancient capital.
 
First, a musical will help you learn more about the story of this past kingdom, and what it was like in its prime. There will be a Baekje Village, in which you can experience daily life, as people would have in Songpa, thousands of years ago. Feel free to poke around the traditional marketplace and food festival, too!  Furthermore, there will be free tours available of the Mongchontoseong Fortress.
 
Traditional games, folk performances, Songpa Sandae Nori (traditional Korean mask dance) and the Hanseong Baekje Youth Music club are sure to keep you intrigued and entertained. Not to mention, there will be an opening and closing ceremony, with a fireworks showcase during the latter.
 
Together, let’s experience and celebrate the cultural and historical treasures of the Hanseong-Baekje period!

name: King Jeongjo’s Tomb Parade Reenactment 2016
summary: From October 8th-9th, starting at the Changdeokgung Palace, over the course of two days, the largest reproduction of the Joseon Royal Tomb Parade will take place. From Seoul to Suwon, the 46km relay will recreate the scene from over 220 years ago, including the rituals, clothing and food.
description_html:
Recreating history – Join us and experience the Reenactment of King Jeongjo’s Tomb Parade
Starting at the Changdeokgung Palace, over the course of two days, the largest reproduction of the Joseon Royal Tomb Parade will take place. From Seoul to Suwon, the 46km relay will recreate the scene from over 220 years ago, including the rituals, clothing and food. On October 8th, the relay will start in Seoul, and the Suwon leg of the relay will take place on October 9th, finishing at the Hwaseong Fortress.
 
A little history lesson: A myeongdang is a site which is believed to be a favorable location for one’s home or tomb. Upon the passing of his father, Sado Sejo, King Jeongjo, the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty, wished to move his father’s tomb to a known myeongdang in Suwon. Not only that, but King Jeongjo also wanted to make Suwon the new capital, and thus began the construction of Suwon’s Hwaseong Fortress. King Jeongjo visited several times, the largest parade recorded being in 1795. 
 
Over 2,000 people will take part in the parade, as well as 100 horses. There will be martial art performances, a lantern festival and traditional markets towards the end. It will be a great opportunity to experience Korean history and culture.  

○ The Tomb Parade Reenactment Relay
   - Time: Saturday, October 8th – Sunday, October 9th, 2016. 8:30AM – 6PM.
            (The parade will have 2 legs, the first being in Seoul and the second in Suwon)
   - Place:    Seoul Relay (Changdeokgung Palace – Nodeulseom Island – Nodeul Naru Park – Siheung Temporary Palace) 21.02km
Suwon Relay (Siheung Temporary Palace - Suwon Hwaseong Palace) 20.5km
 
○ Activities will include:
- Day 1 - Seoul: ‘Leaving the Palace’ ceremony, Baedari photo zone, music and dance performances, exhibition hall, marketplace, etc
- Day 2 - Suwon: Traditional Korean games, music and dance performances, warriors to greet King Jeongjo, etc

For those who are curious about how oriental medicine can be incorporated into meals, there will be a medicinal cooking contest, free samples of herbal bibimbap and medicinal tea’s, as well as food trucks, selling snacks made with medicinal and healthy ingredients.

A highlight will be the Seoul Yangnyeong Market Tours, where visitors will be able to observe how herbal gingseng kimchi is made, experience footbaths and massages, receive free herbal medical consultations and win gifts and raffle prizes, too!

description_html:
The grass is greener at the 2016 Seoul Garden Expo

The grass is definitely greener on this side! Join us at the Sangam-Dong World Cup Stadium, from October 3rd to 9th, for the 2016 Seoul Garden Expo.
 
If you are simply interested in enjoying the beautiful atmosphere, and relaxing in the outdoors, the domestic garden will hold over 500 species of plants for you to take in. name: 2016 Seoul International Fireworks Festival
summary: From October 7th to 8th, experience a thrilling showcase of fireworks in the city, at the Yeouido Han River Park.
description_html:
You’re in for a magical experience – The 2016 Seoul International Fireworks Festival

From October 7th to 8th, experience a thrilling showcase of fireworks in the city. At the Yeouido Han River Park (in front of building 63), join us for a full day of family-friendly festivities and the 2016 Seoul International Fireworks Festival.
 
During the day, the Fireworks Village will be bustling with performances and activities. For two evenings of eye-candy, the Seoul International Fireworks festival will entertain those of all ages. Spain and Japan will also showcase their beautiful fireworks display. The fun doesn’t end there! Following the magical fireworks, there will be an after party with a DJ concert on location. Finishing off on a positive note, we ask that you join Hanhwa’s ‘Clean Campaign’ and help pick up litter around you and leave the Han River park in its initial state.
 
Tip: Be sure to wear long sleeves in case of mosquitoes, and prepare your food in advance, as it will be quite dark in the evening. For comfort, bring along a picnic blanket or mat to relax and enjoy the show.

name: Arts For All 2016
summary: The Arts for All Festival will take place from October 2nd until December 18th 2016, at various culture hubs around Gwanghwamun, Daehak-ro and Changdong. This festival has a fresh and fun concept, celebrating ‘art by the people, for the people’
description_html:
Arts by the people, for the people – Arts for All Festival 2016

The Arts for All Festival will take place from October 2nd until December 18th 2016, at various culture hubs around Gwanghwamun, Daehak-ro and Changdong. This festival has a fresh and fun concept, celebrating ‘art by the people, for the people’.
 
On October 2nd, there will be a opening night, titled ‘All That Dance Floor’ is a ball that is not to be missed. More than 300 attendees will dance the night away at Gwanghwamun Square, featuring live music from an orchestra. Come and join us for Social Latin Dances, like salsa, tango, swing, etc.
 
An art market and exhibition of artwork and daily lifestyle goods made by Seoul locals will be held on October 8th. This will be a good opportunity to discover local creatives, and make a few unique purchases!   
 
Arts for All 2016 will also end with a bang, on December 17th and 18th, with a closing fiesta at Platform Chang-dong 61. Come and enjoy the live music and bands, to celebrate the success of this year’s festival!

name: Seoripul Festival 2016
summary: ‘Get together with culture’ at the Seoripul Festival. Enjoyable for all ages, the festivities will take place from September 24th to October 9st, 2016 in various locations around the Seocho-Gu area.
description_html:
Join us for the 2016 Seoripul Festival!

‘Get together with culture’ at the Seoripul Festival. Enjoyable for all ages, the festivities will take place from September 24th to October 9st, 2016 in various locations around the Seocho-Gu area. 
 
This celebration of culture will kick off with the ‘KBS Opening Concert’. We will also be spoiled with numerous performances from notable orchestras and choir groups, along with a 7080 Seocho Social Club (SCC) concert.
 
A highlight of the Seoripul festival is definitely the Seocho Gangsan Parade. It will feature 5 different sections of amazing floats, music and even some K-pop celebrities!

Adding even more color to the streets will be various cartoon characters, musicians and food trucks. Count us in!

name: The 19th Seoul International Dance Festival (SIDance 2016)
summary: The 19th Seoul International Dance Festival (SIDance 2016) will be held for 15 days, from Saturday, September 24th until Saturday, October 22nd 2016. The festival will take place across the following venues: Seoul Arts Center’s CJ Towol Theater, Sogang University’s Mary Hall Grand Theater and Sindorim D-Cube City.
description_html:
Get in the Groove at the 19th Seoul International Dance Festival

The 19th Seoul International Dance Festival (SIDance 2016) will be held for 15 days, from Saturday, September 24th until Saturday, October 22nd 2016. The festival will take place across the following venues: Seoul Arts Center’s CJ Towol Theater, Sogang University’s Mary Hall Grand Theater and Sindorim D-Cube City.
 
Be ready to be blown away by the skill and passion of this year’s performers! For a bit of foreign-flavor, a special Korean-French partnership will bring us a spectacular showcase of French Modern dance. Also to be expected is a ‘Spain Special’, at which festival-goers will be able to enjoy various contemporary dances originating from 5 regions in Spain. Furthermore, catering to children is a fantastic performance, blending captivating 3D animation and dance. SIDance will also host a variety of fun activities for children, including face-painting!
 
A number of choreography workshops will be held throughout the course of the festival, both for experienced dancers, and those new to dancing. Not to mention, after each performance, meet-and-greets will be held with the choreographers and performers. This will be a great opportunity to discuss, ask questions and learn more about the world of dance and performance!

summary: From September 15th (Thursday) to 16th (Friday), we invite you to partake in the “Five Nobleman’s Harvest Feast”! Join us at the Namsangol Hanok Village and enjoythe atmosphere of Korean Thanksgiving.
description_html:
Let's celebrate Korean Thanksgiving at the Five Nobleman's Harvest Feast!

From September 15th (Thursday) to 16th (Friday), we invite you to partake in the “Five Nobleman’s Harvest Feast”! Join us at the Namsangol Hanok Village and enjoy the atmosphere of Korean Thanksgiving.
 
Taking place in five traditional homes of noblemen, participants will be able to observe Korean Thanksgiving customs and practices, like the traditional ceremony of honoring one’s ancestors and making half-moon rice cakes (songpyeon). The festival will also host a variety of fun activities rooted in Korean history, such as folk games, craft-making and  must-see traditional performances.

name: Chuseok the Great Holiday with a Bright Moon Festival 2016
summary: Sept. 14th - Sept. 16th, 2016. The Chuseok the Great Holiday with a Bright Moon Festival 2016 will take place at the National Folk Museum of Korea.
description_html:
Take Part in Chuseok Festivities at the National Folk Museum

The Chuseok the Great Holiday with a Bright Moon Festival 2016 will take place at the National Folk Museum of Korea from Sept. 14th until Sept. 16th, 2016.

The festival will have a great variety of Chuseok-related activities and events for festival-goers to enjoy. There will also be traditional craft-making and cooking activities for locals and tourists to take part in. Additionally, there will be a chance to sample traditional Korean food as well as traditional foods of other countries such as Vietnam, China, and Japan. Try your hand at making Chuseok's representative food, songpyeon (half-moon rice cake), at no charge! During the three day festival, there will also be many Korean activities and events such as traditional games, live traditional music, traditional dances. Furthermore, a special performance of traditional Peruvian music by Peruvian musicians will add to the cultural atmosphere of the festival.

Enjoy Chuseok festivities with your family and see traditional cultural events at the National Folk Museum of Korea!

Love and Marriage in Myeong-dong

See a special outdoor play in the center of Myeong-dong, "Time Travelers in Seoul : Postman's Proposal," on Fridays and Saturdays from Sept. 2nd through Nov. 5th. The play is set in 1970s Myeong-dong and tells the story of a poor postman who falls in love at first sight with a famous actress and ultimately proposes to her. The performance is interactive, so audience members can interact with the cast and join in during the play's dance time. There will be a proposal event, and photo opportunities with the cast of the play. Make beautiful memories in Myeong-dong and watch this play.

A special exhibition of Spanish artist Joan Miró's works titled "Miró in Mallorca. A Wild Spirit" will run at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts from June 26th through Sept. 24th, 2016.

The exhibition was curated by the Joan Miró foundation and it is the largest Miró exhibition to ever take place in Seoul. This exhibition is also the largest touring collection of his works in either Asia or Europe. There will be 264 works on exhibit.

name: Minhwa and Court Paintings of the Joseon Dynasty : Munja-do and Chaekgeori
summary: From June 11th to August 28th. Visit the Seoul Calligraphy Art Museum at the Seoul Arts Center to see an exhibition of Joseon-era royal court paintings and folk paintings called munja-do and chaekgeori.
description_html:
See Masterpieces of the Joseon Era

The Seoul Calligraphy Art Museum, located at the Seoul Arts Center, will be running an exhibition of Joseon-era royal court paintings and folk paintings called munja-do and chaekgeori. The exhibition will run from June 11th through August 28th, 2016. Munja-do are character paintings that depict artfully illustrated Chinese characters. Chaekgeori are still lifes that feature books as their main subject, and they often utilize trompe l'oeil. The exhibition has been divided into two sections, and there will be 58 works on display. 20 pieces from this exhibition have been loaned by institutions both large and small, as well as privately loaned. The National Museum of Korea and Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art are just two of the donor institutions. Thanks in part to these donors, exhibition-goers will be able to enjoy a large number in one location.

While enjoying Joseon-era art such as royal court paintings and folk paintings, it's possible to view past chapters of history as reflected through art. Visitors have the opportunity to see the world of a bygone era thanks to this exhibition.

name: ASYAAF & Hidden Artists Festival 2016
summary: From July 19th, (Tues) till Aug. 14th, (Sun) 2016. See art from emerging artists at the ASYAAF & Hidden Artists Festival, running at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).
description_html:
See Art by Emerging Artists and Unknown Artists!

ASYAAF & Hidden Artists Festival 2016 will be taking place this year at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) from July 19th through August 14th. The festival highlights and displays works by emerging young artists and older artists who are still relatively unknown.

ASYAAF is an acronym and it stands for Asian Students and Young Artists Art Festival. This year's festival will exhibit works from promising young artists and art students under the age of 30. This year's festival will also have a special exhibition of "hidden" artists; artists (aged 31-59) who are not yet known to the wider public and thus could be seen as unrecognized or "hidden." Winning exhibitors were chosen from across Asia, out of over 3,000 participants. 600 artists from Korea, Japan, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, and other countries were chosen to exhibit at ASYAAF. Among those 600 artists, 400 are young and emerging artists while the remaining 200 are older, "hidden" artists.

Every Friday and Saturday, the Artist-Docent Tour will run. During the "tour" a variety of activities will run. One activity will be one-minute portraits, wherein an artist will draw a one-minute portrait of a festival-goer. Visit ASYAAF for art and fun.

description_html:
Make Memories by the Han River!

The Hangang Summer Festival, Seoul's premier summer festival, will take place at the Han River's parks from July 15th to Aug. 21st, 2016.

Choose to take part in and attend a wealth of events for the festival's 38-day run. Go camping,  take part in water leisure sports, a paper boat race or bicycle along the Han. name: 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Lee Jung-Seob
summary: From June 3rd to October 3rd, 2016. An exhibition of a modern Korean master, Lee Jung-Seob will run at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Deoksugung.
description_html:
The 100th Anniversary of the Birth of a Korean Modern Master

From June 3rd to October 3rd, 2016. An exhibition of a modern Korean master, Lee Jung-Seob will run at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Deoksugung.

Lee Jung-Seob (1916-56) artistic style was a realization of an Eastern aesthetic that built upon a foundation of Western painting aesthetics. His works are marked by a traditional Korean aesthetic and display a deep understanding of anatomy and strong technical drawing skills.

3 pieces on display at this exhibition are on loan from the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York. Roughly 60 institutions have lent 200 pieces of art and 100 pieces of other materials relating to Lee for this solo exhibition celebrating this unsung artistic genius. Visitors will be able to see some of Lee's representative works in addition to his tinfoil paintings, postcard paintings, drawings, and more.

summary: From June 25th to September 25th, 2016. An exhibition of famed illustrator and author Anthony Browne’s works will run from at the Seoul Arts Center’s Hangaram Art Museum.
description_html:
Anthony Browne's Happy Museum

An exhibition of famed illustrator and author Anthony Browne’s works will run from June 25th through Sept. 25th, 2016 at the Seoul Arts Center’s Hangaram Art Museum. The exhibition will be on the Hangaram Art Museum's 3rd floor, in exhibition halls 5 and 6.

2016 marks Browne's 40th year as an illustrator and writer. The exhibition was put together to honor that anniversary and over 250 pieces of his work will be on view to the public. Several works by Browne that have yet to be published have also been specially included in the exhibition. 

In addition to the exhibition, there will be an Anthony Browne library so that visitors can read his books, a draw-your-own art toy activity, an autograph session, and much more. The Seoul Arts Center has put together a wonderful exhibition, events, and activities for fans of art and Anthony Browne.

summary: From July 20th - July 31st, 2016. The 24th ASSITEJ Korea International Summer Festival will take place in Daehak-ro. It is the country's most prestigious performing arts festival for youth theater.
description_html:
The Most Prestigious Performing Arts Festival for Youth Theater : “Turn fear into courage!” 

The 24th ASSITEJ Korea International Summer Festival will take place in Daehak-ro from July 20th - July 31st, 2016. The festival will be place for a family outing as it will feature fun, world-class performances suitable for all age groups. The performances will take place at various locations throughout Daehak-ro. Some of the locations are, the Daehakro Arts Theatre (Small Hall and Main Hall), the Small Hall of the ARKO Arts Theatre, Jongno Children's Theatre, Noonbit Theatre, Mimagi Arts Centre, Marronnier Park's Multipurpose Hall, and select locations off-Daehak-ro. 

The ASSITEJ festival is held annually, and each year one country is spotlighted in order to showcase that country's performing arts scene. As a result of this cultural twist, the performances at the festival are both art and cultural experiences. This year's festival theme is, "turn fear into courage." The festival's shows will deal with issues that young people can easily relate to, as well as worries that young people may face these days. Additionally, 2016 marks the occasion of 130 years of Korean-French diplomatic ties. When the ASSITEJ festival was first founded, France was the world leader in creating plays and other performances for children and youths. France continues to stay a step ahead in the world of youth theater. Foreign and Korean visitors can enjoy French productions and see shows with high levels of artistic maturity at this year's festival.

name: Choi Seung-hee Photo Exhibition
summary: From May 12th (Fri) till Aug. 12 (Fri). The Soorim Cultural Foundation is holding a special photo exhibition of the dancer Choi Seung-hee entitled, "LEAP & EXTENSION" at the Kim Heesun Memorial Soorim Art Center.
description_html:
Dancer of the 1930s, Choi Seung-hee

From May 12th (Fri) till Aug. 12 (Fri). The Soorim Cultural Foundation is holding a special photo exhibition of the dancer Choi Seung-hee entitled, "LEAP & EXTENSION" at the Kim Heesun Memorial Soorim Art Center.

During the Japanese colonial era, Choi Seung-hee became known as Korea's foremost modern dancer. Choi took traditional Korean dance forms and adapted them into modern dance forms, eventually gaining recognition domestically and abroad for her bold, new dances. Choi had a complicated life. During the Sino-Japanese war, she was forced to the frontlines by the Japanese powers in order to perform for Japanese troops and condemned by Korean nationalists by this perceived collaboration with the Japanese. Following the Korean War, Choi defected to North Korea with her husband and eventually disappeared from public view. She was thereafter largely ignored and forgotten by South Korea. This exhibition shows the human side of a forgotten genius of dance.

There are 139 photographs of Choi Seung-hee, and other materials, articles, and books are on display. The Gwangju Museum of Art has loaned 17 photos and artifacts to this exhibition and the Sookmyung Heritage Hall has lent 6 artifacts for this exhibition.

* Photos provided by the Soorim Cultural Foundation

summary: From April 20th (Wed) till August 28th (Sun) at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP). See the 6th installment of Kansong Munhwa with the theme, "Landscape Portraits - Daily Life, Dreams and Art."
description_html:
Landscape Portraits - Daily life, Dreams and Art

From April 20th (Wed) till August 28th (Sun) at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP). See the 6th installment of Kansong Munhwa with the theme, "Landscape Portraits - Daily Life, Dreams and Art."

Landscape portraits are paintings that feature people within a landscape. Historical landscape portraits show the daily realities of past eras, such as the work and leisure activities of common people, scholars studying and partaking in the arts, and so on. In this way, landscape portraits are historic artifacts that capture daily activities of times long past. These artworks also show the emotional lives of their subjects; what they stood for and what they dreamed about.

This exhibition is a wonderful opportunity to see works from some of the Joseon Dynasty's greatest artists. Portraits by Kim Myeong-guk, Yun Du-seo, Jeong Seon, Kim Hong-do, Kim Deuk-sin, Shin Yun-bok, Jang Seung-eop will be on display at DDP.

name: [Project 284] Peach Blossom: Hopeful Flower of Utopia
summary: This multimedia arts project is being held in a place full of history, Culture Station Seoul 284 (Old Seoul Station). There will be an exhibition, performance, movie, talk show, and workshops.
description_html:
A Multimedia Arts Project in a Place Full of History!

From April 30th to June 26th, the multimedia arts project, [Project 284] Peach Blossom: Hopeful Flower of Utopia, will take place at Culture Station Seoul 284 (Old Seoul Station). There will be an exhibition, performance, movie, talk show, and workshops. The artists involved in these project have used various formats to address the idea of a "perfect life" from their respective perspectives. The wide range of ways to experience this arts project means that there are many ways for visitors to enjoy their time at Culture Station Seoul 284. 

What does it mean for a person to have a "perfect life" and what would that perfect life entail? The project is divided into 4 themes: the Garden of Senses the Rectangular Rainbow, Deep into the Land of Desire, and To Flourish. More than 27 artists from several countries came together to create Peach Blossom: Hopeful Flower of Utopia. The artists Moon Kyungwon,  Bully, Kook Hyoung-gul, MyeongBum Kim, Tim Spooner (UK), Marisa Silbatriz Pons (Spain), and Bora Yoon (USA) all took part. 

Because of the breadth of this project, you may want to take an entire day visiting Culture Station Seoul 284. Before its rebirth as a cultural space, it was the Old Seoul Station, built during the Japanese occupation for trains. Now, the space is filled with history and culture and it’s possible for visitors to spend their days enjoying exhibits, performances, and movies here. 

*For program details, please visit the official website.

The Sejong Art Market SoSo has shown steady popularity; writers and visitors have shown steady interest in the market since its opening.

There have been experimental art performances, singer-songwriter stages, outdoor film screenings, drum concerts, and other various artistic performances.

name: SeMA and Palais de Tokyo's Urban Legends
summary: From April 5th to May 29th. The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) and Paris's Palais de Tokyo have come together to present "Urban Legends" on the occasion of 130 year of Korean-French diplomatic ties.
description_html:
International Artists' Productive Misreadings - Marvelous Stories  

From April 5th to May 29th. The Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) and Paris's Palais de Tokyo have come together to present "Urban Legends" on the occasion of 130 year of Korean-French diplomatic ties. "Urban Legends" is a result of a cooperation between SeMA and the Palais de Tokyo in Paris, it is located at the main SeMA branch in Seosomun, on the 3rd floor. 

Through this cooperation, artists were offered a new creative environment. Through this exchange and interactions, artists were able to create new initiatives and projects. In November, 2015, the Paris Pavilion was installed and in March of 2016, five artists were selected to take part in a Seoul workshop. The experimental works and other creative results from that workshop will be on display at SeMA.

The participating artists are Kim Ayoung, Lou Lim, Alexis Guillier, Ange Leccia, Hoël Duret, Ollie Palmer, and Jean-Alain Corre. These artists from different backgrounds explore and cross boundaries of gender, nationality, and culture. Their creative and imaginative initiatives are based on experiences in both Seoul and Paris. The title of this exhibition is a nod to fact that their experiences took place in an urban setting. The works on display are products of the disconnect, new interpretations, and misunderstandings that arise as a result of living in a new environment. Visitors to “Urban Legends” can look forward to seeing new takes on familiar realities.

name: Royal Wedding Ceremony of King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong
summary: A re-enactment of the royal wedding of King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong will take place on April 29th (Sat), 2017 at Unhyeongung Palace.
description_html:
Attend a Traditional Wedding Ceremony at Unhyeongung Palace

A re-enactment of the royal wedding of King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong will take place on April 29th (Sat), 2017 at Unhyeongung Palace.

King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong were married in the third year of Gojong’s reign, in 1866. Once Empress Myeongseong was proclaimed the King’s intended wife, she was moved to Norakdang, a part of Unhyeongung, to learn palace etiquette and the formalities involved in a royal wedding ceremony. Their wedding date was on March 21st by the lunar calendar and the King was 15 and Empress 16 years old at the time of their marriage. The April 30th event is a historical re-enactment of their wedding ceremony. 

*Unhyeongung Palace is historical site no. 257. King Gojong lived here until the age of 12, when he ascended to the throne. Gojong would go on to become the first emperor of Korea and was the 26th king of the Joseon Dynasty. Unhyeongung was also the residence of King Gojong’s father and regent, Heungseon Daewongun.

*This event is held annually, during the spring and fall.

name: Herb Ritts Work : Photography Exhibition
summary: Michael Jackson and Madonna during their pop heydays. New Hollywood. The stars that were a part of New Hollywood filled international media with an endless supply of romance, conflicts, and issues. In the center of this was the legendary photographer Herb Ritts.
description_html:
Blurring the Lines Between Commerce and Art: Genius Herb Ritts' Work

Michael Jackson and Madonna during their pop heydays. New Hollywood. The stars that were a part of New Hollywood filled international media with an endless supply of romance, conflicts, and issues. In the center of this was the legendary photographer Herb Ritts. Through his work, the entire world got to see undiscovered sides of Madonna, Richard Gere, and other Hollywood stars. Ritts' studio was a playground for supermodels, his birthday parties looked more like the Oscars for their star power.

This exhibition has 100 works by Ritts that reflects the splendor of 80s icons and Hollywood in 1980s. Madonna overtook Cyndi Lauper as an international icon of sexiness and became a star thanks in part to Ritt’s photo (shown as this article’s main image). Richard Gere captured the hearts of women all over the world with his sexy image. Herb Ritts played no small part in creating that image with his photos. Visit the exhibition and see Hollywood stars.

name: Seoul Elegy : Photography Exhibition
summary: From March 23rd to May 29th, 2016. In celebration of 130 years of Korean-French diplomatic ties, the Seoul Museum of History will be exhibiting works by famed photographer Françoise Huguier. The exhibition, Seoul Elegy, is on the 1st floor.
description_html:
Seoul Elegy : Photographs by Françoise Huguier

In celebration of 130 years of Korean-French diplomatic ties, the Seoul Museum of History will be exhibiting works by famed photographer Françoise Huguier from March 23rd to May 29th, 2016. The exhibition, Seoul Elegy, will be held in Special Exhibition Hall A, on the 1st floor. 

About 30 years ago, the internationally renown French photographer Françoise Huguier's relationship with Korea began. At the time, she a documentary photographer for the French newspaper, Libération. 1982 marked Huguier's first visit to Seoul. Photographs from that visit as well as photos from her time in Seoul in 2014-2015 will be on display. Seoul's modernization is one of the 20th century's most remarkable transformations; visitors to the exhibition will be able to view it all through Huguier's photos. 

Françoise Huguier first came to Asia to visit Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta, and other Southeast Asian cities. While shooting middle class families in these cities, Huguier became intrigued by the Hallyu Wave and Korea's growing digitial presence. These factors led her to visit Korea.

name: Jean Paul Gaultier Exhibition
summary: From March 26th to June 30th, 2016. The Hyundai Card Culture Project presents its 21st event, an exhibition of Jean Paul Gaultier's works at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).
description_html:
Asia's First  Venue and the Last Stop of the World Tour

From March 26th to June 30th, 2016. The Hyundai Card Culture Project presents its 21st event, an exhibition of Jean Paul Gaultier's works at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP).

In honor of the 130th anniversary of the establishment of Korean-French diplomatic ties, Hyundai Card and the Seoul Design Foundation have co-sponsored this exhibition of world-famous designer Jean Paul Gaultier's designs.

Jean Paul Gaultier made his fashion world debut In 1976 with a ready-to-wear line of clothing. In 1997 Gaultier established a haute couture house in his name and became known as "the enfant terrible of the fashion world" due to his outlandish and eccentric designs. Bold, yet humorous, Gaultier's designs challenged conventionally held societal concepts of identity, culture, and gender. His designs transcend the medium of fashion and are messages to society about upending norms and conventions. 

As a result of this exhibition, the 21st installment of the Hyundai Card Culture Project, Jean Paul Gaultier made his first ever visit to Korea. He also personally designed a dress with the theme "Korea" and it will be displayed during this exhibition.

*Images provided by Hyundai Card.

name: Ancient Tombs, Memories of Seoul
summary: From March 31st (Thurs) till June 6th (Mon) 2016, the Seoul Baekje Museum will be holding a special exhibition, "Ancient Tombs, Memories of Seoul," that shines a light on ancient historical eras via excavated relics and artifacts.
description_html:
A Special Exhibition, "Ancient Tombs, Memories of Seoul" at the Seoul Baekje Museum

From March 31st (Thurs) till June 6th (Mon) 2016, the Seoul Baekje Museum will be holding a special exhibition, "Ancient Tombs, Memories of Seoul," that shines a light on ancient historical eras via excavated relics and artifacts.

This exhibition will have on display artifacts that were recently excavated in Seoul from ancient burial mounds of historical significance. Some of the neighborhoods where Baekje-era tombs and artifacts were uncovered are Seokchon-dong, Garak-dong, and Umyeon-dong. Shilla-era artifacts that were excavated from ancient tombs in Seoul’s Cheonwang-dong and Myeongnyun-dong neighborhoods will also be displayed. By learning about the burial patterns and practices of ancient Koreans, you can learn about the lives of ancient Koreans. The Seoul Baekje Museum is currently excavating the Seokchon-dong burial site and several of the artifacts to be displayed are among the most recently uncovered relics.

The exhibition is divided into three sections. Section 1 is “Seoul’s Prehistoric Tombs,” section 2 is “People of Baekje, Resting in Peace in Seoul” and the last section 3, “People of Shilla, Resting in Peace in Seoul.” See and learn about the burial practices of ancient Koreans through the eras.

Additionally, consider visiting the Joseon Era ruins and burial mounds in Jingwan-dong and Godeok-dong. See some examples of celebrated white porcelain and learn about Joseon thoughts of the afterlife. You can compare what you learn here with what you learned about the Baekje and Shilla burial practices.
