name: The 18 Sparkling Bridges of the Han River
summary: Just 12 of Seoul's bridges were lit up decoratively at night but lighting systems have expanded to 18 of Seoul's bridges.
description_html:
The 18 Colorful Charms of the Han River at Nighttime

Previously, for energy conservation reasons, only 12 of the Han River’s bridges were lit up colorfully at night. However, lighting plans were expanded to include more bridges and now a total of 18 Han River bridges are lit up colorfully at night. This has resulted in an even more beautiful Seoul nightscape.

Currently, 27 of the Han River’s 29 bridges have or are in the process of being fitted with lighting systems. Originally, just 12 bridges had lighting systems. The 6 bridges to have been newly fitted with lighting systems are the Hangang Railway Bridge, the Haengjydaegyo Bridge, the Dongjakdaegyo Bridge, the Hannamdaegyo Bridge, the Yeongdongdaegyo Bridge, and the Jamsildaegyo Bridge.

The 5 “storytelling” bridges and the 13 “outstanding landscape” bridges each have their own personalities, images, and characteristics. 

The light show times are flexible. The exact time the bridges’ decorative lighting turns on varies depending on the season and sunset times. Usually, the lights go on from dark until 11pm. Additionally, from May to October, the warm weather draws many Seoulites to the Han River and so the lights are usually kept on until midnight during these months.

summary: The Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival 2016 will run from April 4th (Mon) to April 10th (Sun).
description_html:
Yeouido is Brimming with Spring Flowers

The Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival 2016 will run from April 4th (Mon) to April 10th (Sun). 

The Yoshino Cherry Blossom originates from Jeju Island but there are 1,886 Yoshino trees in Yeouido. Additionally, there are azalea, forsythia, royal azaleas, bridal wreath spirea, deutzia, among the 13 varieties of flowers found at the festival. There are roughly 87,859 spring flowers in bloom across Yeouido Park. The fragrance of spring's flowers fills the park, and the views of the Han River can't be beat. 

The festival first began in 2005 and this year is the 12th Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival. Located in the middle of Seoul, the festival is a great way to see the Han River and cherry blossoms, as well as people watch. The festival proves to be popular with visitors every year.

A wide variety of events are scheduled to take place during the festival. There will be a singing contest, street performances by the VIAF, an adorable parade of cartoon characters, horse drawn carts of flowers, performances by regional arts troupes, a writing contest, and much more.

From March 21st to March 26th 2016, the Hera Seoul Fashion Week will take place at the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) and the Daesun Flourmill Factory in Mullaedong.

You don't have to be a journalist or a buyer to enjoy Seoul Fashion Week. At DDP there will be the Jewelry Bazaar, with 20-30 fashion jewelry brands offering their wares. At the Generation Next location, the young designers featured there will also have a sampling of their designs for sale to the general public on March 26th (Sat).

summary: From March until November 2016, take part in a traditional tea ceremony at Namsangol Hanok Village in Yoon's Tea Room. The program takes place three times a week.
description_html:
Experience and Enjoy a Korean Tea Ceremony

From March until November 2016, take part in a traditional tea ceremony at Namsangol Hanok Village in Yoon's Tea Room. The program takes place three times a week. Yoon's Tearoom is located inside Namsangol Hanok Village. Normally, visitors are not permitted to enter the Yoon hanok*. Thanks to the tea ceremony program, visitors can enter and enjoy tea and light refreshments in the hanok's tranquil atmosphere. 

The tea ceremony program is a chance for foreign visitors to experience Korea's tea culture. For Koreans, this program is a chance to become familiar with Korean traditions. 

The tea ceremony program runs from March until Nov. 2016. Groups must reserve in advance.
(Cost: 7,000 to 10,000 won)


* The Yoon hanok is a replica of the home of Empress Sunjeonghyo. The empress's uncle, Yoon Deok-yeong, owned the hanok but it fell into disrepair over the years. The actual residence can still be seen in Seoul, at Ogin-dong 47-133 bunji, Jongno-gu.

name: 2016 St. Patrick's Day Celebrations
summary: St. Patrick's Day, in honor of Saint Patrick, is celebrated all over the world and is a cultural and religious holiday. St. Patrick's Day is celebrated on March 17th, the traditional death date of Ireland's patron saint, Saint Patrick (AD 387-461).
description_html:
A Cultural Celebration of the Irish People's Inclusiveness and Diversity

 

St. Patrick's Day, in honor of Saint Patrick, is celebrated all over the world and is a cultural and religious holiday. St. Patrick's Day is celebrated on March 17th, the traditional death date of Ireland's patron saint, Saint Patrick (AD 387-461). Saint Patrick was the first to spread the teachings of Catholicism in Ireland and he remains one of the most respected figures in the Irish Catholic Church. Today, St. Patrick's Day is celebrated all over the world. Instead of celebrates one specific ethnic or religious identity, it has become a celebration of the Irish people. culture, and inclusiveness.

St. Patrick's Day celebrations began in South Korea in 1976. In 2001, the Irish Association of Korea (IAK) began the first official St. Patrick's Day parade and celebrations, and now festivities take place annually on the Saturday closest to March 17th. This year, St. Patrick's Day celebrations will be held on March 19th (Sat.) from 1 P.M. until 6 P.M. at D-Cube City Plaza, Sindorim. The theme of this year's celebrations is, “Craic, Ceoil agus Cairdeas – Great fun, music and friendship.” There will be traditional Irish music (with flutes, violins, accordions, and more) and Irish rock music along with other performances. Ireland's top Irish dance troupe will perform, as will Korea's most experienced Irish dance troupe, Tap Pung. Authentic Irish culture can't be experienced often in Korea, but St. Patrick's Day festivities are a great chance to experience Irish music, see Irish dance and much more. There will be many events and activities throughout the day; in addition to music and dance, there will be face painting, a costume contest, and a demonstration of Gaelic Football, a traditional Irish sport.

name: Lunar New Year's First Full Moon
summary: Celebrate the first full moon of the Lunar New Year (Feb. 22nd) at Namsangol Hanok Village.
description_html:
Celebrate Lunar New Year's First Full Moon at Namsangol Hanok Village!

 

On February 22nd (Mon.), celebrations for the first full moon of the Lunar New Year will take place at Namsangol Hanok Village. There will be both performances and traditional activities, such as the burning of notes, for people to take part in. The burning of notes is signficant as wishes are written on the notes, then burned so that the wishes may come true.

 

Vistors can make a wish on a piece of paper, and have the note burned at the end of celebrations. "Make a Wish" will begin at 15:00 and close at 18:00. Advance reservations are not necessary for admission to any of the activities. Nut cracking, ogok-bap (five grain rice) tasting, liquor tasting are some of the traditional Lunar New Year's first full moon activities that will take place.

 

The first full moon of the New Year has been considered very important since ancient times. The first full moon signified a chance to wish for food luck and to ward off misfortune. Lunar New Year customs pertain to different ways one could bring good luck and ward off bad luck. The making, sharing, and eating of ogok-bap (five grain rice) symbolized taking in good luck. Dried greens and herbs gathered from the previous year are eaten in order to ward off heat exhaustion in the summer. Waking early in the morning and cracking nuts with your teeth is done to ward off boils for the rest of the year. Drinking liquor during the first full moon was thought to make your ears sharper and so receive good news. Other games and activities, such as brush-clearing fires, are also traditional activities.

name: 2016 SeMA Blue <Seoul Babel>
summary: The exhibition is from January 19 - April 5. Look forward to 67 days of performances, artist talks, archive website launching, and a diversity of related events.
description_html:
Seoul Babel, where Korea's contemporary art is highlighted. 

As Seoul Museum of Art's first exhibition of 2016, SeMA Blue is coming to you with works from bright and promising artists. Starting in 2012, SeMA Blue was created with the intention to support and highlight Korea's contemporary works.  

The title for this year's SeMA Blue is "Seoul Babel" and the works of 70 different artists from 15 different teams. Unlike exhibitions from other years where it provided an indepth look at the work of each individual artist, this year's exhibition will put more of an emphasis on the different artistic platforms that are naturally springing up all throughout the city and different creative movements. It really shows off the experimental nature and uniqueness of small design studios that are rapidly appearing all across the city. 

The exhibition is from January 19 - April 5. Look forward to 67 days of performances, artist talks, archive website launching, and a diversity of related events.

name: Monet's Impressionism Exhibition
summary: Around 400 different works of the impressionist artist, Claude Monet (1840-1926), will be reborn in the form of convergence art starting from December 11 at the War Memorial of Korea.
description_html:
Around 400 different works of the impressionist artist, Claude Monet (1840-1926), will be reborn in the form of convergence art starting from December 11 at the War Memorial of Korea.

Typically, oil paintings take 3-4 days to dry but Monet was known for repainting over the paint before it could dry. His work can best be enjoyed by stepping back and taking in the full view rather than going up close.

Monet was also known for painting a picture many times in order to capture the changing of light. This method has inspired other artists such as Kandinsky, Mondrian, and even Andy Warhol.

For this exhibition, the work of Monet will come to life through 60 different projectors that are projected onto 4M high big screens. Viewers will almost feel as if they have been transported to the past as the splendor of impressionist art becomes more tangible than ever.

summary: From January 9 - April 17, 2016, make sure to check out "Van Gogh Inside: Festival of Light and Music" which will take place at Seoul Culture Station 284.
description_html:
The Works of Vincent Van Gogh at Seoul Culture Station 284


2014 was the year of "Van Gogh's A Record of 10 Years Exhibition" and 2015 was the year of "Van Gogh's Media Art" in Daegu. From January 9 - April 17, 2016, make sure to check out "Van Gogh Inside: Festival of Light and Music" which will take place at Seoul Culture Station 284.
 
Just like the title of the exhibition "Festival of Light and Music," the story behind Van Gogh's work will be brought to light through videos, music, and more to satisfy the viewer's 5 senses 200%!

Unlike the previous exhibitions, there will be extra work from 8 impressionist painters. Some of these painters include pioneers such as Édouard Manet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Claude Monet, Paul Gaugin, and other painters name which we would recognize all fairly well.
You don't want to miss out on this mind blowing line up. Look forward to Renoir's " Dance at Le moulin de la Galette", Degas' "L'Absinthe", Turner's "The Fighting Temeraire",  Seurat's "A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte", Gauguin's "The Yellow Christ," and other leading pieces.

name: Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Ritual and Royal Procession
summary: The Jongmyo Jerye, or Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Ritual, is Korea’s Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 56, and its music, the Jongmyo Jeryeak, is No. 1. Together, they have been designated a UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
description_html:
The Jongmyo Jerye, or Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Ritual, is Korea’s Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 56, and its music, the Jongmyo Jeryeak, is No. 1. Together, they have been designated a UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

The Jongmyo Jerye will be performed on Sunday, May 6th, supported by the Society for the Preservation of Jongmyo Jerye (Lee Hwan-ey, Chairman); the Society for the Preservation of Jongmyo Jeryeak (Choi Chung-ung, Chairman); the Cultural Heritage Administration; the Korea Cultural Heritage Foundation; the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; the National Center for Korean Traditional Performing Arts; and the Korea Tourism Organization. 

The event will be held from 1 p.m. until 6:30 p.m., first with the Yeongnyeongjeon Jehyang (Yeongnyeongjeon Rite) until 3 p.m. and then with the Jeongjeon Jehyang (Jeongjeon Rite) from 4:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m.

A reenactment of the Eoga Haengnyeol (Royal Procession) will also be held, starting at about 11:30 a.m. and ending at 12:30 p.m. The procession departs from Gyeongbokgung (Palace), passing through Sejong Intersection and Jongno 1-3 Streets, and arriving at Jongmyo’s Jaegung area.

About 1,700 people will participate in the event, including roughly 500 people in the Yeongnyeongjeon Jehyang (Rite) and the Jeongjeon Jehyang (Rite) ceremonies and some 1,200 in the Eoga Haengnyeol (Royal Procession).

As the biggest and most important memorial service in the Joseon era, the Jongmyo Ancestral Ritual is also called the Jongmyo Grand Ancestral Ritual. The ritual of taking the ancestral tablets of kings and queens was performed five times a year during the Joseon era (spring, summer, fall, winter and in December), but ceased during the period of Japanese colonization and resumed in 1969 as an annual event.

During the ritual, the ancestral tablets of the Joseon dynasty kings and queens are taken to Jeongjeon and the greatest of those are carried to Yeongnyeongjeon. The tablets of subjects who performed great services to the kings are enshrined in Gongsindang.

The name Jongmyo originally referred only to Jeongjeon, but it now includes Yeongnyeongjeon as well. Jeongjeon has 19 rooms, holding 49 spirit tablets, including those of kings Taejo, Taejong, and Sejong. Yeongnyeongjeon, with 16 rooms, contains the tablets of 34 revered kings including Mokjo, Ikjo, Dojo, and Hwanjo. And housed in Gongsindang are the tablets of 83 distinguished commoners. (On the left side of the steps to Jeongjeon is the hall of the seven seasonal rites.)

The royal procession is reenacted in the afternoon with the king and crown prince arriving in a carriage to an audience at Jongmyo. The king then enters the palace in a sedan chair, followed by civil and military officials and with the Hyeonmu unit guarding his front and rear.

The Jeongjeon rite follows Confucian custom, with a reverent greeting to the gods to bring them joy. Throughout the ritual ceremony, Jongyo Jeryeak is performed with traditional instruments and 64 people dance the Pal Ilmu. Jongmyo Jeryeak is the instrumental music, song and dance invented by King Sejong and adopted for use in the Jongmyo Jerye during the reign of King Sejo. The songs are called "Jongmyo Akjang" and the dances are Botaepyeongjimu and Jeongdaeeopjimu.

Some 200 selected members of the royal family and descendents of the queen have also been appointed to perform the sacrifices and serve as royal stewards.

This event is a great opportunity to introduce traditional Korean rituals to both Korean and foreign tourists.

Seoul City hosts the annual Seoul Open Week at the end of summer. Camp overnight on the open grass fields of Seoul Plaza and show off your talents at the talent show. Experience the culture through music and performances at one of Seoul's most memorable summer festival. 

Camping in the City at Seoul Plaza

Seoul Plaza turns into a tent city for one night during the summer.  Participants can spend a memorable night on the last night of August camping with their friends and family in the middle of the city.  Street performers and various cultural activities are sure to keep everyone entertained through the night.  Use one of the tents provided or just sleep on the grass, either way you will have a memorable experience with your loved ones.  For safety reasons, cooking over fire is prohibited.  

Advanced reservations are required to participate.  Apply at www.seoulopenweek.com

Show off your talents at the citizens' talent show.  Watch others show off their skills or be brave and join in on the fun! Everyone is welcome to participate and show off whatever skill they want.  Take this opportunity to create and produce your very own show!
 
Prospective participants must apply at www.seoulopenweek.com  
Please go to www.seoulopenweek.com or www.facebook.com/seoulopenweek for more information.

name: Kukkiwon Taekwondo Demonstration
summary: The 1 hour long taekwondo demonstration at Kukkiwon is incredible to watch. It is considered one of the main attractions in Seoul for tourists who are interested in taekwondo.
description_html:
This is Real Taekwondo! The Kukkiwon Taekwondo Demonstration Team Will Show a New Taekwondo Paradigm Through Their Performances in 2016
 

Kukkiwon and the Gangnam-gu district have put together a taekwondo demonstration performance for tourists to Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters. From Feb. 23rd, 2016 onwards, see the Great Taekwondo! Taking place Thursday through Sunday, this 1 hour Taekwondo demonstration is incredible to watch. The Kukkiwon team puts on an incredible show and it is considered one of the main attractions in Seoul for tourists who are interested in taekwondo. Kukkiwon continues to use taekwondo to provide international and Korean visitors with great memories and a better understanding of the taekwondo as sport and cultural heritage. Thanks in part to the team's efforts, many people around the world and in Korea have surely become fans of taekwondo.

 

 

The Flowers of Kukkiwon, the Kukkiwon Taekwondo Demonstration Team 
 

Ever since its founding in 1974, the team has toured around 120 different countries and has played a major role as cultural diplomats, and in globalizing the sport of taekwondo. The Kukkiwon team tours roughly 14 countries annually and they are firm taekwondo evangelists. Their activites abroad function to spread the word about taekwondo and teach people the world over about this Korean cultural sport. 90 new members are chosen every year through a very strict process, all members must be at least level 5 practioners. Kukkiwon strongly values tradition, yet does not fear or resist change. The team's performances for foreign visitors is also a valuable contribution to the tourism industry.

 

 

Great Taekwondo: Program Introduction 
 

○ Part 1: Real Taekwondo : Let's meet Taekwondo for real 
A dramatic display of Taekwondo's spirit and skill.

○ Part 2: The Legend of Taekwondo : The turbulent period of Taekwondo 
A performance that captures conflicting interests in the Taekwondo world.


○ Part 3: Harmony of Taekwondo : Taekwondo becomes One through Kukkiwon 
A performance that demonstrates how many different facets of Taekwondo became one through Kukkiwon.

○ Part 4: Taekwondo Experience 

Audience members can go up on stage and experience breaking boards themselves

 

*Once the performance ends, there will be an opportunity to take a photo with the team.

summary: From October 23, 2015 - March 27, 2016, you will be able to experience part 5 of the Kansong Munhwa Exibition at Dongdaemun Design Plaza. The theme for this exhibition is "Flowers & Feathers - Embrace Nature."
description_html:
Kansong Munhwa Exhibition - Part 5 

 


From October 23, 2015 - March 27, 2016, you will be able to experience part 5 of the Kansong Munhwa Exibition at Dongdaemun Design Plaza. The theme for this exhibition is "Flowers & Feathers - Embrace Nature."

name: Yeon Deung Hoe(Lotus Lantern Festival)
summary: The Yeon Deung Hoe Lotus Lantern Festival is a modern-day annual tradition that offers visitors the chance to experience Yeondeunghoe and Buddhist culture.
description_html:
Buddha's Birthday

The 8th day of the 4th lunar month is the Buddha’s Birthday. Temples nationwide light lanterns to symbolically transmit the wisdom and compassion of the Buddha. They also perform ceremonies in celebration of his birth.

 

Lotus Lantern Festival

The Yeon Deung Hoe Festival originated in the Silla era more than 1,300 years ago. It has since been passed down through the Goryeo era, the Joseon era (where it was called “Palgwan Hoe”), and is still an annual tradition today. This traditional festival is designated Korea’s Intangible Cultural Property of Korea No. 122. By lighting lanterns at the Yeon Deung Hoe Festival, participants brighten their own hearts as well as the world. People flock to South Korea from all over the world to attend this festival.

summary: This annual festival celebrates the full blossoms of spring flowers in the backdrop of the Han River at Yeoido Park.
description_html:
Enjoy Spectacular Spring Blossoms

The annual Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival celebrates the full blossoms of spring  in the backdrop of the Han River at Yeouido Park. When Seoulites think of spring flowers, they
think of cherry blossoms, and when they  think of cherry blossoms, they think endearingly of this annual festival at Yeouido Park.
 

More than 1,600 yedonsis (Yoshino cherry) trees of Jeju origin will bloom along the Han River
basked in spring frangrances, in addition to nearly 90,000 flowers including azaleas, forsythias and spireas.


Visitors may follow the cherry trees along the circular Yunjung-ro (road), but the best place to
enjoy the blossoms is from the southern edge of Yeouido Park to the KBS Annex Building.

A sister festival, VIAF (Various Integrative Artistic Festival) will present performing acts and
pieces including dance, theater, mime along the blossoms throughout the festival.

 
**Please be advised, this article specifies 2014. Exact event details are to be announced
seasonally**

Part of the collection at the royal castle in Warsaw, it stands at 4 meters high and 6 meters high. Its overwhelming presence is sure to captivate viewers.

name: Andy Warhol LIVE
summary: Originally taken from the the Andy Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh, this exhibition includes photos of Andy Warhol's childhood, unique self-portraits, as well as works that were used in commercial advertising while Warhol was living in New York. There will of course be the extremely well-known Campbell Soup series as well as his silkscreen works, one major way Warhol came to fame during the 60's and 70's.
description_html:
Originally taken from the the Andy Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh, this exhibition includes photos of Andy Warhol's childhood, unique self-portraits, as well as works that were used in commercial advertising while Warhol was living in New York. There will of course be the extremely well-known Campbell Soup series as well as his silkscreen works, one major way Warhol came to fame during the 60's and 70's.
We can't forget about his portraits of Marilyn Monroe, Mao Zedong, Michael Jackson, Muhammed Ali, Mick Jagger, and many more famous figures, a total of 40 different portraits. Films produced by Warhol will also be available at the exhibit as well as a large collection of time capsule items that belonged to Warhol. In total, there will be about 400 different items that will be on display.
Look out also for the camouflage self-portraits, Skulls, Raphael Madonna, $6.99, work that is over 2 meters tall and digital works that were recovered after 30 years. Considering Warhol's status as a leading pop artist icon, you don't want to miss this special opportunity to have such a thorough and comprehensive view of his work. Grab the chance while it's here! The exhibition will take place at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) from June 6-September 27, 2015.

name: Kansong Munhwa- the Scent of a Scholar
summary: Apart from the works of Yi Jung, you can also see the works of Kim Jeong-hui, Sim Sa jeong, Danwon Kim Hong-do, etc. There are approximately 100 different works from 31 different painters.
description_html:
This exhibition will be held from June 4 - August 30.

There's the Japanese apricot that takes the risk of blooming in early spring, the orchid that grows deep in the forest and gives off a delicate fragrance, the chrysanthemum that blooms in the midst of late fall, and the bamboo that does not lose its greeness even while growing in the winter. People from long ago labeled these four plants as the "Four Noble Ones" or the "Four Gentleman." The Four Gentleman were prominently seen in the literature and the arts and paintings of the four flowers became an important contribution.

These four flower paintings started to appear during the middle of the Goryeo dynasty, and then even more in the Joseon dynasty. Especially during the latter half of the Joseon dynasty, the paintings started to include the main colors of the Joseon dynasty. This exhibition will show all the famous four flower paintings from the Joseon dynasty until now.

The majority of the work that will be on display during this exhibition will be from painters that were alive during the middle of the Joseon dynasty.

description_html:

At that time, prints were still considered a new type of art movement and it played an important role in establishing Korean contemporary art. This exhibition attempts to shed light on how this new type of art was birthed from the rapid changes that were happening in society.
Alot of the work is influenced by the artists' own personal experiences and the actual events that were taking place in society at that time. One can certainly get a proper feel for the times and what the artists were interested in.

name: Esprit Dior - Dior Spirit
summary: “Esprit Dior” will be open from June 20th until August 25th at the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP). Explore Christian Dior’s world of dresses, perfumes, accessories, pictures, and more. The exhibition illuminates the uniqueness of The Dior brand and the special history that it has.
description_html:
“Esprit Dior” will be open from June 20th until August 25th at the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP). Explore Christian Dior’s world of dresses, perfumes, accessories, pictures, and more. The exhibition illuminates the uniqueness of the Dior brand and the special history that it has.
The Dior exhibition has 10 different themes: 'Paris,' 'Dior and his artist friends,' 'Dior Garden,' 'Dior Allure,' ‘Dior Atelier’, ‘Dior’s Stars’, ‘Versailles: Trianon’, ‘Miss Dior’, ‘From Pink to Red,' ‘J’adore’. Dior’s library is even open for viewing, making it a total of 11 different exhibitions that are open to the public. In addition, Dior has collobarated with 6 of Korea’s major artists: Do-Ho Suh, Lee Bul, Heryun Kim, Kim Dong-Yoo, Kiwon Park and Seon-Ghi Bahk. Each of the artists showcase art as inspired by Dior.
On the same day as the opening of the Dior exhibition, the “House of Dior” store opened in Cheongdam. The architecture of the store is inspired by haute couture, and is meant to resemble the movement of fabrics and how they weave in and out. It took 4 years for the construction of the store to be completed, and there are a total of 6 floors. The store has accessories, fine jewelry, time pieces, women’s wear, shoes, and the Dior Homme collection. The boutique also has a VIP lounge, gallery, and a cafe operated by the world renown pastry chef, Pierre Hermé.

name: Cuban Culture and Arts Festival
summary: As en effort to get to know modern Cuban culture, the 2015 Cuban Culture and Arts Festival will be taking place from June 26-July 7.
description_html:
As part of a way to encourage cultural exchange between Cuba and Korea, two events will be taking place: 『Nuevo Cuban Jazz Concert』 and the 『Cuban Modern Film Festival』. What’s special about this year is that the Cuban and Korean government cooperated Together to make the festival happen. Alfredo Ruiz, the director of international relations at the Cuban Ministry of Culture will even be be visiting Korea for the first time.

『Nuevo Cuban Jazz Concert』
Date: June 25-27
Location: Ewha University, Samsung Hall

 This concert will give us the best of modern Cuban jazz and dance. One of the leading Cuban jazz duos, Alfertico Lescay & Formas, takes the rhythm and melody of modern jazz And combines it with traditional Cuban folk music. This fusion gives you the feeling of being in a dream and is also a nice harmony of traditional and modern.
Due to her great interest in Latin American culture, Mina Sohn, a former KBS announcer who has now successfully transitioned into travel writing, will MC the opening night of the concert at 8 pm on the 26th.
Also, for the first time in Korea, the 『Cuban Modern Film Festival』 will be taking place from June 27-July 5 at the Korea Film Archive. The film festival will feature 9 modern movies (with one animated short) that were created after 2011. For anyone that’s a movie buff, this is a great way to see a new dimension of Cuban movies.
As an extra event, there will be a chance to discuss the future of the Korean and Cuban movie Industry at the “Korean-Cuban Movie Seminar.” A well-known movie critic from Cuba will lead the discussion. Ernesto Daranas, the director of “Conducta,” a well-received movie in the film world, will also be present and the audience will have a time to ask questions and talk with the director.

name: Dano Festival
summary: Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok.
description_html: Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok. The holiday originated from the Mahan Confederacy, a confederation of Korean states that existed more than 2,000 years ago. Also called Surit-nal, it is celebrated on the fifth day of the fifth month of the lunar calendar. This year it falls on Thursday, June 1. On Dano, women traditionally wash their hair in water boiled with sweet flag, and men wear iris roots around their waist. Tteok (rice cakes) made with herbs are also eaten on this day. You can experience Dano and its related customs at the Namsangol Hanok Village or at the National Folk Museum of Korea. A variety of events are scheduled, including washing hair with sweet flag, making bows, fans, and kites, tasting herb rice cakes, riding swings and more.

name: Music at the Royal Palace
summary: From May to October of each year, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ is held at Changdeokgung (Palace), Deoksugung (Palace), Gyeongbokgung (Palace) and Jongmyo (Royal Shrine).
description_html:
Starting from May 4 until October 13, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ will be held at Changdeokgung (Palace), Deoksugung (Palace), Gyeongbokgung (Palace) and Jongmyo (Royal Shrine). After the first successful traditional arts performance in 2008, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ has become a permanant show since 2009. Every spring and autumn, each palace offers a wealth of cultural events to watch for both locals and foreigners who visit.

｢Music at the Royal Palace｣ not only provides entertainment for vistors with traditional musical performances and storytelling, but also offers visitors a chance to experience the elegance of palaces and the depth of traditional Korean arts by bringing culture, history and arts together. In order for viewers to truly experience the beauty and original atmosphere of the palace and music, the stage, sounds and lightings have all been reduced to a minimum. 
 
Experience the elegance of Court Music ｢Changdeokgung (Palace) Concert｣

Changdeokgung (Palace), designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, will be holding a very special concert. Vistors can take a stroll through Huwon, a garden of natural beauty, and enjoy the traditional music that fills the air. Vistors can watcch traditional court music every Sunday morning at Nakseonjae (the Queen's private residential area). For 270 years, the palace was home to the Joseon government and was also the favored residence of many Joseon Dynasty kings. This makes Changdeokgung (Palace) the longest-serving royal residential palace. Compared to other palaces, Changdeokgung is well-preserved and still has many of its original features. A particular virture of Changdeokgung is the way its buildings blend into the surrounding landscape.
The World of Musical Storytelling ｢Deoksugung (Palace) Concert｣

Deoksugung (Palace), a place where the past and present coexist, will feature storytelling concerts for children. Every Saturday and Sunday, a fusion blend of folk music and folktales will be performed at Hamnyeongjeon (King Go Jong's sleeping quarters). Masterpieces like「The Little Prince」and 「The Giving Tree」are brilliantly recreated with traditional Korean music and animations, satisfying both the eyes and ears. The concert will bring back heartwarming memories for adults and create dreams and fantasies for children. 
 
What kind of music did kings listen to? ｢Gyeongbokgung (Palace) Concert｣

If a king still lived in Gyeongbokgung (Palace) today, what kind of music would he listen to? He would have likely enjoyed a wonderful musical culture that perserves tradition, yet embraces the music of today. Enjoy festivities of Court Music that best matches the ambience Gyeongbokgung. 
One of a kind music ｢Jongmyo Jeryeak with Commentary｣

Jongmyo jeryeak (Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Confucian Memorial Ceremony Music) is a ceremonial music that is dedicated to all kings of Joseon Dynasty. Jongmyo jeryeak was registered as the first Korea Cultural Heritage and is also registered with UNESCO World Intangible Cultural Heritage. It is difficult to listen the Jongmyo jeryeak aside from when it is annually performed at Jongmyo (Royal Shrine) once a year. ｢Jongmyojeryeak with a commentary｣ offers visitors the opportunity to not only listen to, but also to understand the history and culture of Jongmyo jeryeak through commentaries.

name: Seoul International Fireworks Festival
summary: The Seoul International Fireworks Festival is held in early October of each year in front of the 63 City Building at Yeouido Hangang Park.
description_html:
※ The 2016 Schedule Is Coming Soon

The Seoul International Fireworks Festival is held in early October of each year in front of the 63 City Building at Yeouido Hangang Park. This festival is one of Seoul's most popular fall events, and watching fireworks paint the sky and water in a breathtaking spectacle. The massive crowds that gather around the Hangang River also adds to the festive atmosphere. 

For the best views, head over to Yeouinaru Station and walk along the river until 63 City Building. If crowds make you uncomfortable, go to the following locations to enjoy the fireworks in relative peace and quiet: Ichon Hangang Park, Nodeul Island, Hangang Bridge Observatory, Sayukshin Park, Seonyudo Park, and Noryangjin Seafood Market Parking Tower.

name: Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung Palace
summary: The Changing of the Royal Guard is a re-enactment of the ceremony from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) for changing the guards that protected and patrolled the royal palaces, and were in charge of the opening and closing of the gates to the palaces.
description_html:
During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guards were responsible for guarding and patrolling the gates of the capital city and the royal palaces. The royal palace guards, who were known as the "Wanggung Sumunjang", had the very important duty of protecting the king by guarding the entrance gates of the primary royal palace where the king resided. They were in charge of opening and closing the palace gates, inspecting all visitors, and maintaining a close surveillance of the palace. They were divided into day and night shifts, and the Changing of the Guard ceremony took place whenever the shifts changed over. 

In the late period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Changing of the Guard ceremony was conducted at Deoksugung Palace as at that time Deoksugung was the primary royal palace and the king then resided there. The Changing of the Guard ceremony was originally conducted at Gyeongbokgung Palace in the early Joseon period, but was moved to Deoksugung when Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace after Gyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Invasions of 1592 - 1598. 

After some extensive historical research, this splendid and elegant traditional Korean royal court cultural ceremony was first re-enacted in 1996 and has been a must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions ever since. This ceremony is a great opportunity to experience a rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments. A tradition comparable to the Changing of the Guards at Buckingham Palace, this ceremony takes place three times a day in front of Daehanmun, the main gate of Deoksugung at 11:00, 14:00, and 15:30 p.m. (except for on Mondays).

The Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung starts with two mounted soldiers leading the way, and a total of 78 Sumungun making an appearance, led by the Sumunjang in the order of Sumunjang, Sumungun, Sungjeongwon Juseo, Aekjeongseo Sayak and Chwiracheok. Once all the Sumungun have arrived with the drumbeat of the Chwiracheok (a military band), it marks the beginning of the changing ceremony.

name: 2020 Namsangol Hanok Village Taekwondo Performance
summary: The performance is open to the public for free, featuring the dynamic movement and flow of Taekwondo martial artists that display the mental toughness and refined discipline of the sport, as well as the fortitude of traditional Taekwondo.
description_html:
Even COVID-19 cannot put a stop to the extraordinary world of Taekwondo!


Despite the ongoing pandemic continuing to cause a stir across the globe this year, the 2020 Namsangol Hanok Village Taekwondo Performance has discoverd a breakthrough by which this uniquely proud martial art form, native to Korea, will be brought to spectators online in hopes of awakening the drive to better care for ourselves amid the constant routine of home quarantine, in addition to satiating that thirst for a cultural lifestyle. The performance will be hosted by one of the iconic boy-bands of the K-pop world, Super Junior's lead singer, and variety program MC, Lee Teuk, alongside English-speaking TV personality, Eva Popiel, adding even more style and dynamic to the performance, while the Taekwondo masters set to take the stage will showcase both the value and excellence of the Taekwondo tradition.

name: Hanyangdoseong in the Past and Present
summary: Awe at the transformation of the Hanyangdoseong following liberation from Japanese rule to the present day through a compare and contrast with the past appearance of the wall during the 1960s and 70s.
description_html: Ever since the first shovel was dug into the dirt at the start of the Hanyangdoseong restoration project in 1975, the wall went through an extraordinary amount of changes, including the rebuilding of fallen parts of the wall and the restoration of worn or destroyed castle gates, as well as the unearthing of new sections buried in the ground. Hanyangdoseong has always been an intimate part of everyday life for the people of Seoul, but it has gone through many changes over years and year. The Hanyangdoseong from the Records series is the fourth installment of this exhibition that uses photography to closely compare and contrast the present manifestation of the wall with a past not so long ago. The exhibition aims to provide the opportunity for visitors to appreciate all the repairs and restorations gone into the structure, while thinking about the future projects and tasks that lie ahead.

name: A Space for Ideas: A Sculptor's Sketchbook
summary: Visit the memorial exhibition commemorating the 50th anniversary of Song Young-soo's passing, a Korean abstract, metal sculptor.  All 17 of his sculptures will be on display, including 16 of his most signature works, "Martyr" [1967] and "Bird" [1969], and one replica of a public sculpture. In addition, there will also be 150 drawings, esquisses (rough sketch), and public sculpture designs found within nearly 100 sketchbooks for visitors to explore.
description_html: The Seongbuk Museum of Art is holding a special exhibition in commemoration of Korean sculptor, Song Young-soo, and the 50th anniversary of his passing. He was a famous sculptor, home to the Seongbuk area, renowned for his pioneering the art of abstract metal sculptures. From the late 1950s, when he made one of the first attempts at a welded sculpture in Korea, to the day of his passing in 1970, he crafted numerous abstract welded sculptures that helped broaden the horizon of Korea's modern-day sculpturing community. Within a short span of 20 years, he was able to conjure as many as 3,000 drawings and sketches, all of which convey, in detail, the effort in brainstorming varied ideas on his way to bringing his art to life. The exhibition seeks to examine his artwork in a new light, centered around nearly 100 of his own personal sketchbooks that capture each of his drawings that foreshadowed the fruition of both his abstract and public sculptures.

name: History Has Failed Us, but No Matter
summary: Visit the Korean Pavilion of the 58th International Art Exhibition, La Biennale di Venezia.
description_html:
Who was it that defined the norms of narrating history? And who has yet to be included as a part of that history? These questions were initially asked in Venice, Italy, in the summer of 2019, and continue on at the Seoul Arko Art Center for this very special event. The exhibition approaches the themes of modernity and East Asia through the lens and medium of "gender" and "tradition," respectively, while thinking about the relationship with the rise of tradition based on the critical understanding of issues regarding the process of the modernization of Asia. In addition, the exhibition seeks to explore the new possibilities of tradition that go beyond the norms and boundaries of Western modernity through employing a gender-complex awareness.

We hope that Nam Hwa-yeon, Jung Eun-young, Jane Jin Kaisen, and other attending artists are able to keep asking those sharp questions needed to both resist and disprove the norms of history through their artwork, while the rest of us can collectively reflect on this topic together with the artists.

We hope that Nam Hwa-yeon, Jung Eun-young, Jane Jin Kaisen, and other attending artists are able to keep asking those sharp questions needed to both resist and disprove the norms of history through their artwork, while the rest of us can collectively reflect on this topic together with the artists.

name: Fighting Epidemics in Joseon Dynasty
summary: Learn about how the people of Joseon fought back against the spread of an epidemic.
description_html:
The National Museum of Korea (Director General Bae Kidong) is running a theme-based exhibition, "Fighting Epidemics in Joseon Dynasty," from May 11 to June 21, 2020. The exhibition places its focus upon communicating a message of hope to the public amid the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic by shedding some light on how people during the Joseon Dynasty dealt with the fear of epidemics. Especially back in those times, the sudden onslaught of a proliferating disease invoked a gripping fear among everyone. In fact, there are a number of records from the Joseon Dynasty that provide some narration during the spread of a pandemic.


Curious as to how people were able to overcome such a pressing threat back then? Everyone is invited to gain an appreciation of the determination it took to live on through such dark times, especially in comparison to the present, and valiantly overcome the fear that was faced.

name: Seoul as the Main Character of Novels
summary: A special exhibition shedding light on Seoul and its people through literature and poems dating back to the country's Independence, up through the April Revolution.
description_html: In commemoration of the 70th anniversary of the Korean War and 60th anniversary of the April Revolution, the special exhibition, Seoul as the Main Character of Novels, takes an intimate look at the city of Seoul and its people during the period following independence from Japan, up through the April Revolution, through various works of literature. As many as 500 works will be on display, including Park Wan-seo's 『The Thirsty Season』 and 『The Naked Tree』, Cho Ji-hun's 『Stand Before History』, and Park Tae-sun's 『The Collapsed Theater』. The exhibition provides the priceless opportunity to peak inside the pages of history to better understand the lives at the time of independence and the Korean War, as well as the very real anecdotes of those struggling to survive.
